He addressed the assembly, saying: "This matter is direct and precise; even men of immeasurable capacity cannot emerge from it.

Yun said, "The cypress tree in the courtyard.
Wuzu Jie said, "Why does the Master take another person's property and treat it as his own for personal use?
He addressed the assembly, saying, "Brothers, do not stand about for long. If you have matters to discuss, speak; if you have no matters, then exhaust your reasoning beneath the robes and bowl."

Excellent. When this old monk was traveling on pilgrimage, apart from the two daily meals of gruel and rice, there was no other place for the mind to be distracted; outside of these, there was no other point at which the mind could wander.
If one does not act in this manner, the goal of leaving the household life remains very far away.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "If you spend your entire life never leaving the monastic groves and do not speak for ten or five years, no one will call you a mute;
even the Buddha himself will have no recourse against you."
He addressed the assembly, saying: "Brothers, if you come from the south, I shall unload for you; if you come from the north, I shall load for you. Therefore it is said:
'If one approaches a superior person and asks about the Way, one loses the Way; if one approaches an inferior person and asks about the Way, one attains the Way.
Brothers, when a righteous person speaks of heterodox teachings, those heterodox teachings are entirely correct; when a heterodox person speaks of orthodox teachings,"

The Dharma: where the True Dharma is entirely perverse. In other quarters, it is difficult to see and easy to recognize; here with me, it is easy to see and difficult to recognize. Addressing the assembly, he said:
"This matter is like a bright pearl in the palm of one's hand: when a barbarian comes, it appears as a barbarian; when a Han person comes, it appears as a Han person.
This old monk takes a blade of grass and makes it the sixteen-foot golden body; he takes the sixteen-foot golden body and makes it a blade of grass. Buddha...
"These are afflictions. Afflictions are themselves the Buddha.
He said to the assembly, "As soon as there is right and wrong, one becomes distracted and loses one's mind. Is there still any possibility of answering the question?
Later, a monk reported this to Luopu, who tapped his teeth. The monk then reported it to Yunju, who said, "Why bother? The monk returned and reported this to [his master].
The Master said, "In the south, there are many who have lost their bodies and forfeited their lives. The monk said, "I beg the Master to cite one.
As soon as the Master cited one, the monk pointed to a monk standing nearby and said, "This monk speaks such words. Thereupon, the Master ceased speaking.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "The Ultimate Way is not difficult; it simply dislikes discrimination. As soon as there is speech, there is discrimination;
there is clarity. I, the old monk, do not abide within clarity. Do you all, my monks, cherish and protect it or not?
A monk asked, "Since the Master does not abide within clarity, what is it that you cherish and protect? The Master said, "I do not know either. The monk said, "Master..."
Shang said, "Since you do not know, why do you say that the Way does not reside within clarity? The Master said, "It is permissible to ask about the matter;
after prostrating, withdraw.

Later, during a small assembly (xiaochan), the Master addressed the community, saying, "Tonight I shall provide an answer. Anyone who has a question to ask, please come forward. At that time, there was...
As soon as a monk emerged to prostrate, the Master said, "Throwing a brick to draw out a jade; you have drawn out nothing but a brick.
Later, Fayan asked Jue Tiezui, "What was the meaning of the former master? Jue said, "It is like a state appointing a general.
Fayan then asked, "Who could go there? Jue replied, "I could go. Fayan said, "You cannot go. Jue said, "I understand. Fayan said, "I understand too."
Xuedou said: "A person of keen intelligence knows where the point lies as soon as it is raised.
Even so, let us let go of Jue’s Iron Beak. Now, the words of a patriarch are never uttered in vain; one who comes forward must surely be a master.
Why, then, does he throw a brick to draw out a tile? O Zen adepts, do you wish to recognize Zhaozhou? His past exploits on the battlefield are beyond measure."
People recognize this; one need only value his merit, which covers the ages.

The Master gave a teaching, saying: "I do not like to hear the word 'Buddha'. He also said: "If you do not recognize the profound principle (*xuanzhi*), your efforts at meditative stillness are in vain.
A monk asked: "What is the profound principle? The Master replied: "Money hanging on the wall."
The Master gave this instruction: "When I was traveling southward on my pilgrimage, there was a 'no host and no guest' koan at the hearth.
To this very day, no one has brought it forth."
One day, the Master fell in the snow and cried out, "Save me! Save me! At that time, there was a monk who lay down beside the Master;
the Master then got up and left.
Cuiyan Zhi said, "This monk is caught in Zhaozhou’s snare. Is there anyone who can get out?
When the master was informed by an attendant that the Great King was arriving, he rose and bowed, saying, "Ten thousand blessings, Great King!
The attendant said, "He has not yet arrived. The master replied, "And yet you say he has come."

Huanglong Nan said: "Everywhere it is leaked away; rare indeed is the meeting with a transcendental guest. The attendant only knows how to announce visitors, yet does not realize he is already in the imperial capital.
Zhaozhou entered the weeds to seek people, unaware that his entire body was covered in mud and water."
The Master engaged in a debate on doctrine with Wenyuan. They agreed not to compete for victory, but rather that the loser would forfeit a Hu-bing (Persian-style cake).
Wenyuan said, "I request that the Upādhyāya establish the thesis. The Master said, "I am a donkey. Wenyuan said, "I am the donkey’s stomach.
The Master said, "I am the donkey’s dung. Wenyuan said, "I am a worm in the dung. The Master asked, "What are you doing there? Wenyuan—
Yun said, "He has already passed the summer retreat there. The Master said, "Bring me that Hu-bing (sesame cake).

When the Master heard the śrāmaṇera shout "End of Session" (*canshan*), he said to his attendant, "Tell him to go. As soon as the attendant told him to go, the śrāmaṇera said, "Take care" (*zhenzhong*).
The Master said to a monk standing nearby, "The śrāmaṇera has entered the gate; the attendant remains outside the gate."
Yunju Xi said: "Where is the place where the śrāmaṇera enters the gate? It is at the place outside the gate.
If you understand it here, you will see Zhaozhou."
A monk took his leave. The Master asked, "Where are you going? The monk replied, "I am going to study the Buddha-dharma in various quarters.
The Master said, "Do not stay where there is a Buddha; run swiftly past where there is no Buddha. Even three thousand miles away, do not mistakenly raise [the teaching] when meeting people."
The monk said, "If that is so, then I shall not go. The Master said, "Plucking the willow flowers, plucking the willow flowers.
In the Master’s assembly, there were two monks who pushed one another, neither being willing to serve as the First Seat. An administrator informed the Master, and the Master said:

The general instruction was to serve as the second seat. The administrator asked, "Whom does the first seat instruct? The Master said, "Burn incense. [The administrator] said, "The incense has been burned.
The Master said, "The fragrance of precepts, the fragrance of concentration, the fragrance of wisdom, and the fragrance of liberation."

how will you respond? The monk said, "I cannot say it; I beg my teacher to speak for me. The Master said, "In winter, one simply says it is cold."
The monk said, “It is hot in the summer. He continued, “Suppose I were to ask you again: what is the ultimate matter? How would you respond?
The monk said, “I cannot say it. The Master said, “Just say: ‘I have come directly from Zhaozhou; I am no mere messenger.
That monk went to Xuefeng, who asked, “Where have you come from? He replied, “Zhaozhou. Xuefeng asked, “What did he say?”
[This is] a case. The monks brought up the previous story. Feng said, "It must have been our own Zhaozhou who did it.
Xuansha said, "How great Zhaozhou was! He did not even know his own defeat."
The Master asked a monk, "Where have you set out from? The monk replied, "Xuefeng. The Master said, "What words did he say? The monk said, "He usually says:
'The entire earth is the single eye of a śramaṇa. Where will you all go to defecate? The Master said:
"If the Elder returns, send him a spade.
Xuedou said, "Since this monk did not come from Xuefeng, it is a pity for Zhaozhou’s spade."
Langya Jue said: "Among the assembly, some say: 'Send the spade to bury it. If Zhaozhou had said, 'Send the alms bowl,' one would have said, 'To hold rice and gruel.
To apply such wild interpretations is like seeing things in a dream; how can you deliberate upon them?"

[The student] applied his mind. The Master said, "You are enslaved by the twelve hours; this old monk enslaves the twelve hours.

'It is that which this old monk has used throughout his life but never exhausted. The Master [passed away] in the fourth year of the Qianning era of the Tang dynasty, in the tenth...

Chan Master Lizong of Zihu in Quzhou (the tenth): a native of the Zhou family of Duanzhou. He addressed the assembly, saying: "All dharmas are vast and open;
what fetters them, what constrains them? It is you yourselves who within this give rise to notions of difficulty and ease. The source of the mind is a single unity, stretching across all things."
In the ten directions, those of the highest faculties naturally attain clarity. They do not see Nanquan’s words as being "so dull and obtuse" that such people are rare in the world;
rather, they see them as distinct and clear, where existence and non-existence are neither. It is only because they lack the resolve of a true man that they appear so weary.
Do you now wish to understand this easily? From antiquity to the present, there has never been a single ordinary person [who could].
Even when a sage appears before you, not a single word—whether good or evil—reaches your own ground. Why is this so? It is because when one does good, the good has no form;
when one does evil, the evil has no characteristic. Since there is already no self, with what can one define good and evil?
What then can be established as ordinary or holy? Do you still believe this? Do you still take it up and maintain it? There is.
What place is there to evade? It is just like trying to escape one's shadow at midday; can you truly escape it? If it is so now, it was so in the past;
when the present and the ancient coincide, can you still hide from it? The Buddha-dharma is profound and subtle; those who realize it naturally spur one another on.
Trivial, conditioned matters hinder the Great Matter. Have you not seen it said: "It would be better to..."

The body establishes the Dharma. Who can ever suddenly forget conditions? You who are benevolent, do you wish to take the shortcut and meet with Chan? Each of you should go back beneath your robes and bowls and look for it.

For you disciples, where there is no intention, you create intentions; where there is no matter, you create matters. Where there is no internal or external, you forcibly construct internal and external;

where there is no east or west, you falsely speak of east and west. For this reason, *śamatha* cannot be clearly realized, and consequently, the faculties and their objects cannot be mastered with freedom.
At that time, a monk asked, "How can one avoid being deluded by the faculties and their objects? The Master said, "Try to point out what it is that is deluded."
The Master said, "Come forward and look at the fundamental object. The monk replied, "I do not see it. The Master said, "Since you do not see it, from where does the delusive object come?
The monk bowed. The Master said, "You have seen the deluded thought again."

He addressed the assembly, saying: "Fortunately, you are already pitiable enough; why must you go to such lengths before others to seek out a mere fragment of sound and form, or the play of lips and tongue?
Let me ask you: how do you go about seeking those two characters, 'sound' and 'form'? Do you understand? I say that sound and form are like bubbles.
Is this for me to explain it to you, or is it for me to seek out sound and form for you? Try to deliberate on this."

Look! Do not think this is easy. If you understand the source, it is ultimately nothing other than yourself. It is like a round mirror: when a man approaches, a man appears; when a woman approaches, a woman appears;
even monks and laypeople, blue and yellow, mountains and rivers—the myriad phenomena—appear according to their respective forms and characteristics.
A single mirror reflects them all; it cannot be that the mirror itself has many different kinds. It simply reflects objects so they are revealed. Do you recognize this, O worthy one?
Have you attained the mirror yet? If you do not recognize the mirror, you will be entirely obstructed by men and women, blue and yellow, mountains and rivers, and the like;

what outlet for your radiance will there be? If you recognize the mirror, then even blue and yellow, men and women, the great earth, mountains and rivers, those with thought and those without thought, four-footed and many-footed creatures, those born from wombs, eggs, or moisture, and the heavens and hells—all of these [are reflected within it].
Within a single mirror, one fully perceives their respective proportions; whether long or short kalpas, whether form or emptiness, all can be clearly known as nothing other than these.
Have you not heard the meaning of the teaching that all phenomena are like reflections? Time passes with such rapidity; do not waste it in idle indolence.

This is a matter of great importance; you must certainly understand and grasp it. Addressing the assembly, he said: "Virtuous ones, do you still know Zi Hu’s intimate instruction? When walking, simply walk; when sitting, simply sit.
Even in such activities as drinking tea or eating rice—in all these various actions—what is there to hide? Virtuous ones!
Believe and accept this; do not forcibly contrive anything else. It is simply that you now harbor doubt where there is no doubt, and create trouble where there is no trouble.

Within the source of your own mind, you instead give rise to delusion. It is like abandoning a hundred thousand clear, vast oceans and recognizing only a few bubbles, declaring them to be the entire tide;
or like mistaking a few points of firefly light for the radiance of the sun. You will surely feel ashamed.

How shameful! While the number of the various sages who have attained the Way and its fruits is like the sands of the Ganges, you now instead settle for being a lowly ordinary person. Do not be negligent.
Below the triple gate, the Master erected a signboard. On the board was inscribed: "Zihu has a dog;
it takes people's heads at the top, takes people's hearts in the middle, and takes people's feet at the bottom. To hesitate for even a moment is to lose one’s body and life.
A monk asked, "What is Zihu’s dog? The Master said, "Wo! Wo! (Bark!)
Two monks came before Linji. As soon as they lifted the curtain, the Master shouted, "Look at the dog! The monks turned their heads, and the Master immediately returned to his quarters.
Xuedou said: "If I had seen him back then, I would have first chopped down his signboard before entering the temple.
When this fellow said, 'Look at the dog,' I would have let loose a tawny-tailed tiger for him.
Do any of you want to see it now? The sun is already getting late; return to your hall."
Liu Tiemo arrived. The Master asked, "Are you Liu Tiemo? He replied, "I dare not. The Master said, "Turn left? Turn right?
He replied, "Master, do not act so perversely. The Master then struck him.

While the Master and Śrīgupta were hoeing a garden, the Master lowered his hoe, looked back at Śrīgupta, and said, "The matter is not non-existent; yet, the moment you conceive a thought, you have already missed it.
Śrīgupta asked, "What is this 'matter'? The Master stepped forward, seized him by the chest, and gave him a kick. At that, Śrīgupta attained great enlightenment.
One night, at the hour of midnight, the Master was in the back storage area when he shouted, "Thief! Thief! Everyone started up in alarm.
One monk was seized by the Master, who cried out, "I’ve caught him! I’ve caught him! The monk said, "It’s not me, Master. The Master replied:
"It is indeed so; it is simply that you are unwilling to accept it.
The Master had a verse which says: "For thirty years I have dwelt at Zihu; My strength has been sustained by two meals of rice gruel daily.
When there is nothing to do, I go for a stroll up the mountain; I ask those who encounter me: do you understand?"
Chan Master Yunji Shizu of Zhongnan Mountain (Case 1). The Master asked: Nanquan said, "The mani jewel is not recognized by people;
it is intimately held within the Tathāgatagarbha. What is this *garbha*? Nanquan said, "That which comes and goes with you, Old Teacher Wang.
The Master said, "What about that which does not come and go? Nanquan said, "It is also that. He asked again, "What is..."
Zhuanquan called out, "Master! The Master responded, "Yes. Zhuanquan said, "Go; you do not understand my meaning. At this, the Master attained realization.

Xuedou added a comment regarding the point of departure and arrival, saying: "A fellow of the weeds. He further added a comment regarding the place of concealment, saying: "Even before, it was a place of hiding."
The saying goes: "Adding frost to snow. Furthermore, as for the question, "What is it like at the place of the pearl? he replied, "Precipice.

To employ skillful means atop a hundred-foot pole is not being a master. If you can apply a single eye here, and guest and host are mutually exchanged, you will be able to penetrate deep into the tiger's den.
If you do not act thus, even if you were the Patriarch himself who had attained enlightenment, it would still be of no avail.
This is a case of beginning well but ending poorly.
Chan Master Tanzhao of Baima in Jingzhou (Case 1) often said, "How joyful! How joyful! When he was about to pass away, he said:
He cried out, "Alas! Alas! Then he said, "The Old Man of Yama is coming to take me.
The head monk asked, "When you were thrown into the water by the Military Governor, your countenance did not change;
why now do you act like this? The Master picked up his pillow and said, "Tell me: which was it—then, or now? The head monk had no reply. The Master threw down the pillow and passed away.
Chan Master Jingcen of Changsha in Hunan (Total: 19) addressed the assembly, saying:
"If I were to exclusively exalt the teachings and the lineage, the grass before the Dharma Hall would grow a fathom deep. It is because I have no other choice that I tell you all:
the entire world of the ten directions is the single eye of a śramaṇa; the entire world of the ten directions is the whole body of a śramaṇa."
The entirety of the worlds in the ten directions is one's own radiance; the entirety of the worlds in the ten directions is within one's own radiance;
throughout the entirety of the worlds in the ten directions, there is not a single person who is not oneself. I have always told you all:
the Buddhas of the three periods of time, together with all sentient beings throughout the entire Dharma-realm, are the light of Mahāprajñā. Before this light...
At the moment of its arising, where do people find certainty? Before the light has even arisen, there is as yet no news of Buddha or sentient beings;
from where could mountains, rivers, and lands have come? A monk asked, "What is the eye of a śramaṇa? The Master said:

"Long and long, it cannot come out. The monk hesitated. The Master said, "Whether becoming a Buddha or a patriarch, it cannot come out; whether transmigrating through the six realms of existence, it cannot come out.
The monk asked, "I do not understand what it is that cannot come out. The Master said, "By day one sees the sun; by night one sees the stars. The monk said, "I do not understand.
The Master said, "The colors of Mount Sumeru are green and yet green."
The Master sent a monk to ask Chan Master Tongcan Hui: "After you met Nanquan, what was it like? Hui did not answer.
The monk asked, "Before you had met Nanquan, how was it? Hui said, "It cannot be said that there was anything else.
The monk returned and reported this to the Master, who showed him a verse: "The person sitting atop a hundred-foot pole—though..."

"However, merely being able to enter is not yet the truth. One must advance further from the top of a hundred-foot pole; only then will one manifest the entire body throughout the worlds of the ten directions.
At that time, a monk asked, "How does one advance from the top of a hundred-foot pole? The Master said, "The mountains of Lizhou and the waters of Langzhou."
The monk said, “I do not understand. The Master said, “The four seas and five lakes are all within the Imperial transformation.
The Huayan Master asked, “Is empty space definitely existent, or is it definitely non-existent? The Master said, “To say it exists is permissible; to say it does not exist is also permissible.
When empty space is said to exist, it is merely a provisional existence. When empty space is said to be non-existent, it is likewise merely a provisional [non-existence].”
"No," the monk said. "As the Master has explained, what scriptural authority is there for this? The Master replied, "Virtuous one, have you not heard?
The *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* says: 'The empty space of the ten directions arises within your own mind, like a single fragment of cloud appearing within the vast clarity.'"
Is it not the case that when empty space arises, it is merely a conventional name that arises? Furthermore, it is said:

"If even one person among you awakens to the truth and returns to the source, the empty space of the ten directions will all vanish and perish. Is this not the case that when empty space ceases, it is merely a conventional name that ceases?
This is why the old monk says: "Existence is provisional existence; non-existence is provisional non-existence.
A monk asked, "What is Mañjuśrī? The Master said, "Walls, fences, tiles, and pebbles are. The monk asked, "What is Avalokiteśvara?"
The Master said, "Sounds and speech are it. [The student] asked, "What is Samantabhadra? The Master said, "The mind of sentient beings is it. [The student] asked, "What is the Buddha?

The Master said, "The physical body of sentient beings is it. [The student] asked, "If the essence of all Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges is identical, why are there various names for them?
The Master said, "To return to the source through the faculty of the eye is called Mañjuśrī; to return through the faculty of the ear..."
Returning to the source is called Avalokiteśvara. Returning to the source from the root of the mind is called Samantabhadra.
Mañjuśrī is the Buddha’s wondrous discerning wisdom; Avalokiteśvara is the Buddha’s unconditioned great compassion; Samantabhadra is the Buddha’s wondrous, unconditioned practice.
These three sages are the Buddha’s wondrous functions; the Buddha is the true essence of these three sages. In terms of function, there are as many provisional names as there are sands in the Ganges.
In essence, they are collectively named as one Bhagavān.
While the Master was gazing at the moon with Yangshan, Yangshan said, "Everyone possesses this, yet they simply cannot make use of it."
The Master said, "Exactly so. I entrust you with its use. Yang asked, "How would you use it? The Master kicked him in the chest, knocking him over.
As he was rising, Yang said, "Right under your feet, you are like a great tiger" (for this reason, he was called "Mount Cen the Great Tiger").
Baofu Zhan said: "Everyone says that the Great Tiger is extraordinary; you must know that Yangshan possesses the mechanism for trapping tigers.
Lanxi Jue said: "Though Li Ling was a skilled hand, how could he avoid falling into the hands of the barbarians?"
The Master returned from traveling the mountains. Upon reaching the gate, the Head Seat asked, "Where have you come from, Preceptor?

The Master said, "I have come from traveling the mountains. The Head Seat asked, "To what places did you go? The Master said, "At first I followed the fragrant grasses away; then I returned, chasing the falling blossoms.
The Head Seat remarked, "That is very much like the spirit of spring. The Master said, "It is even better than autumn dew dripping upon lotuses."
The Senior Monk Xiū asked, "After Nanquan passed away, where did he go? The Master said, "When Shitou was a novice monk, he went to visit the Sixth Patriarch.
[The monk] said, "I am not asking about when Shitou was a novice monk and visited the Sixth Patriarch.
After Nanquan passed away, where did he go? The Master said, "I will have him ponder it. [The monk] said, "Venerable Sir..."
"There is only a thousand-foot cold pine; moreover, there are no sprouting bamboo shoots from stones. The Master did not respond.
The monk said, "Thank you for answering my question," yet the Master still did not respond. Xiu recounted this to Sansheng, who said, "If it is truly so, it is even superior to Linji’s seven steps.
Nevertheless, I must verify it for myself before I can accept it. He then went to visit and asked, "I have heard that you, the Master..."
Regarding the answer to the story of Nanquan’s passing: it may be said that it outshines the past and surpasses the future, something rarely heard from ancient times to the present.
The Master likewise did not respond. When the official Hauru asked the Master, "An ancient worthy said, 'When one realizes, karmic obstacles are originally empty;
when one has not realized, one must repay former debts. Yet why was it that the Venerable Siṃha and the Great Master the Second Patriarch nevertheless had to repay their former debts?"
The Master said, "Great Virtue, you do not recognize that the original state is empty. Feng asked, "What is the original state of emptiness?

The Master said, "Karmic obstacles are it. Feng asked, "What are karmic obstacles? The Master said, "The original state of emptiness is it. Feng was speechless. The Master then showed him with a verse:
"Provisionally existent, yet fundamentally not existent; Provisionally extinguished, yet fundamentally not non-existent. This is the meaning of Nirvana as the settling of debts: The single nature."
There was no difference between them.
A monk asked, "What is dhāraṇī? The Master pointed to the left side of his sitting platform and said, "This monk can recite it.
He asked again, "Is there anyone else who can recite it? The Master pointed to the right side of his sitting platform and said, "This one..."
The monk also recited it and asked, "Why is it that I do not hear it? The Master said, "Virtuous one, have you not heard it said:
'In true recitation there is no sound; in true listening there is no hearing'? The monk said, "If that is so, then sounds do not enter the nature of the Dharma-realm.
The Master said, "To seek contemplation apart from form is not right vision; to seek listening apart from sound is false hearing."
A monk asked, "What is the ordinary mind? The Master said, "When you wish to sleep, you sleep; when you wish to sit, you sit. The monk said, "I do not understand, Master.
The Master said, "When it is hot, seek coolness; when it is cold, turn toward the fire."
A monk asked, "What is the path that leads upward? The Master said, "A single needle and three feet of thread.
The monk asked, "How should one understand this? The Master said, "Sichuan cloth and Yangzhou silk."
A monk asked, "What is the sphere of activity of those who surpass all others? The Master said, "Like the eyes of a dead man.
The monk asked, "How is it when those who surpass all others meet one another? The Master said, "Like the hands of a dead man."
A monk asked, "Where has Nanquan gone after his passing? The Master said, "He became a donkey for the eastern neighbor and a horse for the western neighbor.
The monk asked, "What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "If you want to ride him, you ride; if you want to dismount, you dismount."
A monk asked, "The Buddhas of the three periods do not know it exists; the stray cat and the white ox, however, do know it exists.
Since they are the Buddhas of the three periods, why do they not know it exists? The Master said, "Before entering the Deer Park, they were still somewhat ahead.
The monk asked, "Why, then, do the stray cat and the white ox know it exists? The Master said, "How can you blame them?"
A monk asked, "How can one transform the mountains, rivers, and the great earth so that they return to oneself?

The Master said, "How can one transform oneself so that it returns to the mountains, rivers, and the great earth? The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "In the city of Hunan, the people are well-nourished."
Rice is cheap and firewood is plentiful; this is sufficient for the four neighbors.
A monk asked, "Form is emptiness, emptiness is form—what is the meaning of this principle? The Master showed him with a verse: "Where there is obstruction, it is not a wall;
where there is penetration, there is no void. If one can understand it thus, mind and form are fundamentally the same."

There was a scholar who, while reading the *Sūtra of the Names of the Thousand Buddhas*, asked, "I have heard the names of hundreds of thousands of Buddhas, but I do not know in what lands they dwell.
The Master said, "After Cui Hao inscribed his verse at the Yellow Crane Tower, did you, Scholar, ever write one yourself?
He replied, "I have never written one. The Master said, "There is no harm; it would be well for you to compose a piece."
A New Verse by Huanglong says: When the battle of Dharma raged before the Yellow Crane Tower, A hundred thousand Buddhas raised their banners of victory.
He has no land—where could he dwell? He won nothing more than a single poem of great talent.
Minister Zhu asked, "When an earthworm is cut in two, both ends move. I do not know in which head the Buddha-nature resides.

The Master said, "Do not engage in false conceptualization. Zhu said, "But what can be done about the movement? The Master said, "If you understand, it is simply because wind and fire have not yet dispersed."
One day, Zhu came to visit the Master. The Master called out, “Minister Shangshu! Zhu responded, “Yes.
The Master said, “That is not your Minister’s original life-source (benming yuanchen). Zhu said, “There cannot be a second master apart from the one who is currently responding to you.
The Master said, “Can you call the Minister ‘Supreme Honored One’? Zhu said, “If that were so, then I would not respond at all.”
[The monk] asked, "Is the Master not the true host of this disciple? The Master said, "It is not only when responding;
even when not responding, from time immemorial, it has been like the very root of birth and death. He then showed this verse:

"The student of the Way does not recognize the Real, Simply because they have long identified with the conscious spirit. This is the root of birth and death throughout immeasurable kalpas; Fools call it..."
To become the person of original substance.
Chan Master Xiangyan Yiduan of Dengzhou (three times) addressed the assembly, saying: "The Buddha is dust; the Dharma is also dust."
Running about seeking all day long—what rest can there be? Simply, at all times, let circumstances not hang upon the mind, and let the mind not hang upon things.
With no goodness to be grasped and no evil to be rejected, do not allow yourself to be caged by them; only then is this the true place of training.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "Speech is slander; silence is deception. Beyond both speech and silence, there is a matter that remains.
This old monk’s mouth is too narrow; I cannot explain it for you."
A monk asked, "For what reason is there nothingness? The Master said, "I have never paused.
He further said, "Even if one were to strip away everything until it is completely exhausted, leaving no pause, this would still be a temporary provision—a skillful means for guiding people.
As for that matter over there, such a thing is impossible."
Chan Master Xian of Lingjiu in Chizhou (Case 1) addressed the assembly, saying: "This is the fundamental matter for each of you.
If I were to tell you how to do it myself, it would be like drawing legs on a snake. This was the sudden teaching for the venerable monks present. At that time, a monk asked:
[The Master] drew legs on a snake and did not ask, "What is this fundamental matter? The Master said, "Try to say something.
As the monk was about to offer a word, the Master said, "Why are you drawing legs [on the snake]?"
Chan Master Zhuyou of Ezhou (Four Episodes). Master Jinlun Kego asked, "What is the Way?
The Master said, "Do not drive a stake into empty space. Kego said, "Empty space itself is the stake. The Master struck him.
Kego grabbed him and said, "Master, do not strike me; you will strike the wrong person in the future. The Master then returned to his quarters.
Yunmen said, "Adding a point to an arrow. A monk asked, "Master, you just said that, did you not?
Yunmen said, "Beating the bell to thank the echo; one catches a frog."
Xuedou said, "If you want this story to spread far and wide, you must have him caned and driven out.

The Master asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Min Province. The Master said, "The venerable masters of Min Province love to cite the saying, 'When a barbarian comes, he appears as a barbarian;
when a Han Chinese comes, he appears as a Han Chinese. Is that so? As the monk was about to open his mouth, the Master struck him with his palm. The monk said, "I wish to penetrate..."
"Longmen has once again suffered his forehead being branded. The Master said, "The gold of Yan fills the sea; a gnat shakes the mountain. The monk clapped his hands, laughed loudly, and departed.
The Master said, "A scabby dog does not wish to be born in heaven, yet it laughs at the white crane in the clouds."

When the Master saw the monk approaching, he made a single stroke with his hand. The monk then departed. The Master said, "This monk came without announcing his name and left without disclosing his surname.
The monk turned around and also made a single stroke with his hand. The Master said, "This monk does not even know my name."
The monk did not know his surname either. The monk said, "Tell me then, what is my surname? The Master said, "Alas! The Persian eating pepper!
The monk shook his sleeves and left. The Master said, "A skilled master-monk; he has natural presence."
A monk asked, "What is the practice of a śramaṇa? The Master said, "As for practicing, it is not non-existent; yet if you perceive it, you have gone astray.
The monk reported this to Dongshan, who said, "Why did you not add a further word, asking, 'What kind of practice is that? The monk returned and offered the further word.
The Master said, "It is the practice of a Buddha! It is the practice of a Buddha! When the monk returned and reported this to Dongshan, Dongshan said, "In Youzhou..."
"That seems acceptable. New罗 (Silla) is the most miserable. The monk then asked Dongshan, "What is the practice of a śramaṇa?
Dongshan replied, "The head is three feet long; the neck is two inches short."
The monk Rizi (Fanyi) was visited by Yaxi. The Master assumed a posture of rising. Yaxi said, "This mountain-demon spirit still sees me.
The Master said, "A transgression, a transgression! Just now I failed to respond properly. As Yaxi was about to offer further words, the Master rebuked him.
Yaxi said, "In the midst of a great battle, it is indeed difficult to withstand. The Master said, "So it is, so it is. Yaxi said, "It is not so, it is not so."
Zhaozhou said, "Pity those two fellows; they do not recognize the phrase for turning around.
Dafu Lu Xun (three times) asked Nanquan, "I have come from the Six Heavens. Is there still a body there?
Nanquan said, "Keep this clearly in mind and present it to a master. Lu said, "The Master is inconceivable. [He] arrived.
Regarding "Accomplishment within the World," Quan said: "What was just now was entirely the business of the Great Officer.
The Great Officer asked Nanquan: 'In my home, I have been raising a single goose in a jar; it has now grown large.'"
"It cannot come out of the bottle. Now, you must not break the bottle, nor may you harm the goose.
Master, how can it be brought forth? Master Quan called out, "Dafu! Lu responded, "Yes. Quan said, "It has come forth."
When Nanquan passed away, a high official went to offer condolences. The head of the monastery asked, "Why do you not weep for the late Master?
Lu said, "If you can speak the Way, then I shall weep. The head was speechless.
The Lay Practitioner Gan-zhi of Chizhou (Six Cases). Because Yan- tou was spending the summer retreat at his home, one day while he was holding a needle, Gan stood before him.
Yan-tou raised the needle and made a gesture as if to prick him. Gan turned to go back inside to put on his clothes and offer his thanks.
His wife asked, "What are you doing? Gan said, "Don't speak of it. His wife said, "What is there to say? Everyone should know. Gan raised [the needle].
Continuing from the previous conversation, the wife said, "From now on, for thirty years, I shall drink water only once and swallow it only once.
The woman said, "Do you know that the lives of all people throughout the entire earth have been pierced by the needle-point of Master Hō and carried away?"

[The monk] remained silent. The Master said, "I thought you were a son of the robe in the true sense; it turns out you are merely a scholar-monk.
He took up his staff and struck him out immediately.
Xuedou said: "Since there are neither sounds nor traces, where would the hunting dog go to seek them?

Is it by means of the cessation of sound and trace that one perceives Huangbo? O Zen adepts, if you wish to clarify the mechanism for falling into the tiger’s trap, you must also be practitioners of the fundamental school."
Chan Master Heshang Andong of Guangzhou (Case 2). While the Master was prostrating before the Buddha, a Chan practitioner asked him, "What is that which you are prostrating to?
The Master replied, "The Buddha. The practitioner pointed to the image and asked, "What is this? The Master was at a loss for words.

That night, he prepared his formal robes and prostrations, then went to ask the practitioner, "Today, I am deeply grateful for your inquiry; what was the meaning behind it? The practitioner—*text fragment ends here*.
The Chan practitioner asked, "Master, how many years of summer retreats (kṣānti) have you completed? The Master replied, "Ten. The Chan practitioner said, "Have you even left the household life yet?
The Master was utterly bewildered. The Chan practitioner continued, "If you do not understand this, what is the point of a hundred summers? He then invited the Master to visit Master Ma together.
By that time, Master Ma had already passed away, so the Master later attained the seal of his mind under Chan Master Baizhang.
When Yangshan was a śrāmaṇera, the Master called out, “Jizi, bring me the bench. Yangshan brought it to him.
The Master said, “Return it to its original place. He then asked, “Jizi, what is on the other side of that bench? Yangshan replied, “Nothing.”
The Master said, "This side for a moment. [The monk] said, "There is nothing. The Master called out again, "Jizi! Shan responded, "Yes. The Master said, "Go.
Changzhou Daci Huanzhong Chan Master (five cases total), a native of the Lu clan from Pufan, addressed the assembly, saying:
"I, this mountain monk, do not know how to answer questions; I simply recognize the illness. At that time, a monk stepped forward, and the Master immediately returned to his quarters.
Xuedou said: "In general, to uphold and establish the School of the Patriarchs, one must distinguish between gain and loss.
Now, Daci recognized the illness [of the monk] and did not answer his question; as soon as a monk stepped forward, he returned to his quarters. Xuedou recognized the illness and did not answer."
A monk came forward; [the Master] struck him across the back with his staff. Those from all quarters who recognized the illness would not engage in dialogue.
When a monk came forward, he surely possessed some extraordinary merit. There was only one who dared to provoke the Son of Heaven of the Great Tang—there were but three such individuals.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "A foot of practice is better than ten feet of talk; an inch of practice is better than a foot of talk.
Dongshan said: "Speak that which cannot be practiced; practice that which cannot be spoken."
Yunju said: "When walking, there is no path of speech; when speaking, there is no path of walking. When neither walking nor speaking, what path should one traverse?
Luopu said: "If both walking and speaking reach [the goal], then the fundamental reality is absent.
If both walking and speaking do not reach [the goal], then the fundamental reality is present."
Zhaozhou asked, "What is the essence of Prajñā? The Master replied, "What is the essence of Prajñā? Zhaozhou laughed heartily.
The next day, seeing Zhaozhou sweeping the ground, the Master again asked, "What is the essence of Prajñā?
Zhaozhou set down his broom, clapped his hands, and laughed heartily. The Master then returned to his quarters.
Xuedou said, "The one who came before laughs; the one who comes after also laughs. Within the laughter there is a blade.
Daowei Zhe said, "As soon as you see him laughing loudly 'he-he,' give him a slap. Tomorrow he asked again."

He waited for him to laugh and then gave him another slap. Had Great Compassion delivered these two slaps, and had Zhaozhou not responded to him, he could truly be called a man forged from cast iron, one whom the wind cannot penetrate.
While the Master was staying in a hermitage, Nanquan asked, "What is the master of this hermitage? The Master said, "Heaven! Heaven!
Nanquan said, "Setting aside 'Heaven' for a moment, what is the master of this hermitage? The Master said, "If you understand, then understand;
stop your incessant prattling. Nanquan then desisted.
A monk took his leave. The Master asked, "Where are you going? He replied, "To Jiangxi. The Master said, "Can you take this old monk with you?
He replied, "Not only the Master, but even those who surpass the Master cannot be taken along either. The Master then desisted.
Fenyang Shanzhao said: "I know your strength is slight.
Chan Master Puan of Pingtian on Mount Tiantai (the fifth) addressed the assembly, saying: "The divine radiance is unobscured; it is a sublime legacy for all ages.
Having entered this gate, do not harbor intellectual understanding."
He addressed the assembly, saying: "The Great Way is vast and empty; it is the ever-constant, true mind. Do not contemplate good or evil; let the spirit be clear beyond all things.
Following conditions to drink and feed—what else is there to do?"
The Master visited Moyuan. As Moyuan rose to greet him, the Master seized him and said, "To open the mouth is to lose;
to close the mouth is to perish. Apart from these two paths, I ask you, Master, to speak otherwise. Moyuan covered his nose with his hand. The Master let go and said, "One step is easy;
two steps are difficult. Moyuan said, "Why such a desperate hurry? The Master said, "If it were not for you, Master, I would not have escaped the various [reproaches]."
Just as he was checking his notes, Linji visited the Master. Upon reaching the crossroads, he first encountered an older sister-in-law tending oxen in a field.
Linji asked the sister-in-law, "Which way does the path across the flat fields lead? The sister-in-law struck the ox with a staff and said, "This beast goes wherever it pleases."
"I do not know this road. Jie said again, "I ask you: where does the path to Pingtian lead? His sister-in-law replied, "This beast;
even at five years old, he is still not fit for use. Jie thought to himself, "If one wishes to observe the person before them, first observe what they employ.
Thereupon, he felt the intent to pull out the nails and extract the wedges. When he met the Master, the Master immediately asked, "Have you ever yet..."
"Have you seen my sister-in-law yet? Ji replied, "She has already been sent away. The Master then asked, "Where have you recently departed from?

Ji replied, "Huangbo in Jiangxi. The Master said, "I knew it; I knew you would come to see a master. Ji said, "I have come specifically to pay my respects to the Master. The Master said, "We have already met.
The Master continued, "According to the etiquette between host and guest, you ought to perform three prostrations. The Master... [The text ends here].
[The Master] said, "Since this is the etiquette between guest and host, you must perform prostrations.
When the Master saw the monk approach, he took up his staff and struck him. The monk caught hold of the staff, and the Master said, "Just now, you were too hasty."
The monk snatched the staff and struck him. The Master said, "An adept! An adept! The monk bowed. The Master seized him and said, "In fact, it was you, Venerable, who acted with haste.
The monk laughed heartily and swept his sleeves, departing. The Master said, "The grass-robber has been utterly defeated."
Chan Master Changguan of Wufeng in Yinzhou (three cases total). He asked a monk, "Where are you going? The monk replied, "I am going to Mount Wutai.
The Master held up one finger and said, "If you see Mañjuśrī there, come back here and I will meet with you.
The monk was speechless.
The Master asked a monk, “Do you see the ox? The monk replied, “I see it. The Master said, “Do you see its left horn? Do you see its right horn? The monk was speechless.
The Master spoke on his behalf, saying, “I see that it has neither left nor right.”
A monk was taking his leave. The Master said, "When you go to various places, do not say that this old monk is here.
The monk replied, "I am not saying that the Master is here. The Master asked, "Then where do you say the old monk is? The monk held up one finger.
The Master said, "That already constitutes slandering me.
Chan Master Xingkong of Shishuang in Tanzhou (Case 1): A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?"
The Master said, "Suppose there is a person in a thousand-foot well, and you have not even an inch of rope to help them. How would you get this person out?
If you can get this person out, then I will answer your question regarding the meaning of the Westward Journey.

The monk said, "The Venerable Chang of Hunan also speaks of this person in all sorts of ways, east and west. At that time, Yangshan was standing nearby. The Master called out, "Novice! Drag this corpse out!"
[The text] records: Yangshan raised this question to Danyuan. Danyuan scolded him, saying, "You foolish fellow! Who is in the well?
Later, he asked Miaoshan, "How can one get out of the person in the well? Miaoshan called out, "Huiji! Yangshan responded, "Yes. Miaoshan said, "He has come out.
After Yangshan ascended to the abbacy, he said, "At that time, I gained my reputation from Danyuan's place; I gained my ground at Miaoshan's place."
Chan Master Changqing Da'an of Fuzhou (the sixth of the series), a native of the Chen family of this province, questioned Baizhang:

"A student wishes to recognize the Buddha; what is the Buddha? Baizhang said, "It is very much like riding a cow while searching for the cow. The Master asked, "What is it like after one has recognized him?
Baizhang said, "It is like a person riding a cow home. The Master asked, "How does one maintain this state? Baizhang said, "It is like tending a cow."
A man holding a staff stood watching them, not allowing anyone to trample the crops. Under these words, the Master attained realization of the ultimate meaning.
Later, when Chan Master You—who was a fellow student—founded the residence at Daopei, the Master went there to personally plow the fields to assist in the Way.
After You passed away, the Master succeeded him as abbot. Subsequently, he returned to Minchuan, where he founded Changqing and spent his final years there.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "All of you who have come here to see me—what are you seeking? If you wish to become a Buddha, you are already a Buddha yourself;
yet you run about in haste to other houses. Like a thirsty deer chasing a mirage, when will you ever attain accord?
If you, Ānanda, wish to become a Buddha, simply cease these many inverted attachments, delusions, and evils."
Awaken! The mind of sentient beings is defiled by impure desires; you yourself are precisely the Buddha of Original Enlightenment. Where else would you go to seek him separately?
This is why he dwelt at Mount Mui for thirty years, eating the rice of Mount Mui and excreting the dung of Mount Mui, yet did not study the Chan of Mount Mui.
He simply watched a single water buffalo. If it strayed onto the road or entered the grass, he would immediately pull it back.
He went out. If someone damaged the crops, he would immediately whip them. Having been tamed for a long time, they became pitiable;

they could understand human speech, and now they have transformed into a white ox in the open air. It is always right before one’s face, staring fixedly all day long, and even if you try to drive it away, it will not go.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "All of you possess a priceless great treasure. From the gateway of the eyes, it emits light that illuminates the mountains, rivers, and the great earth.
From the gateway of the ears, it emits light that perceives and gathers all sounds, whether good or evil. Thus it functions through the six sense-gateways day and night."
It constantly emits radiance; it is also called the Samādhi of Emitting Light. You yourself do not recognize its presence, as it is hidden within the body composed of the four great elements.
It is supported from both within and without, such that it dares not lean or tilt, like a person carrying a heavy burden crossing a single-plank bridge.
Nor does he teach one to lose one's footing. Now tell me: what kind of thing is it that, when thus supported, functions in this way?
If you seek it even for a hair’s breadth, you will not see it. Thus Master Zhizang said: "Seeking within and without, nothing at all is found;
yet the functioning within the realm of objects is entirely present."
He addressed the assembly, saying: "The phrase with meaning and the phrase without meaning are like a vine leaning against a tree. When Shushan heard this, he went directly to Miaoshan.
Finding the Master in the midst of plastering a wall, he asked: "The phrase with meaning and the phrase without meaning are like a vine leaning against a tree—is this not what the Master said?"
The Master said, "Yes. Shu asked, "What if one suddenly encounters a time when the tree has fallen and the vines are withered?

The Master set down his mud-plastering tray, laughed heartily, and returned to his quarters. Shushan followed him, saying, "I have traveled four thousand *li*, sold my bedding, and come specifically for this reason.
Why does the Master deceive me? The Master called to his attendant and said, "Bring..."
He returned the money to him and then instructed him, saying, "In the future, there will be a One-Eyed Dragon who will pierce through your delusions for you.

Later, Shushan went to Mingzhao and recounted the previous conversation. Mingzhao said, "Daguang (Daopei) may indeed be 'head straight and tail straight,' but he simply did not meet a true connoisseur.
Shushan then asked, "What is it like when the tree falls and the vines wither? Mingzhao said, "It would take even more than Daopei."
His laughter shifted into something new. Shushan consequently attained realization and said, "Miaoshan originally had a blade within his smile.
He then gazed toward Miaoshan from afar and prostrated himself.
The *Miaoxi Song* says: "If one uses these words to fixate upon the fundamental principle, One fails the Mingzhao, the One-Eyed Dragon.
Suddenly, within a smile, the paths of mud and water diverge; Only then does one know that from a thousand miles away, we share the same wind."

The Master (Yunmen) received it and said, "A mountain dweller of true character, moreover, leaves no marks from axe or hatchet."

Simply by departing from delusive conditions, one is the Buddha of Suchness. At these words, the master attained awakening and said: "How [marvelous]!"
Approaching old age, he was able to hear the matter of the ultimate principle. When the Master was about to pass away, he addressed the assembly, saying:

As the assembly listened intently, the Master had already entered nirvana.

"I tell you this: do you believe it? The Master said, "The Venerable One speaks with sincerity; how could I dare not believe? Zong said, "It is you yourself.

Under the Master’s words, he suddenly realized the profound meaning.
