now that you have packed your things, let me explain some of the Buddha-dharma to you. When the Master had finished packing, he returned to ask [Guizong].
Xun asked, "The weather is cold; take care on the road.
The Master visited his fellow student, Great Master Shixing. When the Great Master ascended the hall, he took the staff in his right hand and leaned it against his left side.
After a long silence, he said, "If this matter were not my elder brother Fuyong, it would be very difficult to fully comprehend. He then descended from the seat.
Huanglong Nan said: "If you cannot employ the true nature, then simply stop.
To take the Buddha-dharma and treat it as mere human sentiment will provide material for people's laughter for a thousand years to come. Tell me, where does the harm lie?"
Chan Master Gaoting of Hantan in Han (Case 1): A monk came to pay his respects to Jia Shan, and the Master struck him immediately.
The monk said, "I have come specifically to pay my respects; why do you strike me? He bowed again, and the Master struck him once more.
The monk returned and reported this to Jia Shan. Jia Shan asked, "Do you understand? The monk said, "I do not. Jia Shan said, "It is fortunate that you do not understand. Had you understood..."
[The Master] said: "Understood. Then he remained silent at the mouth of the mountain pass.
The Great Master Mao of Silla (two instances): Addressing the assembly, he said, "If you wish to recognize the Buddhas, recognize them within the mind of ignorance.
If you wish to recognize the eternally abiding, non-decaying nature, recognize it amidst the shifting and changing of all phenomena."
A monk asked, "What is the realm of Dameu? The Master said, "The blade is not revealed. The monk asked, "Why is the blade not revealed?
The Master said, "There is no one to meet it."
Chan Master Zhìtōng of Mount Wǔtái (Part II). The Master went to visit Guīzōng. Suddenly one night, he cried out, "I have awakened! I have awakened!
The next day, Guīzōng ascended the hall and asked, "The monk who had a great awakening last night—come forth!
The Master immediately stepped forward. Guīzōng said, "What principle did you perceive that you say you have attained great awakening? The Master replied, "A nun is originally [a man]."
A woman performed this act, which left Zong startled.
When the Master was about to pass away, he presented a verse to the assembly, saying: "Raising my hand, I grasp the Southern Dipper; turning my body, I lean upon the Northern Pole Star."
"Looking out from beyond the heavens: who is there like me?
This was the public teaching given by Zen Master Tianlong of Hangzhou, a successor of Zen Master Daming Meifachang: "The assembly, do not wait for the old monk to come up; [as soon as he arrives...]"
Above and below, as one descends, there are respectively Flower Adornment seas of nature, each fully endowed with merit and unimpeded radiance;
from each, one may take up and examine them.
A monk asked, "How can one escape from the three realms? The Master said, "Where are you right now?
Chan Master Daochang of Guannan in Xiangzhou, a successor of National Teacher Qian'an of Yanguan in Xiuzhou (Case 1). A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?"
The Master picked up his staff and said, "Do you understand? The monk replied, "I do not. The Master then struck him out.
Chan Master Jinzhou Cao, a Dharma successor of Chan Master Zhangjing Huaiyun of Jingzhao Prefecture (Case 1):
Once, when he invited Mihu for a meal, he did not arrange the seating positions. When Mihu arrived, he spread out his sitting cloth (*kaṣāya*).
He prostrated. The Master descended from his rope-seat, and Mi immediately took his place upon it.
The Master, however, sat on the ground. When the meal was finished, Mi departed. Later, the attendant asked, "The Master is revered by all people; today your seat has been usurped by another.
The Master said, "If he comes after three days, I shall receive him; if he does not come, I cannot save him."
Three days later, Guo Lai reported: "The other day I encountered bandits.
Langzhou’s Master Gudī (Fanyi) was visiting Yangshan. The Master said, "Go; you have no Buddha-nature.
Yangshan folded his hands, stepped forward three paces, and simply responded with an "Amen" (*e*). The Master asked, "Where did you obtain this samādhi?"
Mount Yun said, "I received my name from Danyuan and attained the ground at Guishan. The Master asked, "Are you not then a son of Guishan?
Mount Yun replied, "In terms of worldly truth, this is not non-existent; however, regarding the Buddha-dharma, I do not dare [claim it].
Mount Yun then asked, "From where did you, Reverend, obtain this samādhi? The Master replied, "I obtained this samādhi from Zhangjing. Mount Yun sighed and said:
Inconceivable! It is difficult for those who come to find a place of rest.
Chan Master Zhizhen of Guishan in Fuzhou (in two parts) went to visit Zhangjing. Zhangjing asked, "From where have you come?

The Master said, "I have gone nowhere to go; I have come from nowhere to come. Zhangjing silently granted him approval. Later, when he entered the inner quarters, he attained even greater depth in the profound mysteries.
Addressing the assembly, he said: "A movement of the face or a blink of an eye does not go beyond the person themselves. A single thought of pure mind is, from the very beginning, the Buddha.

The Venerable Master Puhua of Zhenzhou, Dharma heir of Chan Master Baoji of Panshan in Youzhou (total of eight [sections]). Whenever the Master saw someone, regardless of their status, he would always ring his bell once. At that time...
He was known as Master Puhua. Sometimes he would take a bell and ring it by a person’s ear, or pat them on the back;
when someone turned their head, the Master would reach out his hand and say, "Give me one coin."

Whenever the Master entered the marketplace, he would shake his bell and say: "If it comes from the bright side, I strike at the bright side; if it comes from the dark side, I strike at the dark side;
if it comes from the four quarters and eight directions, I strike with a whirlwind; if it comes from empty space, I strike with a continuous blow.

Linji then commanded an attendant to grab him by the chest and hold him fast, saying: "What if it does not come in any of these ways? The Master pushed him away and said: "Tomorrow, Great Compassion [Guanyin]."
There was a vegetarian feast at the monastery. On this occasion, the Master related the matter to Linji. Linji said, "I have always harbored doubts about this fellow.
The Master and Linji went together to a donor’s feast. Linji asked, "A hair swallows the vast ocean; a mustard seed contains Mount Sumeru.
Is this the wondrous function of spiritual powers, or is it simply the natural state of things? The Master then kicked over the dining table. Linji—
Ji said, "How very crude! The Master said, "What kind of place is this to speak of the crude or the refined?
Ji then desisted. The next day, they again went together to a family’s vegetarian feast. Ji asked, "Compared to yesterday, how does today's offering measure up?
The Master kicked over the dining table. Ji said, "How very crude! The Master said, "Blind fellow! What 'crude' or 'refined' is there to speak of in the Buddha-dharma?"
Ji (Dongshan) unconsciously stuck out his tongue.
Xuedou said, "These two old thieves have not even finished their meal; they deserve thirty blows of the staff.
Although the blows are dealt, which of the two is the real thief?"
One day, Linji was sitting with three others—He-yang and Mu-ta—in the hearth of the monks' hall.

They were discussing how the Master daily acted "wildly and crazily" in the streets and markets, and how one could not know whether he was a commoner or a sage. Just then, the Master suddenly entered the hall.
Ji asked, "Are you an ordinary person or a sage? The Master said, "Tell me, are you an ordinary person or a sage? Ji then gave a shout.
The Master pointed to the wooden pagoda at Heyang and said, "The new bride of Heyang; the grandmotherly Zen of the wooden pagoda.
Linji, that little fellow, actually possesses a single eye. Ji said, "This thief! The Master said, "Thief! Thief! and then went out.
The Master was in front of Linji’s hall eating raw vegetables. Linji said, “This fellow looks exactly like a donkey. The Master then brayed like a donkey.
Linji called to the steward, saying, “Give him a fine supply of fodder. The Master said, “The people of Shaoshi do not recognize me.”
Jinling has come again. Linji’s single eye opens for people everywhere.
Zhaozhou said: "Why not give him his rightful fodder?"
In the midst of the marketplace, the Master rang his bell and said, "I seek a place to go, yet it cannot be found.
Dao Wu grabbed him and said, "Where do you intend to go? The Master replied, "Where have you come from? Dao Wu was left speechless.
The Master jerked his arm free and walked away.
One day, when Master [Linji] saw Madao shouting "Clear the way!", he also shouted "Clear the way! and then assumed a wrestling stance.
Madao ordered his men to strike him with five blows of the staff. The Master said, "It is similar, but it is not the same."
As the Master was about to enter *parinirvāṇa*, he asked everyone around him for a *zhidu* (straight-cut robe). Everyone offered one to him, yet the Master accepted none of them.
Linji had a coffin purchased; when the Master returned, Linji said, "I have already made you a *zhidu*."
The Master laughed and said, "Linji, you talkative fellow! He then lifted the coffin, walked around the streets crying out, "Linji has finished making me my formal robe;
I am going out through the East Gate to pass away. The people of the market followed him in a procession to see him off. The Master said:
"Today is not an auspicious day for the 'Blue Bird' (Qingwu); tomorrow at the South Gate, he will pass away," the Master said. The people of the market followed him accordingly.
The Master spoke again, "Today is not yet propitious; tomorrow at the West Gate, he will pass away. No one believed him, and those who followed became sparse.
On the fourth day, the Master carried his coffin out beyond the north gate and entered it himself. Passersby on the road drove nails into it;

the townspeople informed one another and gathered around to watch. Suddenly, they heard the sound of bells growing fainter in the air. When they lifted the coffin to look inside, he had completely vanished from his body.
Master Mazu Gu Baoche of Puzhou’s Dharma heir, Lecturer Liangsu of Shouzhou (Case 1).
Initially, he went to visit Mazu. When Mazu saw him coming, he took up a hoe and entered the garden to weed.
The Master followed him to the place where he was weeding. Mazu paid him no heed and returned directly to his quarters, closing the door behind him. The Master [stood] outside.
The day passed and the valley-dweller closed his door again. The Master then knocked on the gate. The valley-dweller asked, "Who is it? The Master replied, "Liangsui.
As soon as he uttered his name, he attained sudden enlightenment and said, "Master, do not deceive Liangsui.

Had I not come to see you, I would have been led astray by the sutras and treatises for the rest of my life. Upon returning to his lecture hall, he began to expound the teachings, saying in brief: "All..."
What people know, Liang-sui knows completely; what Liang-sui knows, people do not know.
Yunmen said: "There is then a wave against the current; to enter now is the meaning of following the current."
This is also called "the occasion of simultaneous release. It is further said: Magu asked, "Whom [are you addressing]?
He replied, "Do not deceive Liangsui. This was not merely recognizing Magu’s moment of meeting him;

had he not come to pay respects to the Master, he would have been led astray by the sutras and treatises for his entire life. Thus, one knows there is a point where even this can mislead people. Furthermore—
[The Master] said: "What is it that Liangsui knows?
Chan Master Chuwwei of Qianzhou, successor to Chan Master Xitang Zhizang of Qianzhou (total of two [entries]).
A monk asked: "Regarding the Three Vehicles and the twelve divisions of the teachings, one attains the subtlety by realizing their fundamental principle."
"Is this the same as or different from the intent of the Patriarchs? The Master said, "You must discern it beyond these six propositions;
you must not turn according to sounds or forms. He asked, "What are the six propositions? The Master said, "Speaking; silence;
neither speaking nor silence; all of these; none of these. How would you do it? The monk had no reply.
The Master asked Yangshan, "What is your name? Yangshan replied, "Huiji. The Master said, "Which one is wisdom? Which one is stillness?
Yangshan said, "It is right before my eyes. The Master said, "There is still a distinction between before and after.
Yangshan said, "What do you see, Preceptor? The Master said, "Go and drink tea."

Chan Master Hui-chao of Shu-shan in Chi-chou, Dharma successor of Chan Master Ju-hui of Dong-si in Hunan (Case 1): When Dongshan arrived, the Master asked, "You have already established yourself in one place."
"Why have you come here? Dōng said. "I can do nothing with my doubt; that is why I have come to see the Master.
The Master called out, "Liang-jia! Liang-jia responded. The Master asked, "What is it? Dōng was speechless. The Master said, "A fine Buddha you have, but he lacks radiance."
Chan Master Jieling of Shanglin, Hunan, Dharma Heir of Chan Master Lingtuan of Yongtai in Jingzhou (Case 1). The Master visited Da Mian. Da Mian asked, "Virtuous One, how have you come?
The Master said, "My armor is fully equipped. Da Mian said, "Take it off before you come to see me. The Master said, "I have taken it off."
Yuanwu said, "The thief has not yet been struck; why do you take off your clothes? Later, when he studied under Yongtai, he finally understood its meaning.
Heshang Zhilin of Hunan (Case 1) constantly reviled Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra as malevolent spirits. Carrying a wooden sword in his hand, he claimed to be subduing demons.
As soon as he saw a monk approach, he would say, "A demon comes! and brandished his wooden sword wildly. [He hid...]
He entered the abbot’s quarters. This continued for twelve years; [Zhaozhou] set aside his sword and remained silent. A monk asked, "Before the twelve years, why did you subdue the demons?
The Master said, "A thief does not strike the home of a poor man. The monk asked, "After the twelve years, why do you not subdue the demons?
The Master said, "A thief does not strike the home of a poor man."
The Monk Bimō of Wutai (Case 1) constantly carried a staff. As soon as he saw a monk approach, he would raise his staff and say:
"What demon has caused you to leave the household life? What demon has sent you on pilgrimage?
If you can speak, you die under this staff; if you cannot speak, you die under this staff. Speak quickly! Speak quickly!"
Fayan Daoyuan said, "Beg for your life! Beg for your life! Xuanjue Daoshi said, "Old man, you may put down your crook.

Wuzu Fayan said, "If I had been there at that time, I would have snatched the crook away from him, thrust it over his neck and pinned him down, then lit a fire and looked closely to see how thick his skin was."
The Fifth Generation of the Southern Peak (Nanyue):
Chan Master Huijiao of Guangxiao Temple in Yangzhou, Dharma Heir of Chan Master Congshen of Zhaozhou Guanyin (Five in total). One day, the Master saw a pillar and joined his palms, saying: "No."
Shen asked, "World-Honored One, the Sangha says that the Preceptor is a pillar. The Master said, "To weep until the blood flows is of no avail;
it is better to keep one's mouth shut and pass through the remainder of spring."

When the Master arrived at Chongshou Monastery, Fayan asked him, "Where have you recently departed from? The Master replied, "Zhaozhou. Fayan said, "I have heard it said that Zhaozhou has the story about the cypress tree;
is this true? The Master said, "No. Fayan said, "Everyone who comes and goes says that when a monk asked, 'What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
Zhaozhou replied, 'The cypress tree in the courtyard. How is it that you, Venerable Sir, can say [it is not so]?"
"No. The Master said, "The former Master truly did not say such a thing. You must not slander the former Master, Reverend.
The Master then asked Song Qiqiu, "Do you understand how to speak? Song replied, "If it were speaking, it would not even admit of being applied. The Master said, "..."
"It cannot be attained through attachment," he said. "It cannot be attained through non-attachment. Song said, "In total, it is not like that.
The Master said, "That which cannot be grasped—[cut off its ear]. Song was speechless.
The Layman Zhang asked, "What about when one is old? The Master said, "How many years are you? The Layman said, "I am eighty. The Master said, "One may indeed be called old.
The Layman said, "Ultimately, what is it like? The Master said, "Even until one reaches a thousand years of age, it is still not yet [the end]."
Someone asked, "A certain person has slaughtered oxen throughout his life; does he still have sin or not? The Master said, "No.
The person said, "How can there be no sin? The Master said, "For every one he kills, he returns one."
Master Feng of Guoqing in Longzhou (in two parts) was asked: "Why did the hundred birds carry flowers to offer to Niutou before he had met the Fourth Patriarch?
The Master said, "A man from Shanfu sends money and goods to an iron ox. [The questioner] asked:
"After he saw him, why did they no longer carry flowers to offer? The Master said, "A wooden horse travels eight hundred *li* by dawn."
A monk asked, "Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings the same or different? The Master said, "The rain nourishes the three types of grasses into splendor;
the spring breeze does not wrap one's head. The monk asked, "What is it to be a renunciant? The Master said, "Copper heads and iron jaws; bird beaks and deer bodies.
The monk asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "Śākyamuni is the Ox-Headed Jailor; the Patriarch is the Horse-Headed One."
Facing Ābāng, [a monk] asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "Striking the west wall with the east wall.
Chan Master Xinjian of Wuzhou (Fanyi) never kept śrāmaṇeras or novices throughout his life. A Dharma Master once asked him:

"The Master is advanced in years; why do you not seek out a junior disciple to attend upon you? The Master said, "If there were one who was blind in his eyes, deaf in his ears, and mute in his mouth, seek such a person out for me. The host had no reply.
A monk asked Master Duofu of Hangzhou (Case 1): "What is the meaning of the single grove of bamboo at Duofu?
The Master said, "One stem, two stems, leaning. The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Three stems, four stems, curved."
Master Xi Mu of Yizhou (in two parts). The Master summoned his attendant; the attendant responded with "Yes. The Master said, "The night is deep and quiet;
let us deliberate together with him."
A layman raised his hand and said, "The Master is a donkey. The Master replied, "I have been mounted by you, old monk.
The man departed without a word. Three days later, he returned and said, "The other day, I was robbed by bandits. The Master took up his staff and struck him out.
Chan Master Rirong Yuan (1), Dharma Heir of Chan Master Lizong of Zihu in Quzhou.
When Upāsaka Huo arrived, the Master clapped his hands three times and said, "A fierce tiger stands in the gateway;
who is there to oppose it? Huo said, "A swift hawk soars toward the heavens; who can catch it? The Master said, "Difficult for both."
Dongshan said, "Stop for now; there is no need to resolve this public case. The Master took up his staff, performed a dance, and returned to his quarters.
Dongshan was speechless. The Master said, "This fellow is dead!"
Master Zitong (Case 1). A monk asked, “What is the realm of Zitong? The Master said, “Can you put sand into your eyes?
The monk said, “I do not recognize even this great and wonderful realm of Zitong. The Master said, “I, the old monk, do not conceal this matter.”
The monk went out. The Master descended from his rope-seat, seized him, and said, "Today there is a fine public case;
I have not yet received so much as a single coin. The monk replied, "Fortunately, I happened to meet you, a monk. The Master said, "Calamity does not come alone."
Master Fushí of Zhāngzhōu (Fàn Yī) addressed the assembly, saying: "I, this mountain monk, have opened a divination shop that can determine people’s wealth or poverty and settle their life or death.
At that time, a monk came forward and asked: "Setting aside wealth, poverty, life, and death, and not falling into the five elements—please, Master, speak directly.
The Master said: "Gold, wood, water, fire, and earth."
The Essential Record of the Linked Lamps, Volume Seven;
The Essential Record of the Linked Lamps, Volume Eight.
Compiled by the monk Wuming, successor to the Patriarchs, residing at Chongfu Chan Temple in Quanzhou.
Chan Master Changshu Jingcen’s Dharma heir, Chan Master Changtong of Xuedou in Mingzhou (Case 1). A monk asked, “What is the secret chamber? The Master said, “No air passes through.
The monk asked, “Who is the person within the chamber? The Master said, “All the sages seek to behold him, yet they do not see him. The monk prostrated.

The Master said: "A thousand sages cannot conceive of it; ten thousand sages cannot deliberate upon it. Whether heaven and earth perish or not, whether empty space encompasses or not—everything is beyond compare;
throughout the three periods of time, it cannot be brought forth by chanting."
The Monk Shiti, Dharma Heir of Chan Master Zhuyou of Ezhou (Two Cases).
When the Master saw an attendant carrying an alms bowl as he ascended the hall, he called out, "Attendant! The attendant responded.
The Master asked, "Where are you going? The attendant replied, "I am going to the hall for the midday meal. The Master said, "How could I not know that you were going to the hall?"
[The Master] said, "I am going to the hall for the midday meal. [The monk] said, "Apart from this, what else could you possibly say?
The Master said, "I am simply asking you about your fundamental matter. [The monk] said, "If the Master asks about my fundamental matter, I am truly going to the hall for the midday meal.
The Master said, "You do not fail to be my attendant."
There was one who came for a brief moment; he stood before the Master for a short while and then departed.

The Master said, "What grounds for clarification were there? The monk returned and stood for a long time. The Master said, "You have clarified it! You have clarified it! The monk asked, "After having clarified it, what then?
The Master said, "It can be buried. The monk cried out, "Heaven! Heaven! The Master said, "Just now you were like that. Like so.
Now, this was not appropriate, so the monk departed.

Chan Master Huiji of Mount Yangshan, a Dharma heir of Chan Master Lingyou of Daomiao in Tanzhou (number forty-five), was the son of the Ye family in Huaihua, Shaoyang Prefecture. Initially, he went to visit...
At Dayu. Daowei asked, "Are you a novice with a master, or a novice without a master? The Master said, "A novice with a master. Daowei asked, "Where is the master?
The Master walked from west to east and stood there. Daowei was struck by this.
Guishan asked the Master, "I have heard that while you were with your late teacher Baizhang, when asked one, you answered ten;
when asked ten, you answered a hundred. Is this true? The Master said, "I dare not say so. Guishan said, "Speak a single phrase regarding the ultimate point of the Buddha-dharma.

As the Master prepared to open his mouth, Guishan gave a shout. This occurred three times; three times the Master prepared to respond, and three times he was met with a shout. The Master shed tears and said:
The former master said, "You must meet the right person before you can attain it; today is precisely that meeting.
Thereupon, he resolved his mind and spent three years tending oxen. One day, when Guishan entered the mountains, he saw the Master sitting in meditation upon a flat rock.
Guishan pointed his staff at the Master’s back and said, "Has Jiji (the Silent Son) spoken yet? The Master replied, "Though I have not spoken, I certainly do not borrow [from another]."
Another person spoke. Guishan said, “Jizi understands.
Guishan said to the Master, “You must turn the light back upon yourself and reflect within. Others do not know the depth of your understanding;
try presenting your true realization to this old monk for him to see. The Master said, “If you command me to look at myself, when I reach this point, there is nothing [to be found].”

Regarding the stage of perfection (*yuanwei*), there is not a single thing nor a single interpretation that can be attained. When [the Master] offered this to his *upādhyāya*, Muzhou said, "The place where there is no stage of perfection is precisely the place where you yourself have formed interpretations;
you have not yet departed from mind and objects. The Master said, "Since there is no stage of perfection, where would there be any dharma?
What object could one grasp to constitute an 'object'? Muzhou said, "Was it just now that you formed such an interpretation? Is that so? The Master said, "It is. Muzhou—

[The Master] said: "If it is so, this is a state of mind and object fully present; you have not yet escaped the 'mine' (mama-kāra) mind. Originally there was the understanding to offer to me—how can you say there is none?
I grant that while your stage of faith (śraddhā-bhūmi) is manifest, your stage as a person (pudgala-bhūmi) remains hidden."

The Master asked Shishuang Qingzhu, "What is the dwelling place of the true Buddha? Shishuang replied, "By means of the wondrous state where thought is without thinking, one returns to the contemplation of the infinite brilliance of the spiritual flame.
When thought is exhausted, one returns to the source; nature and form are eternally present, and principle and phenomena are non-dual.
This is the suchness of the true Buddha. At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment.
While the Master was at Mount Gui, tending cattle, the Venerable Tiantai asked, "When a billion hairs appear, a billion lions manifest—what then?

The Master mounted his ox and returned home. The following day, while standing in attendance by Mount Gui’s side, he was just finishing recounting this previous conversation when he saw Venerable Tiantai approaching.
The Master said, "It is this very same venerable one. Mount Gui then asked, "A billion..."
"Upon a single hair-tip, ten billion lions appear. "Is this not what the Elder said? Tai replied, "It is.

The Master said, "At the very moment they appear, do they appear before the hair or after the hair? Tai replied, "At the moment of appearance, one does not speak of before or after. Miaoshan laughed heartily.
The Master said, "The lion’s waist has broken" (as recorded in the original text).
The Master was tending the oxen when Guishan asked him, "Is there any Bodhisattva here? The Master replied, "There is. Guishan said, "Which one do you see?
Point him out for me. The Master said, "If the Monk intends to point out which one is not [the Bodhisattva], then please point that one out yourself."
[The Master] looked. [Yunmen] said, "I will stop here.
Guishan asked the Master, "Suppose someone were to ask you, how would you respond?
The Master said, "If Master Dongsi were still here, Huiji would not have ended up in such desolation. Guishan said, "I grant you one offense for failing to respond. The Master said, "..."
"Life and death depend on a single word. Mian said, "I do not wrong you; there is another who does not agree. The Master asked, "Who?
Mian pointed to a pillar and said, "This one. The Master asked, "What does it say? Mian also said, "What does it say?
The Master said, "The white mouse moves on, yet the silver platform remains unchanged."
The Master asked Guishan, “When the Great Function manifests before you, I ask you to discern and clarify it. Guishan descended from his seat and returned to the abbot’s quarters.
The Master followed him inside. Guishan asked, “What was it you were just asking? The Master raised the question again. Guishan asked, “Do you remember my answer?
The Master said, “I remember. Guishan said, “Try reciting it for me. The Master then went out. Guishan said, “Wrong! The Master said, “Incense.”
Yan Shi-di arrived. "Do not say that I have nothing to say," [the Master said].
Yan was standing in attendance by Guishan when he suddenly heard a bird singing. Guishan said, "It speaks of matters quite directly.
Yan said, "One must not speak of this to others. Guishan asked, "Why? Yan said, "Because it speaks of matters too straightforwardly. Guishan asked, "By how much?"
The Dharma-gate. Once Jizizi pushed [the bowl] down. The Master asked, "What is the meaning of pushing it down? Guishan knocked on the meditation seat three times.
Guishan was feeding the crows with raw rice; turning his head, he saw the Master and said, "Today, for his sake, I have ascended the hall once more."
[The Master] ascended [the hall]. The Teacher said, "I have followed the custom and heard [the teaching].

Muzhou asked, "What is the matter that was heard? The Teacher said, "The crows cawed, and the magpies chirped. Muzhou said, "How can one escape from sound and form? The Teacher said, "What did you say just now, Preceptor?
Muzhou said, "I simply said that because you were the Great One, you had to ascend the hall once. The Teacher said, "Why is that?"
[The Master] called it "sound and form. Guishan said, "Even so, what harm is there in testing it? The Master asked, "Regarding this great matter of cause and condition, how would you test it?
Guishan raised his fist. The Master said, "In the end, that is merely pointing east and drawing west.
Guishan asked, "What were you just now asking about? The Master replied, "The great matter of cause and condition. Guishan said, "Why do you call it 'pointing east'?"
[The Master] drew a line to the west. The Teacher said, "It is because of attachment to sound and form that I asked this. Mian said, "You have not yet understood this matter.
The Teacher said, "How can one come to understand it? Mian said, "Ji-zi [the Silent Son] is sound and form; I, the old monk, am east and west."
The Master said, "In a thousand rivers, the substance of the single moon is not divided. Guishan said, "One must be like this before it can be attained. The Master said, "It is like gold and gold;
there is ultimately no difference in color, so how could there be different names? Guishan asked, "What is the principle of having no different names?
The Master said, "Vases, trays, hairpins, bracelets, seals, bowls, and basins. Guishan said, "Ji’s discourse on Chan is just like yours, Master."
The lion’s roar startles to death the foxes, wolves, jackals, and their ilk.

While the Master was sweeping the ground, Guishan said, “Dust is not something that can be swept away; emptiness does not arise of itself. “How is it that dust is not something that can be swept away?
the Master asked. He swept the ground once with his broom. Guishan asked, “How is it that emptiness does not arise of itself? The Master— [swept again].
He pointed at himself with his finger and then pointed at Guishan. Guishan said, "Dust cannot be swept away; emptiness does not arise of itself.
Apart from these two paths, what then? The Master swept the ground once more, pointed at himself, and again pointed at Guishan.
When the summer retreat ended, the Master went to pay his respects to Guishan. Guishan said, "I have not seen you for an entire summer.
While you were down there, what were you doing? The Master replied, "While I was down there, I cleared a patch of fallow land with my hoe and sowed a basketful of seed. Guishan said:
"Disciple, you have not spent this summer in vain. The Master then asked Muzhou, "What have you accomplished this summer, Reverend?
Muzhou replied, "One meal at midday; one sleep after nightfall. The Master said, "Reverend, you too have not spent this summer in vain.
Having said this, he involuntarily stuck out his tongue. Muzhou said, "Ji, why do you wound your own life?"

The Master was residing at Dongping when a mirror and a letter arrived from Guishan. Having ascended the hall and finished receiving the letter, he held up the mirror and addressed the assembly, saying:
"Tell me, everyone: is this the mirror of Guishan, or is it the mirror of Dongping?
If you say it is the mirror of Dongping, yet it was sent by Guishan; if you say it is the mirror of Guishan, yet it is here in Dongping."
"Inside my hand," he said. "If you can say something, I shall keep it; if you cannot say anything, I shall smash it.
He spoke thus three times, but the assembly remained silent. The Master then smashed it.
The *Jing Song* of Xichan says: "I recently took up this matter to pose a question: 'How is it that the entire assembly is left utterly bewildered?
If one does not strike it down until it shatters into a hundred fragments, one will surely become a bitter widower in the human world."

Guishan asked, "All sentient beings throughout the great earth are busily driven by their karmic consciousness, having no fundamental basis to rely upon. How do you know whether they exist or not? The Master said, "Huiji has a way of testing this. At that time, a monk passed by in front of him. The Master called out to the monk, who turned his head. The Master said, "Is this not existence? Guishan was silent. The Master then said, "I have already told you; there is no need for further words. Guishan then asked, "What about non-existence? The Master struck him once with his staff and said, "If you can understand this, you will know both existence and non-existence. Guishan remained silent. The Master said, "You are like a person who has lost their way and cannot find the path. Guishan then asked, "How does one find it? The Master called out, "Upādhyāya! The monk turned his head. The Master said, "Upādhyāya! This is precisely what is meant by 'the consciousness of karma busily rushing about, having no fundamental basis to rely upon.
Guishan said, "This is a single drop of a lion’s milk that scatters six bushels of donkey’s milk."
Guishan asked the Master, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "From the fields. Guishan asked, "How many people are there in the fields?
The Master drove his spade into the ground and stood with his hands folded. Guishan said, "Today on South Mountain there are many people mowing grass.
The Master pulled his spade and walked away.
Xuansha said, "If I had seen him, I would have kicked over the spade. Xuedou said, "The various quarters all claim that this 'spade-planted' story is extraordinary;

it is much like following the heterodox and pursuing evil. According to Xuedou’s own view, when Yangshan was questioned by Guishan, he was so thoroughly bound by his own straw ropes that he was ten parts away from death."
While Guishan and the Master were walking along, Guishan pointed to a field and said, "In this field, that end is high and this end is low.
The Master replied, "In fact, it is this end that is high and that end that is low. Guishan said, "If you do not believe me, stand in the center of the field."
"Look at both ends," the Master said. "There is no need to stand in the middle, nor should you dwell at either end.

Muzhou said, "If that is so, look at water. Water can level things. The Master said, "Water itself has no fixed nature; it simply levels what is high by being high and what is low by being low. Muzhou then desisted.

The Master asked Guishan, "After the Abbot has passed away, if someone asks how the Dharma and the Way are transmitted to his successors, what will you say to him? Guishan replied, "One bowl of congee, one bowl of rice.

The Master said, "If the former man does not accept that, what then? Guishan replied: "Even a single bowl of gruel or a single bowl of rice, Is not something that can be grasped by the mind. If you try to grasp it with the mind, It is like trying to catch the wind in a net."
The Master Zhaoshi bowed in reverence. Guishan said, "In the future, it would be improper to cite this as an error.
When the Master was herding oxen at Mount Gui, he saw a monk enter the monastery and leave shortly thereafter. The Master asked, "Why did you not stay?
The monk replied, "It was simply because our karmic conditions did not harmonize; that is why I left the mountain. The Master asked, "What were those karmic conditions? Please tell me."
"Look! [The Master] said. The monk said, "The Master asked me, 'What is your name? I replied, 'Returning to Truth.
The Master asked, 'Where does Truth return? I had no answer. The Master said, "Return to the Master and tell him, 'I was able to answer.
Wait for him to ask you, 'How would you say it? and simply reply, 'In the ears, in the eyes, in the nose.'"
The monk returned and acted exactly as instructed. Guishan said, "You empty-vowed liar! These are the words of a spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra) to five hundred people.
When the Master arrived at Yantou, Yantou raised his whisk; the Master spread out his sitting cloth. Yantou took the whisk and placed it behind him. The Master...
The Master placed his sitting mat over his shoulder and went out. Tou said, "I do not value your letting go; I only value your gathering it up.
The Master asked Dongsi, "May I borrow a path to go over there? Dongsi said, "Generally speaking, a śramaṇa cannot have only one path.
"Is there another? The Master remained silent for a long while. Dongsi then asked the Master, "May I borrow a path to go over here?"
[The monk] asked, "Is that all? The Master said, "Generally speaking, a śramaṇa cannot follow only a single path. [The monk] asked, "Is there nothing else? The Master said, "There is only this.
[The monk] asked, "Does the Son of Heaven of the Great Tang definitely have the surname Jin? The Master said, "Yes."
He addressed the assembly, saying: "All of you, each turn the light inward and reflect back upon yourselves; do not merely memorize my words.
Since beginningless kalpas, you have turned your backs on the light and cast yourselves into darkness; the roots of your deluded thoughts are so deep that they cannot be uprooted all at once.

Therefore, I provisionally employ skillful means to seize away your coarse consciousness, just as one uses yellow leaves to stop a small child's crying. What efficacy is there in this? It is also like..."
A person might take a hundred kinds of goods and precious jewels and set up a single shop to sell them, intending only to respond to the shifting demands of the market.
Therefore it is said: "Stonehead is a shop for pure gold; here, I am a general merchandise shop. If someone comes seeking mouse droppings, I will pick some up and give it to him;
if they come seeking pure gold, I will likewise pick it up and give it to them. At that time, there was a monk who asked:

"Mouse droppings are not wanted; I request the Venerable Master’s true gold. The Master said, "To bite the tip of the arrow and intend to open one's mouth—never in a donkey's year will you understand.
He addressed the assembly, saying, "If I call out for it, there is a transaction; if I do not call out for it, there is no transaction. I...
If one speaks of the Chan school, there is not even a single person to accompany one on the path, let alone a multitude of five hundred or seven hundred.
If I were to speak of this or that, you would all vie with one another to leap forward and snatch at it, like deceiving small children with an empty fist—there is no real meaning in it at all.
I shall now speak clearly to you regarding the matter of the Holy One; for now, do not employ your mind.
Settle yourself and simply direct [your practice] toward the ocean of your own nature, practicing according to reality. You need not seek the three clarities or six supernatural powers. Why?
Because these are matters pertaining to the peripheral branches of the sages. For now, you must simply recognize the mind and penetrate the root.

If you attain the root, you need not worry about the branches; they will naturally be present at a later time. If you have not attained the root, even if you apply your emotions and study with diligence, it will be of no avail.
He, too, does not attain it. Have you not seen what Master Guishan said: "When the sentiments of ordinary and sage are exhausted, the true permanence is revealed;
when phenomena and principle are non-dual, one is the Buddha of Suchness."
The Master pointed to a snow lion and said to the assembly, "Is there anyone who can pass through this form? The assembly remained silent.
Yunmen said, "In that case, you should have pushed it over."
Xuedou said: "Yunmen only knows how to push someone over; he does not know how to help them up.
A monk asked, "In the Chan school, there is sudden awakening; what is the essential meaning of entering the gate? The Master said, "Under the ancestral teachers' gate..."
Those of superior faculties and sharp wisdom attain awakening upon hearing it once and realize a thousand things; they obtain the Great Dharani.

But if one’s faculties are dull and their wisdom inferior, and if they do not practice dhyāna and samādhi, then upon reaching this point, they will all be utterly bewildered. [The student] asks: "Is there another expedient means? The Master says:
"Whether there is another or not, it only serves to unsettle your mind. For instance, where are you from? [The student] replies: "From Youzhou."

A man from the province came forward. The Master asked, "Do you still think of that place? He replied, "I constantly think of it. The Master said, "In that place there are towers and pavilions, groves and gardens, and crowds of people and horses.
When you reflect back on what you were thinking of, do you still have all those various things? He replied, "When I arrive here, I see nothing at all.
The Master said, "Your understanding is still within the realm of objects; this is merely the stage of faith (śraddhā-bhūmi), not yet the stage of a person (pudgala)."
"The Master is not so. According to what you understand, you have only attained one mystery. You may sit and don the robe, but look for yourself hereafter.
The monk made a gesture of realization and thanked him.
While the Master was at Mount Gui, he was conversing with the Senior Monk Tianxing. During their talk, Xing said, "What fine rain! The Master asked, "In what way is it fine?
Xing was speechless. The Master then said, "Fine rain. Xing asked, "In what way is it fine? The Master pointed to the rain to show him. Xing had no reply.
The Master said, "How can one of great wisdom remain silent?"

In the assembly at Yanguan, there were several monks who went to Mount Gui. Their minds were not inclined to submit. One day, during a communal work assignment, they were carrying grain to the western farmstead.
The Master joined them and they rested together at the top of a ridge. The Master took up the grain shoulder-pole, walked once around the group of monks, and said:
"Is there anyone? Is there anyone? No one from the assembly responded. The Master said, "You are all leading people astray," and he went off carrying his grain.

Later, two monks from Shishuang arrived at Mount Gui (Weishan) and said, "There is not a single person here who understands Chan. This was because the Master had been engaged in communal labor (pǔqǐng).
While carrying firewood, [Nanquan] picked up a piece of wood and asked, "Can you say anything about this? Both remained silent.
The Master said, "Do not say that not a single person understands Chan. Upon returning, the Master said to Guishan, "Today, those two Chan guests have been exposed by Huiji.
Guishan asked, "How did you expose them? The Master recounted the previous conversation. Guishan said, "As for you today, how..."
"I have thoroughly scrutinized him.
Yunju Xi asked, "Where was it that Moshan scrutinized Yangshan?
Layman Pang asked, "I have long heard of Yangshan; why did you reverse things upon his arrival? The Master held up his whisk.
The Layman said, "Exactly so. The Master said, "Is it upright or is it overturned? The Layman struck the pillar once and said, "Even though no one sees it, I require the pillar to bear witness.
The Master threw down his whisk and said, "If you go to other places, feel free to present this to them as you see fit."
The Master asked a monk, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From Youzhou. The Master said, "I happen to need news of Youzhou.
What is the price of rice there? He replied, "I happened to pass by the marketplace there and stepped on their bridges."
Baoning Yong, acting on behalf of Yangshan, said: "I grant you thirty blows.
The Master dreamed that he went to the abode of Maitreya and was seated as the second patriarch. A venerable one struck the gavel and announced:
"Today, the second patriarch shall preach the Dharma. The Master rose, struck the gavel, and declared: "The Mahāyāna Dharma transcends the four propositions and cuts off the hundred negations."
Listen attentively, listen attentively!
Daowei Xiu said: "Interpreting the meaning according to the text is not without merit;
however, suppose there were a true adept suddenly present in Maitreya’s assembly, who, upon hearing the words 'Mahāyāna Dharma,' would immediately say, 'Shut that pair of flaps of skin!'"
This not only puts an end to Yangshan’s drowsy prattle, but also spares later generations from dreaming about dreams.

The Master said, "Then you, Reverend, have never traveled the mountains."

"It is certainly not non-existent. Please try to explain it for me. Baizhang said, "I request the Attendant to provide an example. Wang lifted up a pair of chopsticks.
Baizhang said, "This wild fox spirit! Wang said, "This fellow has seen through it completely."
Daguang Zhe said: "Mihu only obtained a single peg. The Attendant looked at the tower and struck the tower.
If it were Daguang, he would have waited until the other had dropped his brush and simply said, 'I have always harbored doubts about you.'"
The Attendant went with Linji into the Sangha Hall and asked, "Do the monks in this hall study the sutras?
Linji said, "They do not study the sutras. The Attendant asked, "Do they practice Chan? Linji said, "They do not practice Chan.
The Attendant said, "If they neither study the sutras nor practice Chan, what are they doing here? Linji replied, "I am teaching them all to become Buddhas and Patriarchs."
[Zhaozhou] said, "Go. The King said, "Though gold dust is precious, when it falls into the eye, it becomes a cataract. Linji said, "I took you for a mere worldly man.
Jingqing said, "Recently, I have been throwing clods of earth to draw out jade. Dayang Zhe said, "Attendant Wang."

He may truly be called a gentleman of the Confucian school and a master craftsman of the Chan gate. Had his wisdom not been sharp and discerning, how could he have so clearly distinguished right from wrong?
When the Attendant asked a monk, "Do all sentient beings possess Buddha-nature or not? the monk replied, "They do. The Attendant then pointed to a painting on the wall.
The Dog-Painting Master said, "What about this? The monk had no reply. Wang said, "Look, it’s biting!

The Venerable Master Chen of Muzhou (24 in total), a native of his own prefecture, was a successor of Chan Master Huangbo Xiyun of Jingzhou who attained the essential meaning under him. Initially, he resided at Mishan in Jingzhou.

Later, he resided at Guanyin Temple in Muzhou, where his community usually numbered over a hundred. Realizing that his path did not harmonize with the world, he left the assembly to live in a room at Kaiyuan Temple.
There, he wove *púxié* (rush sandals) to support his mother. His conduct was lofty and transcendent, earning him the admiration of his contemporaries.

Whenever he received visitors, his quick-witted discernment was so sharp and decisive that there was no room for hesitation or reflection. He directed those who came to see him toward Linji’s study under Huangbo, and he received Yunmen as the successor to Xuefeng.
Feng. All of this was due to the Master’s power. He addressed the assembly, saying:
"I saw Master Baizhang not recognizing good from bad. When he ascended the hall and the great assembly had just gathered, he struck them all down at once with his staff.
He then called out to the assembly; when they turned their heads, Baizhang asked, 'What is it? The Master said: [This is it.]
There was no common ground for conversation; Huangbo was likewise so. He again called to the assembly, and as they turned their heads, Huangbo said, "The moon is like a drawn bow;
little rain, much wind. The Master said, "It is still a bit off."
Xuedou said, "What are you talking about? You are still somewhat off the mark; it is truly not yet there. When Xuedou’s assembly gathered, he struck them all down at once and left it at that.

If there were someone with an unperforated iron hammer who would exert their full strength for the sake of the assembly, being well able to shoulder the burden, they could encompass the past and present and hold fast the very heavens and earth. [He] suddenly picked up his staff and said:
He let it pass with one stroke.
Addressing the assembly, he said: "All of you, have you yet attained a point of entry?
If you have not yet attained a point of entry, you must attain a point of entry. If you do attain a point of entry, do not fail me."
At that time, a monk came forward, paid his respects, and said, "I shall never dare to辜负 (fail) the Master. The Master said, "You have already failed me.
Yunfeng Yue said, "When the ancients spoke thus, they had already cast down their entire bodies. You all—
People, do you understand this thoroughly? If you understand it thoroughly, you have betrayed Muzhou;
if you do not understand it thoroughly, Xuefeng will also be implicated.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "To tear it open is up to me; to close it up is also up to me. At that time, a monk asked, "What is this tearing it open?

The Master said, "Three times nine is twenty-seven. Bodhi and nirvāṇa, true thusness and liberation, 'this very mind is Buddha'—I speak thus for now; what about you? The monk said, "I do not think so. The Master said:
The cup fell to the ground; the plate broke into seven pieces.
Yunfeng Yue said, "In a quarrel, I spare you for your sharp-tongued retorts; in a spat, I spare you for your splashing of water."
The Master said, "I have told you clearly and plainly, yet you still do not understand; how much less could you grasp it if I were to conceal it from you?
At that time, a monk came forward, bowed, and said, "I, this humble one, shall never dare to let the Master down. The Master said, "You have already failed me."
Miaoxi said, "Have you yet grasped the entanglement?
The Master replied, "I have been the abbot here and have never seen a person who is truly 'without affairs' come before me.
Why do you not approach? At that time, a monk stepped forward. The Master said, "The Rector is not here; take him away by yourself outside the Main Gate. He then gave him [a blow].
"Thirty blows for you! [The monk] asked, "Where did my fault lie? The Master said, "Adding shackles upon a pillory.
When the Elder Xifeng arrived, and after tea and fruit had been served, the Master asked, "Where did you spend the summer retreat this year?
Xifeng said, "At Lanxi. The Master asked, "How many people were there? He replied, "More than seventy. The Master asked, "What do you use to instruct them during the course of the day?"
Tudu held up a tangerine. The Master said, "Why such a frantic rush?
The Master asked Elder Wuling, "When the hair swallows the vast ocean, one finally knows that the great earth is but a single mote of dust.
What about that? Wuling said, "Whom are you asking, Preceptor? The Master said, "I am asking you, Elder. Wuling said, "Why do you not acknowledge the meaning of my words?"
The Master said, "I do not understand your words; you do not understand my words.
Xuedou said, "Falling! Falling! He added, "This old fellow with his complications deserves to have them cut off once and for all."
Suddenly picking up his staff, he said, "Where have you gone?
He asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk gave a shout. The Master said, "I have been shouted at by you, old man. The monk shouted again.
The Master said, "After three or four shouts, what then? The monk was speechless. The Master struck him and said, "This swindler!"
The "Empty Han.
At times, the Master would call out to a monk, saying, "Virtuous One! When the monk turned his head, the Master would say, "A fellow carrying a single board.
Xuedou said, "Muzhou possessed only one eye. Since the monk turned his head upon being called, why did it instead result in [this reprimand]?"
The Carrying of a Board. Huanglong Xin said: "Xuedou also possesses only one eye. When this monk called out, he turned his head;
why then did he not become 'one who carries a board'?"

The Master asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? He replied, "Liu-yang. The Master said, "When the senior masters there respond to the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma, what do they say?
He replied, "Everywhere on the ground, there is no path to walk upon. The Master said, "Do those senior masters truly speak these words?"
[The monk] said, "It truly exists. The Master picked up his staff and struck him, saying, "You fellow who merely recites words!
The Master asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? [The monk] said, "From Yangshan. The Master said, "You do not even observe the five precepts.
[The monk] said, "In what way did I speak falsely? The Master said, "A śrāmaṇera has no place here."

The Master asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk said, "Right there, sir. The Master said, "I am being wronged by this old monk. The monk said, "If you, Reverend, know it, that is enough.
The Master said, "Carrying the shackles and passing on the indictment. He then struck him across the back with his staff.
Yunfeng Yue said, "What need is there for Muzhou’s prolixity? 'Over there!'—he would have struck him across the back with his staff immediately.
The Master asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk replied, "From Hebei. The Master said, "There is a Venerable Zhaozhou in Hebei."
"Have you ever been there? The monk replied, "I left that place not long ago.
The Master asked, "What words were spoken there? The monk recounted the story about the tea. The Master said, "How shameful! But tell me, what was Zhaozhou’s meaning?
The monk replied, "It was simply a provisional means for the occasion. The Master said, "Alas! You have splashed a bucket of filth over Zhaozhou," and he struck him.
The Master then asked the śrāmaṇera, "How do you understand this? The śrāmaṇera prostrated, and the Master struck him as well.
The monk went to ask the śrāmaṇera, "Why did the Master strike you just now? The śrāmaṇera said, "If it were not for my Master, he would never have struck me."
Xuedou said: "This monk is truly intolerable; he has taken a ladle of dung and splashed it over these two ancient Buddhas.

All you venerable seniors, if you can discern this, not only will you vindicate the two prefectures of Zhao and Muzhou, but Xuedou himself and all the old monks of the world will be cleared of fault. If you cannot discern it, you will be splashed everywhere."
People have never yet been able to resolve this.
When the Master saw a monk approach, he said, "This is a case already settled; I grant you thirty blows. The monk said, "I am like this."
The Master said, "The Vajra at the gate of the monastery—why does he raise his fist? The monk said, "If even the Vajra is like this...
The Master then struck him.
Yunmen said, "At such a time as this, everyone under heaven is wearing shackles and chains.
When the Master saw a monk walking with a steamed bun, he asked, "What are you carrying? The monk replied, "A steamed bun. The Master said, "This worldly fellow!"
Yunmen came and knocked on the door. The Master asked, "Who is it? Yunmen said, "Wenyan. The Master opened the door, grabbed him by the chest, and said, "Speak!
Speak! As Yunmen hesitated, the Master pushed him out, saying, "The carriage-rim drill of the Qin dynasty."
The Master asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Tiantai. The Master said, "I heard it was said that the Stone Bridge has broken into two sections—is this true?
The monk asked, "From where did you, Master, receive this news? The Master said, "I took you for a visitor from before the Huading Peak."
"Originally, you were just a man from the village of Heirata.
The Master asked the Monk-Administrator (Sōjō), "I have heard that you can lecture on the *Vijñaptimātratāsiddhi*; is this true? He replied, "In my youth, I once studied the texts.
The Master took a *kobiki* (a type of flat rice cake), split it in two, and said, "What do you make of this? The Administrator was speechless. The Master said, "You..."
"It is called a 'Hu-bing' (a sesame cake). Is it not called a 'Hu-bing'? He said, "One cannot but call it a 'Hu-bing. The Master asked the novice, "What do you call it?
The novice replied, "A Hu-bing. The Master said, "You too can lecture on the *Vijñaptimātratāsiddhi* (Treatise on Consciousness-Only)."
When Minister Wu arrived at the gate, he saw the Master and immediately asked, "The three gates are all open; by which gate shall the disciple enter?
The Master called out, "Minister! Wu responded, "Yes. The Master said, "Enter through the Gate of Faith."
There was a scholar who was proficient in the calligraphic styles of twenty-four masters. The Master pointed a dot in the air with his staff and asked, "Do you understand?
He replied, "I do not. The Master said, "Then how can you say you are proficient in the twenty-four styles? You do not even recognize the eight strokes of the character 'eternity' (永)."
Yellow Dragon Nan said: "Muzhou’s single point has been present since before King Wei-yin.
Yet when it came to the *Eightfold Dharma Treatise*, he was exposed by a layman. If it were Yellow Dragon, it would not be so:
'None of the disciples of Confucius recognize him; the blue-eyed barbarian monk smiles and nods his head.'"
A monk asked, "What is it like when one bows high to Śākyamuni and does not prostrate to Maitreya? The Master said, "Yesterday someone asked this;
I chased them out. The monk said, "I fear that I, your disciple, was not sincere. The Master said, "My staff is not here;
I shall give you thirty blows with the broom handle for now."
Xuedou said: "Muzhou only had the heart to accept the jade; he lacked the intent to divide the city. A monk asked: "Regarding the *vajra* at the gate:
if it supports [the world], then heaven and earth and the great land are contained within it; if it does not support it, then even a single hair's breadth is not encountered.
What is the case here? The Master said: "Hūṃ! Hūṃ! I have never seen such a question. First leap three thousand feet forward, then retreat eight hundred paces backward!"
"How will you manage it? The monk said, "Yes. The Master said, "First, I shall issue a written confession of your crimes," and then struck him.
As the monk prepared to leave, the Master called out, "Come here, come here! I am entangling with you. The entire universe and the great earth are supported [by this];
tell me, how deep is the water in Lake Dongting? The monk said, "I have never measured it. The Master said, "And what about Lake Dongting?"
"How is it? The monk said, "It is precisely because of the present age. The Master said, "You do not even understand this tangle," and struck him.
A monk asked, "That which is not formed by the character 'yi' (以) and is not the character 'ba' (八)—what chapter or verse is this? The Master snapped his fingers once and said:
"Do you understand? [The monk] said, "I do not. The Master said, "All the infinite roots of goodness from the praises and expositions above—frogs leap up into the sky;
earthworms pass straight across the Eastern Sea."
A monk asked, “What is the path that leads upward? The Master said, “What difficulty is there in speaking of it?
The monk said, “Please, Master, speak. The Master said, “The first and third days of the month; the ninth and seventh days of the middle and last phases.

The monk asked, “I do not ask about discarding one level by means of another level. But when it is neither discarding one level by means of another level, what then? The Master said, “Yesterday I planted eggplants; today...”
Rizhong planted a winter melon. He asked, "What are words of exposition? The Master said, "Appointing to office according to one's talent.
He asked, "What are words that are not of exposition? The Master said, "I humbly pray you may enjoy [the offering].
He asked, "Can a single breath turn over the entire Tripitaka? The Master said, "What hungry *jiluo* child is there? Quickly bring it down!"
Chan Master Lingguan of Wushi in Fuzhou (sixth in the series) usually kept his door closed, and few people saw him.
One day, Xuefeng came and knocked on the door; as soon as the Master opened it, Xuefeng grabbed him and asked, "Are you an ordinary person or a sage?
The Master spat at him and said, "You wild fox spirit! He pushed him away, shut the door again, and Xuefeng remarked, "Even so, one must still recognize my elder brother."
One day Xuefeng came again to knock on the door. The Master asked, "Who is it? Xuefeng said, "A phoenix chick. The Master asked, "What are you doing? He replied, "To devour Old Guan.
The Master opened the door, grabbed him, and said, "Speak! Speak! Xuefeng hesitated, and the Master immediately pushed him away and shut the door.
After Xuefeng established his own monastery, he addressed the assembly, saying, "If I had been able to enter Old Guan’s question at that time, you all—"
"This crew of wine-dregs eaters—where are they groping?
An old master said: 'Xuefeng had these words in vain; at that time he could not enter, and even now he cannot enter.
Mingzhao spoke on behalf of Xuefeng: as soon as he saw the door open, he said, 'To move is to perish.'"
Daiguang (Daoluan) said, "How magnificent! How magnificent! Xuedou said, "This man who betrays kindness and repays virtue—what connection has he to this?
He could not have entered at that time; was it ever intended for you to enter?
Now that you cannot find him by groping about, you bring shame upon Xuefeng. Both were under the guidance of Old Guanyin."
Caoshan asked, "What is the Vairocana Teacher, the Lord of the Dharma-body? The Master said, "I do not say. Caoshan reported this to Dongshan.
Dongshan said, "A fine point of inquiry; it simply lacks a follow-up question. Caoshan asked, "What kind of follow-up question?
Dongshan said, "Why not ask him, 'Why do you not say? Caoshan went back and posed that question. The Master said, "If he says, 'I do not say,' [then you have found it]."
"I would immediately gag my mouth. If I were to say 'my Way,' I would immediately shave my tongue. Caoshan related this to Dongshan, who deeply approved of it.
While the Master was rolling dough, a newly arrived monk came to pay his respects; the Master showed him the dough, and the monk then departed. Later that evening, the Master...
He asked the Head Seat, "Where is the newcomer today? The Head Seat replied, "He left right then and there.
The Master said, "It is so; he has indeed grasped one peg."
Xuedou said, "The Old Observer is much like one who loses his money and suffers for it.
Cuiyan Zhi said, "Both are sons of the Buddha who have left the household life.
The Master asked Lan’an, "What can be placed upon this patch of ground? An replied, "A 'formless' [image] would be well-placed."
"Buddha. The Master said, "What a fine piece of ground that was; you have defiled it with uncleanness, Monk. A monk asked, "What is the Buddha?
The Master extended his tongue to show him. The monk bowed. The Master said, "What did you see that you bow?
The monk replied, "I thank the Master for showing me the mark of the extended tongue. The Master said, "Lately, on my tongue..."
Shengchuang. Chan Master Chunan of Qianqing, Hangzhou (Case 1). A native of the Zhang family of Southern Min, he addressed the assembly, saying:

"Sons of the Buddha, even if you could explain the teachings of the Buddhas of the three periods as fluently as pouring water from one vessel into another, and even if you were to attain hundreds of thousands of samādhis, it would not be as good as..."

"In a single thought-moment, cultivate the untainted path (*anāsrava-mārga*) so as not to be bound by the causes and effects of the human and celestial realms. A monk asked, "How does one cultivate the untainted path?
The Master said, "Apprehend it when you have not yet become a *śrāmaṇera* [disciple]. The monk said, "If you have not yet become this person [the monk], who is taught to apprehend it?
The Master said, "The one who apprehends is also non-existent."
When Prime Minister Pei Xu (three instances) was serving as the Governor of Xuanzhou, he pointed to a mural of a high monk on the wall and asked a monk, "This figure’s appearance is impressive;
where is the high monk? The monk had no reply. The Prime Minister said, "Are there no Chan monks here?
At that time, Chan Master Huangbo Yun was staying as a guest in the monastery. A monk said, "There is a visiting monk who seems quite like a Chan practitioner."
The Master invited him to come and addressed his previous question. He summoned Pei Xiu, and the Master responded with "Yes. Yun said, "Where are you?
At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment.
One day, the Duke held up a statue of the Buddha before Huangbo and knelt down, saying, "I ask the Master to bestow a name upon it. Huangbo called out, "Pei Xiu!
The Duke responded, "Yes. Huangbo said, "I have finished bestowing the name upon you. The Duke prostrated himself in thanks.
The Master composed a verse on the Transmission of Mind, which says: "The mind cannot be transmitted; it is transmitted through accord. The mind cannot be seen;
it is seen through non-existence. Accord itself has no accord; non-existence itself has no non-existence. Do not dwell in the illusory city;

the jewel is upon the forehead of the deluded. The 'jewel' is but a forced name; how could the 'city' have any form? Mind is Buddha; Buddha is non-arising. This very moment is it—do not seek elsewhere."
Do not strive. Let the Buddha seek the Buddha; this would only double your labor. To give rise to understanding through the Dharma is to fall into the realm of Māra.

When ordinary and sage are not distinguished, one is truly free from seeing and hearing. With no-mind like a mirror, one does not compete with things; with no-thought like space, there is nothing that is not accommodated.
The external dharmas of the Three Vehicles are rarely encountered even throughout kalpas. If you can act thus, you are a hero who has transcended the world.
*The Essential Compendium of the Linked Lamp*, Scroll Eight and Scroll Nine.
Compiled by the monk Wuming, successor to the Patriarchs at Chongfu Chan Monastery in Quanzhou.
The Dharma Heir of Chan Master Xiyun of Huangbo in Junzhou, the Fifth Generation under the Southern Peak (Nanyue):
Chan Master Yixuan of Linji in Zhenzhou (total of forty-eight). A native of the Xing clan from Nanhua in Caoshou. Initially, he visited Huangbo...

Huangbo remained there for three years, his practice and conduct being pure and singular. At that time, Chen of Muzhou was the head seat (shouzuo) and sighed, saying, "Although this youth is of late birth, he differs from the rest.
One day he asked the Master, "How long have you been here, Senior Seat? The Master replied:
[Zhaozhou] was there for three years. [Yunmen] asked, "Have you ever asked him anything? The Master said, "I have not.
[Yunmen] said, "Why do you not ask the Abbot about the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "I do not know what to ask. [Yunmen] said, "You should simply go and ask."
"What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master followed the formal instruction and went up to the high seat to inquire.
Before the question had even ended, Baizhang raised his staff and struck him. The Master was at a loss. Coming down from the seat, he asked, "How did you answer my question? The Master said:
Before [the student] had finished speaking his question, the Head Monk struck him. "I do not understand," he said. The Head Monk replied, "Go ask again.

Thus he asked three times and was struck with painful blows each time. Weeping, he took his leave of the Head Monk and said, "I am fortunate to have received your compassion, which prompted me to go inquire after the Master's health.
Yet though I posed my question three times, I was struck with painful blows on all three occasions. I lament my own karmic obstacles for failing to grasp the profound meaning."
Now, the head seat was about to take his leave and descend the mountain. The seat said, "When you go, you must first take leave of the Abbot before departing.
The Master (Linji) bowed and withdrew. The head seat secretly informed Huangbo, saying, "That young man who asked the questions was truly in accordance with the Dharma.
When he takes leave of the Abbot, you should provide him with skillful instruction; in the future, he will become a great tree for the world."
[The Master] said, "It remains here to provide shade and coolness for people. The Master took his leave of Huangbo, who said, "Do not go elsewhere;
go to Dayu at the head of the Tan River in Gao'an. He will surely explain it for you. When the Master arrived at Dayu's place, Dayu asked, "Where have you come from?"
The Master said, "Huangbo came. Wuzu said, "What words did he speak? The Master said, "I asked him three times, 'What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?
Three times I was struck with a staff. I do not know whether I was at fault or not.
Wuzu said, "Huangbo’s heart was so compassionate that he exhausted himself for your sake; yet you come here to ask whether you were at fault or not."
Upon these words, the Master attained great enlightenment. Unconsciously, he let out a cry: "Aha!
So, it turns out Huangbo’s Buddha-dharma is not much at all! Daoyu grabbed him and said, "You bed-wetting little devil!
Just now you asked whether I had committed an offense or not, and now you say Huangbo’s Buddha-dharma is not much. What principle have you seen? Speak quickly! Speak quickly!"
The Master struck Daoyu three times under the ribs. Daoyu pushed him away and said, "Your teacher Huangbo has nothing to do with me.
The Master took his leave of Daoyu and returned to Huangbo. Huangbo asked, "This fellow comes and goes; when will he ever have enough?
The Master replied, "It was only because of your grandmotherly concern that I finished my business so quickly. He then stood in attendance by his side. Huangbo asked, "What..."
"Where have you come from? Mazu replied, "Yesterday, by your compassion, I was permitted to see Dayu. Huangbo asked, "What were the words and phrases [he spoke]?
Mazu recounted the previous conversation. Huangbo said, "This old fellow is too talkative! How could I let him come here? I would give him a severe beating!
Mazu said, "Why wait for him to come? He shall receive it right now. Having said this, he struck Huangbo.
Baizhang slapped him once and said with a laugh, "This madman has come here to pull at a tiger's whiskers.
The Master then shouted. Baizhang called to his attendant and said, "Escort this madman to the meditation hall."
Miaoshan asked Yangshan, "Did Linji receive the power of Dayu or the power of Huangbo? Yangshan replied, "No.
He simply rode the tiger's head and also knew how to grasp its tail."
Baizhang Yuan’s verse says: A single punch knocks down the Yellow Crane Tower; A single kick overturns the Parrot Isle.
When there is spirit, one adds even more spirit; Where there is no elegance, there is elegance nonetheless.
While the Master was planting pine trees, Huangbo said, "What is the use of planting so many in the deep mountains? The Master replied, "First, to provide a scenic setting for the mountain gate;
second, to serve as a landmark for future generations. Having spoken, he struck the ground once with his mattock.
Huangbo said, "Even so, you have already received twenty blows from me. The Master struck the ground once and said, "Heh heh.
Huangbo said, "When my lineage reaches you, it will flourish greatly in the world."
Guishan asked Yangshan, "At that time, Huangbo entrusted only Linji with his instructions; was there anyone else?
Yangshan replied, "There was, but because the years have been so many, I do not wish to mention it to you, Master. Guishan said:
"Even so, I still wish to know. Just raise it up and let us see. Yang said, "One man points south; the commands of Wu and Yue are put into effect.
When encountering a great wind, they immediately cease."

The Master was working together with the community in a general labor session. While they were hoeing the ground, Huangbo arrived late. After the Master had finished his formal greeting, he stood there pressing down on his hoe. Huangbo said, "Are you exhausted?
The Master replied, "I have only just begun hoeing the ground; why do you say I am exhausted? Huangbo took up his staff and struck him. The Master caught it.
He then pushed Huangbo down. Huangbo called out, "Venerable Karmadāna, pull me up!
The Karmadāna said, "How can you, Master, tolerate such a madman? Just as Huangbo rose, he struck the Karmadāna with his palm.
The Master then brandished his hoe and said, "In other places they perform cremation; here, we bury them alive."
Miaoshan asked Yangshan, "At that moment, what was the intention of Huangbo and Linji?
Yangshan said, "The real thief has fled; the one tracking his footsteps receives a beating. Dayue Zhe said, "Huangbo pushed him down."
The *vinaya* master helped him up. [The master] was to be cremated or buried alive, yet the pure wind had not yet ceased.

Because of this, the Master entered the kitchen with Huangbo and saw the head cook sorting rice. He asked, "What are you doing? The cook replied, "Sorting rice. Huangbo asked, "How much do you eat in one day?
The cook replied, "Two *shuo* and five *dou*. Huangbo said, "Is that not too much? The cook replied, "I am still afraid it might not be enough."
There was a little left. Huangbo struck him. The head cook reported this to the Master (Linji). The Master said, "Wait; let me examine this old fellow for you.
He immediately went to stand in attendance. Huangbo recounted the previous conversation. The Master said, "The head cook does not understand.
Please, Preceptor, provide a turning word on his behalf. The Master then asked, "Is it not too much? Huangbo replied, "Why not say, 'Come back for another meal tomorrow'?"
The Master said, "What do you mean by 'tomorrow'? Eat right now! Having said this, he struck Huaihai with his palm.
Huaihai said, "This madman comes here again to pull at the tiger's whiskers. The Master then gave a shout and went out.
Taisu said, "Only by raising a son does one come to know a father's compassion.
Yangshan said, "It is very much like inviting a thief to ruin the family.
During the summer retreat, the Master went to pay his respects to Huangbo. Seeing Huangbo reading a sutra, the Master said, "I took you for someone else."
"This person was originally just an old monk who soaks black beans. After staying for several days, the Master took his leave.

Baizhang said, "You arrived after the summer retreat has ended, yet you are departing without having completed it. The Master replied, "I came for a short time merely to pay my respects to the Master."
Huangbo struck him and drove him out. After traveling several li, the Master returned and stayed for the remainder of the summer.
When the Master took his leave of Huangbo, Huangbo asked, "Where will you go? The Master replied, "Neither south of the Yellow River nor north of it.
Huangbo then struck him. The Master seized the staff and gave Huangbo a slap across the face. Huangbo laughed heartily and called to his attendant, "Bring the former..."
The Master [Nanquan] held up his meditation board and whisk and called for an attendant. "Bring some fire," he said. Baizhang replied, "You may take it away;
later on, you shall sit upon the tongues of all people under heaven."
Guishan raised the question and asked Yangshan, "Does Linji not fail Huangbo? Yangshan said, "Not so.
Guishan asked, "How do you understand it? Yangshan said, "Only by knowing gratitude can one repay it. Guishan said, [I agree].
Yangshan said, "From the past down to the present, has there not been some matter of repaying one's debt of gratitude?
Yangshan replied, "There is, but because the times are so remote, I do not wish to bring it up to you, Master. Guishan said, "Even so, I still wish to know.
You simply bring it up and see. Yangshan said, "It is like when Ānanda praised the Buddha during the assembly at the Śūraṅgama Sūtra, saying: 'With this profound mind...'"
To serve as many lands as there are motes of dust—this is what is called repaying the Buddha’s kindness. Is this not an act of repaying kindness?

Guishan said, "So it is, so it is. When one's insight is equal to the teacher's, one has diminished the teacher's virtue by half; only when one's wisdom surpasses the teacher's is one fit to receive the transmission."
While the Master was attending Deshan, Deshan said, "I am tired today. The Master replied, "Old man, why do you talk in your sleep?
Deshan then struck him, and the Master overturned the rope seat.
Xuedou said: "These two practitioners possess the eye of simultaneous pecking and hatching; they have the function of simultaneous pecking and hatching.
Xuedou intends to snatch meat from the talons of a hungry hawk and scramble for food in the mouth of a starving tiger.
I dare say that both Deshan and Linji were blind men. If anyone can discern this, they may roam freely throughout the world."
Yunfeng Yue said: "How extraordinary, all you Chan practitioners! Watch these two masters at work;
one presses and the other nudges, briefly revealing their style. It is much like climbing a high mountain hand-in-hand.
Nevertheless, even so, they cannot avoid being laughed at by the bystanders. Now tell me, who is the bystander? He gave a shout.
The Master arrived at the place of Master Ping of Sanfeng. Ping asked, "Where did you set out from? He replied, "Huangbo.
Ping said, "What words or phrases were spoken there? The Master said, "Last night, the Golden Ox suffered in the mire; even until now, no trace remains.
Ping said, "The autumn wind blows through the jade flute; who is it that knows this? The Master said, "It penetrates ten thousand layers of barriers, yet does not dwell therein."
"Beyond the blue heavens. Pingyun said, "These words are too lofty, Master. The Master said, "A dragon gives birth to a golden phoenix chick, which pierces through the azure lapis lazuli.
Pingyun said, "Please sit and drink some tea."
When the Master arrived at Huayan in Xiangzhou, Huayan saw him coming and held his staff crosswise, feigning sleep. The Master said, "Do not sleep.
