However, as for the successive transmission from Buddha to Patriarch, there is no other meaning beyond this. Even if there are verbal teachings, they fall within the scope of transformative ritual.

As for the Three Vehicles and Five Natures, or the causes and effects of humans and devas—these do not apply to the Perfect and Sudden Teaching. Take the youth Sudhana, for instance; he never sought out faults. Great Virtue, do not err!
Apply your mind. It is like the great ocean, which does not harbor a corpse; it simply carries it away, intending to cast it out into the world.

Yet you yourself give rise to the obstacle of views, thereby obstructing the mind. When the sun rises without clouds, its beauty illuminates the heavens everywhere; when there is no film before the eyes, there are no flowers in the sky.
O practitioners of the Way, if you wish to accord with the Dharma, simply do not give rise to doubt. When extended, it pervades the entire dharma-realm; when withdrawn—

Then not even a single hair or thread remains; it is vividly and distinctly solitary luminosity, never lacking for a moment. The eyes do not see it, the ears do not hear it—what thing can you call it?
An ancient said: "To describe it as a single thing is to miss the mark. You need only look for yourself; what more is there?
Even if one were to speak of it, it would never be exhausted. Each of you must exert yourselves. Take care.

When Zhaozhou was traveling on pilgrimage, he encountered the Master while the Master was in the midst of washing his feet. Zhaozhou immediately asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "It happens to be the time when this old monk is washing his feet. Zhaozhou stepped forward and made a gesture as if listening.
The Master said, "I shall give you another ladleful of foul water to splash over you. Zhaozhou then went down.
When the Master heard Deshan address the assembly, saying, "Speak! Speak! If you can speak it, thirty blows;
if you cannot speak it, thirty blows," he sent Lopu as his attendant and instructed him, saying: "Go there, and when you see him speaking thus, ask him:
'Since you say one can speak it, why does he also receive thirty blows? If he strikes you—"
Nanquan took up the staff and gave it a shove; Deshan, as instructed, struck him with the staff and was himself pushed over by Nanquan.
Deshan rose and immediately returned to his quarters. When Nanquan came back and reported this to the Master, the Master said, "I have always suspected this fellow.
Even so, did you see Deshan? Nanquan hesitated, and the Master struck him.
Magu arrived; as soon as he had spread out his sitting mat, he asked, "As for the Twelve-Faced Avalokiteśvara, which one is the front face?
The Master descended from his rope bed, gathered up the sitting mat with one hand, and with the other hand seized Magu, saying, "Twelve-Faced Avalokiteśvara—where has he gone?
Magu turned his body as if to sit upon the rope bed; the Master raised his staff and struck him, and Magu caught it.
[The Master] struck back with his staff and grappled with the monk as they returned to the abbot’s quarters.
One day, while the Master was presiding over the assembly, the two head seats of the two halls looked at each other and each let out a shout.
A monk raised this matter and asked the Master, "Is there still a distinction between guest and host? The Master replied, "Guest and host are perfectly distinct."
The Master asked the head of the monastery, "Where have you come from? He replied, "I have come from the city to sell yellow rice.
The Master struck a line with his staff and said, "Can you sell this as well? The head gave a shout, and the Master struck him. Shortly thereafter, the head cook arrived.
The Master brought up the previous conversation. The Seat-holder said, "The Head of the Monastery did not understand the Master's meaning. The Master asked, "How do you understand it?
The Seat-holder bowed; the Master struck him as well.
Yellow Dragon Nan said: "When the head monk lets out a shout, one must not let him pass. When the kitchen steward prostrates, one must not let him pass.
Linji’s command was put into practice; Guizong let him pass. Thirty years later, someone will explain it through."

While the Master was among his assembly, two fellow students questioned one another. Setting aside the capacities of the middle and lower grades, they requested, "Brother, please offer a single phrase.
One said, "As soon as you intend to ask, you have already missed it. The other said, "If that is so, then I shall go and pay my respects to my elder brother.
The former replied, "Thief! The Master heard this and ascended the hall, saying: "If you wish to understand the Guest-Host phrases of Linji, go ask him."
Two practitioners of the second dhyāna in the hall immediately descended from their seats.
The Master frequently used the "shout" (he) in response to the occasion, and his disciples mostly learned it from him. One day, the Master asked a monk, "You all learn my shout;
let me ask you this: suppose one person comes out from the eastern corridor and another person comes out from the western corridor—what about these two?"
With a single shout, I distinguish guest and host here. How do you distinguish them? If you cannot distinguish them, you must not imitate this old monk’s shouting in the future.
After the Master ascended the seat, a monk stepped forward. The Master gave a shout; the monk also shouted. The Master then struck him.
Cuiyan Zhi said, "Linji was careless. It was fortunate that it was this monk;
otherwise, how could monks of the present day ever manage to get out?"
The Master asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk gave a shout. The Master gestured for him to sit; as the monk hesitated, the Master struck him.
When the Master saw another monk approaching, he held up his whisk; the monk bowed, and the Master struck him again.
Cuiyan Zhi said: "This monk has a grievance that cannot be redressed; he is dead and there is no one to mourn him.
But how will you understand this? Now, how will you provide this monk with vindication?"
When the Master saw the monk approach, he held up his whisk. The monk paid him no heed, so the Master struck him as well.
Yunmen, having finished recounting these three episodes, said, "It was only fitting for this old fellow."
The Master held up a sesame cake and showed it to Luopu, saying, "Myriad kinds and a thousand variations do not depart from this one;
their principle is non-dual. Luopu asked, "What is this principle of non-duality? The Master again held up the cake and showed it to him.

Luopu said, "If that is so, then there are myriad kinds and a thousand variations. The Master said, "That is the understanding of one who knows how to defecate. Luopu said, "It is like Old Luo looking into a mirror."
The Master asked a monk, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From Dingzhou. The Master raised his staff; the monk hesitated, and the Master struck him. The monk did not accept this.
The Master said, "In the future, you will surely meet someone with clear eyes. Later, the monk saw Sansheng and as soon as he brought up the previous conversation...
The Master raised his staff. A monk hesitated; the Master struck him immediately.
Another monk came forward and asked, "Is it right to prostrate, or is it right not to prostrate? The Master gave a shout. The monk prostrated; the Master said, "This thief!
The monk also said, "This thief! and then departed. The Master said, "Do not say that there is nothing to it. [To] the Head Seat.
The attendant stood by his side. The Master looked back and asked, "Is there still a transgression? Zuo replied, "There is.

The Master said, "Is it a transgression on the part of the guest, or a transgression on the part of the host? Zuo said, "Both are at fault. The Master asked, "Where does the fault lie? Zuo then went out.
The Master said, "Do not say that all is well."
A monk approached. The Master spread out both hands. The monk remained silent. The Master asked, "Do you understand? The monk said, "I do not.
The Master said, "It is whole and round, impossible to split apart; I give you two coins."
When the Master was about to pass away, he addressed the assembly, saying: "After I am gone, you all must not let my Treasury of the True Dharma Eye be extinguished.
Sansheng stepped forward and said: "Who would dare to extinguish the Master’s Treasury of the True Dharma Eye? The Master said:
Later, when someone asked [Nanquan], "What would you say to him? Nanquan gave a shout. The Master said, "Who knew that my Treasury of the True Dharma Eye would be extinguished by this blind donkey?
Nanquan bowed. The Master showed him with a verse: "Following the current without ceasing, one asks 'How?
True illumination is boundless; I shall explain it to you. Detached from form and detached from name, people do not understand; It is blown away..."
"Even when hair is used in haste, it must still be ground. Having spoken these words, he sat upright and passed away peacefully.

On the tenth day of the first month of the eighth year of the Xiantong era (the Dinghai year), his entire body was enshrined in a stupa at the northwest corner of Damingfu. By imperial decree, he was posthumously titled Chan Master Huizhao.

Miaoshan asked Yangshan, "Huangbo gave his instructions to Linji alone; are there others besides him?
Yangshan replied, "There are, but the time has been so long that I do not wish to mention them to you, Master. Miaoshan said:
"Just bring it up and see; I too wish to know. Yangshan said, "One person points the way south, and the command is carried out throughout Wu and Yue, but it stops upon encountering a great wind.
The monastic communities all take Chan Master Xueyan Zhao to be the one recorded by this prophecy.
Some, however, say that when examining the dates, Xueyan was at Huayan in Xiangzhou at night when he composed the *Weina* (Venerable Monk) liturgy. It arose [at that time].

Seeking the reality, do not deceive yourself. How can this be compared to a moth rushing into a flame, only to wound and destroy itself?
Others have attained clarity, yet they are obstructed by the cycle of birth and death and cannot break through it; thus, consciousness cannot perceive it, and wisdom cannot know it.
They have not heard the Way. Śākyamuni closed his room; Vimalakīrti remained silent; Subhūti spoke without speaking; and Śakra and Brahmā were left speechless.
To listen and yet listen—this matter is most difficult, most difficult.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "This nature is originally pure and replete with myriad virtues. However, due to the two conditions of defilement and purity, distinctions arise.
Therefore, the sages awaken to it and, by employing it exclusively for purification, achieve the path of enlightenment. Ordinary people, however, remain deluded regarding it."
It functions solely as defilement and thus sinks into saṃsāra; yet its essence is non-dual. Therefore, the Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra says: "There is no duality, nor is there a division;
there is no distinction and no discontinuity."

He addressed the assembly, saying: "As for the śramaṇas and sons of the Śākya, only when they regard what exists as non-existent can they, at all times, be equal to ordinary beings and equal to the sages;
only then do they possess even a slight portion of the life of one who has left the home. If it is not thus, it is a great difficulty, a great difficulty."
The Master asked a monk, "Where are you going? The monk replied, "I am going to live in a hermitage on West Mountain.

The Master said, "If I were to call for you from East Mountain, would you still be able to come back? The monk said, "No, I would not. The Master said, "Then you have not yet attained the ability to dwell in a hermitage."
The Master asked a monk, "Where are you going? The monk replied, "I am going to Mount Emei to pay homage to Samantabhadra.
The Master raised his whisk and said, "Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra are both right here. The monk drew a circle, threw it behind him, and then prostrated.
The Master summoned his attendant to bring some tea for this monk.

While the Master was burning a slash-and-burn field, he suddenly saw a snake. He prodded it with his staff toward the fire and said, "Ho!
This physical form still refuses to let go. If you die right here, it will be like finding a lamp in the darkness. At that time, a monk asked him:
"At such a time as this, is there still sin or not? The Master said: "When the stone tiger roars, the mountains and valleys echo;
when the wooden man bellows, the iron ox is startled."

There was an old woman who sent someone with money, requesting the Master to recite the Tripitaka. When the Master descended from his rope-seat and turned it once, he said, "Give this message to the old woman:

the recitation of the Tripitaka is complete. When the man returned and reported this to the old woman, she said, "I have been requesting the recitation of the entire Tripitaka; why have you only recited half?"

A monk asked, "When the kalpa-fire blazes forth and the great trichiliocosm is utterly destroyed, I wonder: will this [Dharma] be destroyed or not? The Master said, "It is destroyed."
The monk said, "If that is so, then he follows along with him. The Master said, "He follows along with him.
Xuedou’s verse says: "Standing amidst the conflagration at the end of an eon, The patch-robed monk still lingers between the two gates."
"Pitifully, one follows another's words; for ten thousand miles, one travels back and forth alone.
The monk pointed at a tortoise and asked, "All sentient beings have skin wrapping their bones; why is it that this one has bones wrapping its skin?"
The Master took up his straw sandals and placed them upon the back of a tortoise.
The monk was speechless. A monk asked, "What is the mark of a great man? The Master said, "There is no label on his belly. The monk asked, "What is the house style of the Master?
The Master said, "Drawing a winnowing basket with red earth. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "A winnowing basket has..."
Lips. Grain cannot leap out.
A monk asked, "What is the matter of one side of the Great Sui? The Master said, "East, west, south, north.
Miaoxi said, "Tell me, was this an answer to the monk's question, or was it not an answer to the monk's question?"

As the Master was about to pass away, he ascended the hall. When the assembly had gathered, the Master made a gesture with his mouth as if suffering from a wind ailment and addressed the crowd, saying, "Is there anyone here who can cure this old monk's mouth?
The monks and assembly brought medicinal herbs, and when the laypeople heard of it, they also sent medicine.

The Master accepted neither. Seven days later, the Master himself pinched his own mouth to correct its alignment and said, "For so long a time, I have beaten these two pieces of skin, yet to this day no one has been able to cure them. He then sat upright and passed away.
Chan Master Lingshu Rumın of Shaoyang (in two parts). He was a native of Min. A monk asked, "What is the patriarchal style of the Master?
The Master said, "A thousand-year-old field has eight hundred owners. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of this?
The Master said, "A dilapidated house with few people to repair it. The monk asked, "Why is it so difficult to understand? The Master said, "The wind atop the Fire God’s head."
At a carriage station, there was a nun who presented a ceramic bowl to the Master. The Master took it up and asked, "Where did this come from?
The nun replied, "Dingzhou. The Master then smashed it to pieces, leaving the nun speechless.
Baofu Zhan spoke on his behalf, saying: "He who deceives his enemy perishes.
Fuzhou Shoushan Shijie Chan Master (three instances): When the Master arrived at Dongshan, Dongshan asked, "Where is your place of origin?"

The Master said, "In Min. Shanshan asked, "What are your parents' names? The Master said, "Having been questioned by you, Venerable Sir, I have completely lost track of what came before and what followed. Shanshan then desisted.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "Venerable seniors, fortunately there are these words of truth to exhort you; each of you should take this to heart.

When all sentiments of ordinary and holy alike are exhausted, the true and eternal is revealed. You need only, at once, cast off all former delusions and the defilements of clinging to sensory objects."
"The mind is like empty space. At some future time, you will come to recognize a little of what is good and what is bad.
The Military Governor of Min asked the Master, "How old are you? The Master replied, "I am the same age as empty space. The Governor asked, "How old is empty space?
The Master replied, "It is the same age as Mount Shou."
Chan Master Lingyun Zhiqin of Fuzhou (11th case): He was a native of Changxi in his home prefecture.

He studied under Chan Master Changqing Da'an and subsequently traveled to the gates of Xuefeng and Xuansha. One day, upon seeing peach blossoms, he attained sudden enlightenment and composed a verse, saying:
"For thirty years I have sought a swordsman; Several times the leaves have fallen and branches have sprouted again. Since then..."
"Once I saw the peach blossoms, from then until now I have had no further doubts. He presented this to Da'an.
Da'an said, "One who enters through conditions will never again fall back or lose [the realization]. You must maintain it well."
A verse by Miaoxi says: "It is all said that one awakens to the Way upon seeing peach blossoms; yet whether this principle exists or not remains unknown.
Vast and boundless is the universe with its countless people—how many among them are true men?"
Later, he brought this up for Xuansha to consider. Xuansha said, "It is accurate, most accurate; yet I dare say you, elder brother, have not yet reached the ultimate.
Later, a monk asked Changqing, "What was Xuansha’s meaning? Changqing said, "I thought the barbarian had red whiskers, but here is another red-bearded barbarian!"
Wuzu Yan said, "What do you mean by 'correct'? Go and study for another thirty years.
Xuefeng asked, "An ancient said, 'Three before, three after. What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "Fish in the water, birds on the mountain.
Xuefeng asked, "Ultimately, how is it so? The Master said, "High enough to shoot at, deep enough to fish in."
The Master asked a monk, "Where are you going? He replied, "To Xuefeng. The Master said, "I have a letter to send to Xuefeng; would you take it? He replied, "Please give it to me.
The Master took off one of his sandals, tossed it before him, and the monk departed. Upon arriving at Xuefeng, the Master asked, "Where have you come from?
He replied, "From Lingyun. Xuefeng asked, "How is the Master doing? He replied, "He has sent a letter for the Master."
Having finished speaking, he took off his sandals and threw them before Xuefeng. Xuefeng stopped there.

Daopei Xi said, "Since Xuefeng could not discern the essential point of this monk’s message, the monk merely followed the mold and pattern, leaving him at a loss. Lingyun suddenly said at that time, "I have a letter."
He sent [the monk] to Xuefeng. Xuefeng said, "Please come forward. Lingyun simply remained seated. How could this monk have failed to express himself?
A man of great capacity who seeks to benefit others would not fail to utter a single word.
Changsheng asked, "What was it like before the primordial chaos had divided? The Master said, "The pillar reveals its pregnancy. He asked, "What is it like after it has divided?
The Master said, "Like a fragment of cloud touching the vast clarity. He asked, "I do not know for certain—does that vast clarity still receive being touched?
The Master did not answer. He said, "If that is so, then sentient beings have not yet come forth. The Master again did not answer. He said, "It must be that one reaches a state of pure clarity."
"How is it when the point is severed? The Master said, "It is still the flow of true permanence. He asked, "What is the flow of true permanence?
The Master said, "It is like a mirror that is always bright. He asked, "I wonder, is there anything further beyond this? The Master said, "There is."
A monk asked, "What is the matter that transcends [the ordinary]? The Master said, "Bring me a broken mirror, and I will see you.

Another monk asked, "How was it before the Buddha appeared in the world? The Master held up his whisk. The monk asked, "And how was it after he appeared in the world? The Master again held up his whisk.
The Master also held up his whisk. The monk did not accept this. Later, the monk went to Xuefeng and brought up the previous conversation.
Xuefeng asked, "How do you understand it? The monk said, "I do not accept it. Xuefeng said, "Ask me; I will speak for you. The monk posed the same question as before.
Xuefeng held up his whisk. The monk offered the subsequent remark. Xuefeng lowered his whisk. The monk bowed. Xuefeng—
He struck him. The monk went to Xuansha and brought up the previous conversation. Xuansha asked, "What do you say to this? The monk said, "I do not understand.
Xuansha said, "Let me explain it to you. It is like a person selling a piece of land; the boundaries on all four sides have already been demarcated and the contract finalized."
"In the center there is a tree; it still belongs to this old monk.
Daopei Zhe said: "This monk has drawn his bow and set his two arrows, intending to bring order to a chaotic world.
Yet, before Xuansha, he cannot deploy even a single skillful means. Why? A crane has nine [feathers]."
The wild geese find it difficult to spread their wings; the horse lacks the thousand-li stride to chase the wind.
A monk asked, "What is it like when the sovereign goes forth into battle? The Master said, "Outside the Chongming Gate; one does not ask about Chang'an.
The monk asked, "How can one have an audience with the Son of Heaven? The Master said, "A blind crane descends into the clear pond; a fish passes beneath its feet."
A monk asked, "The mani jewel does not conform to various colors; I wonder, what color is it? The Master said, "White.
The monk said, "If that is so, then it conforms to various colors. The Master said, "The Zhao jade was originally without flaw; Zhong Hui deceived the Lord of Qin."
A monk asked, "What is it like when the sovereign goes forth into battle? The Master said, "Guo Pu buries [his father] at Xiong'er Mountain. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of this?
The Master said, "Sitting and watching the white-robed heavens. The monk asked, "Where is he now? The Master said, "Do not offend the Dragon’s countenance."
A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "Planting a *lingqin* tree at the bottom of a well. The monk said, "I do not understand.
The Master said, "This year the peaches and plums are precious; each single fruit is worth a thousand pieces of gold."
When Master Xuefeng arrived with his assembly, he asked the Master, "There are now two hundred people in the assembly who wish to spend the summer retreat here;
may they do so? The Master took up his staff, drew a line across it, and said, "It will not do. He then spoke further.
Feng said, "Cease.
Zheng Shisan Niangzi of Nantai in Fuzhou (two instances), aged twelve, followed her nun-sister-in-law to visit Lan’an.
As soon as she had prostrated herself, An asked, "Where does your sister-in-law live? She replied, "I live by the banks of the Jiang River at Nantai. An—
He shouted at her to leave. He asked again, "Where does that old woman behind you live? Thirteen Niang drew back her hands, stepped forward, and stood there.
Anquan asked once more. Thirteen Niang said, "I have already presented myself to the Master. Anquan said, "Go."
Thirteen-niang descended to the Dharma Hall. The nun asked Thirteen-niang, "You usually say, 'I understand Zen;
my mouth is like a sword. Yet today, when questioned by the Great Master, you have no words with which to respond. Thirteen-niang said, "Alas, alas!
To have such a vision as this, yet still dare to say, 'I am traveling on pilgrimage'—take off your patched robe!"

"Come here; let me put this on you, Thirteen. Later, having arrived at Luoshan, he recounted the previous conversation and asked, "As for Thirteen’s response just now, was it truly steady and secure? Luoshan said, "It was not without fault.
Thirteen asked, "Where does the fault lie? Luoshan rebuked her. Thirteen said, "To add flowers upon brocade."
Baofu went to visit Elder Gan. He then asked, "I have heard that Thirteen Niang visited Dayue; is this true? Thirteen Niang replied, "It is.
Baofu asked, "Now that Dayue has passed away, where has he gone? Thirteen Niang stepped down from her meditation seat and stood there.
Elder Gan said, "When you speak of Chan in your leisure time, your eloquence is like a cascading river; why did you not say [something]?"
[Zhaozhou] took [the bowl]. Shisan Niang said, "What can be done with these two pieces of hide? Ganyu asked, "How else would you do it?
Shisan Niang said, "Shut that dog's mouth!"
Nun Liao Ran of Mount Moshan, in Junzhou, a Dharma heir of Chan Master Dayu of Gaogan.
(Three cases total. When Guankui was traveling about, he arrived at the mountain and said:
If they were equals, [the Master] would simply remain standing; otherwise, he would push over the rope bed. The Master then ordered an attendant to ask:

"Elder, have you come to tour the mountains, or have you come for the sake of the Buddha-dharma? He replied, "I have come for the sake of the Buddha-dharma. Thereupon, the Master struck the drum and ascended the hall. Xian entered for an audience.
The Master asked, "Where did you come from today? He replied, "From the crossroads. The Master said, "Why didn't you cover it over?
He was at a loss for an answer and, after bowing, asked, "What is Mount Moshan? The Master said, "Its peak is not revealed. He asked, "Who is the master of Mount Moshan?"
The Master said, "It is not the marks of male or female. Xian shouted, "Why do you not transform away? The Master said, "I am neither a spirit nor a ghost;
what is there to transform? He then struck him. Thereupon, Xian submitted to his teachings and attended upon him for three years.
The Master asked a monk, "You are truly quite wretched. The monk said, "Even so, I am still a lion cub.
The Master said, "If you are a lion cub, why are you being ridden by Mañjuśrī? The monk was speechless.
A monk asked, "What is the mind of the ancient Buddha? The Master said, "The world collapses and perishes. The monk asked, "Why does the world collapse and perish?
The Master said, "It would rather not have my own body."
Chan Master Daowu of Guannan in Xiangzhou, a successor of Chan Master Chang (Case 1).
Once, while passing through a rural village, he heard a shaman entertaining a deity, who said, "The conscious spirit does not exist.
The Master suddenly attained realization. Later, he visited Chan Master Chang to have his understanding confirmed, and subsequently traveled to Deshan.
This is the gateway. Whenever he ascends the hall, he wears a lotus-patterned hat, dons a cassock, and holds a ritual tablet.
He beats the drum and blows the flute, vocally addressing himself as "Master Sanlang of Lu. At times he says: "The drum of Guannan is struck; the song of Deshan is sung.
A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master gestured with his tablet and said, "Yes."
The Monk Lohan of Zhangzhou (Case 1): Master [Lohan] asked Chan Master Chang, "What is the source of the Great Way?
Chang gave him a punch, whereupon he attained realization. He then composed a song, saying: "In the seventh year of the Xiantong era, I first entered the Way.

Wherever I went, I encountered words that I could not understand. A mass of doubt swirled within my mind like a spinning basket; For three springs I found no joy, dwelling only among the forests and springs. Suddenly..."

Encountering the Dharma King seated upon his mat, he immediately laid bare his doubts before the Master. The Master rose from the mat like a *nāga*, bared his shoulder, and struck him once with his fist.
The mass of doubt was shattered and fell away like a startled monkey; looking up, he saw the sun newly risen in its full orb.
From that moment on, he has been steady and firm, remaining constantly joyful until this very day, hearing only the sound of his own belly being full.
He puffed out his chest and no longer went east or west to carry his bowl.
Miaoxi said, "What a pity—this fine punch has no one to whom it can be entrusted.
This is the record of Fubie, a successor of Chan Master Xianshuangfeng.
Master Shuangfeng Gu Chan of Fuzhou (Case 1). When the Master arrived at Shishuang, he merely joined the assembly and did not seek formal instruction.

Thereupon, Shishuang said, "Attendant Gu, upon seeing Shuangfeng, you have attained a point of entry. Later, when the Master took his leave of Shishuang, Shishuang held up a whisk and accompanied him to the door.
Shishuang called out to the Master; the Master turned his head back. Shishuang said, "If you try to grasp it..."
"It is right here that it is wrong; it is not that it is not intended, yet do not try to form a conceptual understanding of it.
Unless one knows 'there is,' no one else can know. How so? The Master responded, "Yes, yes. Later, while the Master was residing there, a monk asked:
"At that time, Shishuang spoke thus; I wonder what his intention was? The Master said: "He was simply telling me not to be attached to 'is' or 'is not.'"
Chan Master Daoyan (II), Dharma heir of Chan Master Huijue of Guangxiao Temple in Yangzhou, the sixth generation under Nanyue.
A native of the Liu family in Luzhou. He addressed the assembly, saying: "Maitreya enters the monastery in the morning."
At dusk he attained perfect enlightenment and spoke this verse: "The phenomena of the three realms, whether high or low, I say are all mind.
Apart from these mental phenomena, nothing else exists that can be apprehended. Observe how he speaks; he is truly most alert. Compared to us, he would still be considered a dullard.
Thus, in a single thought one perceives the Way, and the afflictions of the three periods of time are exhausted, like a seal impressing its mark upon clay.
There is no before or after. My children, the matter of birth and death is great; you must quickly realize it. Do not treat it with indifference.

The frantic bustle of karmic consciousness arises because one is deluded about oneself and pursues external objects. When the World-Honored One was about to enter nirvana, Mañjuśrī requested that he turn the wheel of the Dharma.
The World-Honored One exclaimed, "Alas! During my forty-nine years in this world, I have never uttered a single word. You ask me to turn the Wheel of Dharma once more;

was there ever a time when I turned the Wheel of Dharma? Yet nowadays, in the monastic communities, they establish a system of host and guest, question and answer, out of necessity—merely for the sake of beginners.
A monk asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "Today is the third day of the third month. The monk said, "I do not understand.
The Master said, "Cease, cease! There is no need to speak. My Dharma is subtle and difficult to conceive."
Chan Master Nanta Guangyong of Yangshan in Yuanzhou, Dharma heir of Chan Master Huiji of Yangshan in Yuanzhou (Part Two). Addressing the assembly, he said:
"All you people here—if you were a true man, you would let out a lion’s roar the very moment you emerged from your mother’s womb. Do you understand?"
A monk asked, "Mañjuśrī is the teacher of the seven Buddhas; does Mañjuśrī have a teacher? The Master said, "He has one whenever he encounters conditions.
The monk asked, "What is Mañjuśrī's teacher? The Master held up his whisk. The monk said, "Is it not just this?
The Master lowered the whisk.
Chan Master Jingtong of Mount Huo in Jinzhou (sixth in the lineage) called himself the "Great Chan Buddha.
When he first met Yangshan, he stood on one foot and said, "The twenty-eight patriarchs of the Western Heaven were like this; the six patriarchs of the Tang land were like this;
the Master was like this; and Jingtong is also like this. Yangshan descended from his meditation seat and struck him with four blows of his rattan staff.
Xuedou said: "The willow switch has not yet reached the point of breaking; for what reason did he strike only four times?
One must be a man who cuts through nails and severs iron before this can be achieved."
When the Master arrived at Huoshan, he said of himself: "Four willow branches beneath Jiyun Peak; the great Buddha of the world. He went to pay his respects.
Huoshan called for the *vinaya-dhara* to strike the bell, whereupon the Master immediately ran away.
The Master heard that whenever National Teacher Bimoksha (Bimiō) saw a monk approach, he would immediately brandish his wooden pitchfork and say:
"What kind of demon or bewitchment has led you to leave home? What kind of demon or bewitchment has taught you to travel as a pilgrim? If you can speak, you die under this pitchfork;
if you cannot speak, you also die under this pitchfork. The Master went to visit him; as soon as he saw him, he did not prostrate, but instead leaped straight into [the pitchfork].
As [the Master] held it in his arms, Bimiō patted him on the back three times. The Master clapped his hands and said, "Brother, you have deceived me by coming from three thousand li!
Brother, you have deceived me by coming from three thousand li!"
A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master struck him. The monk also struck him. The Master said, "It is reasonable that you strike me;
it is unreasonable that I strike you. The monk was speechless. The Master drove him out with a continuous succession of blows.
A lay practitioner asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master then performed a prostration.
The man said, "How can you, Reverend, bow to a layperson? The Master replied, "Have you not heard it said: 'One must honor one's disciples'?"

As the Master’s period of transforming through his conditions was nearing its end, he first prepared firewood in the wilds beyond the city and took leave of all his patrons. At midday, he held a candle and ascended onto the woodpile;

placing his alms-bowl hat upon the crown of his head, he manifested the appearance of a halo. Holding his staff in his hand, he assumed the posture of the *vajra* (magic mace) used to subdue demons, standing until his life ended amidst crimson flames.
Master Dongta of Yangshan in Yuanzhou (Part Two). A monk asked, "What is the King’s Sword? The Master said, "The sail is lowered, yet no credit is claimed.
The monk asked, "How about one who uses it? The Master said, "It does not fall into the hands of ordinary people."
A monk asked, "When the Dharma King and the secular ruler meet, what is it like? The Master said, "Both palms are without partiality.
The monk asked, "What is it like after they have met? The Master said, "In between, all images are severed."
Chan Master Foyan Hui of Dengzhou (Part II). A monk asked, "In years past you had an illness; now again you have been poisoned.
I beg the Master for medical treatment. The Master said, "Both cases require hot water."
A monk asked, "What is the matter that lies beyond the Buddha? The Master said, "The conch-shell topknot.
The Venerable Elder Chen of Muzhou was a dharma successor of Muzhou.
(Five cases total. When he was a Minister of State, Chen Cao, together with various officials, ascended a tower. Seeing several monks walking toward them, the officials...
The official said, "Those who come here are all traveling monks. The Master said, "They are not. The official asked, "How do you know they are not?
The Master replied, "Wait until I have examined them. When the monks reached the front of the pavilion, the Master called out, "Venerable Ones! and they all raised their heads.
The Duke said, "I do not believe in the Way.
Daopei Zhe said, "Minister Chen, you may truly be said to hold the sun and moon of Confucius in your hands and carry the golden seal of Vairocana upon your back.
Not only are Confucian scholars struck with awe, but even monastics are at a loss. Have you not heard it said?"
The opportune moment was like a flash of lightning; only then could he avoid dwelling in sickness among the reeds.
Gushan Yong said: "This monk’s reason is difficult to vindicate; he dies without a funeral.
The Minister presses his sword against the gate—who would dare look upon him with a direct eye?"
The Duke asked a monk, "I have a matter I wish to consult you on; may I do so? The monk replied, "Shut your dog's mouth. The Duke slapped his own mouth and said, "I, this man, am at fault.
The monk said, "One who recognizes their error must surely reform it. The Duke said, "Go to the Senior Monk and ask him if he can find a mouth for you to eat rice from. The monk was speechless.
While the Duke was having a vegetarian meal with the monks, he picked up a hūbǐng (sesame cake) and asked a monk, "Is there such a thing as this in Jiangxi and Hunan?
The monk replied, "What did the Minister eat just now? The Duke said, "I struck the bell to thank its resonance."
One day, the Duke was providing a vegetarian feast for the monks. He personally served the fried cakes (*hubing*), but when a monk reached out his hand to receive one, the Duke withdrew his hand.
The monk remained speechless. The Duke said, "As expected, as expected."

One day, while a Duke was serving food to the monks during a vegetarian feast, he personally went through the distribution and said, "I request the Venerable Elder to accept this offering of food. The monk replied, "The three virtues and six flavors.
The Duke said, "Wrong. The monk was at a loss for a reply.
Chan Master Baoshou Zhao of Zhenzhou, Dharma heir of Chan Master Linji Yixuan of Zhenzhou (sixth in the lineage). Hu Dingjiao came to visit him. The Master asked, "Are you not Hu Dingjiao?
Hu replied, "I dare not [claim to be]. The Master said, "Can you nail the void? Hu replied, "Please let the Master nail it."
The Master broke it and threw it away. The Hu man refused to accept this, so the Master said, "In the future, there will be many talkative masters who will point out the flaws for you.
Later, the Hu man met Zhaozhou. Zhaozhou asked, "Are you not the Hu nail-and-tongue man? The Hu man replied, "I dare not say so."
Zhaozhou said, "Can you still nail the void? Huo said, "I ask the Master to break it open and bring it here. Zhaozhou said, "For now, let us nail this single seam.
At these words, Huo attained realization. He then cited the kōan concerning Baoshou striking a monk and asked Zhaozhou about it.
"I do not yet understand, Master Zhaozhou: where does the fault lie? Zhaozhou said, "I am just like this; I have been a guarantor for Baoshou for thousands of miles.
Xuedou said, "I would like to strike these three fellows. First, I strike Zhaozhou for failing to blind [himself]."
First, he struck Hu Dingjiao on the eye. Second, he struck Baoshou; he could not shut Zhaozhou’s mouth.
Third, he struck Hu Dingjiao; it was not right to let Baoshou off. Suddenly, picking up his staff, he said, “There is yet one more!
The assembly all scattered at once. The Master struck the meditation seat once. Daguang Zhe said, “What a pity.”
Zhaozhou let him off. Had he waited for [the monk] to say, "Where does my fault lie?
and then struck him across the back with his staff, he would not only have inherited Baoshou’s majestic brilliance, but would also have served as a model for the monastic community.
Gushan Yong said: "Although Baoshou possessed the tongs and hammer for shattering empty space, he could not avoid cutting his hand on the blade.
That Hu Gong finally attained awakening at the end—whom would have known that his eyes were still clouded with rheum?"
The Master asked a monk, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From the Western Mountain. The Master said, "Did you see the monkeys there? He replied, "I saw them.
The Master said, "What kind of antics were they performing? He replied, "I saw that not even one of them could perform any antics.
The Master then struck him.
The Master asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk replied, "From Cui Chan. The Master said, "Have you brought back Cui Chan’s shout with you?
The monk said, "I have not brought it back. The Master said, "If that is so, then it did not come from Cui Chan.
The monk then shouted. The Master raised his staff; as the monk hesitated, the Master struck him.
A monk came to inquire after him. The Master said, "The hundreds of thousands of Buddhas do not go beyond this abbot’s quarters.
The monk asked, "As for what the ancients said—that the great trichiliocosm is but a bubble on the ocean—where, then, would you place these abbot’s quarters?
The Master said, "The thousand sages are present right now. The monk asked, "Who can testify to this? The Master threw down his whisk, and the monk moved from west to east.

The monk stood up. The Master struck him. The monk said, "If one had not studied for a long time, how could one know the ultimate point? The Master said, "Thirty years from now, these words will be widely circulated."
A monk asked, "What is it like when the myriad objects of perception come to invade? The Master said, "Do not concern yourself with them. The monk bowed.
The Master said, "You must not touch them. If you touch them, I will break your donkey's back in two."
A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "The face is black, but the eyes are white.
The monk asked, "How is it when there is not a single cloud for ten thousand miles? The Master said, "Even the blue sky must receive a blow of the staff. The monk asked, "I do not understand;
where does the fault lie? The Master then struck him.
Chan Master Huìràn of Sāngshèng in Zhènzhōu (11th case). He went to visit Dēngshān. As soon as he spread out his sitting cloth, Dēngshān said, "There is no need to spread out your napkin;
there is no leftover gruel or stale rice here. The Master said, "Fortunately, I encountered this lack of it.
But even if there were, where would you put it? Dēngshān struck him. The Master caught the staff and pushed Dēngshān onto the rope bed. Dēngshān laughed loudly, "Ha! Ha!"
[The monk] laughed. The Master wept, saying, "Heaven! Heaven! and then departed.
When the Master arrived at Deshan, Tietiantai was serving as the Head Seat (Śrāmaṇera). He questioned the Master, saying, "A traveling monk must possess the credentials of his own school.
What are your credentials, Upādhyāya? The Master said, "Ha! The Head Seat asked again, and the Master struck him.
One sitting mat says: "This bucket of lacquer has offended how many worthy and virtuous men before and after!

Regarding the matter of formal greetings at the seat, the Master asked Xuefeng, "The golden fish that has passed through the net—what do you take as food? Xuefeng said, "Wait until you have managed to get out of the net, and then I will tell you.
The Master said, "Even for a spiritual teacher of fifteen hundred people, this is still just a head-word (a conceptual prompt)."
"Consciousness. Feng said, "The old monk’s administrative duties are too many.
Xuedou said, "What a pity he let him go; he should have been given thirty blows. Not even a single blow would have been excessive;
truly, such a master is rarely encountered. Chengtian Zong said, "To spread a net across the heavens, one must indeed..."
Xuefeng entered the tiger’s den; this must be credited to Sansheng. Among the assembly, there are some who, upon deliberation, say:
"Xuefeng was inside the net, while Sansheng was outside the net. How tragic, how tragic! This is a profound injustice to the ancients.
Were it not for these two masters, they could not have roamed freely throughout the world."
Daguang Zhe said: "The Three Sages may be called the ten-thousand-fathom Dragon Gate; they are seasoned travelers.
Xuefeng is much like the gate of Mengchang opening wide; how could he fear such illustrious guests?"
The Master, while at Xuefeng, saw two monkeys and said, "These monkeys each carry a mirror on their backs.
The Master asked, "They have been without name for kalpas; why do you designate them as 'ancient mirrors'? Xuefeng replied, "A flaw has arisen.
The Master said, "As a teacher of fifteen hundred people, you do not even recognize the core of the teaching. Xuefeng said, "I am the abbot; my responsibilities are many."
Xuedou said, "He deserves thirty blows. It would have been better to let this blow pass, so as to avoid following an error with another.
Yangshan asked the Master, "What is your name? The Master replied, "Huiji. Yangshan said, "Huiji is my name. The Master said, [I am Huiji].
"I am named Huìrán. Shānhé laughed loudly.
Miàoxǐ said, "These two fellows hide their bodies but expose their shadows; they pay no heed at all to those watching from the sidelines."
Xuedou’s verse says: "Simultaneously gathering and simultaneously releasing—what is the principle? To ride a tiger has always required the cessation of all effort.
Having laughed, one knows not where he has gone; Only the mournful wind shall stir for a thousand ages."
The Master was unwell while at Yangshan and went down to the Nirvana Hall to rest. An official came to visit Yangshan, who asked, "What office do you hold?
The official replied, "I am a *tui-guan* (Assistant Official). Yangshan held up his whisk and said, "Can you adjudicate this? The official was speechless.
Yangshan then ordered the assembly to offer their responses, but none were in accord with the truth. Yangshan then instructed his attendant to invite [the official back].
The Master gave a descending word, saying: "Just say it. The Master has business today. Shanshan then ordered him to ask:
"What business? The Master said: "A second offense will not be tolerated."
The Master took his leave of Yangshan. As Yangshan was about to escort him with his whisk, the Master said, "I already have a teacher of my own. Yangshan asked, "Who?
The Master replied, "Master Linji. Yangshan said, "Huiji has committed an offense. He then detained the Master for two days and prepared a tea ceremony to see him off.
The Master arrived at Xiangyan. Xiangyan asked, "Where have you come from? The Master said, "From Linji. Xiangyan said, "Have you brought Linji’s sword with you?
The Master took his sitting cloth and struck him right across the mouth. Xiangyan then desisted.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "When I meet people, I come forth; when I come forth, I do not act for the sake of others. Xinghua said: "When I meet people, I do not come forth;
when I come forth, I immediately act for the sake of others."

The *Zhenjing wen* says: "These two old masters stole a mere fraction of Linji’s livelihood and each established their own boundaries and domains, their vital energy piercing the universe, causing even the clear-eyed monk to do nothing but laugh.
Zen adepts, tell me: what is there to laugh at? Do you know where it lands? If you know—"
"Let them be as they will—upside down and topsy-turvy. If you do not understand, for now, chew upon the tangled vines of the Three Sages and Xinghua.
The Master asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk gave a shout. The Master also shouted. The monk shouted again. The Master also shouted. The monk...
[The Master] said, "If you strike with the staff, you will go blind. He followed this by shouting. The Master raised his staff; the monk turned his body and made a gesture of receiving it.
The Master said, "One who does not run when going downhill finds such a swift opportunity but rarely. He struck him. The monk said, "This thief! and went out. The Master threw down his staff.
Later, another monk asked, "Just now, why did you allow that monk [to leave]? The Master said, "It was because he had seen the former Master."
A monk came forward and asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "Stinking meat attracts flies.
Xinghua Jiang said, "I, this mountain monk, am not like that; it is a swarm of flies on the back of a broken donkey."
Dajue Chan Master of Weifeng (Part Two). When the Master met Linji, Linji held up his whisk. The Master then spread out his sitting cloth. Linji threw down the whisk.

The Master then gathered up his sitting cloth and said, "I am going to attend the hall. At that time, the assembly discussed it, saying, "Could this be because the Master is a personal acquaintance of the Abbot?
He neither prostrates nor receives a blow. When Linji heard of this, he ordered an attendant to summon the Master.
The Master arrived. Linji said, "The teacher says: 'You have come, yet you neither prostrate nor accept a blow;
are you perhaps an acquaintance of the Elder? " The Master then said, "Goodbye," and went down.
As the Master was approaching the time of his passing, he said to the assembly, "I have an arrow that I wish to hand over to someone.
At that moment, a monk came forward and said, "I request the Master’s arrow. The Master asked, "What do you call an arrow? The monk then gave a shout, and the Master struck him.
He then returned to the abbot’s quarters, summoned the monk, and asked him, "Did you understand what just happened? The monk replied, "I do not understand.
The Master struck him several more times, threw down his staff, and said, "In the future, when you meet someone with clear eyes, explain this to them clearly. He then passed away.
Chan Master Xinghua Cunjian of Weifeng (11th case). Initially, he went to visit Linji. Linji appointed him as attendant.
Linji asked a newly arrived monk, "Where have you come from? He replied, "Luancheng. Linji said, "May I ask you a question? He replied, "A novice does not understand.
Linji said, "Even if one were to raze the Great Tang Empire, it would be difficult to find a single person who does not understand. [He was told to] enter the hall for study.
He departed. The Master asked, "Just now, when that newcomer arrived, were you stripping him down or clothing him?
Jie said, "Who am I to concern myself with whether he is stripped or clothed? The Master said, "You only know how to pelt a dead sparrow on the ground;
you do not know how to cover it over with a turning word. Jie said, "And what about you, Master? The Master said, "Please, Master, act as the newcomer. Jie—
He then said, "I, a novice, do not understand. The Master said, "In that case, the fault lies with this old monk. Linji said, "Your words conceal the point.

As the Master hesitated, Linji struck him. That evening, Linji said to the Master, "Today when I questioned the newcomer, it was like picking up a dying sparrow on the ground and flicking it there, or striking it right in its nest.
Yet as soon as you produced a word, I shouted at you and sent you off toward the blue clouds."
[He] struck him from behind. The Master said, "The grass-thief is utterly defeated. Ji struck him again.
Later, the Master went to Sansheng, who invited him to serve as the First Seat. He often said to people, "I have traveled on pilgrimage throughout the South;
I have never once struck against a single person who understands the Buddha-dharma with the tip of my staff. You are here [now]."
"What are you doing? When San-sheng heard this, he asked the Master, "What kind of eye do you possess? The Master then gave a shout.
San-sheng said, "It must be you who can achieve it. The Master then desisted. Da-jue heard of this and said, "How could the wind have blown its way into Da-jue’s gate?
Later, when the Master arrived at Da-jue's place, Da-jue invited him to serve as the head of the monastery (yuan-zhu). One day, he called out to him: "Head of the Monastery..."
The Master said, "I have heard you say that during your travels in the south, you never once struck anyone with the tip of your staff who understood the Buddha-dharma.
What kind of eye do you possess? Jue gave a shout. The Master picked up his staff. Jue struck him. The Master hesitated;
Jue struck him again. The Master shouted once more; Jue struck him yet again. The next day, as the Master was passing below the Dharma Hall, Jue called out, "Director!"
The Master said, "I have no doubt at all about your two shouts yesterday. Try to explain them to me.
The Teacher said, "Since I was with San-sheng, everything I learned there has been completely shattered by my elder brother.
Please grant me a teaching of peace and ease. Jue said, "You blind fellow! You come here to admit defeat. Take off your patched robe; I shall give you a severe beating!"
[He] struck him once. Under that blow, the Master realized the principle by which his late teacher Linji had received blows from Huangbo.
On the day the Master opened the hall, he addressed the assembly, saying: "This one incense offering is primarily for my elder brother Sansheng. Sansheng..."
I was so lonely that I ought to have succeeded to Dajue. Dajue was too distant for me;
however, at the place of Sansheng, I realized the phrase of "host and guest. Had I not met my elder brother Dajue, I would have surely wasted my entire life.
When I received the staff-blow from Dajue, I saw the way our late master Linji had received the staff-blow under Huangbo.
[The Master] said: "This single stick of incense is an offering to my late teacher, Linji.
He addressed the assembly, saying: 'Today, I ask nothing of how or what; I simply request that you enter directly with a single blade, and Xinghua shall provide testimony for you.
At that time, the Elder Minde came forward, prostrated, and as he rose, he let out a shout. The Master also shouted. Minde shouted again."

"Ho! The Master shouted again. Dede bowed and returned to the assembly. The Master said, "If it had been anyone else just now, thirty blows of the staff would not have been withheld even by a single stroke.
Why? Because Elder Minde understands how to employ a shout as something other than a mere shout."
Langya Jue said: "Tell me, which of those two shouts does not function as a shout?
If Xinghua had not had the subsequent words, he would have left the whole world in doubt. Even so, those who understand are few."
Jiaochongguang said: "Xinghua and Minde each put forth one hand, intending to illuminate the treasury of the true Dharma-eye of Linji.
Little did they know that the entire school of Linji would be swept away like dust. Now tell me: [what is this?]"
Wherein lies the point of benefit and harm? Let those with the eye of discernment distinguish it.
The Master said to the assembly: "I have heard that one shouts at the long corridor, and one shouts at the rear quarters. My sons, do not shout blindly or shout recklessly.
Even if you were to shout yourself up to the thirty-third heaven and then crash back down, it would still be but a single drop."
There is no such thing as "qi" (vital energy). Wait until Xinghua rises from the province of Su; then he will speak to you slowly and say, "Not yet.
Why? Because I have never scattered genuine pearls within a purple silk curtain for you all.
What is the point of shouting and bellowing recklessly in empty space?
The Master entered the hall. Seeing the Head Seat, he said, "I have seen you through. The Head Seat gave a shout. The Master struck the pillar once and then went out.
The Head Seat followed him to the Abbot’s quarters and said, "Just now I offended you, Master," and prostrated himself.
The Master struck him with his staff on the ground; the Head Seat was speechless.

When the Master saw a fellow practitioner approaching, as soon as the monk stepped onto the Dharma Hall, the Master gave a shout. The monk also shouted. After walking two or three steps, the Master shouted again;
the monk also shouted. After a moment, the monk drew near, and the Master raised his staff. The monk shouted once more. The Master said, "Look! This blind fellow still dares to act as the host.
As the monk hesitated, the Master struck him and drove him straight out of the Dharma Hall. At that time, there was another monk present.
Question: "In what way did this monk offend you, Master? The Master said: "It was because he just now possessed both the provisional and the real, both illumination and function.
Yet when I extended my hand before him and crossed it twice across his face, [he failed to respond]."
He could not leave. To one such as this blind fellow, if I do not strike him, when shall I ever do so?
Emperor Tongguang asked the Master, "When I reclaimed the Central Plains, I obtained a treasure for which no one has yet offered a price.

The Master said, "May I borrow Your Majesty’s treasure for a moment? The Emperor drew back the hem of his *fodou* (head-wrap) with his hand and showed it to him. The Master said, "This is the treasure of a sovereign."
"Who would dare offer a price? The Emperor was greatly pleased.
Xuedou said, "What the Sovereign has obtained can only be viewed from the sidelines;
had it not been for Xinghua’s mastery as a master of the Way, he would likely have paid a high price. Huanglong Xin said, "In one instance, Xinghua acted upon seeing the opportunity."
Alas, how can one avoid burying this "Son of Heaven" for a single day? At that time, you should have simply said to him:
"The pearl of a clam or oyster—once obtained, it has no further use. This would have allowed him to find another livelihood later on, sparing us from this mutual failure.
Now, if someone were to ask, how would you appraise its value?
The Master called to a monk. The monk responded, "Yes. The Master said, "To point at it is to miss it. He then called to another monk. The monk responded, "Yes.
The Master said, "To arrive at it is not to point at it."
A monk asked, "What is it like when [the wind] comes from the four quarters and eight directions? The Master said, "Strike the one in the center. The monk bowed;
the Master said, "Today Xinghua went to a village feast. On the way, he encountered a sudden storm of wind and rain, so he took shelter inside an old temple and managed to get through."
Kaishan Xian said: "Xinghua carries seven implements with him and faces the enemy from all eight directions;
he is indeed a veteran master. Yet, when the two armies clash, he retreats into a ghost cave.
If someone were to ask Kaishan about this, he would simply say to them: "When they come from the four directions and the eight points, strike them all at once. Wait for him...
As they prostrated, he struck them on the spine with his staff, saying, "There is no place for you to evade.
Once, because the Master had injured his foot while riding a horse, he walked around the monastery leaning on a wooden crutch. He asked the monks, "Do you recognize this old monk?
The monks replied, "How could we not recognize the Master? The Master said, "A cripple-dharma teacher; one who can speak but cannot walk."

He then proceeded to the Dharma Hall and instructed the *vinaya-dhara* to strike the bell for the ascent to the hall. When the assembly had gathered, the Master asked, "Do you recognize this old monk?
The assembly remained silent. The Master cast down his staff and passed away with a composed countenance.
Chan Master Zhixian of Guankxi in Ezhou (Five Cases). The Master visited Linji. One day, Linji suddenly seized him by the chest.

The Master immediately said, “I understand, I understand. Linji pushed him away and said, “For now, I let you off with one blow. After the Master established his own monastery, he addressed the assembly, saying:
“When I saw Linji, there was nothing he could say; even until now, I am full and have no desire to rest.”
Gushan Yong said, "A beggar sees only small profit.
Addressing the assembly, he said, "The ten directions have no walls; the four sides have no gates. It is bare and naked, stark and clear—there is nothing to grasp.
He then descended from his seat.
A monk asked, "I have long heard of Guankui; having arrived, I see only the hemp-soaking pond.
The Master said, "You see only the hemp-soaking pond, but you do not yet see Guankui. The monk asked, "What is Guankui? The Master said, "As swift as a split arrow."
Xuansha said, "Even after studying for another thirty years, you still would not have understood Zen.
A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "Rice in the bowl; soup in the bucket."
The student said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "When hungry, eat; when weary, rest.
When the Master was about to pass away, he asked his attendant, "Who is it that transforms while seated? The attendant replied, "Sengqie. The Master said, "Who is it that transforms while standing?
The attendant replied, "Senghui. The Master then took seven steps, extended his hands, and passed away.
Master Tánkōng of Youzhou (in two parts). Bǎoshòu asked the Master, "If someone comes who has neither the middle nor the lower capacity, what will you do, Elder Brother?
The Master said, "The moment you raised that question just now, you were already mistaken. Bǎoshòu said, "Elder Brother, you cannot escape blame either.
The Master said, "Then you shall be my elder brother. Bǎoshòu tilted his palm and said, "This old thief!"
There was a nun who wished to open the hall for teaching. The Master said, "You have five obstacles; you may not open the hall.
The nun asked, "When the Dragon Girl attained Buddhahood, how many obstacles did she have? The Master said, "The Dragon Girl manifested eighteen transformations;
try to manifest some yourself. The nun said, "I am no wild fox spirit; what would I have to transform? The Master then struck her.
When the Abbot of Zhenzhou heard this, he said, "The Master has broken his staff; with such a view, you intend to teach others?
Cuiyan Zhi said, "Tell me, what kind of eyes does the nun possess? She can only carry a single length of rope for hanging the dead. How do you understand this?"
Chan Master Cui Chan of Dingzhou (Case 1): Holding up his staff, he addressed the assembly, saying, "Come forth! I’ll hit you! Come forth! I’ll hit you!
At that moment, a monk stepped forward and said, "Cui Chan, you’re a dead man! The Master threw down the staff and immediately returned to his quarters.
Guizong said, "How can you utter a single turning word to save Cui Chan? Faldeng replied, "Venerable Sir, first save yourself.
Does this mean he approves of him, or does it mean he does not approve of him?
The Fifth Patriarch Jie said: "He immediately pushed over the rope-bench.
Regarding the Venerable Wansui of Zhenzhou (Case 1): When the Master visited Baoshou, Baoshou did not rise; the Master then unfolded his sitting cloth.
When Shou descended from his rope bed, the Master sat down and pushed back his own rope bed. Shou then returned to the abbot’s quarters and closed the door.
The Master remained seated and did not rise. The administrator said, "The Abbot has closed the door; please go to the storehouse for tea. The Master then returned.
The next day, Shou went again to pay his respects. The Master still sat without rising. Shou unfolded his sitting mat (*zuoju*), and the Master also descended from his rope bed.
Zhushou immediately sat back upon his rope bed. The Master also returned to his quarters and closed the door.

Zhushou went to the attendant’s quarters, took some ash, and drew three lines of ash around the Master’s door. He then departed. When the Master opened the door and saw this, he said, "I am not like that."
Yet he was just like this.
Regarding the monk from Lichun in Xiangzhou (two cases): while the Master was brewing tea, a monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master picked up the tea bowl, showed it to him, and said, "Is it not simply this? The Master then threw the bowl down and turned toward [the monk].
[The Master] was amidst a fire. The monks remained silent.
A monk asked, "What is it like to attain liberation by observing sounds? The Master struck a piece of wood with a fire-tongs and said, "Do you hear this?
The monk replied, "I hear it. The Master said, "Who, then, is not liberated?"
When the Prefect of Cangzhou invited Master Micang (Fanyi) and Baoshou to enter the hall for offerings, he sent someone to deliver a message, saying:
"I request that the two elders engage in a discussion on the Buddha-dharma. Baoshou replied: "I request that the elder brother provide the answer."
The Master then gave a shout. Shou said, "I have not yet even asked a question; how can you give a shout so abruptly? The Master said, "You still consider it too little.
Shou then gave him a shout in return.
The Daoist Ke Fu of Zhuozhou (Five Episodes). A monk asked Linji, "What is 'taking away the person but not taking away the environment'?
Linji said: "The warm sun brings forth life, spreading a carpet of brocade; the infant’s hair hangs down, white as silk."
The Master’s verse says: To take away the person but not the environment—this very condition carries its own confusion.

If you intend to seek the profound principle, your deliberation will only lead to self-reproach. The pearl of the black dragon shines with brilliant luster; the shadow of the moon on the cassia tree sways gently.
To encounter this directly is without error or divergence, yet one would still remain entangled in the net.
A monk asked, "What is 'seizing the environment but not seizing the person'? Linji said, "The Imperial Edict has already been issued; it pervades the world.
The General is beyond the frontier, where smoke and dust have ceased."
The Master’s verse says: "The境 (object) is taken away, but not the person; where is the truth in seeking words? To inquire about Chan is for Chan to be a delusion;
to investigate principle is for principle to be unapproachable. The sun shines upon the pale light of frost; the mountains sway with fresh verdant hues.
Even if you were to attain a profound realization, it would still be but dust in the eye."

A monk asked, "What is 'both person and environment being simultaneously stripped away'? Jie said, "In Bing and Fen, correspondence is cut off; one dwells alone in a single region. The Master composed a verse:
"When both person and environment are simultaneously stripped away, The authentic command has been exercised from the start. It makes no distinction between Buddhas and patriarchs."
To speak of the sentiments of the holy and the profane is like meeting a blind man with a hair-cutting sword;
yet they press forward seeking a subtle understanding, only to needlessly sever their own vital spirit.
A monk asked, "What is it like when both person and environment are not wrested away? Linji said, "The King ascends the jeweled throne;
the village elder sings his song. The Master’s verse says: "Person and environment both unwrested, The intent of reflection is not biased. Host and guest, their words do not differ."
Question and answer, principle and phenomenon, all complete: treading through the moon in the clear pool, piercing open the sky in the azure void.
Failing to clarify this wondrous function, one sinks and perishes within the absence of conditions.
A monk asked, "What is the guest within the guest? The Master said, "Leaning on the gate and hanging by the door, as if drunk;
speaking and breathing without shame. The monk asked, "What is the host within the guest? The Master said, "Murmuring the name of Amitābha with both staffs leaning against him."

The eyes are blind and the pupils do not protrude from their sockets. [A monk] asked, "What is the guest within the host? The Master said, "Holding high the ancestral seal, it is used for the immediate occasion; to benefit beings, one’s words must carry compassion. [The monk] asked, "What is the host within the host? The Master said, "Transversely grasping the Mohe sword, the correct command is fully exercised; throughout the peaceful realm, the deluded and stubborn are executed. [The monk] asked, "Since it is a peaceful realm, why is there execution? The Master said, "If the world were truly at peace, there would be no need for the sword; because there are still those who are not yet at peace, the sword is drawn. The monk said, "I have understood. The Master said, "If you have understood, then you should understand that the sword is not merely for execution; it is also for bestowing life. If you can see this, then you will know that the host within the host is not separate from the guest within the host. The monk said, "I am at a loss. The Master said, "If you are at a loss, then you should look back at your own face before birth. If you can see it, then you will see that the host within the host is originally not two. "Why did you instead execute that dull-witted fellow? The Master said, "He was not permitted to travel at night, yet he stubbornly carried a torch;

When the Master saw a monk, he suddenly seized him and shouted, "Kill! Kill! The monk pushed him away and said, "Why are you shouting?"
The Master asked, "Who is there? The monk gave a shout. The Master struck him. The monk went outside and said, "Wait, wait! The Master laughed heartily.
The Master then asked, "An old man once said, 'Where do you dwell? The old man did not speak. The Master remarked, "He was well able to respond to the occasion."
The old man held up a blade of grass and showed it to the Master. The Master then gave a shout. The old man bowed; the Master then returned to his hermitage.
The old man said, "In this way, you leave the whole world in a state of doubt."
The Hermit of Huxi (in two parts): A monk came to visit him. The Master did not look at him. The monk said, "I know the Hermit possesses this one pivot.
The Master snapped his fingers once. The monk asked, "What is the essential principle? The Master struck him.
The monk said, "I knew today I would fall into the other's trap. The Master said, "You still want to eat another blow of the staff."
When the master saw the monk enter the gate, he gave a shout. The monk remained silent. The master struck him. The monk then shouted back.
The master said, "What a fine petty thief!"
A monk asked, "How many years has the Master lived in this hermitage? The Master said, "I have only seen spring come and summer grow;
I do not remember it all. The monk said, "Excellent, not remembering! The Master said, "Tell me, how many years? The monk said, "Spring comes and summer grows, you say?

The Master of Fupo Hermitage (Case 1): A monk was weeping as he ascended from the foot of the mountain. The Master closed the door;
the monk drew a circle on the gate and stood outside. The Master emerged from behind the hermitage and likewise ascended from the foot of the mountain while weeping.
The monk then shouted, "You still think you can get away with this! The Master beat his breast and said, "What a pity!
My late teacher has been utterly buried by you. The monk said, "Alas! Alas! The Master said, "The Abbot has been deceived by you today."
Master Sōzan Yōan (Case 3) asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Jiangxi. The Master held up his itch-comb and said, "Is there such a thing as this in Jiangxi?
The monk rested his chin on his knees and closed his eyes. The Master said, "That boy from the eastern neighbor's house!"

[The monk] went instead to the house on the west side to work for them, saying, "Having a mouth, I do not trouble the host and guests to speak. The Master said, "Just now you were afflicted with deafness;
now you are afflicted with dumbness. The monk said, "Buying iron and obtaining gold—what a great fortune! The Master said, "Working as a hired laborer without merit."
The monk could not help but try to evade him. The Master struck him. The Master said, "It is still forgivable that you have brought trouble upon yourself, but do not bring trouble upon me, old monk.
The monk returned and prostrated himself. The Master said, "Had it not been so, you would have lost your descendants in the future."
A monk asked, "Master, what have you attained that you dwell on this mountain? The Master said, "I also wish to explain my origins, yet I fear being scrutinized by others.
The monk said, "How can you avoid it? The Master then gave a shout and said, "Exactly! He then struck him. The monk said, "Precisely so! The Master then struck him again.
The monk laughed loudly and departed. The Master said, "Today I am utterly defeated! Today I am utterly defeated!
A monk asked, "Master, if you suddenly encounter a karmic realm appearing before you, how would you deal with it? The Master shouted, "You demon!"
[The monk] said, "Today I have been deluded once; it is no small matter. The Master said, "Fortunately, this is a deep mountain where no one sees you.
[The monk] said, "If I knew, I would have attained it. The Master laughed heartily.
Master Yunshan (Case 2). The Master asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From the Western Capital.
The Master said, "Have you brought a letter from the host of the Western Capital? The monk replied, "I dare not falsely convey any news. The Master said, "A masterful monk indeed."
"It naturally exists," [the Master] said. "It is like leftover soup and stale rice; who would be willing to eat it? The Master replied, "Only you, Senior Monk, would not eat it, would you?
The monk made a gesture of vomiting. The Master called to his attendant, "Escort this sick monk out. The monk then departed.
When the Master saw the monk approaching, he rose from his seat. The monk then departed. The Master said, "How remarkably quick-witted!
The monk then shouted, "To possess such an eye as this—to be a successor of Linji—is also a great humiliation. The Master said, "I simply hope that you, Dharma brother, will transmit it well.
The monk turned his head back; the Master then shouted, "To possess such an eye as this is to misjudge the reputation of all quarters."
[The Master] spoke, and immediately thereafter struck him.
(This occurred three times. The Master asked Linji, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?

Xuedou’s verse says: "Duanji’s total functioning continues the legacy; why must one wait for leisure to bring it forth?"
The Great Spirit raised his hand with little effort, splitting the myriad peaks of Mount Hua asunder.
While the Master was at Zhenzhou, he returned to rest on a bridge. There were three presiding lecturers (zhuazu) there;
one asked, "What is the bottomless depth of the river of Chan? The Master seized the monk and prepared to throw him off the bridge. At that moment—
The two presiding masters hurriedly intervened, saying, "Stop, stop! It is not right to offend the Senior Monk; we pray you will show us compassion.
The Master said, "If I were not looking at the faces of these two presiding masters, I would have driven him to his ultimate exhaustion."
As the Master was traveling along the road, he encountered Yantou, Xuefeng, and Qinshan—these three men. Yantou asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "I have come from Linji.
Yantou asked, "Is the Master well? The Master said, "He has passed away. Yantou sighed and said, "We three were of little merit;

[The assembly] requested, "Venerable Sir, please cite one or two cases. The Master said: "One day Linji addressed the assembly, saying:
'Upon this ball of red flesh, there is a true person of no rank who enters and exits through the gate of your face. Those of you who have not yet realized this—look, look!'"
At that time, there was a monk who came forward and asked, "What is the true person of no station? Linji stepped down from his meditation seat, grabbed him by the chest, and said, "Speak!
Speak! As the monk hesitated, Linji pushed him away and said, "The true person of no station—what a dried-up shit-stick!
When Yantou heard this being cited, he involuntarily stuck out his tongue. Qingshan said, "Why not say it is 'not the true person of no station'?"
A man was seized by the master, who split open his chest and held him fast, saying: "The true person of no station—how much does he differ from one who is not the true person of no station?
Speak quickly! Speak quickly! Qianshan was so struck that his face turned greenish-yellow and he could not utter a word.
Yantou and Xuefeng advised him, saying: "This newly ordained monk should not have offended you, Elder; please show some compassion. The Master said: "If it were not for..."
"Look at the faces of these two old men! [I swear by the earth! I will kill this bed-wetting ghost!

When the Master arrived at Deshan, he went to the straw mat seat at the foot of the mountain and made a gesture as if to spread his sitting cloth.

A monk asked: "What was the intent behind the ancients' raising of the mallet and brandishing of the whisk?"
