When Minister Chen Cao arrived, the Master drew a circle. Chen said, "I have come as a disciple; even so, I am already at a disadvantage.
To draw a circle on top of that! The Master then returned to his quarters and shut the door.
Xuedou said: "Minister Chen Cao possesses only one eye. Dayue Zhe said:
"Although Zifu was indeed a furnace of fundamental quality, how could he have known that Chen Cao was already refined pure gold?
Do you all wish to recognize Zifu? He casually cast down his hook, startling the dragon from the azure depths."
When Master Hehe (Fanyi) was inaugurating his hall, Zifu sent someone to deliver a pattern for socks to him.
The Master wrote the character "fire" (huo) on it and returned it unopened. When Zifu opened the seal and saw this, he knit his brows and remained silent for a long time.
Master Luyuan drew a perfect circle; Zifu said, "In Kuśinagara, he personally issued this command."

Chan Master Huiqing of Bajiao in Yingzhou, a Dharma successor of Chan Master Guangyong of Nanta at Yangshan in Yuanzhou (fourth in the lineage), was a native of Silla. He addressed the assembly, saying:
"Suppose a person is walking along when suddenly they encounter a precipice ten thousand feet deep ahead, while a wild fire pursues them from behind, with thorny brambles on both sides."
In this forest, if you move forward, you will fall into pits and ditches; if you retreat, wild fires will burn your body;
if you turn to the side, you will again be obstructed by thorns and brambles. At such a time, how can you avoid it?
If you can avoid it, you must possess a way to emerge from this state. If you cannot avoid it, you are a man doomed to perish.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "If you have a staff, I will give you a staff;
if you have no staff, I will take yours away."
The Master said to the assembly, "When I was eighteen, I went to Yangshan and visited the Southern Pagoda. He ascended the hall and said:
'All of you here—if you are a true man, as soon as you emerge from your mother's womb, you should let out a lion’s roar. Do you understand? "
Under these words, my body and mind came to rest, and I remained there for five years.
A monk asked, "What is the school of Deva? The Master said, "The red banner is on the left. The monk asked, "When a thief comes, one must strike;
when a guest comes, one must welcome. But what if both guest and thief arrive at once? The Master said, "There is a pair of worn-out straw sandals inside the house."
[The student] asked about shoes. [The Master] said, "It is just like a worn-out straw sandal; is it still fit for use?

The Master said, "If you take it with you, there will be misfortune ahead and no auspiciousness behind. [The student] asked, "How was it before the Buddha appeared in the world? The Master said, "A thousand-year-old eggplant root.
[The student] asked, "How is it after he appeared? The Master said, "Vajrapāṇi opens his eyes. [The student] asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "The chest."
Inscription on the *Svastikan*. Carrying a halo upon his back.
Chan Master Quanfu of Qinghua in Yuezhou (1). A native of Kunshan in Suzhou. A monk asked, "What is the Buddha?
The Master said, "A wooden crane flies atop the pillar of the flower-tablet. He was asked, "When meeting a person who has attained the Way on the road, one does not use words..."
[The monk] remained silent. [The Master asked: "I do not know what you are using to respond. The Master said: "The pupils in the eyes; the blowing of the whistle. The monk asked:
"How many years have you been a monk, Reverend? The Master said: "Last year on the ninth day of the ninth month, I first saw it;
now again I see the autumn leaves turning yellow. The monk said: "If that is so, then they are beyond numbering. The Master said: "Go ask the yellow leaves. The monk asked: "Ultimately, how is it?"
The Master said, "Six dice, the entire board is red. Question: "When a deceased monk passes away, where does he go?
The Master said, "The long river flows without interruption; gathered foam is left to the wind's blowing."

Chan Master Ximing Siming of West Monastery in Ruzhou, successor of Chan Master Baoshou of Zhenzhou (three cases total). A monk asked, "What is it like when one has trampled through the provisional city?
The Master said, "I do not strike down this dead man. The monk said, "Strike! The Master said, "I do not strike. The monk said again, "Strike! The Master then struck him. The monk... [left off].
The Master called out ten times, "Cut! and struck ten blows, then drove him out. The Master said, "This monk uses his bare flesh to meet his dry blows;
what such urgency for death? Next, another monk said, "I, your disciple, inform the Master:
the monk who asked questions earlier came from where Da’ue was. We two have studied together, and here our understanding is entirely the same."
"Master, you must expel these two men. If you do not expel them, I fear that they will fully comprehend your Dharma-way, and it will be difficult to find successors hereafter.
Before the sound of his words had faded, the Master struck him and immediately expelled the two.
A monk asked, "I have a question for the Master; how should I proceed? The Master said, "Even if you had one, I would cut it into three pieces.
The monk bowed, and the Master then ceased speaking. Later, a monk in the assembly saw the monk who had asked the question and said to him:
The Master said, "If the Abbot speaks, he speaks far too much; that is still not the ultimate point.
He called out to the monk who had asked the question and dragged him into the Dharma Hall, saying, "This monk does not acknowledge the Abbot! The Master asked, "Upādhyāya, do you not acknowledge me?
The monk replied, "I was not aware of anything, nor did I say anything. The Master shouted at him once and sent him down. As the monk returned to the hall, the Master added, "He spoke!"
"What way you speak is indeed a very great way," [the Master said], "but it simply has not yet reached the point of finality.
He then called the monk who had asked the question over and pulled him toward the Master. The Master said, "Upādhyāya, do you not agree with me? The monk replied, "Preceptor, do not trust this monk."
Today I have seen him lose his composure twice. The Master took up his staff and struck them all down at once.
Before the Master had settled in, he heard that Nan-yuan of Ru-zhou had begun his public ministry; as they were fellow practitioners from their original training, he went specifically to visit him.
As soon as the formal greetings were concluded, [Nan-yuan] said, "I, this humble one, address the Abbot: I have nothing to offer as a gift for my arrival. Since leaving Xu-zhou, I have..."
He obtained a Jiangxi razor and presented it to the Abbot. The Abbot said, "You have come from Xuzhou;

"Xiyuan obtained the razor of Jiangxi, yet had no place to display it;
only upon meeting a fellow student did he finally bring it forth. Is there anyone present now who has obtained such a razor? Try displaying it to this old man."
The monks looked; as there was none, they asked, "What do you usually use?
The second-generation Chan Master Baoshou of Zhenzhou (Part II): Previously, Baoshou asked the Master, "Before your parents were born, bring me back your original face.

Amidst the vast and turbulent red dust of the world, he constantly preached the True Dharma, and his disciples dared not disobey him. One day, on the street, he saw two men quarreling;

even if Baoshou had exerted his full capacity, he would still have been three thousand li short."
Wuzu Jie said: "Baoshou remarked, 'A crossbow capable of launching a thousand-jin bolt does not fire its trigger for the sake of a field mouse.

Suddenly he seized his staff and said: 'Where have you gone?'"
Daguai Zhe said: "Baoshou is much like an emperor issuing a decree within the realm;

Upon meeting with the old monk, he sought to settle a matter of injustice. After a long silence, he said: "Holding Mohe Panthei crosswise, I issue the full command;

"Simultaneously lost. The Master said, "This is not yet the point of your inquiry. What is the point of your inquiry?
The monk said, "Lost. The Master then struck him. The monk did not accept this.

Cuiyan Zhi said: "To deploy strategy within the tent and decide victory a thousand *li* away—though Nan'uan may have possessed the complete mechanism to face the enemy, alas, the terrain was vast and the men were few."
Daguai Zhe said: "Nanyuan held up the ancestral masters with great loftiness, wielding both granting and seizing according to the occasion. This monk was well able to act as a formidable adversary;
yet, alas, his strength was exhausted and his stratagems were spent. Is there now any monk of true substance? Come forth and meet Daguai!
It is not for the sake of stirring up a clamor or raising one's voice, but rather because we desire that the spirit of our school shall not decline."
"Is there? Is there? [The Master asked. "If not," [he continued,] "today at Dayang, it seems as though I have sought battle in vain.
Later, when this monk arrived under Yunmen’s assembly, he heard two monks raise this same conversation. One of them said, "At that time, Nanquan’s staff broke!
Upon hearing this, the monk suddenly attained awakening. He then returned to pay his respects, but the Master had already passed away.

He then went to visit Fengxue. Upon seeing him, Fengxue immediately recognized him and asked, "Upādhyāya, are you not that monk from the former Master’s assembly who asked about the saying, 'The chick pecks and the hen pries open the shell at the same time'? He replied, "I am.
Fengxue said, "How did you understand it then? He replied, "At that time, it was as if I were walking within the light of a lamp. Fengxue said, "..."
"You understand it.
Langya Huijue said, "You only know how to raise the white flag of surrender; you do not know how to seize the sword and halberd.
Cuiyan Zhen quoted Fengxue’s words, saying, "At that time, had I waited for him to attempt a reply, I would have struck him square in the mouth with my sitting mat."
Tianfeng Chengyun and Fengxue at that time, as soon as he was about to offer a response, gave him his rightful fodder.
Do you understand? True gold has been smelted a hundred times; entering the fire, it becomes even more brilliant.
The Master asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk replied, "Xiangzhou. The Master said, "What have you come to beg for?
The monk said, "I have come specifically to pay my respects to the Master. The Master said, "It happens that Baoying is not here.

The monk then gave a shout. The Master said, "I told you he was not here; why did you shout again? The monk shouted once more. The Master raised his staff. The monk hesitated. The Master struck him. The monk bowed.
The Master said, "This staff is my rightful portion; it is you who strike me, yet I shall strike you instead so that these words may be put into practice.
You blind fellow, go to the hall!
A monk asked, "Where have all the sages of the past gone? The Master said, "Neither to heaven, nor into the earth."
[Yunmen] said, "What about you, Master? The Master said, "Do you know where Old Man Baoying has fallen?

The monk hesitated, and the Master struck him across the mouth with his whisk. He then said, "Come forward. When the monk approached, the Master said, "The command should have been carried out by you," and struck him again with the whisk.
Xuedou said, "The command is already in his own hand; yet he does not know where the whisk comes from.
Xuedou uttered the word "blind" to add frost to snow. Huanglong Xin said, "A flaw in a white jade disk can still be polished away;
even a malady in the vital organs (gao-huang) should be treated. This monk has the command in his hand—why [does he not know its source]?"

"If you do not act thus, where does the fault lie? Miaoxi said, "To weigh Linji’s Three Essentials and Three Mysteries, one must be Nan-yuan to achieve it. Why did Xuedou say, 'The whisk does not know its place of origin'?
Miaoxi also said, "Blind! This is merely to ensure that both can see one another.
A monk came to visit him and said, "It is lost! It is lost! The Master then raised his staff toward the monk; the monk remained speechless.
The Master struck him several times with the staff.
Yunfeng Yue said: "This monk has light upon his head, yet he does not know there is lacquer beneath his feet. How do you understand this?
Even if you were to strike three thousand blows in the morning and eight hundred blows in the evening, with your ten directions crisscrossed in every way."
The Master asked the Garden Head, "Has the bottle gourd flowered yet? The Head replied, "It has flowered long ago.
The Master said, "Has it set fruit or not? He replied, "Last night it was struck by frost. The Master said, "What will the assembly eat?
As the Garden Head hesitated, the Master struck him.
A monk asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master gave a shout. The monk said, "Master, do not poke your head out.
The Master shouted again. The monk bowed. The Master said, "To let you go would be unacceptable," and struck him.
Another monk asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master also shouted. The monk bowed. The Master said, "Today, both of you have performed [the task]."
The two Chan guests from Jia, together with the old man of Baoying, uphold the treasury of the true Dharma-eye of Linji.
If you wish to discern guest and host beneath a single shout, go ask the two Chan guests from Er.
The Master asked a monk, "What is your name? The monk replied, "Puchan. The Master said, "If you suddenly encounter a piece of excrement, what then?
The monk said, "I do not know. The Master then struck him.
The Master asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk replied, "From Changshui. The Master said, "Does it flow east or flow west?
The monk said, "It is not like that at all. The Master said, "How then? The monk then said, "Goodbye," and the Master struck him.
One day, the Master seized a monk and said, "What? What? The monk was speechless. The Master said, "Thirty years of riding a horse.
A monk asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "The source of immeasurable great illnesses. [The monk] said, "I beg the Master to heal me."
The Master said, "The worldly physicians fold their hands in helplessness.
A monk asked, "What is it like when the ancient hall is restored? The Master said, "The eaves jut out from the tiles of the bright hall.
The monk said, "In that case, the adornments are fully complete. The Master said, "When the grass is cut, the snake's head falls."
A monk asked, "What is the seamless stupa? The Master said, "Seven flowers and eight rags. The monk asked, "Who is the person within the stupa?
The Master said, "The hair is not combed and the face is not washed."
A monk asked, "Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings the same or different?
The Master said, "The Minister Huang, the Chancellor Li, Chan Master Kebin of Taixing Mountain, and [Master] Fan Yi.

One day, Xinghua said to the Master, "Before long, you will become a teacher who proclaims the Way. The Master said, "I will not enter this protective community. Xinghua said, "Do you know it and yet refuse to enter?"
Huihua said, "It is not that he does not enter. The Master said, "In no way is it so. Huihua then struck him.
He continued, "Venerable Kebin, you have been defeated in the battle of Dharma; you shall pay a fine of five strings of cash and provide a meal for the assembly.

When the next day’s mealtime arrived, Huihua struck the gavel and announced, "Venerable Kebin, having been defeated in the battle of Dharma, you are not permitted to eat; you shall immediately leave the monastery."
Xuedou said: "Kebin wanted to inherit Xinghua’s lineage. Let us set aside for a moment the matter of his fine and expulsion from the monastery;
he must first exact this one blow of the staff. Now, I ask you all: since the blow has already been taken, how can it be exacted?
Xuedou wishes to settle this injustice; today, I shall clear Kebin’s name."
[He] bowed. [Huanglong Nan said: "Kebin lost his money and suffered punishment;
though he had reason, it was difficult to vindicate. Xinghua used the rigid to resolve the yielding, yet this was not sufficient to bring glory."
Daguang Zhe said: "Although Xinghua’s command was put into practice, it was very much like using force to intimidate others.
Kebin lost the strategic initiative for a time, yet how could his fame and glory not remain undiminished for a thousand ages? But tell me, where does the point of benefit and harm lie?
If one has not endured many battles on the field, how can one raise the great war-drum and scatter the dust of the red world?"
The nun Zishou Miaozong said: "Under a heavy reward, there must be brave men. Zhenjing Wen’s verse says:
"A man of stature should sever [delusions] himself; Xinghua is a thoroughgoing man for the sake of others.
Hereafter, let his eyes open of their own accord; he shall be caned, fined, and expelled from the monastery."
Shoukō Shijie (three times). One day the Master said to himself: "Where have all the sages of antiquity gone?
When Deshan heard this, he said: "What? What? The Master replied: "When the imperial decree summons the flying dragon horse, the lame tortoise sticks its head out.
Deshan then desisted. The next day, after bathing, Shoukō went to serve tea to Deshan. Deshan patted the Master’s back and said: "Yesterday..."
"What about this koan? The Master said, "This old fellow has only just now had a flash of realization.
Xuedou said, "Even so, though true gold may pass through a hundred refinings, it still requires the authentic tongs and hammer.
Since Deshan obstructed others with his own [views], this monk likewise suffered an injustice. He took up his staff, drew a line across it, and said, "Just now..."
Setting aside this public case for a moment: where have all the sages of the past gone?
As the assembly hesitated, the Master drove them out all at once. Huanglong Nan said: "Deshan feigned deafness and dumbness;
although he gained the advantage in secret, Kuang was like one who covers his ears while stealing a bell—how could he avoid the laughter of bystanders?"
Daguizhe said: "If one does not ascend the Dragon Gate, how can one know the depth of the vast ocean?
Even if the waves surge a thousand fathoms high, what can be done when the Dragon King pays them no heed?"
The Master, citing the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, addressed the assembly, saying: "Today I grant you fearlessness.

If you were the descendants of Linji, Deshan, Gaoting, Dayu, Niaoke, or Huian, you would not need to ask 'How? or 'What?'—simply request to enter directly with a single blade, and I, Huayan, shall serve as your witness.
The Master came forward and paid his respects; upon rising, he immediately shouted. Huayan also shouted. The Master shouted again.
Yan shouted again. The Master prostrated himself, then rose and said, "Everyone, look! This old fellow has suffered a total defeat.

He shouted once more, clapped his hands, and returned to the assembly. When Huayan returned to the abbot’s quarters, Fengxue, who was serving as the *vinaya-dhara* (rector), went up to pay his respects.
Yan said, "I cannot stand that Zhejiang guest Shoukuo; today he gave me a thorough thrashing. Now—"
The assembly gathered and gave him a beating, driving him out of the monastery. Xue said, "It was too late to drive him out.
The Master said, "Then please 'enter directly with a single blade. It was the Master’s own fault; he is a descendant of Linji, and it is his natural way to act in this manner.
Please cease your anger. Xue came down and reported the matter in detail to the Master. The Master said, "What have you done?"
Regarding the origin of this: he urged the old man, "Before I have even finished asking, you already wanted to eat my staff; my words were put into practice.
Now that you do not strike me, you have nullified these words of mine. Xue said, "These words have already been put into practice."
When the Master arrived at Lumén, one day while he was in the rear hall, he saw the monk Chù engaged in conversation with several monks.
Lumén came down and asked, "What are you doing all day long, looking so disheveled and distracted?
Chù replied, "Does the Master see me as disheveled and distracted? Lumén gave a shout; Chù also shouted. Both sides then desisted. The Master said, "All..."
"Venerable Elder, look at these two blind men! Having said this, he gave a shout and returned to his quarters.
He then ordered an attendant to invite the Master up, saying, "Just now, when the old monk met with Chan Master Chu as host and guest, what fault or deficiency was there?
The Master replied, "I see only that your illness has grown even deeper. Yunmen said, "Since I first met Xinghua, I have understood it thus."
The Master said: "When the Abbot arrived at Xinghua, I was serving as his attendant and remember the words spoken at that time.
The Gatekeeper said: "Please cite them for me. The Master then cited them: Xinghua asked, "Where have you come from?
The Abbot replied, "From Mount Wutai. Xinghua said, "Have you seen Mañjuśrī? The Abbot then gave a shout. Xinghua said, "I am asking you: have you seen Mañjuśrī?"
Again, when he provoked [the Master] with wickedness, the Master shouted at him once more. Xuanhua remained silent. The Master bowed and departed.
When the next day arrived, the Master instructed someone to summon Xuanhua, saying, "Wait until I have questioned the Master. By then, the Master had already left.
Xuanhua then ascended the hall and said, "Look at this fellow! He has taken up a single broken length of rope and is heading south. Thus it was.
Later, [Zhaozhou] said, "I once saw Xinghua come. The Master said, "The present case is exactly like that from back then.
The Gatekeeper asked, "Why did Xinghua remain silent at that time? The Master said, "He knew the Abbot would not understand the phrase of host and guest."
"This is why I did not speak [yesterday]. Tomorrow I shall wait to engage in debate with you. The Master had already departed.
On the following day, Lumen specifically prepared tea for him. In the evening *can*, he addressed the assembly, saying: "Those who study as dragons and elephants must be thorough and meticulous.
Entering the room for decisive discernment cannot be taken lightly. Do not take up a mere phrase and consider it the ultimate limit, claiming, 'I am a spiritual patriarch.'"
It is just like me: when I first saw Xinghua at that time, I recognized his shifting movements;

when I heard people talk of one shout or two shouts, I simply stopped there, taking it to be the Buddha-dharma. Today, having been seen through by those with clear eyes, it has become nothing but a source of ridicule.
What was the point of it? It was all because of my pride and ignorance, which prevented me from turning back and drawing near [to the truth].

As for the "Upstreamer" (Urdhvasrotas): it was truly fortunate that a man of clear vision, not sparing even his own life, came forth before the assembly to provide testimony for this old fellow of Lukmen. Truly, this kindness is difficult to repay. Why? Xinghua said:
"Even if you were to shout yourself up to the thirty-third heaven and then crash back down until you have not a single breath left, I would still wait for you patiently."
Having rested, he said to you, "It is not yet so. Why is this? Xinghua has never scattered genuine pearls from within a purple silk curtain for you all;
why do you remain here in the empty void, shouting wildly and at random?
These words are truly like medicine or a stone—remedial and corrective—but it is difficult for practitioners to believe them. Now you must discern this clearly; how could it be otherwise?
What joy! My lifelong aspiration has been fulfilled; my studies are now complete.

The Dharma-heir of the practitioner Kefu from Zhuozhou, the Venerable Jì (one instance), was at the capital of Luoyang. Because Military Commander Zhu was providing a vegetarian feast for the monks, he entered the hall to burn incense. Looking around—
[The Master] looked up and down and said, "Straight down is it! Straight down is it! [Zhu] followed the path as he walked, his mouth never ceasing for a moment.
Upon reaching the Master’s presence, the Master asked, "What is this straight down? Zhu then gave a shout. The Master said, "You are a military man;
fortunately you are among those who follow the Buddha-dharma, so why do you act so aggressively? Zhu said, "If you were acting aggressively, you would not be permitted to do so. The Master then—
"Ho! Zhu said. "The hook is in a place beyond doubt. The Master shouted again. After Zhu had finished his meal, he requested the Master to speak.
The Chief Monk (Senglu) said, "I address you, General. Just now, how could you tolerate this monk’s such impertinence?
Zhu said, "If all of you had shouted when I did, I would have had my sword ready. The Chief Monk said, "I am but a team of purple cloth bags."
"Not so. It must be an Elder of Nanchan [Nanyuan] before it can be achieved. The Master said, "If it were an Elder of Nanchan, he would not have even dreamed of it yet.
This was the Dharma successor of Chan Master Huiqing of Bajiao in Yingzhou.
Chan Master Qingrang of Xingyang in Yingzhou (Case 1). A monk asked, "The Buddha Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū sat at the site of enlightenment for ten kalpas;
yet the Dharma did not manifest before him, and he could not attain the Way of Buddhahood. What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "Your question is most profound and accurate.
The monk said, "Since he was already sitting at the site of enlightenment, why could he not attain the Way of Buddhahood? The Master said:
Because he did not become a Buddha.
Chan Master Jiche of Bazhao in Ruizhou (four cases total). The Master went to visit Fengxue, who asked, "What is the True Dharma Eye?
The Master replied, "A clay pellet. Fengxue marveled at this. Later, he visited Bazhao and heard him ascend the hall, where it was said:
"Two mouths, neither possessing a tongue—this is my fundamental tenet. Upon hearing this, the Master attained a great awakening.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "In the past, when the Tathāgata was in the kingdom of Vārāṇasī, the Brahma King requested him to turn the Wheel of Dharma.

The Tathāgata did not remain silent; out of deference to the spiritual capacity of his followers, he adapted his teaching to their needs, and thus the names of the Three Vehicles came into circulation."

From the heavens to the human realm, it has been gloriously propagated until now without falling into decline. Yet, when measured against the gate of our ancestral patriarchs, there is a vast disparity between heaven and earth.
For those of the highest capacity, they transcend suddenly without distinction. What is the single phrase of total integration? Is there anyone who can speak it?
If you can speak it, you possess the eye of study; if you cannot speak it, heaven is wide and earth is narrow.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "When there is no film before the eyes, there are no flowers in the sky. When the water rises, the boat ascends; when the mud is deep, the Buddha is large.
Do not bring questions; I have no answers. Do you understand? The question lies within the answer; the answer lies within the question."
An ancient verse says: "The essential meaning of the plantain tree does not hang upon lips or teeth; the wooden boy sings and responds, while the stone man leans his ear.
Chan Master Tianpeng Ceshuo (Fan Yi) addressed the assembly, saying: "To uphold the orthodox command is still to fashion a nest and create a counterfeit.

To provide an answer regarding the Buddha-dharma is, in itself, a deliberate deception that overreaches the superior stream. If you question it, there is discrepancy; if you answer it, there is entanglement."
"Mutually, O Venerable One, where would you set your teeth? Although it is thus, matters are not always one-sided;
the authority is in his hands, and bestowing or taking away depends on the occasion. If you have doubts, please ask. A monk asked, "What is the primary meaning (paramārtha)?
The Master said, "The myriad peaks pierce through to the sea; a drop of water descends from the cliff."
Chan Master Xingyang Guijing of Yingzhou, Dharma heir of Chan Master Xisi Siming of Ruzhou (Case 1). The Master asked, "When you intend to ask but do not ask, what is the situation?
Xisi struck him immediately. After the Master remained silent for a long while, Xisi said, "If you call this a staff, your eyebrows and whiskers will fall off. The Master [remained silent].
Upon hearing these words, he attained realization.
Baofu Zhan said, "Even so, how many hairs do you have on your eyebrows?
He was a dharma successor of Chan Master Nanyuan Yongyong of汝州 (Ruzhou).
Chan Master Yanzhao of Fengxue in汝州 (17th case): A native of the Liu family of Yuhang.

When he first visited Nan’uan, as soon as he stepped across the threshold, Nan’uan said, “Upon entering to inquire, one must discern the host. The Master said, “I ask the Master to distinguish it for me definitively.
Nan’uan patted his left knee; the Master gave a shout. Nan’uan patted his right knee; the Master shouted again. Nan’uan said, “A single strike on the left side—”

[The Master] followed. [The Head of the Monastery] struck once from the right side and asked, "What is this? The Master said, "Blind! The Head of the Monastery raised his staff. The Master pointed it out and said, "Do not apply blind fetters or strike blindly.
He snatched the staff away and said, "I am going to hit you, the Abbot! Do not say I did not warn you. The Head of the Monastery leaned his staff against the wall and said:
"Today I have been left standing there by this yellow-faced man from Zhejiang. The Master said, "It is very much like being unable to hold one's alms bowl and yet falsely claiming one is not hungry.
The Abbot asked, "Have you ever been to this place before? The Master said, "What kind of question is that? The Abbot said, "I am asking you in all good faith.
The Master said, "In that case, I cannot let you off the hook," and he immediately prostrated himself. The Abbot gestured for him to sit and said, "Please sit and have some tea. They drank tea.
[The Master] stopped. The Abbot asked again, "Between you and your companion, who was it? The Master said, "It was with Attendant Kuò;
we were in the same summer retreat at Huayan in Xiangzhou. The Abbot said, "I knew you would meet a master. He asked again, "What did he say to you?
The Master said, "He told me to act as the host exclusively. The Abbot said, "This blind fellow! You have come here to suffer defeat."
[The Master] struck him. The Master then submitted himself to the rank of disciple.
One day, Nan-yuan asked the Master, "How do you deliberate upon 'one blow' in the South? The Master said, "I deliberate upon it as something extraordinary.
The Master then asked in turn, "I wonder, Reverend, how do you deliberate upon 'one blow' here in this place? Nan-yuan [struck him] across the chest.

Leaning on his staff, he said: "Under the blow of the staff is the patience of non-arising; when facing the situation, the teacher is not seen. At these words, the teacher attained a great realization of the profound principle.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "In general, for those who study the Way, your eyes must be such that the great function manifests before you at every moment; do not constrain yourselves."
Regarding minor details, even if one were to attain realization prior to words, it would still be a lingering shell and a deluded enclosure.
Even if one is thoroughly proficient within the phrase, one cannot avoid wild views wherever one encounters the path. I exhort you all:

whatever conceptual understandings you have hitherto relied upon—whether clear or obscure, the two diverging paths of ordinary and sage—should be swept away all at once. This will ensure that each and every one of you becomes like a lion cub, letting out a roar.
Shadi let out a roar. Standing like a cliff ten thousand fathoms high, who would dare look him directly in the eye?
To look is to blind one's own eyes.

He addressed the assembly, saying: "The coming of Bodhidharma from the West was for the purpose of transmitting [the Dharma] to this Eastern land. He pointed directly at the human mind, so that by seeing one's nature, one becomes a Buddha.

He alone singled out the myriad phenomena, proclaiming them beyond all material things. Those who awaken to this are not separated by even a hair’s breadth; those who remain deluded turn their backs on awakening and unite with the dust of the senses.
Even those of middling or inferior capacity must be diligent; do not let the time and light of your days pass in vain. Each and every one possesses it—how much more so for those like me!"
This is the intent transmitted from the West, a separate transmission outside the scriptures. When the Way accords with a single word, one is free and sovereign in all directions.
One smashes the skull and strips away the cranial lid; is this not a source of great joy?
The Master asked a monk, "At dusk you cast yourself into the forest; at dawn, from where did you depart? The monk replied, "I am not a monk who studies Chan.
The Master said, "With this very body, you shall enter hell."
Mingjiao Kuan said in his commentary: "The key is in the Master's hand.
The Master asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk replied, "Xiangzhou. The Master dragged the attendant boy, gave him a slap, and shouted, "Get out!"
The Master was attending to a sick monk. The monk asked, "The four great elements are fundamentally empty; from where does illness arise?
The Master replied, "It comes from the very place where you, Venerable, have asked. The monk, gasping for breath, said, "After I have finished asking, what then?
The Master said, "Let go of your hands and lie in the vast expanse of space. The monk said, "Ye-ye," and immediately passed away.
A monk asked, "When the fundamental matter has not yet been clarified, what serves as the verification? The Master said, "Striking the gong for silence in the midst of a bustling marketplace.
The monk asked, "What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "Lighting a golden lamp at midday."

Question: "If a person of great *icchantika* nature comes, will you still act as his teacher for him? The Master said: "The Dharma has long since fallen into decay; where is compassion to be found? [The questioner] said:
"When one grows old, one becomes a demon. The Master said: "When one grows old, one becomes a demon."
Question: "How is it when the precious sword has not yet emerged from its scabbard? The Master said: "Strike right on the mouth. Question: "How is it after it has emerged from the scabbard?
The Master said: "Pull out the teeth."
Question: "What is the body revealed alone amidst the dust? The Master said: "A thousand tents in the north of the Great Wall; ten-thousand-hu ships in the south of the River. [The student] said:
"If that is so, then it is not the dust. The Master said: "This is the talk of those who merely parrot words. A single letter contains ten thousand practices."
Question: I shall not ask about other matters. What is the arrangement for today? The Master said: "There is that blind donkey of yours here. [The student] said:
"In that case, we shall beat the drum and play the lute. The Master said: "That is the sound of pressing down on one's belly and passing wind."

Chan Master Cizhao Cong of Shimen in Xiangzhou (Total: fourteen cases). While the Master was at Shoushan, Guanghui Liang asked Shoushan, "When a student has personally reached the Treasure Mountain but returns empty-handed, what then? Shoushan said, "A torch before every door.
Upon hearing this, the Master attained great enlightenment beneath the words and composed a verse, saying: "I am now twenty-seven years old; seeking the Way..."
"I have been searching for you for a long time; today I am glad to meet you. Yet, we do not know each other. Shoushan agreed with this and addressed the assembly, saying:
"For those of the highest capacity, both person and dharma are cast aside. For those of middling or lower capacity, one merely removes their questioning, yet a trace of dharma still remains.
For those of the lowest capacity, one acts according to their questions. But as for the extraordinary man of the Way, he manifests his entire being."
"Use it! All you senior elders are men of the Way who transcend the ordinary; how would this old monk dare to employ such means?

He addressed the assembly, saying: 'Before the fifteenth day, all Buddhas are born; after the fifteenth day, all Buddhas pass away. Before the fifteenth day, when all Buddhas are born, you must not depart from here. If you depart from here, I..."* *(Note:
The source text appears to be an excerpt from a Chan discourse, likely ending abruptly. The ellipsis indicates the sentence continues with a conditional consequence for departing.)*
There is a hook; it hooks you. After the fifteenth day, all Buddhas will have passed away, and you shall not remain here with me.
If you remain here with me, I have an awl; it awls you. Now tell me: at the very moment of the fifteenth day, is it the hook that is used, or is it the awl?
Thereupon, he spoke in verse: "At the very moment of the fifteenth day, The hook and the awl are both stilled at once."
I was about to ask further how it is, when I turned my head and the sun had already risen. He addressed the assembly, saying:
"In question and answer, one must ensure that both the beginning and the end are complete; otherwise, to leave the dragon’s head and the snake’s tail is to deceive oneself.

It is like a king wielding a sword—everything depends on the king’s intent; it is like a mirror set upon a stand—it requires the cessation of all viewing. Once the mouth is opened, one has already traveled thousands of miles; to lower the head..."
"Ten thousand layers of thought and consideration. If a person lacks the true eye, how could they avoid becoming a jackal on their future path?
He addressed the assembly, saying: "As soon as the bells and drums cease, guest and host are distinguished. When the great assembly comes together, both illumination and function are complete.
If you can understand it thus, you will succeed the ancients. If you cannot understand it, it is truly a matter of bitter regret. Is there anyone here who understands?"
"Come forth and provide testimony before the assembly!
He addressed the assembly, saying: "If you can utter the first phrase, you have burst forth from within the rock. If you can utter the second phrase, you have been summoned forth.
If you can utter the third phrase, you will not even be able to save yourself."
Addressing the assembly, [the Master] raised the case of Fengxue, who said: "A white cat with five claws, fierce and powerful; raised in the hall, it leaves no trace of insects.
This is clearly the method of finding one's place atop a tree; one must strictly avoid uttering words that permit outsiders.
The Master asked: "What is the phrase that permits outsiders? After a long silence, he said: "Do not misquote me."
He addressed the assembly, saying: "To conceive a thought is already an error; to stir a single念 (mental movement) is already to deviate.
To neither conceive nor stir—this is precisely to devise a livelihood within stagnant water. What is the point where a patch-robed monk turns his body?
As for the ancients speaking thus, was there anything in it to benefit people? If you say they benefited people, you are bound and killed by their words; if you say they did not benefit people..."
For what reason is it said: "The mind of nirvāṇa is easy to understand; the wisdom of differentiation is difficult to clarify"? He addressed the assembly, saying:
"Upon the jeweled flower king-throne, there is only the Compassionate Honored One. Within the sandalwood grove, there is no other faction.
A fox is not of the same species as a lion; a lamp is not as bright as the sun and moon. Those who know this have already fulfilled their lives; those who do not yet know it—"
"You must be thorough and meticulous.
The Master asked the steward, "The Qingliang Weir is dammed by you; when a flood suddenly comes and the waters overflow the heavens, can the weir still hold?

The steward replied, "It is within it. The Master asked, "With whom does it keep company? The steward was speechless. The Master requested him to provide a substitute answer, and the Master said, "It penetrates through."
He passed on to Silla. One day, Seok (Sae) asked him, "If you suddenly encounter a great flood that reaches the heavens, can you hold back the dam?

The Master said, "Above it supports the heavens; below it supports the earth. Seok asked, "What if you encounter the kalpa-fire blazing forth? The Master said, "Horizontally emerging, vertically submerging."
A monk entered the room and asked, "At this very moment, is there still a teacher? The Master said, "The lamp has shone through the night;
where is it not clear? The monk asked, "Ultimately, what is the matter? The Master said, "Tomorrow is the Cold Food Festival."
A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the ancient saying: 'A wool ball at a rapid on a river滩'? The Master said, "The clouds part and the sun shines bright.
The monk asked, "What is the meaning of: 'A stone reaching the bottom at a rapid on a river滩'? The Master said, "The roof collapses and the blue sky is revealed."
"What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "It penetrates from above and through to below.
A monk asked, "As the days pass and the months come, one does not realize that the years have grown old. Is there anyone who does not grow old? The Master said:
[The monk] asked: "What is it that does not grow old? The Master said: "A coiled dragon exerts its strength and lets out a loud cry;

as evening falls, its spiritual essence becomes even more abundant. [The monk] asked: "What is the place of profound depth for the student? The Master said: "The tortoise hides its six limbs deep within the water.
[The monk] asked: "I do not yet understand what the matter therein is. The Master said: "Let the travelers on the road know nothing of it."
A monk asked, "Kāśyapa Matanga entered China long ago, and his words have already become numerous and complex. Now that Bodhidharma has come from the West, I pray the Master will point directly.
The Master said, "The winter is not yet at its coldest; wait until after the twelfth lunar month to see. The monk asked, "The five eyes cannot behold its form, and the two ears cannot hear its sound.

Is it within the realm of sound and color? Or is it beyond sound and color? The Master said, "From where does your question arise? The monk asked, "I gaze upon it, yet it is here. The Master said, "Gaze upon it, yet it is here."
[The student] asked: "Suddenly [the object] is behind; what thing is this? The Master said: "It strikes right into your nostrils. [The student] asked:

"If one is not hung by even a single thread of silk, the Dharma-net is boundless. Why, then, do you distinguish between delusion and awakening? The Master said: "Two buckets on one shoulder. [The student] asked:

"The mind follows the environment, and the environment pursues the arising of the mind. When both mind and environment are forgotten, where is that? The Master said: "Wait until you awaken, and then I will tell you."
"Yes. The questioner asked, "Sentient beings have utility, while insentient things lack it. How is it that insentient things lack utility?
The Master said, "The single-leafed door stands open all night long."
Chan Master Yuanlian of Guanghui in汝州 (total of thirteen cases). He was a native of the Chen family in Jinjiang, Quanzhou. Initially, he went to visit Master Nan’uan Nian.
Nan’uan asked, “Where have you recently come from? The Master replied, “From Shoushan. Nan’uan said, “The old monk’s staff is not in my hand.
The Master said, “Even if it were in your hand, you would still not be able to strike people indiscriminately. Nan’uan said, “Wild fox spirit! The Master—
He said, "Exactly so," gave a single rap, and then went out.
One day, while standing in attendance, the Master asked, "What is it like before the drum for the fish has been struck? Nan said, "Looking at the sky, one does not see the sky.
The Master asked, "What is it like after it has been struck? Nan said, "Gazing at the ground, one does not see the ground. At these words, the Master attained realization and prostrated himself.
Zhiguan said, "What have you seen? Nanquan then prostrated. Zhiguan said, "In the midst of a bustling marketplace, there is still one or half of a person.
Zhiguan said, "You people of the South are clever. Nanquan then said, "I take my leave. Zhiguan said, "Be careful. Nanquan then departed.
One day, the Master asked Shoushan, "When a student arrives at the Treasure Mountain in person and returns empty-handed, what then?

Nanquan said, "A torch before every door. At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment and said, "From this day forward, I shall no longer doubt the tongues of the old monks throughout the land. Nanquan asked, "How do you understand this? Try explaining it."
The Master said, "It is merely water in a jar on the ground. [The monk] thought, "Do you understand? The Master then prostrated himself.
When the Master arrived at Shoushan, Shoushan asked, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From Hanshang. Shoushan held up his fist and said, "Is there such a thing as this in Hanshang?
The Master said, "What kind of bowl is this that makes a ringing sound? Shoushan said, "Blind! The Master clapped his hands once.
[He] clapped his hands once and went out.
Addressing the assembly, he said: "In the past, at the assembly of Linji, when the two head monks of the two halls met, they looked at each other and each let out a shout, and then it was over.
You all, tell me: was there guest and host or not? If you say there was, it was merely this..."
"Blind fellow! If you say 'it is not,' you are likewise just a blind fellow. If you say 'neither existent nor non-existent,' you will be sent ten thousand *li* away to Yuzhou.
If you can speak here, I shall give you thirty blows; if you cannot speak, I shall also give you thirty blows.
When a monk reaches this point, how can he escape the mountain monk’s entanglement? After a long silence.
He said, "Alas! The frogs and earthworms leap up to the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven and crash into Mount Sumeru, shattering into a hundred fragments.
He then took up his staff and said, "This troop of unperforated iron hammers—retreat quickly, retreat quickly!"
He addressed the assembly, saying: "The Patriarch’s command is being put into practice; the traces of humans and devas have vanished.
If you can pass through this single thread of the Way, I shall speak of its entanglements for you. Why is this so? In the mere interval of a deliberation, one has already lost one's body and life.
This mountain monk, undaunted by the censure of the various quarters, enters the mud and the water for all of you. Is there anyone who understands? Come forth!"
"Let us see if you can pass along this message. After a long silence, he said, "Look! Look! You are all making your living within the realm of Māra.
He then took up his staff and said, "Speak quickly! Speak quickly! As the assembly hesitated, the Master gave a shout and struck the ground once with the staff.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "The Buddha-dharma is fundamentally without affairs.

All the sages of the past were merely fabricating wonders, needlessly creating complications, degrading the noble to the lowly, and burying their descendants. Furthermore, Yunmen, Dongshan, and Linji died without awakening;
they suffered indignities for their entire lives. Here in my place, it is not so. Even if Śākyamuni Buddha himself were to appear,"
He even casts him out to other worlds, teaching him to leave no trace behind. Why is this so? It is to avoid the worry of losing his descendants.
When the old monk speaks thus, how do you all understand it? If you can understand it right here, will you not be joyful and relieved?
He teaches him to cast off his fur robe and become a truly free and easy patch-robed monk.
The assembly departed. "If you still do not understand, there will be new regulations next year; the vexation of the spring breeze shall never cease.

He then descended from his seat. At that time, a monk requested further instruction, saying, "Just now the Master said that even if Śākyamuni Buddha himself were to appear, he would have to be banished to another world.
Before he had finished speaking, the Master said, "If you understand it in this way..."
"Entering hell is like being struck by an arrow. The monk asked, "I do not yet understand how this is to be realized. The Master struck him. The monk hesitated.
The Master said, "Do you understand? The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Today, though I do not avoid being censured by those of other quarters, I shall explain it for you:
'To offer this body and mind to every dust-mote world—this is what is called repaying the Buddha’s kindness.'"
When Vice Minister Yang Yi arrived at the temple, he encountered the Master ascending the hall. The Master took up his staff and addressed the assembly, saying:
"Vertically it exhausts the three periods of time; horizontally it spans the ten directions. Tell me, where do Śakra and Brahmā establish their dwelling and sustain their lives?
Yang stepped forward from the assembly, intending to respond, but the Master struck him immediately. Yang said, "I have not yet spoken a word; why did you strike me, Reverend?"
[The Master] struck him. The Master said, "When you, Minister, had not yet stepped over the gate of Guanghui, you already deserved thirty blows from this old monk.
Yang said, "Lower your voice, lower your voice. The Master said, "If you know, that is well enough. He then continued, "Had it not been for you, Minister, just now..."

This is indeed a great responsibility to undertake. Nevertheless, thirty years from now, there will be one whose eye at the crown of the head has opened who will emerge as a patch-robed monk, and our school will flourish greatly. Examine these words closely; do you all understand? Listen to this verse:
When the bird comes, there is speech; when the person goes, there is no sound. The green cassia tree is renowned throughout the four seas. Yang.
He then asked, "I do not yet understand what extraordinary words or phrases Linji possessed that surpassed all others, such that you, Master, became his Dharma heir.
The Teacher replied, "The taste of the olive served with tea is long-lasting."
The Imperial Protector Liu asked, "What is the家风 (family style) of an elder? The Master spat directly in his face.
The Imperial Protector reacted with indignation and said, "What was that spitting for? The Master replied, "What kind of place is this? Take it upon yourself and leave.
Wang the Section Chief remarked, "Elder, even when the Imperial Protector asks such a question, there is no need to act like this. The Master said, "Why mention the Imperial Protector?"
When Brahmā and Śakra came, he taught them to leave no trace behind. Taibao said to Bibu, "This elder is truly worthy of great esteem.
The Master called his attendant and had him bring a dustpan and broom. Taibao and Bibu bowed in thanks.
The Master then sat upon his seat, laid his staff across his lap, and said: "Under the sword of the General, heaven and earth were already settled; he alone has remained to guard them."
Pervading the center of the universe, his body spans the three realms. With the Three Seals in his hand, he seizes or releases as the occasion demands.
In the mere space of a thought, one loses one’s very life. Is there anyone like a dragon-like warrior or a tiger-like youth who will come forth to engage in a bout of combat?
To settle matters for a lifetime—is there such a person? Is there? After a long silence, he said: "The red banners flash; the young men wail in grief. He then leaned on his staff.
[The Master] struck the rope bed once with his staff.
As the Master sat within the abbot’s quarters, Layman Zhang arrived. No sooner had he entered the gate than the Master asked: "Within the Lion's Den..."
"Why? Zhang, possessed by a wild fox spirit, prepared to offer a deliberation. The Master immediately pushed him out and slammed the door shut.
Zhang went to the shrine of the local deity (Tandi), took a string of paper money, hung it on the gate of the abbot’s quarters, and then returned.

When the Master opened the door and saw this, he said, "One must indeed be this man to succeed. The next day, Zhang came to see the Master again. The Master grabbed him and said, "Yesterday's case was—"
"How is it? Zhang hesitated. The Master gave him a slap.
The Master asked a monk, "Do you have a staff? He replied, "No. The Master said, "I give you a staff," and as soon as these words were spoken, he struck him.
Three newly arrived monks came to pay their respects. The Master asked, "When three people travel together, there must be someone among them who can serve as my teacher.
Which of you is that teacher? They replied, "We have only recently entered the monastic community; we do not understand. The Master said, "It is your fault, and it is also my fault."
The monk intended to mock him, so the Master said, "You lacquer bucket, sit down and drink some tea.
The Master asked the lecturer, "Is it true that you can lecture on the Three Sutras and Five Treatises? He replied, "I dare not say so.
The Master held up his staff and asked, "What about this? As the lecturer hesitated, the Master struck him. The lecturer said, "How could you do such a thing?"
Next, the Master said, "This fellow who chews spit—what are you saying? The host had no reply. The Master said, "Come forward. The host approached.
The Master drew a line on the ground and said, "Does this come from the sutras? Does it come from the śāstras? The host said, "It does."
This is not recorded in any of the sutras or treatises. The Master said, "An unperforated iron hammer. Go to the hall. After a short while, he returned to pay his respects.
The Master asked, "Where are you from? The guest replied, "I have just finished paying my respects to the Master."
The Master said, "What kind of place is this of mine, that you, a fellow like this, would speak? Having finished speaking, he gave a single kick and felled him.
The Master rose up and said, "I understand! I understand! The Master seized him and said, "You wretched spirit! What were you saying?"
"Quick way! Quick way! [The host] struck the Master with one palm. The Master said, "You blind fellow, coming here to act recklessly.
[The host] further said, "I pay my respects. The Master said, "Raising a son who does not equal his father; the family lineage shall decline for a generation."
Chan Master Hongyin of Shendeng in Tanzhou (the fifteenth), a native of Xiangshui, addressed the assembly, saying:
"In the kingdom of Magadha, this edict was personally enacted. Does the great assembly know where it has fallen? A single phrase encompasses heaven and encloses earth;
it utterly transcends the extraordinary and stands before all the sages. For this reason, the harmony of the five regions is not uniform, and the Sanskrit scriptures cannot be brought here."
Śākyamuni closed his room in Magadha; Vimalakīrti sealed his mouth in Vaiśālī. Beyond the teachings of the Three Vehicles, there is a single phrase transmitted separately.
I venture to ask the assembly: what is this separate transmission? Try to speak for the assembly and let us verify it together. After a long silence, he said:
"Even if you could speak it, it would still not accord with the Patriarch’s intent. But tell me, how then does one accord?"
To grasp the meaning of the Patriarchs, brothers, you must directly exert your spirit and thoroughly investigate the root source.
Upon reaching this point, one cannot speak of bodhi, nirvana, suchness, or liberation; nor of moving upward or downward, entering meditative concentration, building bridges, or digging wells.
Can it be attained? Nevertheless, even so, one cannot depart without words. Thus, I, this mountain monk, when...

At first, when I set out on my travels, I had no fixed intention to practice Zen or study the Way; I simply wished to hear one or two volumes of sutras or treatises in the Eastern Capital to supplement my lifelong studies.
Unexpectedly, as I traveled further and further, I arrived at Xiangcheng County in Ruizhou.
Just then, the "Wind" of Ruizhou arose and I was summoned to Shoushan. There I met an old monk, who struck me right on the head with his staff.
He was so overcome that sweat poured down his back; without realizing it, he prostrated three times. Now, he regrets it too late. Tell me, assembly, what is there to regret?
He regrets not having dragged him down from the meditation seat and given him a severe beating. Nevertheless, this being so—
The official authority admits not even a needle; yet in private, carriages and horses pass through. To the assembly:
A monk asked Shoushan, "How is it when not a single hair has yet emerged? Shoushan said, "A traveler with pierced ears encountered on the road.
[The monk] asked, "And after it has emerged? Shoushan said, "There is no need for further hesitation. Once, a monk asked Shending: "One..."
"How is it when not even a hair has been stirred? To him I say: "On the peak of the white clouds.
"How is it after it has been stirred? To him I say: "The water flows in the mountain stream. If these were two turns of phrase from Shoushan, they would be worth chewing over; look east, look west.
If you take these words about the "divine cauldron" as something to be consumed like wooden shavings or bamboo chips, they will truly have no flavor.
Only by seeing for yourself and awakening on your own can you attain it. Do you understand? The heavens are high in the southeast; the earth slopes toward the northwest.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "The wind does not whistle through the branches; the rain does not break up clods of earth. Let us stop there for now.
How would you strike a cartwheel somersault and reach the Brahma Heaven? If there is anyone capable, come forward and show me your skill! Is there such a one? Do not let Śakra grow indignant.
Later, a monk entered the room to seek instruction. [The Master] said: "At that time, I would have come out and turned to the left."
After making one turn, he returned to the assembly. The Master said, "Do not let Śakra become angry. Furthermore, how about this? The monk said, "Those who recognize kindness are few;
those who betray it are many. The Master said, "You have struck the bridge of my nose."

He addressed the assembly, saying: "Nanquan said, 'At eighteen, I already knew how to manage my livelihood. Zhaozhou said, 'At eighteen, I already understood how to break up the family and scatter the household.
The Master asked: 'Which do you prefer—breaking up the family and scattering the household, or knowing how to manage one's livelihood?
For those at the beginning of their practice, take the former statement; for those who have long studied under the former worthies, they must indeed break up the family and scatter the household.'"
There is yet another saying: "Ten thousand li away is Yuezhou.

When the Master was traveling on pilgrimage, he was wandering the Southern Peak (Nanyue) with several senior monks. One monk was discussing the *zongcheng* (the vehicle of the school), being quite eloquent.

They happened upon a meal at a mountain inn where provisions were being prepared; while that monk continued his discourse without ceasing, the Master said: "The three realms are mind-only. Ten thousand..."
“The Dharma is consciousness-only; it is consciousness-only and mind-only. “Who said this? The monk replied, “Fayan said it.
The Master asked, “What did he say? The monk replied, “Because it is mind-only, the sense organs and their objects do not reach one another; because it is consciousness-only...”
The sounds and colors were all at once overwhelming. The Master asked, "Are the tongue and flavors not root and object? They replied, "They are.

The Master took some vegetables with his chopsticks, placed them upon his tongue, and spoke with a muffled voice, "Can this be called mutual penetration? Those seated were struck with awe and could offer no further reply.
The Master said: "Learning on the road never reaches home; insight that merely penetrates subtleties is not called seeing the Way.
One must practice with true practice and realize with true realization. King Yama does not fear much talk."
A monk asked, "What is the phrase for receiving beginners? The Master said, "Mountains, rivers, and the great earth. The monk asked, "What is the phrase for discerning a patch-robed monk?
The Master said, "Seven blows for thirteen. The monk asked, "What is the phrase for the true command being put into effect? The Master said:
He did not even blink. The monk asked, "What is the phrase that settles heaven and earth? The Master said, "How do you intend to understand it?
The monk asked, "What is it like before one has heard all dharmas? The Master said, "The wind whistles and the rain falls. The monk asked, "What is it like after one has heard them?
The Master said, "It is good to receive the words."
A monk asked, "How was it before the ancient sail had even been hoisted? The Master said, "We have already reached the shore. The monk asked, "What is it like after reaching it?
The Master said, "Still a dull-witted fellow."
Question: “How was it before you met the former masters? The Master said, “Walking east, walking west. Question: “And how was it after you met them?
The Master said, “Carrying my staff slung across my shoulder.”
Question: "When Bodhidharma has not yet arrived, what is it like? The Master said: "Western Heaven and this land. Question: "After he has arrived, what is it like?
The Master said: "This land and Western Heaven."

Question: "What is it like when the precious sword has not yet emerged from its scabbard? The Master said: "The signal fires of war have already risen. Question: "What is it like after it has emerged from the scabbard?
The Master said: "Above heaven and below heaven."
Question: "How was it before Niutou had seen the Fourth Patriarch? The Master said: "Heaven knew, and earth knew. Question:
"How was it after he had seen him? The Master said: "There was still a slight difference."
Question: "As for those who transmigrate through the six realms, what is their ultimate state? The Master said: "They do not wish to become Buddhas. Question:
"Why do they not wish to become Buddhas? The Master said: "Even Buddhahood is not ultimate. Question: "I beg the Master for a word.
The Master said: "Yesterday I still remember; today there is no gate to the talk."
Question: "What is it like when one is alone on horseback with a single spear? The Master said: "Shendeng beats the drum.
Question: "Ultimately, what is it? The Master said: "I suspect you do not have such hands and feet."
Question: "What is the pure Dharma-body? The Master said: "Ash on the head, dust on the face. Question: "Why is it like this? The Master said:
"How can you blame me, this mountain monk? Question: "I wonder, is there still something further beyond this? The Master said: "There is."
[The student] asked, "What is the matter that transcends [the phenomenal world]? The Master said, "The golden crown atop the head of Vairocana.
[The student] asked, "When one brushes away the dust and beholds the Buddha, what then? The Master said, "The Buddha is also dust."
Chan Master Shengtian of Songshan in Bingzhou (11th in the series). The Master asked Shoushan, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?
Shoushan replied, "At the foot of the city of King Chu, the Ru River flows eastward. Upon these words, the Master attained great enlightenment and composed three verses.

Chan Master Shouzhi of Dayu in Junzhou (total eleven cases). A native of the Wang family of Taiyuan, he addressed the assembly, saying:

"This mountain monk is of humble station and has never possessed virtue or conduct. Yet, having received the secret counsel of my colleagues and various officials, I have been firmly requested to ascend the hall.
This is to repay the imperial grace so that the state may enjoy eternal peace and the Wheel of Dharma may turn constantly. But tell me, how is the Wheel of Dharma turned? If you wish to know..."
Do you understand? Turning one’s body upside down atop Mount Sumeru, one then comes to sit cross-legged within the hall.
A-he-he! What is this? Sitting inside a rice basket, one yet suffers from hunger; mixing mud with water, one passes the time in such a manner. When those of superior capacity hear this, they rejoice;
when those of inferior capacity hear it, they merely nod in agreement. If you ponder it closely, however, it becomes a verbal transgression. Do you wish to understand? One.
6342. Directly stated: 471. Peach and plum flowers bloom amidst the fire; at twilight, one awaits the rising sun. He addressed the assembly, saying:
"If you seek the principle within words or clarify the mechanism within phrases, it is much like losing one's head and recognizing only its reflection.
If you attempt to proclaim the essential teaching (zongcheng), it is just like talking in one's sleep. Nevertheless, the public administration does not admit even a needle. Privately...
Allowing passage for both carriage and horse, he leaves open a single thread of the Way; yet there is a tangle of complications. Striking his meditation seat once, he says:
"All Buddhas of the three periods of time suffer from headaches. Now tell me, do any of you have a way to avoid this?
If there were one person who could avoid it, such a thing would be impossible. If you cannot avoid it, the Sea-Seal emits its light. Holding up his whisk, he says: "This!"
"This is the seal. Which one is the light? This one is the light. That one is the seal. The mechanism of a flashing lightning bolt—vainly exhausting your thoughts.
Do you understand? For now, this monk speaks of a dream. But tell me, what did he see in his dream? Ten watches in the "South Branch" (Nankuo).
If you still do not understand, listen to this verse: "The Northern Dipper hangs from Mount Sumeru; The staff-tip carries the sun and moon. How beautiful are the forests and springs!"
Deliberation. At the end of summer, the autumn wind cuts sharp.
Addressing the assembly, he struck his whisk and said: "A single strike rings out clear and resonant; its thunderous roar penetrates the universe.
As soon as a true knower leans their ear, it is like Xiang Yu crossing the river eastward. If you understand it thus, you have merely recognized the bridge of a donkey’s saddle as your father’s chin.
He nodded and addressed the assembly, saying: "When Deshan entered the gate, he would strike with his staff; when Linji entered the gate, he would shout.

If one staff-strike and one shout were to emerge alternately from Shuangfeng, guest and host would remain undistinguished, and one would wander anxiously ten thousand miles from home. Only when illumination and function proceed together [is there true mastery]."
When one attempts to deliberate upon it, a thousand differences block the way. Venerable Elders, having arrived here, on what basis can you speak of its meaning?

Thus there is a verse: "Whipping and shouting applied together—already too late. Throughout antiquity and today, praise is ceased; it is utterly beyond description. Not involving either of the two paths, on what could one rely to speak?
A Persian from the South Sea presents an elephant tusk."
He addressed the assembly, saying: "There is no oil in sand—truly pitiable! Cuiyan is chewing up his own food to feed an infant.
When you eventually come to know the ultimate reality of good and evil, you will realize that all your previous efforts have been nothing but ashes covering your face."
He addressed the assembly, saying: "Vimalakīrti’s silence has already entailed prolixity; Bodhidharma’s coming from the West flatly deceives the land of Han.
Let me open a single thread of the Way, for there is something to deliberate upon. Thus, Master Li said: 'The root of sentient beings relies on the ocean of wisdom as its source;
the stream of conscious beings takes the Dharma-body as their substance. O worthy ones, since it is the totality of the Dharma..."
Taking this physical body as one’s substance, one must still realize the Way. Does Mount Sumeru swallow up the Dharma-body, or does the Dharma-body swallow up Mount Sumeru?
O worthy ones, morning and evening you have been studying together with the Buddhas of antiquity; you have been studying together with the old masters of all quarters;
and today, I, this mountain monk, am studying together with the great assembly. But tell me, what is it that you are studying? If you can resolve this with certainty, then recognize it.
Even if you have attained the state of one who wears robes and eats rice, you are still half a month’s journey away from the level of a true monk.
If you cannot settle this with certainty, there will be new rules for you next year; the winds of vexation shall not cease until the end of spring.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "Dagui received the Great Hero’s grandson; the cloud-and-water travelers of the Five Lakes compete to rush toward him.
They compete to rush toward him—what gate is there? Striking the arrow, how could one know that withered wood remains? Withered wood remains—once a year, spring comes twice."
Twice in spring, pearls were scattered from within the curtains for others to take. Scattered for others to take—considering it, one still yearns for the Western Qin.
A monk asked, "What is the master’s house style? The Master said, "Once a word has been uttered, even four horses cannot overtake it.
He asked, "What is the Buddha in the city? The Master said, "The stone pillar at the crossroads."
Question: "What is the Master’s one phrase for benefiting people? The Master said: "Four corners, six sides. Question:
"What is the meaning of this? The Master said: "Eight concavities, nine convexities."
Question: "When one does not fall into the 'three inches,' how is it? The Master said: "Three segments of Qian, six sections of Kun.
Question: "What is the meaning of this? The Master said: "One must strictly avoid excess or deficiency."
Question: “What is the Way? The Master said: “Eight pecks and four bushels. Question: “What is one who is on the Way? The Master said:
“Cooking porridge and boiling rice.”

Question: "What is it like before the precious sword has been drawn from its scabbard? The Master said, "By all means, do not speak of it. Question: "What is it like after it has been drawn from the scabbard?
The Master said, "The celestial Māras' courage fails them."
Chan Master Huìjué of Lángyá in Chūzhōu (Seventeenth Case) addressed the assembly, saying: "The harmony between ruler and subject is still a matter on the level of the Dharmakāya.
Not seeing the ruler and not seeing the subject is still a matter beyond the Dharmakāya.
These 'beyond' and 'below' cause your minds to be unsettled; so, what is the Dharmakāya? After a long silence, he said: "Even if it were a monk..."
"By hand. It is difficult to exhaustively describe Master Zhi’s true nature.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "The Samādhi of the World-Honored One was not known by Kāśyapa; the Samādhi of Kāśyapa was not known by Ānanda;
the Samādhi of Ānanda was not known by Śāṇakavāsin; and as for my own Samādhi, you do not know it either. Why is this so?"
"I do not know. It is only natural that it should be so. If one can understand this, then north, south, east, and west are all accounted for; if it were otherwise, where else would one go?
He addressed the assembly, saying: "Those who come in such a manner shall be accommodated in the upper quarters; those who do not come in such a manner shall be registered in the lower quarters."
When one who has transcended comes, he crosses the river alone in silent sorrow. Yet there is yet another person—where shall they be placed?
After a long silence, he said: "The fishing pole is worn out, so I plant bamboo anew; regardless of the time or effort, I rest when I find my ease."

He addressed the assembly, saying: "The phrase that exists and the phrase that does not exist are like a vine leaning against a tree. When the tree falls, the vine withers. At such a moment, one deserves a blow of the staff.
But tell me, where does the fault lie? After a long silence, he said: "If it were not for the hand of Monk You, one would merely be speaking of painting in colors."

Addressing the assembly, he raised the words of the World-Honored One: "Sentient beings delusively take the four elements to be their own physical form, and the shadows of conditions from the six sense-objects to be their own mental consciousness.

Now, I ask you, noble friends: that which sees when it is in the eye, hears when it is in the ear, smells fragrance when it is in the nose, knows flavor when it is in the tongue, grasps and seizes when it is in the hands, and runs and moves when it is in the feet—is this not called a sentient being? Nor...
"It is not called Buddha-nature. But tell me, what do you call it? After a long silence, he said: "Xiangyan holds his staff while weeping with grief;

Addressing the assembly, he said: "I, this mountain monk, while reading the *Huayan Jinsiierzhang* (The Golden Lion Chapter of the Avatamsaka), came across the ninth section, 'The Door of Skillful Accomplishment through the Turning of Mind.

If this is so, then one may say it exists; one may say it does not exist; one may say it is neither; and one may say it is both. Although it is thus, furthermore—"
You must know that there is a single aperture at the head of this staff. If you do not understand it, the staff will pass through the lantern and enter the Buddha hall;
it will strike Śākyamuni and knock down Maitreya, while the pillar claps its hands and laughs out loud. "Tell me," he says, "what is it they laugh at?
He strikes the ground once with the staff.

A blow! But how will you deliberate upon this? If you can distinguish the black from the white, there is no harm in your eyes opening at the tip of the staff to illuminate the four quarters of the world.

Addressing the assembly, he raised his staff and said: "If the staff is [the truth], it is to add a head upon a head;

If you do not understand, the staff has already passed through the Bohai Sea. Look! [The Master] strikes the ground once and addresses the assembly, saying:
"The Buddhas of the past have already entered parinirvāṇa—well-deserved are thirty blows for them. As for the Buddhas of the present..."

Venerable elders, if you wish to repay the profound kindness of the Buddha, you must train yourselves in this way. As for training, it depends on you all;
do not bring shame upon this old monk."

He addressed the assembly, saying: "If you can realize it within the phrase, the wandering child returns to his native village. If you can realize it within the meaning, only then will you understand how to serve your honored mother.
If this is so, you must know that you must turn your body and breathe freely before you have attained it.

If you can do so, only then will you understand how to advance further from the top of a hundred-foot pole. When there is no meaning within the phrase and no phrase within the meaning—since this is the case, for now, act thus."
"How can one exhale this? If you do not understand, let this staff exhale it for you. [He strikes once. He addresses the assembly, saying:
"Host and guest alternate; they cut off heaven and earth. The dual application of discernment—whom will they look upon?
The Holy Lord Śākyamuni entered parinirvāṇa at the Twin Śāla Trees; Master Bodhidharma truly returned to Mount Xiong’er. Under the gate of Langya, does anyone still..."
Are there any monks with the true eye, any who belong to the lineage of the genuine Way? If there are none, I shall administer medicine according to the ailment, diagnosing as the occasion requires.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "All of you who are passing the summer retreat here with me—I shall point out five kinds of illness for you."

First, you must not go to a place ten thousand *li* away where there is not even an inch of grass. Second, you must not dwell alone on a solitary peak. Third, you must not draw a bow and set an arrow.
Fourth, you must not seek refuge outside of all things. Fifth, you must not stagnate in the realms of birth and death. Why is this?
If one is obstructed in even a single place, it is difficult to save oneself; if one is unimpeded in these five places, only then can one be called a true Guide. You all—
If you travel to various regions and encounter a master with clear vision, convey this message to me, so that the ancestral wind may not fall into ruin.
As for ordinary practitioners, they must simply cease their efforts. Why? To boast about one's finery within the land of the naked—surely you are far too ignorant of the times.
The Master ascended the hall. A monk came forward and drew a perfect circle. The Master struck him and said, "Speak! Speak! The monk said, "I do not speak;

who knows how he established the teaching according to the occasion? The Master said, "There is not a single inch of earth to be found; there is no kindness from the previous night that has not been requited."

The stone ox roars within the water; the auspicious flower’s fragrance is within the wood. The monk said, "If that is so, how could one have seen the southern star without observing the northern dipper?
