The Master said, "This old man says it is indeed the local fruit of your region; you may eat it together. Fasu replied, "Since the passing of my former teacher, I have not been able to obtain this food for a long time.
The Master asked, "Who was your former teacher? Fasu replied, "Ciming. I have had the honor of serving him for thirteen years.
The Master then said with astonishment, "Thirteen years! To endure the toil of such service—this is no small achievement."
"What is this path? he asked. The Master then offered him some leftover fruit and gradually grew more intimate with him.
Su Wen asked the Master, "Who was it you saw? The Master replied, "Dongshan Wenyi. Su Wen asked, "Whom did Wenyi see? The Master replied, "Huanglong Nan.

Su Wen remarked, "Nan the Junior had seen our late teacher for only a short time, yet later his Dharma path flourished to such an extent. The Master became even more perplexed and struck with awe; he then tucked incense in his sleeve.
He went to Huisou and paid his respects. Huisou rose to avoid him, saying, "I am of meager merit; my late master received a prediction that I would not be permitted to take on disciples.
The Master [Daoyi] was even more reverent. Huisou then said, "Out of pity for your sincerity, I shall violate my late master’s prediction.
Tell me what you have attained throughout your life. The Master fully explained his insights. Huisou said, "It is acceptable. You can enter the Buddha, but you cannot enter the Dharma."
"Also Māra," the Master said. Su asked, "What do you mean? The Master replied, "Have you not seen what the ancients said: 'The final phrase is where one first arrives at the secure barrier'?

For several months, Su pondered this until he finally attained realization. The Master then granted him approval, yet cautioned him, saying: "The texts shown to you all contain correct knowledge and vision;
however, you have departed from the texts too soon and were unable to exhaust their subtle wonders. I shall now, for your sake, break through these points for you."
"Let my son enjoy this and attain great mastery; on another day, do not by any means succeed me. Later, the Master succeeded Zhenjing and addressed the assembly, saying:
"The peach blossoms on the stream are in full, riotous spring; leaning on my staff, I look idly at them and laugh at Lingyun.

The sprouting of branches and leaves is but an ordinary matter; to have awakening and yet be without doubt is also a forced distinction. O practitioners of Zen, since you have raised the doubt regarding this forced distinction between awakening and non-awakening:
What profound principle could possibly be fixed? It is simply that when ordinary sentiments are completely purified, sagely understanding is naturally forgotten.
When this is so, what "right" or "wrong" can there be? What "gain" or "loss" can there be discussed? What "movement" or "stillness" can there be grasped?
Why divide this from that? Upon reaching this point, the wondrous essence becomes void and luminous; its wondrous function, whether horizontal or vertical, is entirely free of discrimination.
Good and evil are practiced together—does anyone dare to take this up? If you can take it up, I shall give you my staff from Tuṣita Heaven, and you may travel freely across the world.

He addressed the assembly, saying: "All you practitioners of Chan: Vimalakīrti, having taken on the illness of the multitude, drew forth Mañjuśrī to lead his followers here.

Sometimes he rolls back his eyes; how many eyebrows stand upright? He let out a shout.

birth and death, as well as nirvana, are like springtime dreams. These are merely the provisional arrangements of the teaching hall."
Deceiving children—this is the opening of the gate of skillful means. These knotted patterns and interlocking corners are all mere illusions before the eyes of a patch-robed monk.

A single phrase cuts off all deliberation; all phenomena do not reach one another. He addressed the assembly, saying:
"Great wisdom appears as if ignorant; great skill seems as if clumsy. Do not think it is merely this morning; it is the Mid-Autumn festival. Throughout the eight directions the wind is the same;
across a thousand ponds the moon is one. Thirty years hence, the reeds will reflect the snow. To awaken in this way—to realize it thus—is to [shatter] the skull."

The gate splits into a hundred pieces. He addresses the assembly, saying: "By the hedge, the chrysanthemums are in full yellow bloom; the wondrous discourse on the meaning of the Western Patriarch resounds clearly.

Pervading all, they manifest as Mañjuśrī, Samantabhadra, Avalokiteśvara, and Mahāsthāmaprāpta, piercing through the skulls of all people.

If you can fully know their place of origin, you may be said to be making offerings to Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges within each inhalation and exhalation; if you do not know it, [you remain deluded].
He entrusted [the Dharma] to Deshan and Linji. Brandishing his whisk and striking once, he addressed the assembly, saying:
"The Buddhas did not appear in the world; Bodhidharma did not come from the West. The Patriarchs' Mind-Seal is like the mechanism of an iron ox; thus it seals the sky.
When the sun and moon sink their radiance and heaven and earth grow dark, it seals the water. He then drew a wrinkle [on the whisk].
Turbulent waves and surging billows; fish and dragons lose their lives. It is like pressing a seal into mud. When the great earth’s ice melts away, the path for the holy and the common is cut off.
If it were that one seal, who would dare look upon it with a direct eye? Yet, alas, everywhere people imitate its form and paint its likeness.
If you come before the gate of the Arhat, I shall reduce it to powder and shatter it completely.
Chan Master Yongcheng of Nanfeng in Quanzhou (Fanyi) addressed the assembly, saying:

"Beginning with the transmission of the flame from Mount Jiji and the spreading of fragrance from Shaoshi, the clouds of compassion were widely spread and the sun of wisdom was grandly opened. The teachings were divided into the Three Pitakas, yet they point directly to the One Mind.

Sometimes it is like a lion’s somersault; sometimes it is like a flash of light or a thunderclap; sometimes it is like a lightning bolt striking with a sharp pivot.

All of these are nothing other than the cutting away of delusions and falsehoods, the opening up of the profound and subtle, and the direct clarification of the fundamental principle to reach the ground of reality. You worthy ones, only when you have reached this point may I allow a single thread of the Way to be discussed with you.
If you have not yet attained this, you are entirely relying on your teachers to form intellectual interpretations; there is no such thing as [true realization].

Chan Master Guangjian Ying of Kaixian, in Luzhou, successor to Chan Master Changzong of Donglin in Jiangzhou (the third in his lineage). He was a native of the Mao clan from Yongfu in Guizhou. He addressed the assembly:

He said: "To discuss the profound and expound the subtle is like trying to satisfy hunger with painted cakes; to enter the state of sainthood and transcend the mundane is much like a moth flying into a flame.

"All those views and understandings from just now have been swept away. What is it that you all must penetrate?"
He left off one phrase. After a long silence, he said: "The iron ox does not eat the grass by the fence; it goes straight to sleep atop the summit of Mount Sumeru.
With his whisk, he struck the meditation seat.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "There is one person who can speak ten feet, yet cannot walk even an inch.
There is another who can walk ten feet, yet cannot speak even an inch. There is another who can both speak and walk. And there is another who can neither speak nor walk.
Among these four people, if you wish to find one to serve as your teacher, you discerning monks, try it out!"
"Please examine this.

A monk asked, "What is the Way? The Master said, "Ten thousand acres of fertile fields. The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "If you do not plow in spring, there will be nothing to hope for in autumn."

Chan Master Nantai Yungong of Mount Heng, successor to Chan Master Dabui Huaxiu of Tanzhou (Case 1), addressed the assembly, saying: "Rarely encountered and difficult to meet—this is precisely that time.
Why say Śākyamuni has already passed away and Maitreya is not yet born? He held up his whisk and said, "Right now, this very day."
The Buddha-dharma is entirely upon the tip of this mountain monk’s whisk. To let go or to hold fast is entirely a matter of the moment. If one lets go, the wind blows and the grass bows;
even tiles and pebbles give off light, and Shi-de and Han-shan nod their heads and clap their hands. If one holds fast, there is no leakage of water;
even true gold loses its luster, and De-shan and Lin-ji swallow their breath and silence their voices. At such a time as this—
"Letting go is it; holding fast is it. After a long silence, he said, "Look again in five days.
Chan Master Wuzu Fayan of Wuzhou was a successor of Chan Master Baizhang Shouduan of Shuzhou (thirteen in total). He was a native of Shu. Initially, he went to visit Chan Master Yuanzhao Ben.

He composed a verse of spontaneous inspiration (*tōki*) which said: "A plot of vacant land before the mountain; With palms joined, I earnestly questioned the patriarch.
How many times have I sold it only to buy it back? Out of affection for the pines and bamboos, it draws in the pure breeze. Duan nodded his head in approval.
Addressing the assembly, [the Master] raised the case of Deshan’s informal teaching (xiaocan), which says: "Tonight I will not answer questions; anyone who asks a question shall receive thirty blows.
Many among the assembly have cited this, and few have failed to understand it. But tell me, where do you see Deshan?
If there is anyone here who disregards their very life, please come forward and speak. If there is none, I, this mountain monk, shall act on behalf of the great assembly for the sake of Old Deshan.
People meet and part. Wait for Deshan to say, "Tonight I will not answer questions; those who ask questions shall receive thirty blows," and simply tell him:
"I will ask no question, nor shall I take a blow. Do you think this accords with that old man Deshan?
To reach this point, one must be a true man. I have been traveling as a wandering monk for over ten years.
For many years he traveled across the seas in search of the Way, meeting several venerable masters whom he considered to have attained realization.

Yet, upon arriving at the assembly of Fushan, he found himself utterly unable to speak. Later, under the guidance of Baoyun, he bit into a single "iron sour jujube," whereby all flavors were made complete.
Now tell me: how would you express this one phrase regarding the jujube? He then said: "The flower blooms on the rooster."
The cap adorns the early autumn. Who can dye its purple silk tip? Sometimes stirred by the wind, it leans against itself repeatedly, as if competing incessantly before the steps.
To the assembly: I cite the Patriarch’s words:

The leaves fall; the fruit ripens naturally. Great Master Bodhidharma came with his feet and spoke with his mouth. Yet the descendants of later generations have mostly fallen into calculating schemes.
Do you wish to understand the place where the flowers bloom and the fruit ripens? Pear trees in Zhengzhou, jujubes in Qingzhou—among all things, nothing surpasses a good source.
Addressing the assembly, [Miaoyan] cited an ancient saying: "If I were to speak for you, my tongue would fall out;
if I were not to speak for you, my mouth would be mute. Tell me, is there still a way to benefit others?
Sometimes Si-mian intended to swallow you whole, but he was obstructed by his own front teeth; he intended to spit you out, but again he was blocked by his throat.
"Small. Now tell me, is there still a way for him to benefit others? He then said: "On all four sides, he has always been Liu Xiaohui. Addressing the assembly, he said:
"True Suchness, ordinary beings, and sages—all are but dream-like words. Buddhas and sentient beings are both merely added designations.
Suddenly, if someone were to come forward and say, "What about Old Pan-shan? you should simply say to them: "Were it not for the early blossoming of flowers along the purple roads..."
"Who can catch the yellow oriole as it descends the willow branches? If you further say, "What about Old Laozi on all four sides? he himself replies, "Yes. Be alert! Addressing the assembly, he said:
"If you go on perpetually like this, the Way is cut off and the path lies desolate. If you come back perpetually like this, you betray the former sages.
Depart from these two paths, and even Buddhas and Patriarchs cannot approach you. Even if you were to share life and death with Baiyun, it would still be so."
This does not yet match his lifelong practice. Why? A phoenix is no ordinary bird; it vows never to perch unless it finds the wutong tree.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "The Buddhas of the ten directions, the six generations of patriarchs, and all the good spiritual friends of the world—all share this very same tongue.
If you can recognize this tongue, only then will you understand the 'great empty talk. Then one may say: 'Mountains, rivers, and the great earth...'"
"This is Buddha. Grasses, trees, thickets, and forests are Buddha. If you do not yet recognize this tongue, you will merely achieve a small deception and delude yourself;
there is much more to come tomorrow and the day after. When Taiping spoke these words, was there anything substantial in them?
He himself said, "There is. "What is the substantial point? "Return to the hall and drink tea."
Addressing the assembly, he said: "Yesterday, I entered the city and saw a stage of puppet plays. Unable to resist, I went forward to watch.
I saw some figures that were dignified and extraordinary, while others were ugly and repulsive. They moved, walked, sat, and rose; they were green, yellow, red, and white—I saw every detail.
Yet when I looked closely, I realized that there was actually a person behind the blue cloth curtain. [The Master] could not contain his amusement.
Jin then asked, "What is the surname of the High Official? The other replied, "Old Monk, let it be; why ask what his surname is?
"O assembly, because of that single phrase from him, I was left with no words to respond and no logic to defend myself.
Is there anyone who can speak for me? Yesterday I fell at that point; today here I pull up the roots."
He addressed the assembly, saying: "White Cloud does not know how to speak of Chan. The three gates stand open on both sides;
if someone moves the pivot, the two panels swing one to the east and one to the west."
He addressed the assembly, saying: "The Buddhas and Patriarchs give birth to enemies; awakening to the Way is being stained by the mud.

"Whether it be 'thus' or 'not thus,' neither is permitted. Suddenly, if there is a man who comes forward and says, "It is permissible to be 'thus,' and it is also permissible to be 'not thus';

"I know that you are making your living inside a ghost cave."
[The Master] addressed the assembly, citing the Venerable Deshan. Once, a monk asked him: "How do the sages of all generations instruct people? Deshan replied:
"In my school, there are no words or phrases, nor is there a single dharma given to anyone.

At that time, he went empty-handed and returned empty-handed. Today, Baiyun speaks to those who have not yet penetrated this:
there was a man coming from Dongjing who, when asked where he had come from, replied, "From Suzhou.
When asked how things were in Suzhou, he said, "Everything is as usual. Although it is so, he could not deceive Baiyun. Why? Because—
It is simply because their voices and expressions differ. Ultimately, how is it so? "Water chestnuts from Suzhou; lotus roots from Shaobu. He addressed the assembly, saying:
"To speak of the Buddha or the Dharma, to wield the mallet or raise the whisk—ten thousand miles of white clouds. When Deshan enters the gate, he strikes with his staff;
when Linji enters the gate, he shouts. Ten thousand miles of white clouds. Yet even after that, doing so is not permitted, nor is not doing so."
Not so is not permitted; neither "so" nor "not so" is permitted. Even so, it is ten thousand miles of white clouds.

He addressed the assembly, saying: "All of you, when you see this old monk moving his lips and raising his whisk, you immediately form a conceptual understanding.

The Master addressed the assembly, saying: "Dai-fu Lu Xuan once asked Nanquan, 'In my home, there is a piece of stone that I have used for sitting and lying upon.
Now I intend to cast it as a Buddha; would this be permissible? Nanquan said, 'It would. Lu Xuan said, 'Would it not be impermissible? Nanquan said, 'It would not. The Master said:
'One who acts as a good spiritual friend must possess clear discernment. Why is this? Because he [Nanquan]..."
"One can say it; one can say it. Others cannot say it; they also cannot say it. Do you know where Nanquan has landed?
Baiyun, not sparing his own eyebrows, shall explain this through for you. Who was it that said 'can'? And who was it that said 'cannot'?
If you still do not understand, I, the old monk, shall today provide you with a model."
He then raised his hand and said: "Take the three realms and twenty-eight heavens to make the head of a Buddha;
take the golden wheel and the waters' edge to make the feet of a Buddha; take the four great continents to make the body of a Buddha.
Even so, once you have become sons of this Buddha, where will you all establish yourselves and find your livelihood? Has the assembly understood yet? I, this old monk, shall act as the..."
Two models have gone forth: take Pūrvavideha and make it a Buddha; take Jambudvīpa and make it a Buddha; take Aparagoyānī and make it a Buddha;
take Uttarakuru and make it a Buddha. Grass is not a forest—it is Buddha;
all wriggling, moving sentient beings are Buddha. Since this is so, what then do you call "sentient beings"? Do you understand?
No. It is not like Pūrvavideha; it returns to Pūrvavideha. It is not like Jambudvīpa; it returns to Jambudvīpa.
It is not like Aparagoyānī; it returns to Aparagoyānī. It is not like Uttarakuru; it returns to Uttarakuru.
It is not like grasses, trees, and forests; it returns to grasses, trees, and forests. It is not like wriggling and moving sentient beings; it returns to wriggling and moving sentient beings.
It moves all sentient beings; thus it is said: "This Dharma abides in its own place; the characteristics of the world are eternally constant.
Since this is so, what then do you call a Buddha? Suddenly, if there is someone who comes forward and says, "White Cloud, stop your drowsy talk," everyone should take note of this turn of phrase.
Question: "How was it before Niutou had seen the Fourth Patriarch? The Master said, "A heavy burden hanging from his head. Question: "How was it after he saw him?

"The sound of song follows the flow of the water.

[The monk asked about] the "lower matter. The Master said, "A red banner flashes. [The monk asked], "What is the lower matter of the Miu-yang school? The Master said, "A broken stele lies across the ancient road.

Chan Master Zhiben of Yungai in Tanzhou (fourth in the lineage), a native of the Guo family of Junzhou, held up his staff and addressed the assembly, saying:

Chan Master Fǎng of Heshan in Jízhōu, Dharma heir of Chan Master Wùxīn of Huánglóng in Hóngzhōu, the fifteenth generation under Nányuè (in total two records).

First illumination, then function; no trace remains. Illumination and function are simultaneous; standing like a cliff ten thousand fathoms high.

A single aperture. If you follow the waves and drift with the current, carrying water and dragging mud, you will辜负 (betray) your own spirit and fail to possess the true eye at the crown of the head.

He addressed the assembly, saying: "Before Bodhidharma had yet come to this eastern land, everyone harbored the pearl from the Mimi River, and every individual possessed the raw jade of Mount Jing.

Yet, once the Second Patriarch had completed his three prostrations, each one went south to seek out friends and north to pay homage to Mañjuśrī—how unmanly! Perhaps there might be one or two..."
This person seeks nothing from the holy ones and values not their own spiritual brilliance. With a single horse and a solitary spear, they cast their blade into the void;

thus, they may enjoy a lifetime of unimpeded joy. Is there anyone like this today? "Since one has not yet returned, upon returning it can be attained; who would strive for the misty realms of the Five Lakes?"

He conceals his traces. Otherwise, having let this one move pass, there is spring according to one's lot: "A branch with three or four flowers. He addresses the assembly, saying:

"You are wasting your breath, monk; it would be better for you to simply stop and rest. After a long silence, he said: "When the Way prevails, the Emperor’s edicts need not be proclaimed;

Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "For the family of patch-robed monks, the four requisites follow the body and the three mysteries clothe the person. When meeting the critical moment, they do not err, like a pearl rolling upon a platter.

This requires the sword that kills and the sword that gives life. Under the sword that gives life, the dead lie scattered in all directions; at the tip of the sword that kills, the living are beyond counting. Killing and giving life are mastered with ease;

When the school is clarified and the meaning is pointed out, how then would you do it? It is well said: "One should carefully re-embroider the mandarin ducks; let others compete to find the golden needle."

The Chan Master Chongyue of Doushuai in Hongzhou was the dharma heir of the Chancellor, Layman Wujin Zhang Shangying (three parts). When the Master was nineteen years old, he entered the capital to take the imperial examinations.

On his way, he passed through the home of the Xiang family. The Xiangs had previously dreamed that someone informed them, "Tomorrow you shall receive the Chancellor. At dawn the next morning, the Master arrived.
He inquired after him with detailed courtesy. Later, he gave his daughter in marriage to him. Consequently, he entered a Buddhist monastery and saw the Tripitaka;

the Sanskrit manuscripts were so perfectly arranged that he sighed in indignation and said, "The teachings of our Sage Confucius are not equal to the books of these barbarians, which are thus revered by all.

Sitting in his study at night, he ground ink, took up his brush, and composed long verses upon paper. His wife, Lady Xiang, called out to him, saying, "It is late at night, sir; why do you not [rest]?"
He fell asleep. The Duke spoke to him regarding his previous intention. [The monk] was precisely at that moment composing a "Treatise on the Non-existence of the Buddha.
The Duke said, "Since there is no Buddha, what treatise could there be? You must compose a 'Treatise on the Existence of the Buddha' before it will do.
The Duke, doubting these words, then desisted. Later, he visited a colleague and saw a scripture before a Buddha niche. He asked, "What book is this? His colleague replied, "The *Vimalakīrti*..."

This is a sutra spoken by Māmakīrti (Mojie). Gaoxin opened the scroll with his own hand and, upon reading to this passage on "this illness," [noted that] it is neither the earth-element nor separate from the location of the earth-element.
He sighed, saying, "Can the language of the Hu people also be like this? He then asked how many fascicles this sutra contained.
It was said to be in three fascicles. He borrowed it and returned it after reading it entirely. When Xiang asked him what book he had been reading, the Master replied, "The Vimalakīrtinirdeśa Sūtra.
Xiang said, "You should read this sūtra thoroughly before you compose your 'Treatise on the Non-existence of the Buddha' (Wufo lun). The Master was struck by these words;

from then on, he placed deep faith in the Buddha Vehicle and devoted himself to the Way of the Patriarchs. Later, while serving as the Grain Commissioner of Jiangxi, he traveled extensively to visit the seats of the patriarchs.
He visited Donglin Zong again, who interrogated him regarding his insights; finding them to be in perfect accord with his own, Zong granted him formal approval (*kanna*).

Later, when he was assigned to the province of Ning, various Chan masters came to welcome him. Doushuai was at the end of the procession. After the Master had paid his respects to each one in turn, it was Doushuai’s turn.
Hearing that the Master’s intelligence surpassed that of others, Doushuai asked, "I have heard that you are skilled in literary composition—is this true? The Master laughed heartily.
[Chang] Yun said, "Administrator, you have lost one of your eyes. Congyue was a ninth-generation descendant of Linji;

when he discussed literature with the Administrator, it was exactly as the Administrator [discussed it]. When the Administrator discussed Chan with Congyue, the Administrator’s mind was not at ease, so he asked, "How many li is it from here to Yuxi?
Congyue said, "Thirty li. The Administrator said, "As for Doushuai? Congyue said, "Five li. That night they stayed overnight at Doushuai. Congyue—
The night before, he had a dream in which the sun was rising in the sky; Yue seized it with his hand. He then said to the Head Seat:

"The 'Discourse on the Sun' (Rilun) signifies the meaning of movement and revolution. I have heard that Commissioner Zhang will arrive here before long. I shall prick him deeply and strike him painfully;
if he is willing to turn his head, it will be a fortunate event for our school. Gong and Yue conversed until late at night, and their discussion turned to the Gate of the Patriarchs (Zongmen).

Shishi asked, "I have heard that you, Official Yin, have received the seal of approval from Donglin. I wonder, does the Official have even the slightest doubt regarding the words and teachings of the Buddhas and Patriarchs?
The Official replied, "I do. Shishi asked, "What kind of words do you doubt? The Official said, "The 'One-legged Verse' of Xiangyan and the story of Deshan with the almsbowl.
Shishi said, "If you have doubts about these, how could you possibly have no doubts about the rest? Take, for instance, Yantou..."
Yun asked, "As for the 'final phrase,' does it exist or not? Yun said, "It exists. Yue laughed heartily and returned to his quarters, closing the door behind him.
Yun could not sleep peacefully; at the fifth watch, he got out of bed and accidentally overturned the footstool.

Suddenly, he attained awakening and composed a verse: "The drum falls silent and the bell has ceased; returning with the alms bowl, Yantou’s single thrust was like a clap of thunder. Indeed, I have only just..."

He lived for three years. [The Master] wondered, "Could it be that he has received a prediction from him? He then knocked on the door of the abbot’s quarters and said, "I have already caught the thief.
Yunju asked, "Where are the stolen goods? The official was speechless. Yunju said, "Go for now; we shall meet again tomorrow."

The Duke presented the previous verse to Yue the following day. Yue said, "The reason one studies Chan is precisely because the life-root has not been severed and one gives rise to interpretations based on words.

You, my lord, have already deeply realized this; however, at the most subtle and minute level, there is a place that causes people to fall into a conceptual realm without even realizing or knowing it.
Later, he composed a verse to seal [the Duke's understanding], saying: "In the midst of ordinary conduct, every step is as it should be."
Though dwelling amidst sound and form, how could one remain stuck in existence or non-existence? With a single mind there is no difference; the myriad dharmas are not distinct.

Cease distinguishing between essence and function; do not select between the refined and the coarse. Unimpeded when facing the opportune moment, responding to things without constraint. When sentiments of right and wrong are exhausted, both ordinary and sage are eliminated.
Who gains and who loses? What is near and what is distant? To take the head for the tail and point to reality as empty;
to turn one’s back on the realm of demons and set foot upon the path of deviance—this is neither contrary nor compliant, and it does not violate the essential practice.
Furong Daokai went to visit Master Gong to request a stele inscription for Master Zantang.

As soon as they met, Gong asked, "Why have you come such a long distance on foot, wearing these straw sandals? Daokai replied, "I have come specifically from thousands of miles away to see you, Master.
Gong then asked, "How old are you? Daokai said, "Twenty-eight. Gong said, "And how old is the water buffalo? Daokai said, "Two. Gong said, "..."
"Where did you learn this pretense? Gao said, "Today I have met you, sir, in person. The official said, "Since you have come from afar, sit and drink some tea.
After the tea was finished, the official asked, "You have come from far away; what business do you have?
Gao stepped forward and said, "The Master of Lestam has passed away. During his cremation, his eyes, teeth, and prayer beads remained unburnt, and there were many śarīras."
The senior monks of the mountain all wished for the Great Calligrapher’s hand to compose an inscription for the stupa, so as to inspire future students;
thus they had come from afar to trouble your esteemed hearing. The Official said, "I have a question now. If you can answer it, I shall write the stupa inscription.
He then asked, "I have heard that Old Zhun’s eyesight is not impaired—is this true? Gao replied, "It is true. The Official said, "That is not what I am asking."
"This eye. Gao said, "What kind of eye does the Excellency ask about? The Excellency said, "The Vajra-eye.
Gao said, "If it is the Vajra-eye, it is upon the Excellency's pen. The Excellency said, "In that case, I, this old man..."
He illuminated the way for others, enabling them to shine upon both heaven and earth.
Gaoyao bowed in thanks, saying, "It is my great good fortune that the Minister has composed this stele inscription for my late master. The Minister merely nodded and smiled.
The Duke said to Furi: "I have been reading Xuedou’s *Niangu* (Verses on Ancient Cases). Upon reaching the karmic account of Baizhang’s second visit to Mazu, he says:
'In a great smelting furnace, refined gold shall not change its color. As I rolled up the scroll, I sighed and said:
'If this is truly so, how could there be a Linji today? I then composed a verse, which says: 'Mazu’s single shout at Daxiong Peak / Penetrates deep into the skull.'"
He was deaf for three days. Upon hearing this, Huangbo was so startled that he stuck out his tongue. From that time on, the school of the Jiangxi region established its own patriarchal style.
Later, Chan Master Ping sent a letter saying: "Last summer, while reading the lineage of the Linji school, I realized that you, Layman, have attained great capacity and great function."
Furthermore, I sought out the original verse and composed one myself to send it to him, saying: "The Master who sticks out his tongue and deafens our ears has already babbled;
Beating one's breast, one can do no more than cry out to the blue heavens. In the assembly at Panshan, he performs somersaults; Only upon reaching this point does one realize the madness of Puhua.
In various quarters, people often regard me as clever and widely learned, yet few truly know me. Since you have come from the Dharma-cave of Jiangxi, you must surely [know better].
"Distinguishing between superior and inferior—let me speak for this old man. Foyi said, 'The perspective of the Layman (Fayan) accords with that of Zhenjing and Sijian.
The Master asked, 'What do you mean? Foyi then cited a verse by Zhenjing: 'Guest sentiments turn with every step one takes;

Great majestic light cannot manifest. Suddenly, a shout deafens both ears; Narayaṇa’s eyes [are opened].'"* *Narayaṇa’s eyes refers to the mythological figure Nārāyaṇa tearing open his own eyes to see.*
[Zhaozhou] opened Huangbo’s face. Sijian Shixin took up the case, saying: "Yunyan wanted to question Xuedou:

'Since you are refined gold from a great furnace, you should have no change of color; why then were your ears deaf for three days? Do you all wish to know? 'No one has recognized the sweating horses of the past;
it is only to re-examine the merit that covers the age. Gufu Fanchan said: "Were it not for your words, how could I see [this]?"
Regarding the application of the True Purity of Shisi (Shixin): were it not for these two great elders, it would have been difficult to manifest the legacy of Xuedou and Mazu.
Chan Master Chengdu Fu Zhaojue Keqin (eight fascicles), a native of Shu, was a Dharma heir of Chan Master Wuzu Fayuan of Qizhou. After leaving the Gorges, he first visited Beiwu.
Chan Master Yafang attained the essence of the straightforward and practical teachings of Zhaojue. He subsequently visited Daopei Zhe and later entered the room of Wuzu Fayan.
Throughout his life, he made no use whatsoever of intellectual understanding; instead, he remarked, "The Patriarch merely deceives people," and spoke disparagingly of him.
He departed in a fit of indignation. The Patriarch said, "I will wait until you catch a severe fever; only when you are struck by it will you finally reflect upon me.
The Master arrived at Jinshan and contracted a case of shanhan (a cold), nearly succumbing to it. He then tested his usual insights and perspectives, but none proved effective.
Recalling the words of the Fifth Patriarch, he made a vow to himself: "As soon as my illness subsides, I shall return to the Fifth Patriarch."

He soon returned to the Fifth Patriarch. Upon seeing him, the Patriarch was delighted and said, "Have you come? That very day, he was admitted to the hall and assigned to the quarters of the attendants (*śaikṣa*).

After only half a month, it happened that Chen, the Judicial Commissioner, who was returning to Shu after resigning his office, passed by the mountain to inquire about the Way. The Patriarch asked him:

"Have you, O Provincial Commissioner, ever read the *Xiaoyan shi* (Poems of Minor Elegance)? There are two lines in it that are quite similar: 'Frequently calling for Little Jade is originally a matter of no concern;
it is simply that one wishes the gentleman to recognize the sound. The Commissioner responded with an affirmative nod. Zuzhao said, 'But listen closely.
While the Master had just come from outside and was standing in attendance, he asked Zuzhao, 'The Master cited the *Xiaoyan shi*; does the Provincial Commissioner understand it?'"
"No," Zhaozhou said. "He only recognizes sound. The Master said, "I only want the patron to recognize the sound. Since he has already recognized the sound, why is it not so?
Zhaozhou asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? "An old pine tree in the courtyard," Zhaozhou replied.
At this, the Master suddenly attained great enlightenment. He hurried out and saw a rooster flying onto the collar of his robe, spreading its wings and crowing.
The Master said to himself, "Is this not indeed sound? He then placed incense in his sleeve and entered the room to communicate what he had realized.
The Patriarch said, "The great matter of the Buddhas and Patriarchs is not something that can be attained by those of small roots or small capacity. I rejoice with you.
He then announced throughout the mountain community of senior monks, "My attendant has attained Zen."

The Master, along with Fojian and Fuyan, were attending the Fifth Patriarch on the pavilion. While sitting there at night, they returned to the abbot’s quarters, where the lamp had already been extinguished.
From the darkness, the Patriarch said, "Each of you, offer a turning word. Fojian said, "A variegated phoenix dances in the crimson sky.
Fuyan said, "An iron snake lies across the ancient road. The Master said, "Look beneath your feet. The Patriarch said, "It is you, Keqin, who will extinguish my school."

On the day the Master opened the hall, he addressed the assembly, saying: "If you have consistently looked toward the clouds and the sky, standing like a thousand-fathom cliff, you have failed the Buddhas and Patriarchs.
If you have consistently dragged through mud and water, with faces covered in dust and heads smeared with ash, you have buried your own spiritual brilliance.
Now, it is acceptable to be thus, and it is also acceptable not to be thus; yet we must ensure that the true eye flows freely. Do you understand? Even if..."
Treading high upon the crown of Vairocana, he receives no instruction from Śākyamuni; he regards the śrāvakas as maidservants and calls the bodhisattvas slaves.

Even if they were to come here, they would have to lose their sharpness and remain tongue-tied; as for all others, they simply cannot show their heads. Therefore it is said: "The Buddhas of the three periods of time only speak of self-knowledge;
the patriarchs of successive generations have never been able to lift up [the Dharma]; the entire Great Canon of teachings cannot fully explain or annotate it."
Even a clear-eyed monk cannot save himself. Even according to the fodder of one's own fundamental allotment, it is still merely adding branches outside the joints.
For now, how do you speak that single phrase which does not involve the gate of transformation? "The battle clouds hang across the sea; drawing the sword, he stirs the Dragon Gate."
He addressed the assembly, saying: "The whole body is eyes, yet they do not reach what is seen. The whole body is ears, yet they do not penetrate what is heard.
The whole body is mouth, yet it does not touch upon what is spoken. The whole body is mind, yet it cannot reflect it out.

Even if you were to realize this throughout the entire earth, such that there were not a single thread’s breadth of leakage, you would still be halfway there. To uphold the command and bring it forth in its entirety—how can it be displayed? Within this realm, the sun and moon..."
Hanging crosswise: A single expanse across the clear sky, ten thousand ages of spring.

He addressed the assembly, saying: "When the land has no sword for suppressing disorder, the four seas are peaceful and clear; when the gate has no chart of Baidai, the entire family enjoys auspicious celebration.
If you say there is a power to receive grace, that is truly adding mud upon earth. Or if you further seek to erase all traces and swallow [the world]..."

As for sound, it is like taking south for north. Reaching this point, even though one may traverse it in all directions—vertically and horizontally across the ten directions—one cannot avoid confusion.
To settle upon one’s own station and seize the opportune moment is still a matter of some degree; but what is the phrase for "settling upon one's own station"? It is when Hanshan meets Shide.

Clapping his hands, he laughed heartily. Addressing the assembly, he said: "A single word cuts it off; the voices of the thousand sages are silenced. A single sword held aloft leaves corpses strewn for ten thousand miles. Therefore it is said:
sometimes the words reach the meaning but the meaning does not reach the words; sometimes the meaning reaches the words but the words do not reach the meaning. Words can sweep away meaning."

The mind can eradicate phrases; yet mind and phrases race against one another. As for the "nose" of the patch-robed monk (*bābī*), if you can turn it over in this manner, even the blue sky must receive a blow of the staff.
But tell me, by what means? Piteous are the countless people who play in the tide; in the end, they fall back into the waves and die.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "When a single mote of dust enters right concentration (*samāpatti*), the entire earth becomes a cold, still pool.

When all motes arise in samādhi, throughout the ten directions it is a vast, bustling expanse. To manifest a hundred billion bodies is not considered many; to sit upright in an empty hall has never been called 'stillness.
Reaching this point, whether rolling up or unfolding, gathering or releasing, seizing or letting go, killing or giving life—one uses the Vajra King’s precious sword to cut it off completely."

Regarding the matter of doubt: take up the nostril of the patch-robed monk to pass through the barrier of birth and death; sit and cut off the essential ford so that neither ordinary nor sage can pass.

When thousands or tens of thousands cannot ensnare you, and hundreds or thousands of realms cannot transform you, only then can you act as the Tathāgata’s messenger and universally manifest the form-body.
But tell me, at such a time as this, how is it? In daily life there is no shifting or evasion. When—
Faculties vary in depth.

He addressed the assembly, saying: "To let go at the edge of a ten-thousand-fathom cliff requires a man of true caliber; when a crossbow capable of launching a thousand-jin bolt is released, how could it be aimed at a mere field mouse?
Yunmen and Muzhou missed the mark right before their faces; Deshan and Linji deceive the common folk. Himself...
Others establish objects and establish capacities, creating nests and dens; thus they are those who extinguish the Hu lineage. For now, let us consider this single phrase alone: How would you say it?
"The shifting and changing of myriad conditions is but a trivial matter; in the mountain chamber of the fifth month, it is cold as ice."
A monk asked, "In the entire Tripitaka, which one is the head? The Master said, "'Thus have I heard.
The monk said, "That belongs to Ānanda. What about yours, Master? The Master said, "I use it with great ease."
Chan Master Huiqin of Mount Jiang at Jiankang Prefecture (total of four entries). The Master studied under Wuzu.

Once, while conversing with Yuanwu, he raised the kōan concerning Dongsi’s question to Yangshan regarding the "Luminous Pearl of the Tranquil Sea. When they reached the point where no further reasoning could be applied, [Wuzu struck him].
Yuanku asked, "Since you said you had obtained it, yet when this pearl was sought, you also said there were no words with which to respond and no principles by which to argue.
The Master was unable to provide a further answer. The next day, he said to Yuanku, 'Regarding yesterday's koan, I have words for it.'"
Wu said, "Try to bring it forth. The Master said, "Dongsi only asks for a single bright pearl. Yangshan immediately tipped out a full wicker basket.
Wu deeply approved of this and told him, "Brother, you should go and attend upon the Old Monk more closely.
One day, the Master went to the abbot’s quarters; before he had even spoken, he was scolded by the Patriarch [Huangbo], who drove him away with a blow. He returned home.

Xuanzong locked his quarters and slept, harboring resentment toward Guishan that would not cease. Guishan, having already known this in secret, went immediately to knock on the door and called out, "Brother Xuanqin!
The Master asked, "Who is it? Guishan said, "It is I. The Master then opened the door. Guishan asked, "When you saw the Old Monk [Guishan], what did you think?
The Master said, "I originally had no intention of going, but I was enticed and dragged along by you. I suffered the insults and abuse of this old fellow. Guishan rebuked him.
He laughed loudly and said, "Do you remember the words you spoke the other day? The Master asked, "What words? Wuzhuo said, "You also said:
'Dongsi only asks for a single bright pearl; Yangshan pours out a wicker basket. At that moment, the Master was suddenly relieved.
Wuzhuo then led the Master together to the abbot's quarters. As soon as the Patriarch saw him, he immediately said, "Brother Qin, for now..."

Rejoicing that this great matter is now concluded, he addressed the assembly, saying: "The ultimate Way is not difficult; it only dislikes discrimination. The peach blossoms are red and the plum blossoms are white—who says they blend into a single color?
The swallows chatter and the yellow orioles sing—who says their calls are but a single sound? You do not recognize the Patriarch."
The Master twists his nose; he vainly takes mountains and rivers to be his own eyes.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "The matter prior to the fifteenth day is like adding flowers upon brocade.
The matter after the fifteenth day is like a single bubble rising from the great ocean. On the very fifteenth day itself, it is much like a one-foot mirror reflecting a thousand li."
The image: Although it is empty and void, leaving no trace, how can one resist the radiance of the ocean-seal? Let the incense pillar bloom as it may;
what need is there to speak of the hundred uglinesses on the Buddha’s face? Why is this so? At the end of the frosty night, the moon falls spontaneously into the stream before us.
Addressing the assembly, [the Master] raised an anecdote: A monk asked Zhaozhou, "What is the meaning of 'non-transmigration'?
Zhaozhou made a gesture with his hand as if water flowing. The monk attained realization. Another monk asked Fayan, "'Do not grasp at appearances; suchness is unmoving.
How does one not grasp at appearances and see suchness as unmoving? Fayan said, "The sun rises in the east and sets in the west at night. The monk...

There is also a point of realization. If you can see it here, only then will you know that the whirlwind overturning the mountains is fundamentally ever-still, and the rivers rushing in competition are originally not flowing.
If this is not yet so, I cannot help but speak further: Heaven revolves to the left and Earth revolves to the right;
through how many cycles have they passed from antiquity to the present? The golden crow flies and the jade hare runs; as soon as one has just emerged—
"At the gateway of the sea, again behind the green mountains, the waves of the rivers flow vast and wide; the tides of the Huai and Ji stretch out endlessly.
They enter directly into the azure depths, flowing day and night. Then, he shouted aloud: "Do you see that which is suchness, unmoving?"
Chan Master Qingyuan of Longmen in Shuzhou (the seventh in the series). He was the son of the Li family from Linqiong in Shu.
At the age of fourteen, he left home to receive full ordination and relied upon the *vinaya*, investigating its doctrines in depth. While reciting the *Lotus Sūtra*, he reached the passage:
"This Dharma cannot be understood through thought, deliberation, or discrimination. He took this up to question his lecture master, but the master was unable to answer. The Master sighed and said:
He realized that the study of doctrinal categories and terminology was not the means for resolving the great matter of birth and death.

He subsequently rolled up his robes and traveled south, proceeding directly to the seat of Master Yan of Taiping in Shu. There, in the inner quarters, they engaged in dialogue until their understanding merged like water and milk.
For seven years, he penetrated the ultimate depths of the teaching. Later, he emerged into the world at Wanniu Monastery in Shu, then moved to Longmen, and finally presided over Baochan in Hezhou.

He addressed the assembly, saying: "From the time the single sandal returned to the West and the robes were rolled up for the journey south, the news has been heard in vain as it drifted through the human world.
From antiquity to the present, they have been handed down from one to another; it is much like one person spreading a rumor and ten thousand people taking it as truth.

This mountain monk, having suffered much illness, has become well-versed in the nature of medicines; being old, he has grown wise. It is not that I wish to dissect or diminish the ancients, but rather to avoid mutual confusion."
They are buried within one another. All people must have previously experienced this through sensory contact and known it through vision in former days;

they have obtained it by requesting instruction from others, and it is indeed present when raised within the midst of discourse and during the play of coming and going. Yet, as for the ultimate reality of the Great Matter, it can never be attained.
It is only when emotions are forgotten, principles are lost, calculations are exhausted, and paths are blocked, that there is no place for further contrivance.
"Applying the mind" is precisely where one applies effort. In my ordinary practice, I simply say, "Go drink tea. Today, too, I say, "Go drink tea.
Even if you master all the five flavors of Chan from every quarter, how can that compare to my saying, "Go drink tea"?
He addressed the assembly, saying: "In short, it cannot be recorded. Heavenly flowers fill the sleeves; even with a thousand words, they are not worth a single moment of silence.
He addressed the assembly again, saying: "It would be fitting to speak but a single phrase. If there were someone who could understand it, it would still be somewhat better.
But if no one can understand it, this mountain monk would end up speaking falsehoods. Upon reflection, it is better to simply stop for now. Let us all rest together."
Drinking tea in the hall, one is free and at ease. This is to avoid being seen through by others on another day or at another time. Why?
Because the General already possesses a fine reputation; it is no matter if he does not receive a fief or a noble rank.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "To resolve through deliberation and to know through reflection—how can a solitary lamp rival the radiance of the sun?
It is not the mind; it is not the Buddha. For your sake, I shall sweep away the lair of the spirit: a falcon soaring to the heavens flies into the clouds;
a thousand miles, ten thousand miles, in but a single swoop. *Alala!*"

He addressed the assembly, saying: "A thousand explanations and ten thousand expositions are not equal to seeing me face-to-face once. Even without speaking, it is naturally clear. The analogy of the Prince’s precious sword;
the analogy of the blind men feeling the elephant; the matter of beckoning from across the river in the study of Chan;

the matter of meeting at Wangzhou Pavilion; the matter of being in a remote place where no one dwells; and the matter of being amidst deep mountains and rocky cliffs—all of these are instances of face-to-face encounter."
Yet one sees it; it does not reside in verbal explanation. A monk asked, "Is the Way far?
To touch upon things is to encounter the Real. What is the Way? The Master said, "Eight feet five inches above the head.
The monk asked, "I do not understand how this principle works. The Master said, "Seven or eight inches square. The monk asked, "What is the path that leads upward?"
"Would you allow a student to understand this? The Master said, "Whether one speaks of 'upward' or 'downward,' I nonetheless allow you to understand.
Chan Master Daoning of Kaifu in Tanzhou (fourth in the series) addressed the assembly, saying: "When the true command is fully upheld, a wind arises that sweeps the earth;

when the essential pass is firmly secured, who can distinguish between superior and inferior? As for the three mysteries and the critical examination of cases, they do not yet discern the monk; as for the five ranks of the sovereign..."

Your servant: This is utterly contrary to the essence of the Way. It is simply plain and devoid of affairs, yet it deceives the common folk. To speak of entering into profound principle is like sticking to the skin and clinging to the bone.
Why? Because not even a hair’s breadth has moved since before the empty kalpa; numbers cannot encompass it. Upon what basis can one discuss and realize it?
O practitioners of Zen, do you understand this thoroughly? How many times have I cast it before the assembly? Even the Great Compassionate One with a thousand eyes cannot see it.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "The autumn sun shines across the vast sky; the autumn river reflects the azure void. Alas for those outside our gate, who seek Maitreya everywhere.
Suddenly lifting their heads upon the road, they meet him yet do not recognize him. O Zen practitioners, since you have met him, [why do you not know him?]"
Why is it that you do not recognize one another? Having completely clipped the bamboos before the frost, you fail to transform into dragons when facing the stream.

Addressing the assembly, he said: "At the assembly on Vulture Peak, there was already excessive elaboration. When a fine horse catches sight of the whip, how could it be considered merely 'talented and noble'?

To sit in meditative repose amidst the crags while the Lord of Heaven rains down flowers—this is to remain without speaking and without hearing, concealing the body while revealing the shadow. At Shaolin, he sat facing the wall; this was a calculation."
The former was not yet established; standing in the snow and severing one’s arm, one brings shame upon fellow monks. At Huangmei, presenting a verse, victory and defeat were partial and withered.
At midnight, the transmission of the robe deceived people no small amount. As for the matter that has come down from of old—how should it be handled?

How could it depend on the presence of gods and men to wag the tongue and move the lips, competing for sharpness and contending for the vanguard, mutually establishing host and guest, with questions and answers intermingled? Let us examine this!
"Come! Though your offenses fill the heavens, even so: were it not for the early blossoming of flowers along the purple road, how could the yellow oriole descend upon the willow branches?
He addressed the assembly, saying: "The true command of Mahākāla is unavoidable hardship; the compassion of Shaoshi already compromises one's wind and bone. Waist...
Carrying a staff and a bowl, you have betrayed your lifelong vows. Refining your conduct and extinguishing the mind, you merely pass the time in mutual stagnation.
How can this compare to a spring rain clearing away the mist and the green mountains appearing? Three clouds, five clouds; a single song, two songs of the yellow birds.

The Great Compassionate One with a thousand eyes cannot gaze upon them enough; even the masterful hand of Wang Wei could not paint them so perfectly. Even if you were to simply be like this, you would still be traversing the path. O practitioners!
"Chan Master, how is it with that single phrase that does not involve the journey? After a long silence, he said: "A person comes from Chenzhou, yet receives no news from Dongjing."

Chan Master Chengtian Zicheng of Tanzhou, Dharma heir of Chan Master Yun’gai Zhiben of Tanzhou (the second of two): Addressing the assembly, he said: "It is not mind, it is not Buddha, it is not an object. Striking his meditation seat, he said:
"I shall break open the cave of your numinous spirit for you; though one sifts through dust and stirs up clouds of soil, there is nowhere to be found."
"Thousand mountains, ten thousand mountains, all stark and imposing. He then struck his meditation seat and said, "Return to the hall.

Addressing the assembly, he said: "The waning moon falls at the fifth watch; the heavens roar as white clouds fly. This is a matter clearly before one's eyes, yet it is not the mechanism of the present moment.
Since it is a matter before one's eyes, why is it not the mechanism of the present moment? After a long silence, he said: "Desiring..."
Words fall short; it is best discussed beneath the forest trees.

Chan Master Jingyin Jicheng of Dongjing, successor to Chan Master Zhikai Ping of Dongjing (the ninth): Addressing the assembly, he said, "The treasury of the true Dharma-eye leaks through every single thing."
The true mechanism is revealed: the wondrous mind of *nirvāṇa* manifests everywhere and at all times.

If you seek it within words, look for it outside of phrases, skillfully strive for intellectual understanding, or forcibly give rise to discrimination, it is much like mistaking a reflection for one’s own head or climbing a tree to catch a fish;
you will spend a lifetime in inversion, never finding rest. You must directly turn the light back upon yourself and draw near to an enlightened master to recognize [it].

To take up one’s own native land is precisely the livelihood of a person of realization. When the mind of delusion and awakening comes to rest, and the sentiments of grasping and rejecting are forgotten, all myriad distinctions and thousandfold differences do not depart from this very point.
If this is not yet so, you are like a man waiting by a tree stump under the clear breeze and moonlight;
the cool rabbit grows distant as the fragrant grasses spread.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "Meeting on a narrow path, do not harbor doubt; even lightning and sparks are already too slow.
If you can, right now, penetrate through the three minds, it will all be contained within this very moment. Reaching this point, even if one were to question and answer back and forth,"
Sparks fly like shooting stars; host and guest shift positions. Illumination and function, gain and loss—waves surging, peaks standing firm.

Like jade turning and pearls revolving, before the eyes of the patch-robed monk, there is absolutely no point of contact. Have you not seen? At Vulture Peak, the Flower was held up, and only Kāśyapa was granted permission.

At Vaiśālī, when asked about his illness, who else could have been the Golden Grain Buddha? Who knows that this smile has already become a worn path? Even if one remains silent, it is still not enough.
To avoid the winds and waves, one must meet beyond the ordinary; only then can one achieve a profound resonance within. Do you understand?
A single melody, vast and silent, moves through past and present—the thirty-six peaks of Mount Luoyang lie to the west.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "A single expanse of emptiness atop the mountain of the five aggregates; though we enter and exit through the same gate, we do not meet.

For immeasurable kalpas we have lived in rented quarters, yet in the end we do not recognize the master of the house. If you were to recognize him, it would be nothing more than mistaking a servant for the lord.
If you do not recognize him, how can you avoid the Ancients speaking thus? At first, I thought only of the thatched hut..."
"Long and short; it has been burned away, yet the ground was originally uneven.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "If you do not look back when the word is raised, you are already mistaken; if you attempt to deliberate, when will you ever awaken? O Great Assembly!

A withered mulberry tree knows the wind from heaven—is this looking back or not looking back? The ocean water knows the cold of heaven—is this thinking or not thinking? For now, what shall we call it?"
The principle realized: one carries the Dharma-realm upon a staff made of hare’s horns; one dances with a whisk made of tortoise hair at the Three Terraces.
Addressing the assembly, he said: "Sound is in the nose; fragrance is in the ear. Saline and bland are in the eye; blue and yellow are in the tongue.

the sunflower turns with the sun, the rhinoceros-patterned skin contemplates the moon, fragrant maples transform into an old man, and the larvae of the moth become the wasp. If one does not know this, how bitter it is, O Buddha!
"I grant you a single eye.

He addressed the assembly, saying: "When a single thought of purity arises, the Buddha dwells in the Demon King’s palace; when a single thought of evil arises, the Demon King dwells in the Buddha’s palace.
Master Huai said: "Simply believe in this way; it is called walking with one's feet firmly planted on the ground."

Ultimately there is no separate dharma, nor is there any separate principle. Once this old monk has spoken thus, I fear you all will be like those who release the hound after the rabbit has been caught, or like those who mark the boat’s edge to find the sword that fell into the water.

Addressing the assembly, he cited Fengyang’s raising of his staff and said: “The Buddhas of the three periods are right here.

"Such as yourselves, you shall all become Buddhas. Having spoken these words, he performed a somersault and departed toward the city of Kuśinagara.

The Master gave a shout and asked, "Did you hear that? Xuanshan replied, "I heard it. The Master said, "Since you heard this shout, it was 'existence'; this can lead one into the teachings of the Hīnayāna.

At the southern end they sell cheap; at the northern end they sell dear. When one examines this closely, he deserves thirty blows—but let us pass over this one instance for now.

Addressing the assembly, he raised his staff and said, "Striking the void produces sound; a true connoisseur is rarely encountered. He then struck the meditation seat and said, "Striking wood produces no sound;

He addressed the assembly, saying: "Before a word is uttered, the transmission is already bestowed; yet at the moment one attempts to deliberate, ten thousand mountains stand in between.

Cold tea can kill a man with grief.

This teaching is merely old paper used for wiping impurities. Bodhidharma sat facing the wall for nine years, yet he remained drowsy and failed to awaken.

He addressed the assembly, saying: "Cease, cease! There is no need to speak; my Dharma is subtle and difficult to conceive.

"Where do you all see Old Śākyamuni? If you can see him, you have entered the gate of Deshan, though you have not yet entered Deshan’s room.
But how does one enter Deshan’s room? After a long silence, he said: "Thirty years hence."

The bowl-chiming sound of Śākyamuni; the stench of excrement from Bodhidharma’s coming from the West.

It is accomplished. Yet, alas, there is the saying that "excess is as bad as deficiency. Fortunately, the clouds have gathered and dispersed, the waves have subsided and stilled;

the bright sun hangs in the sky, and ten thousand households share in the celebration. But as for the phrase, "The Great Achievement is without a Master"—how do you speak of it? The rustic old man knows nothing of the labors of Yao and Shun;
he merely beats the drum, *dong dong*, to sacrifice to the River God.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "When the precious sword is drawn, it is used immediately; how could there be any hesitation? When the eyebrows are raised, one proceeds at once;

there is no room for evasion or retreat. In every place, it illuminates the present and manifests the ancient; in every place, it cuts through all nets and cages. It does not touch the blade's edge, nor does it look into a mirror.
Let us set aside for a moment the fact that it alone transcends the mundane world—when all ten thousand functions have been exhausted, what then? (8)
"Where is there heat in the autumn moon?

He addressed the assembly, saying: "To awaken to the Way by hearing sounds is inevitably to pour water into one's ears; to clarify the mind by seeing forms is likewise to scatter sand into one's eyes.

Without anything to grasp or look up to, solitary and remote, severed from the dust of worldly emotions; steep and towering, free from discrimination—this is still the matter of "that side.
But as for the matter of "this side," how is it? Do not linger by the cold pond’s shadowless tree; just watch the snowflakes fall in the sixth month.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "If there is movement, shadows appear; if there is awakening, ice forms. To be neither moving nor awakening is no different from being earth or wood.
For a patch-robed monk, reaching this point, there must be a path for turning around before it is possible.

"Attained! Yet guarding another’s ghost cave, one cannot avoid being a mere spirit.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "To realize the emptiness of persons and the emptiness of phenomena does not yet accord with the tradition of the Patriarchs and Buddhas.

To embody total function and total illumination is likewise not the essential subtlety of a patch-robed monk. One must directly shatter the sturdy barrier and recognize the single aperture above. As it is said:
"What is this single opening that points upward? The spring chill is biting; it freezes the young man to death.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "There is no other path to Nirvana, yet there are many gates of expedient means. Holding up his staff, he said: "Look! Look!"
This mountain monk’s staff has swallowed up the waters of the West River in a single gulp. A carp from the Eastern Sea leaps upward to the Thirty-three Heavens;
Śakra, filled with wrath, seizes Mount Sumeru and strikes it until it crumbles to dust. The Earth Goddess Sthāvarā joins her palms in praise, saying:
"Behold the Dharma of the Dharma King—the Dharma of the Dharma King is thus! With his staff, he strikes the meditation bench.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "Deshan’s immediate striking upon entering the gate creates a mound where there was level ground.
Linji’s immediate shouting upon entering the gate stirs up waves where there was no wind. Juzhi merely raising a single finger cannot avoid being crude and superficial.

Xuefeng rolling out three balls is but the play of a child. When it comes to this point, none of these are of any use. How can they compare to the sweet rain that universally nourishes during the third month of summer?"
The waters reach the eastern ridges; the grain turns green in the southern fields. The farmers drum upon their bellies; the woodcutters sing aloud.
The ancestral style of the ancient Buddhas is as if still present. If you can realize this here and now, you shall together enjoy the peace and prosperity of the age.
Should you not yet have done so, you will merely know that affairs pass before your eyes, unaware that old age creeps upon you from above.

The Dharma Heir of Chan Master Chengdufu Zhaojue Keqin, the Sixteenth Generation under Nanyue:
Chan Master Jingshan Zonggao of Lin’anfu (Total: twenty-nine). A native of the Xi clan in Xuanzhou, he first visited Baofeng.
Chan Master Zhun had merely dipped his fingers into the Way. He next went to visit Chan Master Yuanwu Keqin. While attending a formal lecture, he heard [Keqin] cite a monk’s question to Yunmen:
“What is the place where all Buddhas emerge? Yunmen replied, “On the water above the East Mountain. Keqin then said:
Someone asked Tianning, "What is the place where all Buddhas emerge? He replied to him directly: "A fragrant breeze comes from the south;
at the corner of the hall, a subtle coolness arises. Upon these words, the Master’s past and future suddenly severed.
Although the movement of mental phenomena did not arise, he nonetheless remained seated in a state of pure nakedness. Qín said, "It was no easy matter for you to reach this stage."
Do not begrudge [your life]. Once dead, one cannot be revived. Not doubting the words and phrases is itself a great illness. It is said:
"Letting go at the edge of a precipice, one spontaneously accepts it; after death, one revives again—this cannot deceive the Sovereign. You must believe that such a principle exists.

In every room, he interrogated them with the words regarding "the phrase that has it" and "the phrase that does not," as well as the saying, "like a vine leaning against a tree. As soon as the Master opened [his mouth]...
Wumen said: "Diligent" (Qin) immediately replied, "It is not so, it is not so. This went on for half a year, yet he could not bring himself to speak further.
The Master then requested further instruction, saying, "I have heard that you, Reverend, once asked this same question of the Fifth Patriarch.

I wonder what the Fifth Patriarch said. Diligent smiled but did not answer. The Master said, "Reverend, you must ask before the assembly; what harm is there in speaking now? Diligent said, "Let me ask."

"There is a phrase and there is no phrase, like a vine leaning against a tree. What is the meaning of this? The Patriarch said, "It cannot be traced; it cannot be painted. I asked, "What about when the tree falls and the vine withers? The Patriarch said, "He has come along with you. At that moment, the Master was suddenly relieved and said, "I understand! Daowu then cited several kōans to interrogate him, and the Master responded to each as follows: [The following is a summary of the subsequent exchanges: Daowu cited the story of Mazu’s encounter with the monk who asked about the Buddha-nature. The Master replied, "The Buddha-nature is not a thing; it is like the wind blowing through the trees. Daowu cited the story of Nanquan’s response to the question about the Buddha-nature. The Master replied, "The Buddha-nature is not something to be grasped; it is like the moon reflected in water. Daowu cited the story of Baizhang’s response to the question about the Buddha-nature. The Master replied, "The Buddha-nature is not a fixed entity; it is like the empty sky. Daowu cited the story of Linji’s shout. The Master replied, "That shout was like a thunderbolt; it struck directly at the source. Daowu cited the story of Zhaozhou’s "No. The Master replied, "That 'No' was like a great sword; it cuts through all conceptualization. Upon hearing these responses, Daowu was completely satisfied and said, "You have truly attained the Way. He then bestowed upon him the seal of certification. The Master then returned to his own monastery. Later, when he was asked by others, "How did you attain enlightenment under Daowu? the Master replied, "It was like a man waking from a dream; everything was clear. When asked again, "What did Daowu say to you? the Master replied, "He said nothing; I simply understood. When pressed further, the Master said, "If you ask me, I would say: 'The tree falls and the vine withers. When asked, "What does this mean? the Master replied, "When the tree falls and the vine withers, the patriarchal mind is revealed. When asked, "What is the patriarchal mind? the Master replied, "It is like the vast, open space—neither coming nor going. When asked, "What is the ultimate meaning of the Buddhas and Patriarchs? the Master replied, "It is like the great ocean; it contains all things without distinction. When asked, "What is the meaning of the First Patriarch coming from the West? the Master replied, "It is like the rising sun; it illuminates all beings. When asked, "What is the meaning of the Sixth Patriarch’s verse? the Master replied, "It is like a mirror reflecting forms; it is neither the mirror nor the forms. When asked, "What is the meaning of the Zen school? the Master replied, "It is like a wild fox; it is beyond all categories. When asked, "What is the meaning of the Dharma? the Master replied, "It is like the sound of the wind in the pines; it is neither sound nor silence. When asked, "What is the meaning of the Buddha? the Master replied, "It is like the empty fist; it holds nothing within. When asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch? the Master replied, "It is like the flowing river; it never ceases. When asked, "What is the meaning of the Way? the Master replied, "It is like the great earth; it supports all things. When asked, "What is the meaning of the Mind? the Master replied, "It is like the bright moon; it shines everywhere. When asked, "What is the meaning of the Self? the Master replied, "It is like the vast void; it has no boundaries. When asked, "What is the meaning of the Truth? the Master replied, "It is like the great fire; it burns away all delusions.
