yet, being unable to carry on this lineage, you would rather willingly cast yourselves aside, acting like thieves who break through walls—how unmanly! I venture to ask the assembly: [Is this truly so?]

He addressed the assembly, saying: "The Dharma has no fixed form; it takes shape according to the object it encounters. Affairs have no fixed necessity; when the work is accomplished, there is no presiding agent.

To treat them with familiarity and intimacy is easy; otherwise, it is difficult. Both worldly dharmas and Buddha-dharmas become mere frivolous discourse.
You must know that this old monk is not here. Tell me, where is he? Standing to the side, wearing a straw raincoat atop a thousand peaks;

The Master said, "Zhigong was no ordinary monk. The monk asked, "What is the Dharma?
The Master said, "Yellow silk, young lady; nephew, pickle mortar. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "Exquisite and wonderful beyond measure."

A monk asked, "Regarding the story of Xiangyan climbing the tree, what is its essential meaning? The Master said, "It cannot be depicted; it cannot be painted.
The monk said, "Though Li Ling was a skilled hand, how could he avoid falling into the barbarian camp? The Master said, "Where have you come from?"
Chan Master Daoben of Jianfu Temple in Raoyou (five fascicles), a native of Jiangzhou, addressed the assembly, saying:

"To those who bow high to Śākyamuni and do not pay homage to Maitreya, I give thirty blows of the staff. Why? Because they only know how to climb higher step by step, but do not know how to let go from the void.
To those who pull the plow for the eastern neighbor and drag the handle for the western neighbor, I give thirty blows."
The staff. Why? Because others only know how to cast it down from emptiness; they do not know how to ascend step by step.
When I, this mountain monk, speak thus, is there any fault in it? Is there anyone among the assembly who can discern this?
If you can discern it, we shall walk hand in hand beyond the southern flank of Mount Sumeru. If you cannot discern it, you are but an old crow in a cloth bag.
"Though alive, it is as if dead.

Now tell me: are they different or not? After a long silence, he said: "Exhausting one's own mind, one laughs the mouths of others to pieces."
He addressed the assembly, saying: "A single phrase at the summit of a thousand peaks is not known on the street of ten directions;

if it were fathomed at the summit of a thousand peaks, it would be the street of ten directions. Thus it may be so, yet thus it may not be."

It is so. Whether it is thus or not thus, both are acceptable. Only then does one till the fields for food, pulling the handles and guiding the plow, blending with the mundane and harmonizing with the light, trailing mud and carrying water.

He addressed the assembly, saying: "To sit squarely at the head and fail to turn the body; to step forward and miss the mark at the heels.

Old Zhaozhou, at eighteen, already knew how to break up his house and scatter his home; all else is but empty sophistry. Nevertheless..."
Thus it is. One does not grow in wisdom without undergoing a single event.

Addressing the assembly, he said: "One who is skilled in speech speaks that which cannot be spoken; since there is no speech in what is spoken, though one speaks all day long, one has never truly spoken.
One who is skilled in traces leaves traces that cannot be traced; since there are no traces in what is traced, though one leaves traces all day long..."
It has never left a trace, being like empty space. Its essence is not composed of various forms, yet it does not obstruct the manifestation of all phenomena.
When the sun rises, its light pervades the world, yet empty space has never become bright. When the sun sets, darkness pervades the world [yet empty space remains unchanged].
Yet empty space has never been dark. Now, suddenly there is one who cannot be deceived; hearing such talk, he cannot restrain his impatience.

"A thousand awls piercing the ear"—is this not indeed having some "monk's air"?
Even so, while it is true that one has entered the gate of the Patriarch, one has not yet entered the Patriarch’s chamber. I dare ask the assembly:
tell me, how does one ultimately enter the Patriarch’s chamber? Do you understand? White clouds may easily come to the green peaks, but the bright moon—
Difficult to instruct, he descended from the azure heavens.

each mystery contains the path of the three essentials. When there are mysteries and essentials, who can know them? [Only] one with eight arms."

A great debt is difficult to repay. All such deliberations based on intellectual consciousness remain within the realm of the shadows. Consider, for instance, Linji’s awakening:

was it through the power of Huangbo, or was it through the power of Dayu? If you can see this, I grant you that the eye at the crown of your head is upright and the talisman behind your elbow is efficacious.

their failures are not few. If you all understand this, I grant that their nostrils reach the heavens; if you do not yet know, then for now, do not speak.

These three phrases are like the three eyes of Maheśvara: neither vertical nor horizontal, neither unified nor separate.

They illuminate and shatter the primordially present spiritual mechanism, ensuring that every step is fundamentally free from waste. Only then does one understand what Zhaozhou said: "Where there is a Buddha, do not dwell; where there is no Buddha..."

Do you see it? Even if you were to see it, you would enter hell as fast as a shooting arrow. He struck the ground once with his staff.

"Do not speak before others; I shall split your head into a hundred pieces!
He addressed the assembly, saying: "The lion teaches its cubs the secret of the hunt; as they prepare to leap forward, they already turn their bodies.

Mountains, rivers, and the great earth; grasses, trees, and groves; sentient and insentient beings—all are shattered into a hundred fragments. Is there anyone who knows how to repay this kindness?
If you lack the strength to lift the cauldron and pull up the mountain, the black steed of a thousand li will not be easy to ride.

Mastery over killing and giving life: picking up a single blade of grass, he pierces the nostrils of all the monks under heaven;

spreading a net that covers the heavens, he strikes the magnificent dragon leaping through the waves. While this is so, if one proceeds in just this manner, the entire school of Bodhidharma will be swept away like dust.
Suddenly grasping his staff and drawing a line across it, he says: "The sword leaves its precious scabbard because of injustice; the medicine comes from the golden casket to save the sick."
[He strikes the floor with his staff once.
He addresses the assembly, saying: "When the master craftsman has not yet appeared, jade and stone cannot be distinguished; when the skilled smelter is absent, gold dust and sand are mixed together.
Even if one were to attain self-awakening without a teacher, under the gate of Tiantong, they would still rightly receive three thousand blows in the morning and eight hundred blows in the evening."
Suddenly picking up his staff, he said: "To call it a staff is to fail to distinguish jade from stone; not to call it a staff is to confuse gold dust with sand.
Among them, there may be one or two who are well able to discern the underlying principle; such people will surely soar through the crimson clouds.
If this is not yet the case, he planted the staff on the ground and said: 'Quickly, fix your eyes upon it!'"
Addressing the assembly, he said: "Those who practice Zen must take care not to apply their minds erroneously. To seek awakening and clarify the nature of reality is to apply the mind erroneously.
To aspire to become a Buddha or an ancestral patriarch is to apply the mind erroneously. To study sutras or lecture on the teachings is to apply the mind erroneously.
To walk, stand, sit, or lie down is to apply the mind erroneously. To eat porridge or rice is to apply the mind erroneously. Even to defecate and urinate is to apply the mind erroneously. (1)

To move the one while remaining still, or going and coming—this is a mistaken application of the mind. There is yet another point where the mind is mistakenly applied, which Guizong does not dare to reveal to you all.
Why? "Once a single character enters the gates of officialdom, even a cart drawn by nine oxen cannot get out."

Chan Master Xingji of Guoqing Monastery in Taizhou, Dharma heir of Chan Master Hugu Jingyuan of Taizhou (the third of three). He was a native of this very province. Addressing the assembly, he said: "The staff of a patch-robed monk—if not used, it is simply that;
but when used, it is like a poison bird falling into the water: fish and turtles all die. It presses straight on the main point while bypassing the side."
Ti! With a whistling wind, he strides alone across the Great Way; killing and giving life are within his own grasp. Thus it is said:

"A thousand people pushing against a gate is not as good as one person pulling the bolt open. If one person pulls the bolt, then thousands and tens of thousands will reach the field of peace and bliss.
Do you know this? "The embroidered mandarin ducks are for you to behold; I do not hand the golden needle over to anyone."
He addressed the assembly, saying: "To contemplate form as emptiness is to realize great wisdom, and thus one does not dwell in birth-and-death.

To contemplate emptiness as form is to realize great compassion, and thus one does not realize nirvana. Dwelling neither in birth-and-death nor realizing nirvana, it is not contained within the land of Han, nor is it governed by the land of Qin.
Tell me, where do you establish your body and settle your life? Is it not that which is luminously manifest within the heart and mind?"
In the space between them, their forms cannot be seen; within the shimmering realm of sensory objects, their principle cannot be divided.
Is it that rising and sitting they always follow one another, and speaking and remaining silent they dwell together? If it were so, you would all be merely tapping at the skull.
You must know that those of transcendent capacity possess transcendent function. But tell me, what is this transcendent capacity?
Using it: Although the Hidden Body of the Northern Dipper has words, few people know the news that transcends the crowd.

He addressed the assembly, saying: "When ancient Buddhas appeared in the world, those who fulfilled the human potential were few; since the Patriarch came from the West, those who have ruined themselves are many.

Reaching where there is no place to go; wielding extraordinary mechanisms beyond the mundane; speaking words of no meaning in places where even Buddhas and Patriarchs cannot open their mouths.
To those he instructs who possess superior spiritual practice, they do not move a single step, yet they are free to roam in all directions.

To those he instructs who possess subtle and wondrous speech, they do not utter a single word, yet they are free to speak constantly and fervently. He hides in stillness while leveling the high and low.
[The Master] lowered [his whisk]. He could not help but bring up the story of Campā and Silla vying for precedence. Therefore it is said: "In this way it is permissible;
in that way it is also permissible. Sometimes within 'this way' there is 'not that way'; sometimes within 'not that way' there is 'this way.'"
Sometimes he instructs them to raise their eyebrows and blink; sometimes he does not instruct them to raise their eyebrows and blink.

The "sword that kills" and the "sword that gives life" are both contained herein. Suddenly, if a monk comes forward and says, "The Master acts in such a way..."

He addressed the assembly, saying: "Yesterday was a bustling turmoil; this morning is a profound stillness. Within the bustle, there is the matter of stillness;
within the stillness, there is the matter of bustle. Having said this, he raised his staff and said: "This staff is the simultaneous raising of both stillness and bustle."
How will you all manage this? If you can understand it, you have a staff; I shall give you a staff.
If you do not have a staff, I shall snatch yours away. The nostrils of the plantain tree fall into the hands of you all.
If you cannot understand it, the plantain tree is beneath the feet of you all.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "Purple ferns stretch out their fists as bamboo shoots break through the tips; the willow catkins have flown away, and the green shadows interlace.
This is clearly the single-line transmission of the Western Patriarch: the yellow oriole sings and the swallow speaks at its nest.

If you can see it here and believe it with deep conviction, then according to the standards of other quarters, you would certainly be settled beneath a bright window. But under the gate of Longxiang, we simply strike you dead with a single blow.
Why is this? It is not that one finds it difficult to dwell with others; rather, for the most part, the distinction between the monastic and the lay must be clear.
Chan Master Zhiqing of Fuzhou Tianwang Monastery (five cases in total) addressed the assembly, saying: "Before Mount Kukkuṭapāda, all talk and understanding are but weary toil;
along the path of Caoxi, there is a total absence of deliberation. Even if one possessed profound and subtle eloquence that exhausts the heavens, or the utmost skillful means that deplete the world—"

There is not even a hair's breadth of attachment. If one can penetrate at a single blow and achieve dual clarity in a single stroke, it is not a matter of raising eyebrows or blinking eyes, nor is it a matter of halting thought or waiting for the mechanism to engage.
Only then can one pluck the whiskers of a fierce tiger and grasp the tail of a venomous snake;
casting off body and life, entering water and mud, moving freely and at will in the north, south, east, and west, penetrating every point through and through until all is clear.
To clarify: severing deliberation and forgetting words. Thus, it may be said that for an eon one is on the road, yet not leaving home;
for an eon one is at home, yet not leaving the road. But tell me: right now, are you at home or on the road? Do you understand? The jade palace half-opened, the golden lock is stiff;
At night’s depth, who beholds the Lord of Purple Microcosm?
He addressed the assembly, saying: "A rushing torrent passing through a blade is not yet the work of a master; a swift flame passing through the wind is still the act of a dullard.
Thus, when Caoxi held up his whisk, he made the monks laugh to death; when Xuefeng rolled the ball, it turned into mere child’s play.
This single path of guidance is known in its details by the wise; this final mechanism seizes the vital ford. If you possess the eye that looks toward the ultimate..."
Before his feet have even crossed the threshold, he flings up his robes and goes—yet this is still like thrusting one's head into a vat of glue.
Apart from this, it is much like a monkey wearing a paper hat. If it is not like this at all, then how is it? After a long silence, he said:
"To offer this profound mind to every dust mote and land is what is called repaying the Buddha’s kindness."
He addressed the assembly, saying: "The lion teaches its cub the secret of the hunt; as it prepares to leap forward, it has already turned its body.
At the point where the interlocking patterns meet in combat, even the eagle-eyed observer loses the track in the moment. Such talk is not mere sophistry."
To display one’s brilliance and agility, one must exhaust all skillful means and forget both gain and loss; responding to the moment like the wind, responding to the occasion like lightning.
Even so, this is not yet the state of a true man of the Way. What, then, is the state of a true man of the Way?
Before the cold hawk has even raised its head, the swift falcon has already soared into the sky.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "The profound Way cannot be attained through the exertion of effort; holy wisdom cannot be known through a conscious mind;
the ultimate truth cannot be realized through the persistence of self-conception; and supreme merit cannot be sought through the cultivation of affairs.
When the ancients spoke thus, they saw only the sharpness of the chisel’s point, yet failed to see the squareness of the chisel’s head. A gentleman of universal penetration—"
At times it is thus; at times it is not thus. At times that which is thus is correct; at times that which is thus is not correct.

Do you all understand this thoroughly? Even if you were to see through to the point where all dharmas are neither "is" nor "is not," neither "non-is" nor "non-is-not"—and even if you were to directly forget both "is" and "not"—this would still be like scratching an itch while wearing boots. Furthermore, regarding these words...

Manifesting the pivot. To discern the mark within words—the sword has long since departed, yet you are still marking the boat. When I, this mountain monk, speak thus, is there still a way to benefit others?
"The void shatters into dust, leaving nothing to rely upon; one does not know how many springs the peach tree has endured."
Addressing the assembly, he held up his whisk and said: "Just this very thing—Heaven cannot cover it, and Earth cannot support it.
It pervades the world and pervades space; it forms a single mass and a solid whole. Reaching this point, where can the Buddhas of the three periods go to seek it?
Where can the Patriarchs of the six generations go to uphold it? Where can the monks of the world go to describe it? He set the whisk down.
It is not attained through self-acquisition nor realized through self-verification; rather, it is the simultaneous practice of "knocking" and "singing.
Although this is so, it is still not the place where a patch-robed monk walks. What, then, is the place where a patch-robed monk walks? He plunges his body across the sea of right and wrong;
he strides freely through the thicket of jackals and tigers.
The Hermitage Master Anfen of Jianmen Hermitage in Nanjian Prefecture (Five in total). A native of the Lin family from Yongfu, Fuzhou.

At an early age, he attained a slight degree of realization regarding the Way. By nature, he was easygoing and unconstrained. At the beginning of the Shaoxing era, when Miaoxi presided over Mount Jing, the Master went there to seek lodging.
Fearing that he might disturb the community, Miaoxi turned him away. The Master entered the city, and amidst a dense crowd, suddenly—

Hearing those clearing the path announce, "The Senior Secretary is coming," the Master attained a sudden and great enlightenment. He composed a verse, saying: "For years this matter has hung upon my breast;
I have questioned all quarters, yet my eyes remained unopened. Today, liver and gall are fully revealed: A voice on the riverbank cries, 'The Senior Secretary is coming!
Thereupon, he traveled extensively throughout the rivers and lakes before returning directly to Yangyu, where he took refuge under Chan Master Lan’an Xu.

Day by day he reached ever deeper into the profound mysteries. One day, having selected certain words, he requested that they be sent to him with a verse, which said: "The wind is fierce at the riverhead, and spray flies;
North and south we meet, yet no brow is unknitted. Only the hand of the refined Chan master Fen Casually snatches the silken prize and returns home.
Thereafter, he resided at Ben-an.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "Regarding this very field of land, you people—tell me, before heaven and earth were yet divided, where was it?
If you can penetrate this directly, you have already failed the Venerable Upādhyāya by no small measure.
If you further hesitate or engage in deliberation, it will be more than ten thousand miles away amidst white clouds. Suddenly, he took up his staff and struck the assembly, dispersing them.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "Cutting the grass on the summit of Mount Hushan is neither a conditioned achievement nor an unconditioned dharma.

Suddenly grasping his staff, he drew a line across it and said: "Who dares to look upon this with the true eye? If you retreat out of awe before the precipice, you will have brought your entire life to naught.
No matter how clever, eloquent, or wise you may be, or what kind of supernatural powers you possess—here, not even a single point of them will suffice."
[The Master] said: "Even if you were an iron man, walking upon the heads of Buddhas and Patriarchs, you would still be but a guest outside the gate.
Those who can enter this mountain monk’s door—I shall break your legs and smash your waist; do not say I did not warn you!
Why is this so? Gold has its own price; it is never sold to people mixed with sand."
He addressed the assembly, saying: "From the Buddhas above down to all sentient beings below, their very lives and natures are entirely in the hands of this mountain monk.
When one examines the matter, there are immeasurable transgressions; this mountain monk also has immeasurable transgressions.
Is there anyone here who can examine and find them? [He plants his staff. Hatred has its source and debt has its owner. He then looked east and west and said:
"Since leaving the cave, I have encountered no rival. Where one can afford to be generous, one should be generous.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "Before the fifteenth day, all the stars in the heavens bow toward the North Star. After the fifteenth day..."
"Among humans, there is no one who does not face east. Having cast away both what precedes and what follows, the local dialects differ in every place. He then bent his fingers with his hand and said:

This establishment does not sell on credit for even a single coin.

Chan Master Zongdai of Gushan, Fuzhou—the fifth successor in the lineage of Chan Master Siyue of Dongchan, Fuzhou—was a native of this very province. Initially, he studied under Dongchan and attained a profound, secret realization.
He further visited Miaoxi to penetrate its ultimate depths and mysteries. Later, he established the Dharma and passed away at his home mountain.
Addressing the assembly, he said: "To pour forth eloquence like a cascading river does not avoid entanglements; to set a trap like one for a tiger merely results in a stale cliché.

Even if one discusses emptiness and existence, citing the ancients and deliberating the present, with thoughts and phrases racing together and host and guest alternating—this is precisely [the problem]."
This is like raising waves where there is no wind, or gouging a sore on healthy flesh. Within the gateway of transformative teaching, such expedients are not out of place.

However, if one wishes to fully uphold the true command, to block off the vital thoroughfare, to manipulate the pivot and mechanism of the Buddhas and Patriarchs, and to seize the very core of the monk’s nostrils, it must be that the eye atop the head is correct and the talisman behind the elbow is efficacious;
only when one is peerless, transcends categories, and surpasses all precedents will this be achieved. Although...
It is indeed so; yet this remains the ultimate standard of the Chan school.
Take, for instance, the single phrase for the "Blessing the Sage" opening of the hall:
how would you express it? "The imperial foundation encompasses the three thousand worlds; the sagely calculation extends through ten million springs."
Addressing the assembly, he cited Master Yunmen, who said: "On level ground there are countless dead people;
those who can penetrate the thorny forest are true masters. He then held up his staff and said: "Everyone, if you call this a 'staff,' you are precisely a dead person on level ground.
If you do not call it a 'staff,' you have not yet penetrated the thorny forest. Ultimately, how is it?"
After a long silence, he said: "The winter is not cold until after the twelfth lunar month.

He struck his staff once and descended from the seat. Addressing the assembly, he said: "Set aside the staff of Deshan and the shout of Linji. Need I even bring forth the grappling hook of Bimozhi or the arrow of Shigong?
As for the Buddhas of the three periods and the patriarchs of successive generations who preach horizontally and vertically—what kind of hot bowl is this?"
[The Master] made a sound. "When people arrive here, how is it then? After a long silence, he said, "Today Drum Mountain has suffered a loss.
He descended from his seat and addressed the assembly, saying: "The World-Honored One said: 'One should know thus, see thus, and believe and understand thus; do not give rise to dharmas.'"
[The Master] then summoned the great assembly and said: "Jade is originally without flaw, yet it possesses flaws.

This was Chan Master Zongying of Qianyuan Temple in Fuzhou, a successor of Chan Master Shoujing of Xichan Temple in Fuzhou (sixth in the lineage). He was a native of Minqing in this province. Addressing the assembly, he took up his staff...

[He] strikes the meditation desk once and says, "A hot-tempered fellow! A single blow is enough. He then leans his staff against it and says, "For a clever person, there is no need for further action.
He then asks, "Is there anyone here now who is clever? After a long silence, he says, "One might as well try to catch a mythical unicorn."
The hare, too, did not encounter it. He addressed the assembly, saying: "Who is without mind? Whose mind is without Buddha? The Buddha is always present within people;
people are always chasing after external things. Holding up his whisk, he said: "If I call this object a 'whisk,' I cannot avoid being turned by things. If I do not call it..."
"This thing," he said, "even when made into a whisk, cannot avoid being turned by objects. Ultimately, how can one discern and clarify this? After a long silence, he said:
'The embroidered mandarin ducks are displayed for you to behold; do not attempt to pass the golden needle to another.'"
Addressing the assembly, he said: "Kāśyapa Mātanga’s entry into the Han lands already involved excessive verbiage; Bodhidharma’s coming from the West naturally revealed his flaws.
For me, a mountain monk, to speak in such a manner is already a transgression as vast as the heavens."

He addressed the assembly, saying: "If one discusses this matter, to affirm it is a deviation; to deny it is an error. To neither affirm nor deny is like an ant circling in a loop or a silkworm spinning its cocoon.
Upon reaching this point, you must brandish the sword. Were it otherwise, you would be like a man waiting by a tree stump under the clear breeze and moonlight;
the cool rabbit grows ever more distant as the fragrant grass turns green."
A monk asked, "When the first teaching was given, one did not know there was a final phrase; when the final teaching was given, one did not know there was an initial phrase.
I do not ask about the initial phrase; what is the final phrase? The Master said, "Receive this question with full attention."
Yun said, "If it is so, then one cannot deceive him in the slightest. The Master said, "He has already been deceived.
A monk asked, "What is right knowledge and right view? The Master said, "A cat; a dog.
The monk said, "Even they possess but one eye. The Master said, "Not even half an eye."

Chan Master Youquan of Huazang in Changzhou, a Dharma successor of Chan Master Faquan of Daofang in Huzhou (the third of three): A native of Lin’an Prefecture. When the Master ascended the hall to address the assembly, he said:
"The plucking of the flower and the smile buried an ordinary man; nine years facing the wall broadcasted the family’s disgrace. From this point on..."
When one person transmits it as empty, ten thousand people transmit it as real. This causes descendants of later generations to inherit the void and follow the echoes.

Since today there is no way to escape this, we cannot help but take the wrong for right; pointing at emptiness, speaking of emptiness, the fan leaps up to the Thirty-three Heavens, striking the nostrils of Śakra.
When the carp of the Eastern Sea is struck once, the rain falls like a basin.
Tilting [the world]—this is called the first turning of the Dharma wheel, the proclamation and exposition of the ultimate truth (*paramārtha-satya*).
If one attains clear realization here, the assembly on Vulture Peak will stand solemnly before one’s eyes; there is neither past nor present, neither distinction nor difference.
If you have not yet attained such clarity, I shall further provide a single phrase of impartial speech as a supplementary aid.
May the imperial domain flourish for ten million springs.
Addressing the assembly on the commencement of the summer retreat, he said: "Today, the mouth of the sack is tied shut; Eyeballing monks, do not run about in confusion.
Where mental activity ceases, one turns the body around; Even a sneeze becomes a lion’s roar. In a sandalwood forest, let them gallop as they please. He then picked up his whisk.
"Rising from the crown of the eyebrows, it is born; carving the flesh to form a sore reveals the family’s shame.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "Long rains have not cleared, yet today it is bright; who can listen to the raindrops falling from the eaves?

Suddenly the skull breaks and the functioning of the senses is exhausted; seeing forms and hearing sounds are all already perfected. He took up his staff, struck the meditation seat, and said: "This is..."

Sound and form are presented together; hearing and seeing are distinct and clear. Furthermore, which among these is the ever-present reality? Do you understand? A person from Zhejiang does not look at another’s complexion;
a person from Hu does not look at another’s nose.

Chan Master Xianjie of Tiantong in Mingzhou (4th in the lineage), a successor of Chan Master Tanhua of Tiantong in Mingzhou, was a native of Fuzhou. He traveled extensively, visiting various masters before finally relying on Master Hua.
Master Hua asked, "What is the True Dharma Eye? The Master replied, "A broken sand pot. Master Hua nodded in approval. One.
Ri took the words and sent Hua with a verse, the last line of which said: "I have my final word; when you return, I require that you follow it.
Hua received Tian Tong’s command, and the Master served as the First Seat. Later, the Master opened the Dharma path at Wugu and passed away at his home mountain.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "To use a wedge to extract a wedge merely creates another track; to transmit mind by means of the mind only deepens the malady.

Receiving echoes and responding to reverberations, raising eyebrows and blinking eyes, striking with the staff and shouting with the "ho"—all these are but yellow leaves used to stop a child's crying.
When Wugū arrives here, he finds himself with no way to ascend to heaven and no door to enter the earth; biting down on his teeth, he joins with all of you in mixing mud and water.
(He plants his staff and says: "Were it not for a single frost that pierces the very bones, how could one obtain the plum blossom?"

A fragrance that strikes the nose. He addressed the assembly, saying: "When the strings are moved, the distinct melody is heard; when the leaves fall, one knows autumn. To raise one and clarify the three is to discern the subtlest weights and measures.

The Path. A thousand sages walk hand-in-hand together; they would surely fall into the Hell of Plowing Mud. At such a time as this, what should one do?
In Jiangnan and Liangzhe, spring is cold and autumn is hot.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "To call the entire expanse of heaven and earth 'one phrase' is to be burdened with shackles and fetters.

To be without even a hair’s breadth of fault or affliction is still a turning phrase (*zhuǎnjù*). Not seeing a single dharma is only half the presentation (*bàntí*).
One must further know that there is a time for the full presentation (*quántí*). Great Yunmen’s sword has long since departed; you are merely marking the boat now.

The Master asked the Sixth Patriarch, "What should one apply oneself to in order to avoid falling into the stages [of gradual cultivation]? The Patriarch replied, "What have you been doing until now?"

The Master said, "I do not even practice the Noble Truths. The Patriarch asked, "In what rank or stage do you fall? The Master said, "Since I do not even practice the Noble Truths, what rank or stage could there be?
The Patriarch said, "So it is, so it is. Guard and maintain this well for yourself."
Shitou came to pay his respects. The Master asked, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From Caoxi. The Master held up his whisk and said, "Is there such a thing as this at Caoxi?
He replied, "Not only at Caoxi; even in the Western Heavens it does not exist. The Master said, "Have you perhaps been to the Western Heavens?
He replied, "If I had been there, then it would exist. The Master said, "That is not it yet; speak further. He replied, "The Master, too..."
"You must say that you will take half; do not rely entirely upon me. The Master said, "I do not decline to tell you, but I fear that in the future there may be no one to uphold [the Dharma].

"Come. I shall give you this hoe; go and dwell in the mountains. Xuefeng Qian arrived at Mount Nanyue.
Before he had even sent a letter of introduction, he asked, "If one seeks not after the sages and does not prize one's own spiritual essence, what is the state of affairs?

Xuedou said, "Great as he was, Dahui could not enforce his command.

[He was] the second-generation successor under Qingyuan, Zen Master Xingxi of Qingyuan in Jizhou, a dharma heir of [Nanyue Huairang].

"Do you recognize me? The Master said, "Even if you were to recognize me, how could you truly recognize me? Huizhi said, "Though there may be many horns, a single unicorn is sufficient.
Because Qingyuan had said, "Some say there is news from Lingnan," the Master remarked, "There is someone who does not speak thus."
Yuan said, "If it is so, from where do the Great Canon and the Lesser Canon emerge? The Master replied, "They all emerge from right here.
Qingyuan approved of this.
The Master asked Elder Qingyuan, "Since leaving Caoxi, in what year did you arrive here to reside? Qingyuan said, "I know exactly when you left Caoxi.
The Master said, "I did not come from Caoxi. Qingyuan said, "I also know where you came from.
The Master said, "Venerable Sir, as you are a person of great stature, please do not be hasty."

He addressed the assembly, saying: "The Dharma-gate of our school has been transmitted by the Buddhas of the past. It does not concern itself with meditative concentration or diligent effort, but only with attaining the Buddha’s knowledge and vision.
Mind is Buddha; mind, Buddha, and sentient beings; enlightenment, bodhi, and afflictions—though their names differ, their substance is one.
You should know that the essence of your own spiritual mind is free from the extremes of annihilation and permanence; its nature is neither defiled nor pure. It is profoundly still and perfect."
The sages are equal and identical; their applications are boundless. Transcending mind, intellect, and consciousness, the three realms and six paths are manifested solely by one's own mind.
Like the moon in water or images in a mirror, how could they have arising or ceasing? If you can know this, there is nothing that is not fully provided.

The Master gave this instruction: "Words and actions have no connection [to the truth]. Yaoshan stepped forward and said, "Even when one reaches the state where there is neither speech nor action, it still has no connection.
The Master said, "In my place here, not even a needle can pierce through. Yaoshan said, "In my place here..."
It is like planting flowers upon a stone.
Dadian asked, "An ancient said, 'To say there is the Way, or to say there is no Way—both are slanders. I beg the Master to remove these slanders. The Master said:
"In my place here, there is not a single thing. What is there to remove? The Master then asked Danyuan, "Close off your throat, lips, and mouth, and speak it forth.
Danyuan said, "I have nothing such as that. The Master said, "If it is so, you have entered the gate."
The Master asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Jiangxi. The Master said, "Do you still possess the Great Master [Mazu]? The monk said, "I see him.
The Master pointed to a piece of firewood and said, "How does Mazu compare to this? The monk was at a loss for words. Upon returning, he recounted the exchange to Mazu.
Mazu asked, "What did you see as the size of that piece of firewood? He replied, "It was immeasurably large. Mazu said, "So it is with you."
"You have great strength. The monk asked, "Why? The Master said, "From Nan-yueh, you have carried a bundle of firewood here;
is that not evidence of your strength?"
A monk asked, "What is liberation? The Master said, "Who has bound you? The monk said, "No one has bound me. The Master said, "Then who seeks liberation?
The monk asked, "What is the Pure Land? The Master said, "Who has defiled you? The monk asked, "What is nirvana?
The Master said, "Who gave you birth and death? The monk asked, "What is Chan? The Master said, "A brick. The monk asked, "What is [it]? The Master said, "A tile."
[The monk] asked about the Way. The Master said, "A wooden post. He asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "Go ask the pillar.
[The monk] said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "I, too, do not understand."
The Third Generation under Qingyuan:
Chan Master Tianhuang Daowu of Jingzhou, Dharma Heir of Chan Master Nanyue Shitou Xiqian (Part Two). A native of the Zhang family of Dongyang in Wuzhou, the Master asked Shitou:
Dongshan asked, "Setting aside concentration and wisdom, by what dharma do you instruct people? Touzi said, "In my place, there are no servants;
what is there to set aside? The Master asked, "How can one understand this? Touzi said, "Can you grasp empty space?
The Master said, "If that is so, then I shall not follow from this day forward. Touzi said, "I wonder, at what time and from which direction have you come? The Master—
Xuefeng said, "I am not a man from that place. Baizhang said, "I have long known where you come from.
Xuefeng said, "How can you, Master, falsely accuse me with stolen goods? Baizhang said, "Your body is right here before me.
Xuefeng said, "Even so, after all, what will you show to those who come after? Baizhang said, "Tell me, who is 'one who comes after'? At these words, Xuefeng attained awakening.
He had completely exhausted the traces of the mind he had previously attained.

When the Master was about to pass into nirvana, the assembly inquired after his health. The Master suddenly called out to the head cook, "Come forward; do you understand? The cook replied, "I do not understand.
The Master picked up his pillow, threw it to the ground, and immediately brought his life to an end.

Chan Master Weiyen of Yaoshan in Lǐ Prefecture (25th): A native of the Hàn clan from Jiàng Prefecture, he maintained the precepts with great purity and was extensively learned in the sūtras and śāstras.
One day, he sighed to himself, saying: "A true man of great character should transcend phenomena to achieve self-purification; who could afford to be so trivially occupied with them?"

[Zhaozhou] asked, "What about the subtle practice of affairs? He went straight to Shitou and asked about the Three Vehicles and the twelve divisions of the teachings. [Zhaozhou] said, "I have a rough understanding of these.
However, I have heard that in the South there is the 'direct pointing to the human mind' and 'seeing one's nature to become a Buddha,' yet I truly do not understand it clearly.
I humbly hope that the Master will compassionately provide instruction. Shitou said, "It cannot be thus, nor can it be otherwise. It is neither thus nor otherwise."
"How? "Not at all. "How do you do it? The Master remained silent for a moment. Baizhang said, "Your karmic conditions do not lie here.
Go to Mazu Daishi in Jiangxi; he will surely explain it for you. The Master went to Jiangxi and again posed his former question.
Mazu Daishi said, "Sometimes I instruct them to raise their eyebrows and blink; sometimes I do not instruct them to raise their eyebrows and blink."
At times he would instruct him that "raising the eyebrows and blinking the eyes" was it; at other times he would instruct him that "raising the eyebrows and blinking the eyes" was not it.
Under these words, Shanshan attained sudden enlightenment and immediately prostrated himself. Master Mazu asked, "Son, what principle have you seen that you prostrate yourself?
The Master replied, "When I was with Stonehead, I was like a mosquito on an iron ox."
Master Mazu said, "Since you are thus, you should protect and uphold [the Dharma] well.
Fayan Xiu remarked, "Shitou’s 'iron hammer without a hole' is quite like handing it over to someone who cannot receive it.
Yaoshan realized awakening in Jiangxi; alas, he suffered a fall on level ground—what support was there for him?"
[This is] the place for [discerning] strategy. Let those with the eye discern and examine it.
One day, Mazu Daoshi asked the Master, "How is your realization these days? The Master replied, "The skin and flesh have fallen away entirely;
there remains only the true reality. Mazu said, "What you have attained may be called being in accord with the substance of the mind and spreading it..."
"Your four limbs are thus; you ought to take three strips of bamboo and bind them around your belly, then go to dwell in the mountains wherever you may be.
The monk said, "What kind of person am I that I would dare speak of dwelling in the mountains? The Master said, "Not so.

There has never been one who travels far without dwelling, nor one who dwells long without traveling. To seek benefit where there is nothing to benefit, and to act where there is nothing to do—this is futile."
"You ought to set out upon the vessel; do not remain here for long. The Master then paid his respects and took leave, returning once more to Shitou.
While the Master was seated, Shitou asked him, "What are you doing? The Master replied, "I am doing nothing at all. Shitou said, "If that is so, then you are sitting idly.
The Master said, "If it were idle sitting, then I would be doing something. Shitou said, "You say you are doing nothing, yet..."
"For what reason? The Master said, "Even the thousand sages do not recognize it. Tou praised him with a verse: "From the beginning we have lived together, yet its name is unknown;
Spontaneously following along, we simply proceed as we are. Since the ancient worthies of the past could not recognize it, How could ordinary people in their haste possibly understand it?"
He addressed the assembly, saying: "The Patriarch taught you only this: to protect [the mind]. If greed, anger, or delusion should arise, you must strictly guard against them;
do not allow them to stir up trouble. If you wish to know it, you must take up the responsibility for withered trees and stones, for there are truly no branches or leaves to be found.
Nevertheless, you should still examine yourself further; you must not cut off speech entirely. I shall now act for your sake."
By speaking these words, he reveals that which is beyond speech. That which is primordial has no form such as ears or eyes.
At that time, a monk asked, "How can there be the six realms of existence? The Master said, "Although this essential wheel of mine is within them, it is fundamentally unstained.
The monk asked, "What is it like when one does not understand the afflictions within the body? The Master said, "What appearance do the afflictions have?"
I shall first test you. There is a certain class of people who merely memorize words upon the surface of paper; they are largely deluded by the sutras and treatises.
I have never looked at sutras, treatises, or examination manuals. You simply run about, lost in mundane affairs, and fail to find your own ground of non-attachment;
for this reason, the mind of birth and death arises. Before you have even learned a single word or phrase, or a single sutra...
The Treatise says: "To speak in such a manner regarding Bodhi and Nirvana—whether they are subsumed within the world or not—if you understand it this way, it is nothing but birth and death.
If you are not bound by these gains and losses, then there is no birth and death. You see how that Vinaya Master speaks of *naiḥsargika* and *duṣkṛta* offenses;
these are the very root of birth and death. Nevertheless, even though it is thus, one must still exhaust birth and death. And yet, it cannot be avoided.
It is so. From the Buddhas above down to the ants below, all possess these variations of long and short, good and bad, large and small.
If they did not come from without, where would there be such idlers digging in hell to wait for you?

If you wish to recognize the realm of hell-beings, it is those being boiled in cauldrons right now. If you wish to recognize the realm of hungry ghosts, it is those who are now full of falsehood and lacking in truth.

Those who do not inspire faith in others are those who wish to recognize the realm of animals—those who, even now, do not understand benevolence and righteousness, nor distinguish between kin and stranger.
Why must they wait until they have grown fur and horns, or until they are slaughtered, disemboweled, and hung upside down?

To recognize the realms of humans and devas, look at those who, right now, maintain pure and dignified deportment, carrying their water jars and alms bowls. You must guard this with all diligence to avoid falling into the various destinies; this is the foremost priority.
One may discard this; yet this is not easily attained. One must stand upon the summit of the highest peak and walk upon the floor of the deepest sea.
To practice in such a place is no easy matter; only then will there be a slight degree of resonance. Nowadays, those who emerge from the depths are all people of many affairs.
It is impossible to find a single person who is dull-witted and simple-minded. Do not merely memorize the words within the manuals.
When one sees others who do not understand what one has perceived and known for oneself, one immediately gives rise to contempt and arrogance. Such people are all icchantikas and non-Buddhists;
this state of mind is utterly off-center. You must examine this with great care. Even to speak in such a manner remains a matter pertaining to the periphery of the three realms.
"Do not let this patched robe pass you by in vain. When you reach this point, it becomes even more subtle; do not treat it as trivial. You must know how to cherish it.

For a long time the Master had not ascended the hall. The head of the monastery said, "The assembly has long been longing for the Master’s instructions. The Master said, "Strike! (and struck the gavel).
The bell was struck; the head of the monastery (yuanzhu) rang the bell, and as soon as the assembly had gathered, the Master descended from his seat and returned to the abbot’s quarters (fangzhang).
The head of the monastery followed him and asked, "The Master promised to speak for the sake of the assembly; why did you not utter a single word?
The Master replied, "The sutras have masters of the sutras; the treatises have masters of the treatises. How can one blame this old monk for that?"
Langya Huijue said: "When Yaoshan descended from his seat, there was no harm in it; yet when the monastery director pressed him, he lost one of his eyes.
Cuiyan Zhongzhi said: "The monastery director resented that Yaoshan did not speak for him;
this can truly be called 'misleading the three armies.'"
The Master held an evening *can* (informal discourse), saying: "I have a phrase; I shall tell it to you when a hornless ox gives birth to a calf.
At that time, a monk came forward and said, "A hornless ox has given birth to a calf—it is simply that you, Master, do not speak. The Master called to his attendant, "Bring the lamp!
The monk then withdrew and returned to the assembly.
Dongshan said, "This monk understands; he simply refuses to prostrate.
Faldeng said, "[He is] a young bull calf; a young cow calf. [The Master] provided the verse: "Born as twins."
The Master usually did not permit others to read the scriptures. One day, he took up a scripture and read it himself.
A monk asked, "Master, you usually do not allow people to read the scriptures; why then do you read them yourself? The Master said, "I simply want to cover my eyes.
The monk said, "May I learn from the Master and read them as well? The Master said, "If you were to read them, even ox-hide would have to be pierced."
Changqing Ling said: "What fault is there in the eye?
Once, when the Master was traveling with Daowu and Yunyan on a mountain excursion, they saw two trees, one flourishing and one withered. The Master asked Yunyan:
"Which is the withered? Which is the flourishing? The Master said, "Flourishing. The Master asked, "In that case, then everything everywhere would be radiantly brilliant.
He then asked Dao-wu. Dao-wu said, "The withered. The Master said, "In that case, then everything everywhere would be left to be withered and dull.
After a short while, the novice Gao arrived. The Master asked Gao again. Gao—
Yun said, "The withered withers of itself; the flourishing flourishes of itself. The Master looked back at Yunyan, Daowu, and said, "Not so, not so."
Baoning Yong’s verse says: Powdered and plastered, then wrapped in cloth; All pulled by the thread of the master of the rite.
The drum beats and the frown breaks, the flute is blown to its end; Gather everyone together and go home to rest.
The Master said to Yunyan, "Call the novice monk here for me. Yunyan asked, "What will you do with him once he has arrived?
The Master replied, "I have a broken-legged cauldron; I want him to carry it up and down.
Yunyan said, "In that case, I and the Master shall each contribute one hand."
Daguang Zhe said: "If Yaoshan had not obtained Yunyan, his broken-legged cauldron would have nearly become a discarded vessel.
One day, as the Master was going out carrying his rain hat, Yunyan pointed to it and asked, "What will you do with this?

The Master replied, "I have a place to use it. Yunyan asked, "What will you do when wind and rain come? The Master replied, "I will cover myself with it. Yunyan asked, "Does it still receive [the elements]?"
"Covering it over, there is nothing. The Master said, "Even so, there is nonetheless no omission.
One day at mealtime, the head of the monastery announced, "The bell has been struck; please come to the hall, Master. The Master said, "You go and hold my alms bowl for me.
The head of the monastery said, "Master, you have been without hands for quite some time now. The Master said, "You..."
"You are merely a fellow who wears the kāṣāya in vain. The host said, "I am just like this; how about you, Master?
The Master said, "I have no such followers."
While the Master was seated, a monk asked, "Master, you sit there in a state of stillness; what are you contemplating? The Master said, "I contemplate that which is not contemplated.
The monk asked, "How can you contemplate that which is not contemplated? The Master said, "It is not contemplation."
Zun Bunan served as the temple director (dianzhu). Once, while he was washing a clay Buddha statue, the Master asked him, "You can wash this one;
can you also wash that one? Zun replied, "Bring me that one."
Changqing Ling said, "A false dharma is difficult to support. Huanglong Nan said, "As for these two venerable masters, one comes out and one goes in;
I have not yet seen who has won or lost. Thirty years from now, do not misquote them."
The Master wrote the character for "Buddha" on his hand and asked Daowu, "What character is this? Daowu replied, "The character for Buddha.
The Master said, "Talkative old fellow!"
The Master asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Nanquan. The Master said, "How long have you been there?
He replied, "I have spent several winters and summers there. The Master said, "In that case, after thirty years you will become a water buffalo.
The monk said, "Although I was there, I never once went up to their dining hall. The Master said, "Are you sucking south wind?"
The Master said, "Do not be mistaken, Reverend; there is naturally someone here who holds the spoon and chopsticks.
He asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Hunan. The Master said, "Is the water in Lake Dongting full yet? The monk replied, "Not yet."
The Master said, "It has rained for so long; why is it not yet full?
Yunyan spoke on his behalf, saying, "Profoundly still. Daowu said, "It is full."
The Master asked a monk, "How old are you? The monk replied, "Seventy-two. The Master said, "Is it seventy-two? The monk said, "Yes. The Master then struck him.
Caoshan said, "The first arrow was still somewhat bearable; the second arrow pierced the man deeply. A monk asked, "How can one avoid this?"
Having received this staff, Cao said, "Once the royal decree has been issued, the feudal lords will clear the way.
He then asked the head cook, "How long have you been here? The cook replied, "Three years. Cao said, "I do not know you at all.
The monk, finding no resonance with these words, departed in a fit of indignation.
A monk asked, "I have a doubt; I pray that you will resolve it for me. The Master said, "Wait until evening, and I shall resolve it for you.
At the evening assembly, when the congregation had gathered, the Master said, "The monk who requested a resolution of his doubt today—where is he? The monk immediately stepped forward.
As the Master descended from his seat, he seized him and said, "Assembly, this monk has a doubt! He then let go of him and returned to his quarters.
Cuiyan Zhi said: "Yaoshan resolving the doubt in such a manner is like adding mud to the surface of the earth.
Nevertheless, this monk did not fail Yaoshan."

A monk asked, "My own matter is not yet clear; I beg the Master for instruction. The Master remained silent for a long while and then said, "It would not be difficult for me to speak for you, but it is only fitting that you see it directly beneath my words;
this would still leave some room for improvement. If you go on to deliberate and ponder, you will instead create my own fault.
It is better that each of you simply close your mouths and avoid implicating one another."
A monk asked, "In the level fields and shallow grass, the deer and roe form a herd. How can one shoot the leader among the deer?
The Master said, "Watch the arrow! The monk threw his body down and fell. The Master called to his attendant, "Drag this monk out! The monk then ran away.
The Master said, "This fellow who plays with mud balls—what limit is there to him?"
A monk asked, "What is the supreme treasure within the Way? The Master said, "Do not be sycophantic or crooked. The monk asked, "How is it when one is not sycophantic or crooked?
The Master said, "Even if the entire kingdom were offered, it could not be exchanged for it."
A monk asked, "When a weary person intends to return to their hometown, what then? The Master said, "Your parents' entire bodies are red and festering within a thicket of thorns;
where would you go upon returning? The monk said, "If it is so, then I shall not return. The Master said, "You must indeed return.
If you do return, I will show you a prescription for ceasing the intake of grain. The monk said, "I request it at once. The Master said:
On two occasions he ascended the hall. [The Master] said: "One must not chew even a single grain of rice. A monk asked:
"Before the Patriarch had yet arrived, was there still the meaning of the Patriarch? The Master said: "There was. The monk asked: "Since there was..."
The Patriarch asked again, "Why have you come? The Master replied, "It is precisely because there is [something] that I have come.
When the Master was about to pass away, he cried out, "The Dharma Hall is collapsing! The Dharma Hall is collapsing! The assembly all took up objects to prop it up.
The Master raised his hand and said, "You do not understand my meaning," and then he passed away.
Chan Master Tianran of Danxia in Dengzhou (Ten cases). Initially, he studied the Confucian classics and entered Chang’an to take the imperial examinations.

There he met a Chan practitioner who asked him, “Where are you going, virtuous one? The Master replied, “I am going to select an official. The practitioner said, “How does selecting an official compare to selecting a Buddha?
The Master asked, “To select a Buddha, where should I go? The practitioner said, “The Great Master Ma in Jiangxi is the one who selects [Buddhas].”
"This is the field of the Buddha; you, O benevolent one, may go there. The Master then proceeded directly to Jiangxi.
As soon as he saw Mazu Daishi, he placed both hands under the brim of Mazu’s head-wrap. Mazu looked at him and said, "I am not your teacher. Go to Shitou at Mount Nanyue."
The Master then went to visit Shitou and presented his previous intention to him. Shitou said, "Go to the fodder shed. The Master then served him diligently for three years.
One day, Shitou addressed the assembly, saying, "Tomorrow, everyone must clear the weeds in front of the Buddha Hall. The next day, the great assembly each prepared their tools.
While others used spades and hoes to clear the weeds, the Master alone washed his head with water and knelt before a stone. The Head smiled and shaved his hair;
he also preached the precepts to him. The Master covered his ears and departed.
The Master visited Mazu again. Without yet having paid his respects, he entered the Sangha hall, mounted the neck of the Holy Monk (Śālistamba), and sat there.
The assembly was all astonished and informed the Great Master Mazu. When the Great Master entered the hall and saw him, he immediately smiled and said, "My son is naturally so.
The Master leaped down, prostrated himself, and said, "I thank you, Master, for bestowing my name. Consequently, he was named Tianran (Natural). Mazu asked, "Where have you come from? The Master—
[The Master] said, "Shitou is coming. The Patriarch said, "The path at Shitou is slippery; will you fall down? The Master said, "If I were to fall, I would not have come."
The Master passed by a temple when the weather was bitterly cold. He took a wooden Buddha from the hall and used it to kindle a fire for warmth.

When the temple administrator suddenly saw this, he rebuked him, saying, "How can you burn my wooden Buddha? The Master prodded the ashes with his staff and said, "I am burning it to retrieve the *śarīra*.
The administrator asked, "How can a wooden Buddha have *śarīra*? The Master replied, "Since there are no *śarīra*, please bring two more statues."
He took it again and burned it. Thereafter, the head of the monastery’s eyebrows and hair fell out.
The Master asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "I have come from below the mountain. The Master said, "Have you finished eating yet? The monk said, "I have finished eating.
The Master said, "Does the person who gave you the food to eat possess eyes? The monk was speechless.
Changqing asked Baofu: "When one gives food to another to eat, there is a share of gratitude. Why is it that [the recipient] does not possess the eye?
Baofu said: "Both the giver and the receiver are blind men. Changqing said: "They have exhausted their skillful means."
"Does this not result in blindness? Fú said, "Can you say that I am blind? The Master visited Layman Páng.
Upon meeting at the gate, the Master asked, "Is the Layman at home? The Layman replied, "When hungry, one does not choose one's food.
The Master asked, "Is Old Páng at home? The Layman replied, "Heaven! Heaven! and then entered his house. The Master said:
"O Heavens! O Heavens! With that, he turned back.
The Master asked the layman, "Yesterday we met; how does it compare to today? The layman said, "Bring forth yesterday's matter according to the Dharma and make it the 'Eye of the School' (zongyan).
The Master said, "As for this 'Eye of the School,' can it contain Master Pang? The layman said, "I..."
[The Layman] said, "In your eyes. The Master said, "My eyes are narrow; where can one find a place to settle? The Layman said, "How can these eyes be narrow?
How can this body be settled? The Master stopped speaking. The Layman said, "If you would speak one more phrase, this dialogue would be complete.
The Master did not respond. The Layman said, "Among all [phrases], this one sentence is something no one can utter."
As the Master and the layman were walking along, they came upon a pool of water. The layman pointed at the water and said, "Even if one attains it like this, one still cannot discern it.
The Master said, "Indeed, even though one has attained it, one cannot discern it. The layman scooped up two handfuls of water and splashed them on the Master.
The Master said, "Do not do so! Do not do so! The layman said, "It must be done so! It must be done so! The Master then scooped up three handfuls of water himself.
Jukupō asked, "At such a time as this, what can be done? The Master said, "There are no external things.
Jukupō said, "Few obtain the advantage. The Master did not respond. Jukupō said, "Who is it that falls into disadvantage?"
The Master went to visit a layman. At the gate he encountered the girl Lingzhao, who was carrying a basket and washing vegetables.
The Master asked, "Is the layman at home? Lingzhao set down her vegetable basket and stood with her hands clasped. The Master asked again; Lingzhao picked up the basket and walked away.

The Master then returned to the mountain. A short while later, the layman returned. Lingzhao recounted the previous conversation. The layman asked, "Was Danxia there? Lingzhao replied, "He has already left."
The scholar said, "Red earth smeared on a cow's udder.
Daopei Zhe said, "Both the Great and the Small Danxia were exposed by this laywoman.
While traveling, the Master encountered an old man with a young boy. The Master asked the old man, "Where do you live? The old man replied, "Up there."
"This is heaven; this is earth. The Master said, "If suddenly heaven collapses and the earth opens up, what then? Weng said, "Heaven! Heaven!
The youth let out a single sigh. The Master said, "It is not without a father that a son is born," referring to Weng and the youth.
He entered the mountains and departed.

Nanquan came from Lingnan. Touzi asked, "At the head of Mount Dayu, there is a single panel of merit;
is it yet accomplished? Nanquan replied, "It has been accomplished for a long time; it simply lacks the dotting of the eyes. Touzi said, "Do you wish for me to dot the eyes?
Nanquan said, "Please do so immediately. Touzi lowered one leg, and Nanquan prostrated himself. Touzi asked, "What principle have you seen that you prostrate yourself?"
The Master said: "It is like a single speck of snow upon a red-hot furnace. Xuedou said:
"With infinite merit, where is there any speck to be found?
Nanhua Bing said: "To call it 'one set of merit' is already a forced designation. Shitou let it hang.
One foot. Changzi said, "It is like a single speck of snow upon a great furnace; the more one turns it over, the more one sees its leakage.
Although this is so, though the road at Sword Pass is perilous, those traveling by night are even more numerous.
After the Master had ascended the seat, Layman Pang arrived. Once the assembly was settled, the Layman stepped forward and said, "Each of you, please examine yourselves well.

The Master then began his formal discourse. The Layman, however, stood to the right of the master’s seat. At that time, a monk asked, "Without touching upon the 'Master of the House,' I request the Master to answer my question.
The Master replied, "Do you recognize Layman Pang? The monk said, "I do not. The Layman seized the monk and said, "What a pity!"
"How bitter! How bitter! The monk said nothing. The layman then pushed him away. After a short while, the Master asked the layman, "Did that monk just now take the staff?

The layman replied, "I will wait until he is willing. The Master said, "The layman sees only the sharpness of the chisel's tip, but does not see the squareness of the chisel's head. The layman said, "If you, Master, speak in this way, I can accept it; but others—"

[The Master] heard this. [The Layman] said, "In any case, it does not hinder [the point]. The Master asked, "What is so bad about it? The Layman replied, "You, Master, see only that the head of the chisel is square;
you do not see that the tip of the awl is sharp."
As the Master was walking down the corridor, he saw a monk coming to inquire after his well-being. The Master said, "Every step is a place where you provide proof;
do you know this? The monk said, "I do not know. The Master said, "If you knew, what would I be capable of doing? The monk bowed. The Master said, "I am not capable;
you, however, are quite capable."
One day, when a monk approached, the Master suddenly seized him and said, "Lion cub! You belong to the wild jackal pack! The monk made a gesture with his hand as if brushing back eyebrows.
The Master said, "Even so, you still lack the roar. The monk seized the Master and said, "I specifically wanted to exercise this single function.
The Master gave him a slap. The monk let go and clapped three times. The Master said, "If you see one who is the same..."
"Feng, do you still agree with this? The monk said, "Ultimately, it does not depend on anyone else. The Master made a gesture of flicking his eyebrows.
The monk said, "There is still a roar missing. The Master said, "I suspect it does not depend on anyone else."
A monk came, circumambulated the meditation platform once, and stood there upright. The Master said, "If this were the Dharma seat of Shitou, not even a single point would be required.
The monk circumambulated it once more. The Master said, "But at such a time as this, it is not easy to state where you have come from.
The monk then departed. The Master called out, "Upādhyāya! The monk did not look back. The Master said, "This..."

Hanshou was still in the midst of giving instructions when the monk turned his head back and said, "There is one person who does not receive it from another, who does not undergo instruction, and who does not fall into stages.
Do you, Master, grant this? The Master said, "Meeting him, yet not meeting him; if one meets him, there must be something."

The monk stepped back three paces. The Master, however, circumambulated the meditation seat once. The monk said, "Not only is the eye of the school made clear, but the lineage of the teacher is also well-founded.
The Master struck him three times with his staff.
The Master asked a monk, “Where have you come from? He replied, “From the Kòngshí Hermitage at Jiuhua.
The Master said, “Who is the hermitage master? He replied, “A venerable elder under Mazu. The Master said, “What is his name? He replied, “I do not know his name.
The Master said, “He does not know you; you do not know him. He asked, “Where are the eyes of that venerable elder? The Master said, “If it were the hermitage master himself...”

"Come! You must also receive a blow. [The monk] said, "Fortunately, I have encountered the Master, who has let me pass. The Master said, "A hundred years from now, it will be difficult to find even a single monk like you."
Xuedou said: "It is so; both are masters of the craft. Yet they do not know how to seize the tiger's tail;
they only know how to grip the tiger's head. If Deshan’s command were put into effect, both would have to crumble like tiles."
The Master asked, "Li Xingpo, do you remember the events when we were in Jangzhou? The old woman replied, "Were it not for the Master, I would not know.
The Master said, "Much is empty and little is real. The old woman said, "What is there to hide? The Master said, "Out of consideration that you are a woman, I let you go with your staff.
The old woman said, "I shall never see any fault in the Venerable Elder. The Master said, "Where does the old monk’s fault lie?"
The Master asked, "Where? The old woman said, "Since the Master has no fault, how could I have any fault? The Master asked, "What is it like for one who has no fault?
The old woman raised her fist and said, "In this way and not in this way—both result in inversion. The Master said, "Truly, there is nowhere to hide."
Dashi Chan Master Dachu of Tanzhou (Case 1) asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Jiangling. The Master said, "When did you set out?
The monk lifted up his sitting cloth (*kaṣāya*). The Master said, "Thank you for coming from so far; go down. The monk circled the meditation seat once and then departed.
The Master said, "If it were not like this, how could one know the true measure of the eye? The monk clapped his hands once.
The monk below said, “It would have killed me; it was almost a wrongful judgment by the various quarters. The Master said, “You have grasped the principles of the Chan school very well.
Later, the monk reported this to Danxia. Danxia said, “Dachuan’s way of the Dharma is acceptable, but here with me it is not so.
The monk asked, “How is it here in your monastery, Master? Danxia said, “It is still three steps ahead of Dachuan. The monk bowed. Danxia—
It is said: "Many have misjudged the various quarters.
Dongshan said: "If it were not for Danxia, it would also be difficult to distinguish jade from stone.
Regarding the Venerable Dadian of Chaozhou (five instances): he first visited Shitou. Shitou asked, "Which one is your mind?"
The Master said, "He who sees words is [the one]. Mazu then gave a shout and sent him out.

After ten days had passed, the Master went to the abbot’s quarters and asked about their previous conversation, saying, "Since that was not it, apart from this, what is the mind? Mazu said, "Set aside raising eyebrows and blinking eyes;
bring me the mind. The Master said, "There is no mind to be brought forth. Mazu said, "So, you originally have a mind!"
"How can you say it does not exist? To deny the existence of the mind is equally a slander. Upon these words, the Master attained a realization. He addressed the assembly, saying:
"A student of the Way must recognize their own original mind. Only by pointing to the nature of that mind can one truly see the Way.
I see many of our contemporaries who merely recognize a raised eyebrow, a movement of the eyes, a single word, or a moment of silence, and immediately grant their seal of approval."
This is the essential core of the mind. This has truly not been understood. I shall now clearly explain it for all of you;
each of you must listen and receive it. Simply eliminate all deluded movements of thought, views, and measurements, and that is your true mind.

This mind has no interaction whatsoever with sensory objects, nor even with the state of maintaining or recognizing silent stillness. This very mind is the Buddha; there is no need for cultivation or refinement. Why?

For this reason, responding to conditions and illuminating accordingly, it functions with a clear, cool autonomy. When one exhaustively investigates the locus of its functioning, it is utterly ungraspable.
To call this "sublime function" is precisely the original mind; it must be guarded and sustained with great care, and must not be treated lightly.
Master Shuikong arrived. The Master seized his sitting mat and said, "There is no need to exchange seasonal greetings, nor is there any need to state where you have come from.
Shuikong said, "I intended to do so, yet I feared it would be insufficient as a matter of human courtesy. The Master let go of the mat and said, "Is it sufficient now?
Shuikong lifted up his sitting mat and said, "If I were to exchange seasonal greetings, I would fear losing track of where I came from. The Master said, "For a moment..."
"It is no hindrance to meet at such a time.

The Master, using "itching" as a means of harmony, was walking along the corridor when he encountered a monk who offered him greetings. The Master, still using "itching" as a means of harmony, struck him across the mouth.
"Do you understand? he asked. [The official] said, "I do not. The Master said, "The old wild fox Dadian has never failed anyone.
When the Minister Han Yu, Duke Wen, asked the Master how many years he had been in the Way, the Master held up his rosary and asked, "Do you understand?"
Yu said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "One hundred and eight times, day and night. Yu was at a loss for words. Upon returning home, he was dejected and unhappy.
His wife asked, "Minister, you seem troubled; what else has happened? Yu recounted the previous conversation. The wife said:
"Why do you not go forward and say: 'One hundred and eight times, day and night. What is the meaning of this?
The next morning at dawn, Han Yu went again. Upon reaching the gate, he met the Head Seat (Śrāmaṇera). The Head Seat said, "Minister, why have you come to the temple so early?

Han Yu said, "I have come specifically to converse with the Abbot. The Head Seat asked, "What is the matter? Han Yu recounted the previous conversation. The Head Seat asked, "How do you understand it, Minister? Han Yu—
[Zhao] Yun said, "A hundred and eight times day and night—what is the meaning of this? The Head Seat knocked on his teeth three times. He then went to the Abbot’s quarters and repeated the question.
The Master also knocked on his teeth three times. [Zhao] Yun said, "I now know that the Buddha-dharma is one and the same. The Master said, "What principle is there in that?
Yun said, "Just now at the gate, when I asked the Head Seat, it was also like this. The Master called for the Head Seat.
Question: "Was what you just said in response to the Minister regarding the Buddha-dharma correct? The Master replied, "Yes. The Master then struck him and immediately drove him out.
Baoning Yong composed a verse on this: "One step has barely been taken when the second is shifted; The phoenix is startled from before the gate."
The child’s traces do not rest upon the wutong tree; flocks of birds circle its branches in vain from east to west.
Fenzhou Shilou Heshang (Two Cases): A monk asked, “I do not yet recognize my original nature; I beg the Master for a skillful means. The Master said, “Shilou has no ears.
The monk said, “I know myself that I am at fault. The Master said, “I, the old monk, also have my faults.”
The monk said, "Where does the Master's fault lie? The Master said, "The fault lies in your being in the wrong place. The monk bowed, and the Master struck him.

The Master asked another monk, "Where have you recently come from? He replied, "From the land of Han. The Master said, "Does the Son of Heaven in the land of Han hold the Buddha-dharma in high esteem?"
"No. The monk said, "Alas! It is fortunate that I was questioned; had you questioned anyone else, disaster would have ensued. The Master asked, "Why is that?
The monk said, "Since I do not even see a person, what Dharma of the Buddha could there be to value?
The Master said, "How many years since you received the precepts, *ācārya*? The monk said, "Twenty summer retreats. The Master said, "Excellent! Not seeing a person," and he struck him.
Xuedou said: "This monk has indeed received the blow; however, he has gone and will not return.
Although Shilou’s command was carried out, alas, it was like stirring up waves where there was no wind.
Chan Master Fotuoxun of Fengxiang Prefecture (three cases). When Mishu arrived with his assembly to pay a visit, the Master pulled over his rope bed and sat facing the wall.
Mishu stood behind him for a short while, then returned to the guest quarters. The Master said, "It is indeed so;

As soon as Mihu arrived, he pulled over the rope bed and sat down. The Master circumambulated the rope bed once and then returned to his quarters.
Mihu overturned the rope bed and led the assembly out.
The Master visited Layman Pang. The Layman said, "I remember a saying from when I was in my mother's womb;

The Layman said, "I told you not to analyze or rationalize it. The Master said, "This is a startling statement; how could one not be afraid?"
The Layman said, "Your master’s insight may indeed be called startling. The Master said, "By not applying intellectual reasoning, one instead achieves the true principle.
The Layman said, "This is not merely a matter of being separated by one or two lifetimes. The Master said, "As for you, monks who live on rice gruel, you may be examined and rebuked as you please."
When the Master saw the layman approaching, he closed the door and said, "An old man of great learning—do not come to meet me.
