I do not dare deceive myself. The Head (the Abbot) said, "I thought that after this, you would go to the summit of a solitary peak, build a thatched hut, and revile the Buddhas and scold the Patriarchs! Yet you are still making such remarks as these. Feng said, "I am truly [not settled]."
"Still not settled," [Baizhang] said. Baizhang asked, "If it is truly so, bring forth each point according to your understanding;

where you are correct, I will testify for you, and where you are not, I will cut it away. The Master said, "When I first arrived at Yanguan, I heard him expound the meaning of form and emptiness, and I attained a point of entry.
Baizhang said, "From now on, for thirty years, you must strictly avoid mentioning it. The Master said, "I understand."

Furthermore, regarding the verse on Dongshan’s realization of the Way while crossing water, there was a point of awakening. [Dongshan] said, "If it were like this, I would not even be able to save myself.
The Master said, "Once I asked Deshan, 'In the matter of the ancestral vehicle from of old, does a student have any share in it?
Deshan struck me with a staff and said, 'Say something! At that moment, it was as if the bottom of my bucket had fallen out."
Yunmen was about to speak when Yantou let out a thunderous shout, saying, "Have you not heard it said: 'That which enters through the gate is not the family treasure'?

Yunmen asked, "How is it, then? Yantou replied, "In the future, if you wish to propagate the Great Teaching, you must let it flow forth one by one from your own breast, so that it may cover heaven and earth. At these words, Yunmen attained realization.
He attained great enlightenment. Leaping down from his bed, he prostrated and said, "Elder brother, today is when the Path was realized at Mount Ao.
Elder brother, today is when the Path was realized at Mount Ao."
Jiaochong Guang said: "As for Yantou’s statement, 'Each and every thing flows forth from one's own breast,' tell me:
when Yunfeng attained enlightenment three times, if it flowed from his own breast, why did [Yantou] say he was still not stable?
If it did not flow from his own breast, then from where did it come?"

Come forward! Is there anyone here who can cut it off? If you can cut it off, not only will Xuefeng’s Attainment of the Way at Nao Mountain be realized, but all sentient beings throughout the entire world will simultaneously achieve perfect enlightenment. If you cannot cut it off, then what is this "Attainment of the Way at Nao Mountain"?
Even if one were to transmit the mind at Shaoshi, one would still not have seen it in a dream.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "On South Mountain there is a turtle-nosed snake; you all must watch it very carefully.
At that time, Changqing came forward and said, "In the hall today, many will lose their lives. Yunmen then took up his staff.
[The monk] lunged toward him and made a gesture of fear. The monk reported this to Xuansha. Xuansha said, "It must be Brother Leng for it to be so.
Nevertheless, I am not like that. The monk asked, "How about you, Master? Xuansha said, "What need is there for the South Mountain?"

He addressed the assembly, saying: "At Wàngzhōu Pavilion, I have already met you. At Wūshí Ridge, I have already met you.
Before the Sangha Hall, I have already met you. Later, Bǎofú asked Éhú:
"Setting aside for a moment the Sangha Hall, at which place did you meet me at Wàngzhōu Pavilion and Wūshí Ridge? Éhú took a sudden stride and returned to his quarters.
"Venerable. Baofu then entered the Sangha Hall. Xuedou said:
"Both elders were correct, yet they only knew that Xuefeng let go; they did not know that Xuefeng held fast.
Suppose a monk were to come forward and ask: 'I wonder, what would Xuedou have done? How could he [not speak]?"
This is not some other expedient. Is there anyone among you who recognizes good and ill fortune? Is there anyone at Wangzhou Pavilion or Wushan Ridge?
After a long silence, he said: "Board-carrying Chan practitioners are as numerous as hemp and millet."
He addressed the assembly, saying: "The entire earth, gathered up, is as small as a grain of millet. Thrown before you, you lacquer buckets fail to understand.
Let us beat the drum and all be invited to look!"
Changqing Ling asked Yunmen, "When Xuefeng spoke in that way, was there not a point where he could not show his head?
Yunmen said, "There was. Changqing asked, "How so? Yunmen said, "One must not take it all as the interpretation of a wild fox spirit," and added, "The mess is no small matter.
Yunguang Yue said, "It is insufficient even when compared to the peerless."
I shall further entangle you with me. [He] suddenly picks up his staff and says: "Do you see Xuefeng? *Du!* The royal decree is now strict;
no more crowding the path or seizing the market. Daguang Zhe said:
"I shall further add mud upon the earth for all of you. He then picks up the staff and says: "Look, look! The old man Xuefeng [is] before you all..."
"Defecating right before one's face. *Duh!* Why? You do not even perceive the stench of the excrement.
Xuedou’s verse says: "The ox-head vanishes and the horse-head returns; In the mirror of Caoxi, not a speck of dust remains.
Though the drum is beaten, you do not see it; When spring arrives amidst the myriad flowers, for whom do they bloom?"
He addressed the assembly, saying: "In my place here, it is like an ancient mirror: when a barbarian comes, a barbarian appears; when a Han person comes, a Han person appears.
At that time, a monk stepped forward and asked, "What happens when a bright mirror suddenly encounters [this mirror]? The Master said, "Both the barbarian and the Han person are hidden."
Xuansha said, "I do not think so. At that time, a monk asked, "If one suddenly encounters a bright mirror coming toward you, what then?
Xuansha said, "Shatter it into a hundred pieces! Mingzhao said, "At such a moment, do not say that both barbarian and Han are hidden;
how else would you speak? Xuansha said, "Broken. Mingzhao said, "Lost!"
He addressed the assembly, saying: "The entire earth is this gate of liberation. I hold out my hand to pull you in, yet you are unwilling to enter.
At that time, a monk came forward and said, "Master, you cannot blame me. Another monk said, "What is the use of entering? The Master then struck him.
Xuedou said: "Among these three, there is one who receives salvation. Suddenly, if you cannot discern them all clearly, how many are there on level ground?
He addressed the assembly, saying:
"The Buddhas of the three periods are fellows from within the weeds; the Three Sutras and Five Treatises are hitching posts for donkeys. Eight...
The ten-fascicle *Avataṃsaka* is but the talk of one who eats coarse rice at the edge of a village path;
the twelve divisions of the teachings are matters from the mouth of a frog. Do you understand? Therefore it is said:
"If among the thousands and hundreds of people today there were even one person who attained great realization, I would serve him as a donkey carrying goods—what sin would there be in that?"
Addressing the assembly, he said: "The Buddhas of the three periods have been unable to show their heads here. The entire Great Canon of Teachings cannot accommodate a single word here.
The old monks of the world are reduced to a hundredfold fragments here. Do you understand?
If you people can truly attain clarity and move forward, you will avoid being deluded by others. Even if there are words and phrases, you will not harbor doubts about them. As for yourself..."
If you have not yet attained clarity, you must not engage in empty pretense or waste your time.
Do not merely fixate on the countenances of teachers from all quarters, memorizing a word or two and imagining it to be your own realization—this is a great error.
Brothers, I say that these very three inches can kill and can give life. I often tell the monks: what is it?
"Ma! he would say, his mouth chattering on and on. How could such as these ever understand how to take responsibility?
Let me ask you, all you monks and venerable elders from all quarters: have they ever explained the matter to you, Ananda?
Have they ever pointed it out to you? Have they ever deliberated with you? You must examine this thoroughly and verify it with great care.
He addressed the assembly. After a long silence, he said: "If you can accept it just like this, it would be well to save your mental effort.
Therefore it is said: 'The Buddhas of the three periods of time cannot proclaim it; the twelve divisions of the teachings cannot describe it.
Now, as for those who merely chew on spit and saliva, how could they possibly understand it? I usually ask the monks, 'What is it? Then they come forward further, seeking an answer to my words."
"When will you ever understand? Out of necessity, I speak to you in this way; I have already deceived you.
Furthermore, I told you that even before entering the gate, we had already reached a mutual understanding. This too is the 'old woman's heart'—the point of least effort.
Yet you refuse to accept it; you only know how to step forward, seeking words and seeking phrases."

I say to you: the entire great earth is this gate of liberation, yet you refuse to enter it altogether; you merely wander aimlessly, asking about the Buddhas and the Patriarchs whenever you meet someone.
Do you have any shame? You willingly endure such humiliation. If you have truly not attained a state of awakening and entry, [then your conduct is understandable].
Do not treat this with indifference; you must truly awaken and enter into it before you can succeed. Do not let your time pass in vain; exert some spirit and vigor!
When Bodhidharma came from the West, he transmitted mind by means of mind and did not establish written words. But tell me, what is the mind of you all?
You must not simply leave things as they are in a state of confusion. If your own eye has not yet been clarified, how can you possibly exhaust such a multitude of delusions?

Reflect: within this world, there is no place for you to find peace. You will see that all who are holy—monks and laypeople, men and women, high and low, superior and inferior—are spread out before you like sand upon the great earth, clamoring and bustling. Not for a single thought-moment do they turn back their divine light;
they wander through birth and death, never ceasing throughout kalpas. You must feel deep shame and remorse; each of you must exert yourselves with diligence.

He addressed the assembly, saying: "Countless people die of thirst by the river; those who suffer hunger at the edge of a grain basket are as numerous as the sands of the Ganges—not merely one or two.
Brothers, if your faculties and thoughts falter, you must instead apply yourselves with diligent vigor."
Do not merely spend the winter here and the summer there, gathering up a few drops of mucus and spittle, and considering that to have settled the affairs of your entire life.
Any attempt to copy down or memorize [the teachings] is entirely mere intellectual learning and superficial understanding.
Such people as these, I call "guests beneath the frog’s robe," and I also call them "black oxen lying dead in stagnant water. Do you understand?
He addressed the assembly, saying: "If one discusses this matter, it is like a single plot of land. It is left entirely to everyone to plow and sow;
there is no one who does not receive the power of its bounty. Xuan Sha asked: "But tell me, what is this single plot of land?"
The Master said, "Look. Sandow said, "It is indeed so, yet I do not regard it in that way. The Master asked, "How do you understand it?
Sandow said, "It is simply what everyone possesses."

The Master spoke these words: "This matter is so noble; it is so subtle and pervasive. A monk said, "Since I first arrived at this mountain several years ago, I have heard the Master instructing his disciples in such a manner. The Master said, "Although I did not possess it before, I now do. Is there any hindrance? The monk said, "I dare not say so. This is the Master's [work]. The Master said, "Not so. The monk said, "It is indeed the Master's. The Master said, "Not so. The monk said, "How can it not be the Master's? The Master said, "If it were the Master's, you would not be able to see it. The monk said, "I am not able to see it. The Master said, "If you could see it, you would not be able to speak of it. The monk said, "I cannot speak of it. The Master said, "If you could speak of it, you would not be able to hear it. The monk said, "I cannot hear it. The Master said, "If you could hear it, you would not be able to understand it. The monk said, "I cannot understand it. The Master said, "If you could understand it, you would not be able to realize it. The monk said, "I cannot realize it. The Master said, "If you could realize it, you would not be able to attain it. The monk said, "I cannot attain it. The Master said, "If you could attain it, you would not be able to dwell in it. The monk said, "I cannot dwell in it. The Master said, "If you could dwell in it, you would not be able to depart from it. The monk said, "I cannot depart from it. The Master said, "If you could depart from it, you would not be able to transcend it. The monk said, "I cannot transcend it. The Master said, "If you could transcend it, you would not be able to return to it. The monk said, "I cannot return to it. The Master said, "If you could return to it, you would not be able to enter it. The monk said, "I cannot enter it. The Master said, "If you could enter it, you would not be able to exit it. The monk said, "I cannot exit it. The Master said, "If you could exit it, you would not be able to abide in it. The monk said, "I cannot abide in it. The Master said, "If you could abide in it, you would not be able to move within it. The monk said, "I cannot move within it. The Master said, "If you could move within it, you would not be able to rest within it. The monk said, "I cannot rest within it. The Master said, "If you could rest within it, you would not be able to awaken within it. The monk said, "I cannot awaken within it. The Master said, "If you could awaken within it, you would not be able to manifest it. The monk said, "I cannot manifest it. The Master said, "If you could manifest it, you would not be able to conceal it. The monk said, "I cannot conceal it. The Master said, "If you could conceal it, you would not be able to reveal it. The monk said, "I cannot reveal it. The Master said, "If you could reveal it, you would not be able to grasp it. The monk said, "I cannot grasp it. The Master said, "If you could grasp it, you would not be able to let it go. The monk said, "I cannot let it go. The Master said, "If you could let it go, you would not be able to hold onto it. The monk said, "I cannot hold onto it. The Master said, "If you could hold onto it, you would not be able to abandon it. The monk said, "I cannot abandon it. The Master said, "If you could abandon it, you would not be able to embrace it. The monk said, "I cannot embrace it. The Master said, "If you could embrace it, you would not be able to release it. The monk said, "I cannot release it. The Master said, "If you could release it, you would not be able to bind it. The monk said, "I cannot bind it. The Master said, "If you could bind it, you would not be able to untie it. The monk said, "I cannot untie it. The Master said, "If you could untie it, you would not be able to tie it again. The monk said, "I cannot tie it again. The Master said, "If you could tie it again, you would not be able to cut it. The monk said, "I cannot cut it. The Master said, "If you could cut it, you would not be able to join it. The monk said, "I cannot join it. The Master said, "If you could join it, you would not be able to separate it. The monk said, "I cannot separate it. The Master said, "If you could separate it, you would not be able to unite it. The monk said, "I cannot unite it. The Master said, "If you could unite it, you would not be able to disperse it. The monk said, "I cannot disperse it. The Master said, "If you could disperse it, you would not be able to gather it. The monk said, "I cannot gather it. The Master said, "If you could gather it, you would not be able to scatter it. The monk said, "I cannot scatter it. The Master said, "If you could scatter it, you would not be able to collect it. The monk said, "I cannot collect it. The Master said, "If you could collect it, you would not be able to lose it. The monk said, "I cannot lose it. The Master said, "If you could lose it, you would not be able to find it. The monk said, "I cannot find it. The Master said, "If you could find it, you would not be able to forget it. The monk said, "I cannot forget it. The Master said, "If you could forget it, you would not be able to remember it. The monk said, "I cannot remember it. The Master said, "If you could remember it, you would not be able to know it. The monk said, "I cannot know it. The Master said, "If you could know it, you would not be able to see it. The monk said, "I cannot see it. The Master said, "If you could see it, you would not be able to hear it. The monk said, "I cannot hear it. The Master said, "If you could hear it, you would not be able to speak of it. The monk said, "I cannot speak of it. The Master said, "If you could speak of it, you would not be able to hear it. The monk said, "I cannot hear it. The Master said, "If you could hear it, you would not be able to understand it. The monk said, "I cannot understand it. The Master said, "If you could understand it, you would not be able to realize it. The monk said, "I cannot realize it. The Master said, "If you could realize it, you would not be able to attain it. The monk said, "I cannot attain it. The Master said, "If you could attain it, you would not be able to dwell in it. The monk said, "I cannot dwell in it. The Master said, "If you could dwell in it, you would not be able to depart from it. The monk said, "I cannot depart from it. The Master said, "If you could depart from it, you would not be able to transcend it. The monk said, "I cannot transcend it. The Master said, "If you could transcend it, you would not be able to return to it. The monk said, "I cannot return to it. The Master said, "If you could return to it, you would not be able to enter it. The monk said, "I cannot enter it. The Master said, "If you could enter it, you would not be able to exit it. The monk said, "I cannot exit it. The Master said, "If you could exit it, you would not be able to abide in it. The monk said, "I cannot abide in it. The Master said, "If you could abide in it, you would not be able to move within it. The monk said, "I cannot move within it. The Master said, "If you could move within it, you would not be able to rest within it. The monk said, "I cannot rest within it. The Master said, "If you could rest within it, you would not be able to awaken within it. The monk said, "I cannot awaken within it. The Master said, "If you could awaken within it, you would not be able to manifest it. The monk said, "I cannot manifest it. The Master said, "If you could manifest it, you would not be able to conceal it. The monk said, "I cannot conceal it. The Master said, "If you could conceal it, you would not be able to reveal it. The monk said, "I cannot reveal it. The Master said, "If you could reveal it, you would not be able to
"Once attained, it is already so.
One day, while sitting before the Sangha hall, the Master picked up his staff and said, "This is for those of middling and inferior capacities.
At that time, a monk asked, "What if someone of superior capacity should come? The Master picked up his staff.
Yunmen said, "I am not like Xuefeng, who merely cleared up the mess. A monk then asked, "In what way, then, did you, Master, do so?

The Master struck him. Later, while the Master was in session, a monk bowed respectfully with "Chanzhong" (take care) and departed. The Master said, "If everyone were like this monk, I would save myself much effort."
[The Master] had little strength of mind. Xuansha said, "If you act as a teacher in this way, you will blind the eyes of everyone in the city of Min.
The Master asked, "And what about you? Xuansha said, "You should have given him thirty blows. The Master said, "In the future, no one will be able to do anything with you."
One day, the Master ascended the hall. When the assembly had gathered, the Master rolled out a wooden mat. Xuansha then seized it and placed it back in its original position.
Baizhang Yuan said, "At this moment, everyone says that father and son have together performed one great [act]."
"Regarding this matter: have you ever seen such a vision even in a dream? Today Baiyun bestows upon the great assembly, saying:
'He grinds fragrant ink thickly and dips his purple-hair brush deep.'"

During the evening session, the Master lay down in the middle courtyard. Upādhāya Fu of Taiyuan remarked, "Within the jurisdiction of the Five Prefectures, there is only this old monk who has a modicum of worth. The Master then rose and departed.
One day, while inside the Sangha Hall, the Master closed the door and lit a fire, then cried out, "Put out the fire! Put out the fire!
Xuansha took a piece of firewood and threw it in through the window lattice; the Master immediately opened the door.

The Master was leading his disciples on a southern tour. At that time, Huang Niepan (Yellow Nirvana) had foreknowledge of this; he took up his staff and went out to meet him. Upon reaching Suxi, they encountered one another by chance.
The Master asked, "Where have you recently departed from? He replied, "From Pizhi Rock. The Master said, "Is there still a master within that rock?
Niepan struck the Master’s sedan chair with his bamboo staff. The Master then stepped out of the chair to meet him. Niepan said, "Greetings, Elder Lang! The Master extended his staff.
Regarding ritual propriety (*li*), Pan performed the woman’s bow. The Master asked, "Are you a woman?

Pan then performed two prostrations and, using a bamboo staff, traced lines on the ground while circumambulating the Master’s palanquin three times to the right. The Master said, "I am a person within the triple world."
"You are one who stands outside the three realms; you should go on ahead. I shall follow later. Baopan then returned first.
The Master subsequently arrived at Zhinan Mountain, where he rested for several days. Baopan provided for his traveling disciples with everything necessary, lacking nothing at all.
The Master escorted Elder Nanji to the gate. Upon reaching the door, he performed a woman’s bow. Nanji folded his hands and responded with an "Amen.
The Master struck his forehead with his hand and then returned home.
When the Master arrived at Guoqing, he held up his alms bowl and asked the presiding lecturer (zuozhu), "If you can say something, I will give you this bowl.

The lecturer said, "This is the business of the transformation Buddha" (Xuedou offers an alternative: "I fear it would simply leave the Master at a loss"). The Master said, "Even being a servant to a lecturer, you have not attained that yet.
The lecturer said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "You ask, and I will tell you. Just as the lecturer was about to bow, the Master [struck him].
With one step, he tripped and fell. The master brought this up to Yunmen, saying, "It took me seven years before I saw it.
Yunmen said, "Did it take you seven years to see it? The master replied, "Yes. Yunmen said, "Wait another seven years before you truly attain it."
Xuedou said, "The grass-thief is defeated.
Xuansha asked, "I am now about to employ the Great Function; how will you respond, Master? The Master took up three wooden balls.
At once he rolled it out; the sand formed the shape of a chopping board. The Master said, "Only because you have come from Vulture Peak yourself can you act like this.
Sanda said, "It is simply my own thing."
There was a monk who had established a hermitage at the foot of a mountain. For many years he had not shaved his head and kept a long-handled ladle, drawing water from a stream.
When someone asked him, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? the monk held up the ladle and said, "The stream is deep and the handle of the ladle is long.
Hearing of this, the Master remarked, "That is quite extraordinary. One day, with a razor tucked in his sleeve, he went to visit him accompanied by an attendant.
As soon as he saw them, he asked: "If you can speak, I will not shave your heads. The monk then washed his head, knelt before the Master, and the Master shaved it off for him.
One day, two monks arrived; the Master propped himself against the gate of the hermitage with his hands and, leaning his body out, said: "What is this? The monks [remained silent].
He also asked, "What is it? The Master lowered his head and returned to his hut. Later, when the monk took his leave, the Master asked, "Where are you going?
The monk replied, "I am going to Hunan. The Master said, "I have a fellow practitioner there who resides at Yantou;
I will entrust this letter to you. The Master wrote in the letter: "From the time after I attained the Way on Mount Ao, until now—"
Nowadays, people eat until they are full and never stop. A fellow practitioner, [named] So-and-so, who had faith in his elder brother teacher, arrived at Yantou.
Yantou asked, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From Lingnan. Yantou asked, "Have you ever been to Xuefeng? He replied, "I left there recently; Xuefeng sent a letter for the Master.
After Yantou finished reading the letter, he asked again, "What words or phrases did the Master say? The monk then related what had occurred previously.
The Master asked, "What did he say? The monk replied, "He was speechless and bowed his head as he returned to his hut.
The Master said, "Alas! I regretted at first that I did not tell him the 'final word. Had I told him, no one in the world could have done anything with Old Xue.

At the end of the summer retreat, the monk requested further instruction on this previous matter. The Master said, "Why did you not ask earlier? The monk replied, "I did not dare to wait [for the opportunity]."
Yi said: "Xuefeng was born of the same lineage as I, yet he did not die of the same lineage as I.
If you wish to recognize the final word, it is simply this."
Daguizhe said, "The great Xuefeng and Yantou were both exposed by this monk.
Xuedou’s verse says: "The final word, I shall tell you for your sake: At the moment when light and dark are paired together, Those born of the same root know one another;
Those dead of different roots are utterly severed. Utterly severed—Huangtou!"
"Those with azure eyes must discern: go, return, south, north, east, or west. At night deep, we shall view the snow upon a thousand crags together.
The Master asked a monk, "I have heard it said that you, Venerable One, once came as a celestial messenger—is this true? He replied, "I dare not say so. The Master said, "How so?"
[The monk] understood [the situation] as he approached. He said, "I have long admired your virtue and character; how could I have feared the mountain passes?

The Master said, "You are still drunk; get out! The monk then departed. The Master called out to him again, "Virtuous One! The monk turned his head. The Master asked, "What is it? The monk also said, "What is it?
The Master said, "This lacquer bucket! The monk was speechless. The Master looked back at Jingqing and said, "What a fine one!"
The Master said, "The teacher-monk has ended up inside a lacquer bucket. Qing said, "Does this not mean, Preceptor, that you have reached a verdict based on the facts?
The Master said, "This is also what I use for my daily practice. He added, "Suppose he were suddenly called back and asked, 'What is this?
and he replied, 'This lacquer bucket'—then what would you do? Qing said, "How could that possibly be reasonable? The Master said, "I am like this..."
[The Master] said, "And 'yi' (and). You also say that the case was settled based on the evidence; he treats me in such a manner, yet you ask, 'What principle does this establish?
At one and the same time, why is it that some attain it while others do not? Qing said, "Have you not heard it said:
'The supreme flavor of clarified butter is prized by the world, yet when encountered by such people, it turns instead into a poisonous drug'?"
Xuedou said: "Look at this father and son; their words and spirits accord. Those who understand it say that even grinding one's bones to powder cannot repay such kindness.
Those who do not understand it say that he elevates the high and suppresses the low, striking terror into people at a moment of peril.
It is like poison or nectar—a mirror for a thousand ages. Do you understand? This lacquer bucket!"
The Master, because the monk had prostrated, struck him five blows. The monk said, "What fault have I committed? The Master struck him another five blows. Xuedou said:
"I have never entangled myself in complications with others. As for the first five blows, the sun shines upon heaven; as for the latter..."
"Five blows! Clouds rise and rain falls. If you can discern this, I shall likewise give you five blows.
A monk bowed and took his leave. The Master asked, "Where are you going? He replied, "I am going to pay my respects at Mount Jing.
The Master said, "If Mount Jing suddenly asks you, 'How is the Buddha-dharma here? how will you respond? The monk said, "I will speak when I am asked. The Master—
[The Master] struck him. Then he looked back at Jingqing and said, "Where did this monk go wrong that he received a blow?
Jingqing said, "He asked about Jingshan until he was utterly exhausted. The Master said, "Jingshan is in Zhejiang; why did he ask until he was utterly exhausted?
Jingqing said, "Have you not heard it said: 'A distant question receives a proximate answer'? The Master then desisted.
The Master called to a monk. The monk responded with an assent. The Master said, "Come closer. The monk stepped forward. The Master said, "Go.
Yunmen raised this up and asked a monk, "How would you express it? Can you utter the phrase of 'joined palms'?
If you can utter the phrase of 'joined palms,' then you will see Xuefeng."
The Master asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Zhejiang. The Master said, "Did you come by boat or by land?
The monk said, "I did not take either of those two paths. The Master said, "How then did you get here? The monk said, "What obstacle could there be?
The Master struck him and drove him out. Ten years later, the monk came again. The Master asked, "Where have you come from? The monk said, "From Hunan. The Master said, "Hunan and..."
"How far is it from here? [The monk] replied, "It is not far. The Master held up his whisk and said, "Is it still separated by this?
He added, "If it were separated, you would not have arrived. The Master then struck him and drove him out. Afterward, whenever the monk saw anyone, he would scold them.
A fellow practitioner heard of this and went specifically to visit him, asking, "Brother, when you reached Xuefeng, what words or phrases did he say?"
This was so. He reviled him incessantly, until the monk finally recounted the previous conversation. His traveling companion then rebuked him, whereupon he confessed the truth to him.
The monk wept bitterly; from then on, he would burn incense at night and prostrate himself from afar to repent his transgressions.
The Master asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk replied, "From Fu-xian. The Master said, "You have not yet crossed the sea of birth and death;
why then have you overturned your boat? The monk was speechless.
Xuedou spoke on his behalf: "He has long been renowned as Xuefeng. As soon as that old fellow hesitated, he shook out his sleeves and departed.
Later, a monk cited this to Fushan. Fushan said, "Why did you not say, 'He is beyond birth and death'?
The monk went back and offered these words. The Master said, "This is not your own speech. The monk said, "It was Fushan’s speech. The Master said, "I have twenty..."
"Strike! Send this blow back to the boat. Twenty blows—this old monk shall drink them himself;
it is no concern of yours, *ācārya*. Xuedou added a comment: "He can distinguish and differentiate; he can kill and give life. If you can discern this, you may roam freely throughout the world."

The Master asked a monk, "Where are you going? The monk replied, "If you recognize it, you will know where I am going. The Master said, "You are a man who understands matters; why are you wandering about so restlessly?
The monk said, "Master, do not smear me with false accusations. The Master said, "I am not smearing you at all."
"The ancients blew on a cloth-hair; what was that? Tell me and I shall see. [The monk] said, "Leftover soup and stale rice—someone has already eaten it. The Master then withdrew.
Yunmen commented on the previous statement, saying: "To strike it is to produce the stench of excrement. He further provided a substitute for the subsequent statement, saying:
"I thought this was a falcon piercing the heavens; it turns out to be a frog in stagnant water."
Xuedou quoted Xuefeng as saying, "Once dead, one does not live again.

The Master asked a monk, "What is your name? The monk replied, "Xuánjī (Mysterious Mechanism). The Master said, "How much do you weave each day? The monk replied, "Not a single thread hangs [upon me]."
The Master said, "Go to the hall. As soon as the monk had walked three or five paces, the Master said, "Your kashaya has fallen to the ground.
The monk turned his head back; the Master struck him and said, "How excellent—completely naked!"
The Master saw the monk and called out, "Come closer. The monk approached. The Master asked, "Where are you going? He replied, "I am going on the communal work detail (*pǔqǐng*).
The Master said, "Go."
Yunmen said, "This is merely recognizing a person by their words.
The Master asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Jiangxi. The Master said, "How far is it from Jiangxi to here?"
[The monk] said, "It is not far. The Master held up his whisk and said, "Is it still separated by this? [The monk] said, "If it were separated, then it would be far.

The Master then struck him out. The Master asked a monk, "Where have you come from? [The monk] said, "From Huiri (Wisdom Sun). The Master said, "When you came, had the sun risen yet? [The monk] said, "If the sun..."
[The monk] went out. [Dongshan] immediately dissolved the matter of Xuefeng. The Master retired.
The Master asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? He replied, "From Mount Gui. The Master said, "What words or phrases did Mount Gui have?
He said, "I once asked him, 'What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Mount Gui sat there crouching. The Master said, "Do you approve of him?"
[The monk] said he was unwilling. The Master said, "Taiso is a descendant of an ancient Buddha; go quickly to pay him homage and repent. A monk reported this to Xuansha.
Xuansha said, "That old fellow on the mountain has missed the mark, yet he does not even realize it. The monk asked, "I do not know what your honorable intention is, Master.
Xuansha said, "Great Taiso would have been reduced to a hundred fragments by this monk’s single question."
A monk asked, "The śrāvaka perceives nature like seeing the moon at night; the bodhisattva perceives nature like seeing the sun by day.
I wonder, Master, how do you perceive nature? The Master struck him three times with his staff. Later, that same monk asked Yantou, who struck him three times with his palm.
Xuedou said, "Prescribing medicine according to the illness, I shall give you three blows. But if one were to act strictly according to the rule, how many blows would it take?

A monk asked, "What is it like when there is a cold spring in an ancient ravine? The Master said, "Staring with wide-open eyes, one cannot see the bottom. The monk said, "As for those who drink from it..."

"What? the Master asked. The monk said, "It does not enter through the mouth. Later, the monk cited this to Zhaozhou. Zhaozhou said, "Since it does not enter through the mouth, it cannot enter through the nostrils.
The monk then restated his previous question. Zhaozhou said, "Suffering. When the monk uttered the subsequent words, Zhaozhou said, "Dead.
The Master heard of this and, looking toward him from afar, paid homage, saying, "Zhaozhou is an ancient Buddha. From that time on, he no longer answered questions.
Xuedou said: "In the assembly, everyone deliberates by saying that Xuefeng did not respond to the monk’s question;
therefore, Zhaozhou did not approve. To interpret the matter in such a way is to deeply wrong the ancients. Xuedou, however, does not think so."
Decisive as a sword cutting through iron. A master of the fundamental school who brings down the high with the low—truly difficult to emulate.
Tianyi Huai said: "O virtuous ones, how do you understand the principle of 'not answering'?
While it is not that I do not praise Zhaozhou, do you know where a flaw has appeared in Zhaozhou’s jade? If one examines this...

He was able to discern it. When Sima Qian did not deceive the King of Qin, a monk asked, "What is it like when a cowherd can both sing and dance? The Master descended from his rope seat and performed a dance. Xuansha said:
"This old fellow has not even set foot on the ground," the Master said. The monk asked, "And what about you, sir?
Xuansha then clapped his hands three times.
Another monk asked, "I beg the Master for instruction. The Master said, "What is it? At these words, the monk attained great enlightenment.
Yunmen asked, "What did Xuefeng say to him? The monk replied, "He said, 'The master has finished building the niche for you.
The Master said, "Bring it here. The monk said, "Venerable Sir, the niche is completed. The Master said, "Carry it in."
The coffin was placed before the hall and carried in by the monks. As soon as the Master saw it, he asked the assembly, "If you can utter the First Phrase, I shall keep it.
He asked this twice. A monk stepped forward and said, "I, [Name], ask the Master. The Master then shouted, "Do not make a fuss!
and immediately had the coffin burned.
*The Essential Record of the Linked Lamps*, Scroll Twenty-one:
In the early years of the Qiandao era, while I was a guest at Mount Jiangshan in Jiankang, I happened to meet an elderly monk from Quanzhou who possessed a record of Yantou.
Upon reading it, I saw him ask a monk, "Where are you going? to which the monk replied, "I am entering the mountains to pay my respects."
Xuefeng departed. Yantou said, "If Xuefeng asks you, 'What about Yantou?', simply tell him:
'Lately Yantou has been living by the lake; for only three coins, he bought a fishing net.'"
"Netting shrimp, crabs, and clams—just passing the time like this. Because he asked the old monk about it, I read the *Record of Yantou*.
In his original text, all instances are written as "lǎopó" (老婆), whereas here it says "lāobō" (撈波). Why is that? He laughed and said, "Lǎopó is an error.
Yantou and Xuefeng were both countrymen; in my home village, the bamboo tool used for netting shrimp is called 'lāobō'."

The local people have called him by this name to this day. Later generations misheard it and changed it to the word "old woman" (lǎopó), leading people to interpret it solely as a metaphor for Chan practice.
Yantou’s record has the original text as "buying a wife and children," while Xuefeng’s record changes it to "buying an old woman.
Later, Zhenjing cited this and said: "I will simply use a single coin..."
"Money. He marries a black wife. This is what is meant by the saying: 'After a document has been transcribed three times, the character for "crow" (烏) becomes "horse" (馬).
Although this holds no significance for the Zen school, it is something one must understand. Chan Master Xuefeng Kung’s verse says: 'Three coins for a catch from the waves; the ages have grown deep.
Transformed, she has become an old woman, black and ugly. This is because there is a specific meaning in the local dialect."
"It is not known; there is no cause for wonder. As a proverb in Fuzhou says: 'To beat wild piles' means to engage in a chaotic scuffle over a pile of wood.
Now, in Mingzhao’s records, it is written as 'to beat wild firebrands' (*yězhāi*). Later, in Yuanwu’s *Biyanji*, the commentary explains:
'Wild firebrands' refers to the tips of firewood sticks that could not be burned on the mountain. This may be compared to the Elder..."
Po. One case has been concluded.
*Lian Deng Hui Yao*, Volume 22, compiled by the monk Wuming, a successor to the Patriarchs residing at Chongfu Chan Temple in Quanzhou.
The Sixth Generation under Qingyuan;
the Dharma heir of Chan Master Xuanjian of Deshan in Dingzhou.
[Recorded by] Monk Waguan of Quanzhou (Total: One). While the Master was at Deshan, he served as an attendant. Deshan was about to chop some wood.
Shan held out a bowl of water and offered it to the Master. The Master accepted it and drank it. Shan asked, "Do you understand? The Master said, "I do not understand.
Shan again held out a bowl of water and offered it to the Master. The Master accepted it and drank it once more. Shan asked, "Do you understand now?"
The Master said, "I do not understand. Mount said, "Why do you not strip away that which does not understand? The Master said, "If one does not understand, what is there to strip away?
Mount said, "It is very much like an iron stake. After the Master had taken up residence [at Yunmen], Xuefeng visited him.
During a conversation over tea, Xuefeng asked, "Regarding the incident from years ago at Deshan when you were cutting wood—what was it about? The Master said, "My late teacher..."
At that time, he agreed with me. Feng said, "The Master left the Former Teacher too soon. At that moment, there was a bowl of water before him.
Feng said, "Bring the water here. The Master passed it to Feng; as soon as Feng received it, he poured it out.
Yunmen said, "Do not degrade the noble into the base.
Chan Master Gao Ting Jian of Xiangzhou (Case 1): When the Master first met Deshan, he was sitting on the riverbank.
From across the river, the Master offered his greetings. Deshan beckoned him with a fan, and the Master suddenly attained realization; he strode across the water sideways and did not return.
He crossed the river and returned to Gaoting to serve as abbot.
There, he met the monk Tanziguo of Danning in Hongzhou (Case 1), who came from Baimiao to inquire about him. At that time, a funeral was being held in his household.
He requested the Master to offer his condolences. The Master said, "Alas, the heavens! What agony! The monk asked, "Is it my father who has died?
Is it my mother who has died? The Master then struck him with his staff. Whenever monks came to see him, the Master would frequently drive them away with his staff.

Chan Master Jiufeng Daogyan of Yunchou, successor to Chan Master Shishuang Qingzhu of Tanzhou (five cases total). He was the son of the Liu family of Fuzhou. The Master served as the attendant to Shishuang.
After Shishuang passed away, the assembly requested the First Seat to succeed him. The Master said, "One must first understand the late master’s meaning before one may do so."
Zuo said, "What was the meaning of the former master? The Master said, "The former master said: 'Rest! Cease! A single thought for ten thousand years!
Like cold ashes or withered wood! Like an incense burner in an ancient temple! Like a cold, still pool! Like a single strand of white silk! What do you say to this?
Zuo said, "This clarifies the matter of the 'one color' (monochromatic) side. The Master said, "So you truly do not understand the former master."
The Master’s intention was this. The Head Seat said, "Do you not approve of me? He then prepared incense.
The Head Seat burned the incense and said, "If I do not understand the late Master’s intention, may I not be able to depart as soon as the smoke rises. Indeed, he departed following the rising smoke.
The Master patted his back and said, "To die sitting or standing—this is certainly no small feat for the Head Seat. Yet, as for the late Master’s intention, you have not even dreamed of it."

Nanhuabing said: "Having penetrated the barrier of birth and death, one transcends far beyond the mundane world; wielding the sword that kills or gives life, one stands alone at the center of the universe.
Were it not for the clear illumination of the eye of wisdom, one could not avoid leaning on a fence or groping along a wall. Do you wish to understand?
The spring orchid and the autumn chrysanthemum each flourish in their own season."
A monk asked, "What kind of practice does one who dwells in the Avīci Hell perform? The Master said, "The practice of a beast.
The monk asked, "And what practice does a beast perform? The Master said, "The practice of Avīci. The monk said, "This is still someone on the path of long life.

The Master said, "You must know there is that which does not share the same life-force. The monk asked, "With what life-force does it not share? The Master said, "The life-force of the long-lived is not constant. The Master said.
He spoke again: "Do you still recognize life? If you wish to know life, flowing springs are life and profound stillness is the body.
A thousand waves rising in competition is the realm of Mañjuśrī; a single expanse of clear sky is the couch of Samantabhadra. Furthermore, borrowing a single phrase is like pointing at the moon;
within it, the actual matter is like talking about the moon. The matters of the ancestral school of the Gate are like those of a military governor.

The banner of faith is similar. For instance, before the masters of various quarters had established so many categories and designations, and prior to their detailed explanations—brothers, upon what basis would you have deliberated?
At this point, without relying on the three inches [of the tongue], try to speak!
Do not rely on the faculty of hearing; try to listen and see. Do not rely on the faculty of sight; try to discern and observe. Therefore it is said:
"Before sound, nothing can be cast out; after a phrase, no form is concealed. Throughout the entire universe, everything is entirely your own original essence.

Where do you direct your eyes, ears, nose, and tongue? If you attempt to calculate and form an intellectual understanding within the faculty of the mind, you will reach no end of realization throughout the limits of the future.
Therefore, Master Dongshan said: "If you intend to study the profound mystery with the mind and intellect..."
"It appears as if heading west, yet it turns toward the east. Take care.
A monk asked, "I have heard your teacher’s words that although various sages appear from time to time, they are merely people who transmit messages. Is this so? The Master said:

[The student] said, "It is so. Why is it that when the World-Honored One pointed one finger toward heaven and one finger toward the earth, saying, 'Heaven and earth, heaven and earth—only I am alone honored,' he was called a person who merely transmits words?
The Master said, "Precisely because he pointed one finger toward heaven and one finger toward the earth, he was called a person who transmits words."
A monk asked, "What is one's own self? The Master said, "Ask anyone else. The monk asked, "If one accepts it directly as such, what then?
The Master said, "One cannot place Mount Sumeru upon Mount Sumeru."
A monk asked, "Master, why was it that even with a single stroke of the brush, Zhiyi could not capture the true likeness of Master Zhigong?

The Master said, "Xiaowu Zengyou, however, did grant his approval to Zhigong. The monk asked, "Why did Zengyou grant his approval to Zhigong? The Master said, "The tortoise bows its head to the pillar of Mount Sumeru."

Chan Master Jingxin of Yongquan in Taizhou (Four Parts) addressed the assembly, saying: "If one relies on worldly conditions as a secondary support, these are all matters of the gate of a thousand differences.
When the two thoughts of good and evil have not yet arisen, that is the Dharma-body. As soon as they arise, it belongs to the Reward-body; the Reward-body belongs to the Transformation-body.
One transformation leads to a thousand transformations. I say that where [all things] reach their end is the body, and where there is emptiness is the seat. Ten thousand...

The garment of action is simply called the "three periods. When causes are perfected and fruits are fulfilled, this is the place where Bodhi is established. It reaches the point where even a layperson attains the rank of Chancellor;

where Sudhana, the Dragon Girl, and the butcher Pāṇḍuka cast down their weapons and immediately proceed. This is indeed the Perfect and Sudden One Vehicle, yet it is still the Pure Land of ordinary people.
It is also called "attaining the position of succession in one lifetime. It reaches the point where there is no fixed direction and all objects of perception are severed.
Not being restricted by any particular thing is itself the ignorance of the Buddha-ground. If it were that [consciousness], how could it ever consent to sit fixed within a specific location?

I say: when going out, it does not follow after objects; when entering, it does not dwell in emptiness. To internally realize and see stillness is to fall into guarding the aggregates (*skandha*); to externally realize and perceive emptiness is likewise a delusion.
If one perceives existence, one falls into eternalism; if one perceives non-existence, one falls into nihilism. To perceive neither existence nor non-existence is to fall into the Middle Way.
If you do not understand this matter, you will be carried away entirely by the realms of humans and devas. You must take heed of this; do not treat it with indifference.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "In my forty years here, I still have moments of deviation.
You all must not open your mouths too wide. Those with intellectual understanding are many; those who possess both realization and practice are not even one or half of a person in ten thousand.

Intellectual understanding and verbal proficiency are matters that all must master. If your recognition is not complete, I dare say you will surely return to the cycle of rebirth. Why is this so? It is because..."

Because the outflows (*āsrava*) of consciousness have not yet been exhausted, you need only exhaust them in this very moment, and you will immediately achieve realization; this is also called "establishing merit within.
To turn that merit over to others is also called "transferring merit to reach them directly. This is why I say: "The one who reaches others cannot be reached by them;
the other cannot reach the one who reaches them. Even with such a metaphor, you still do not understand how to realize it—this is a total, undifferentiated mass.
This is simply to ensure that you believe; do not move your tongue in disorder. Have you not seen Dongshan say: "Continuity is also very difficult"?
You must know that there is this matter. If you do not know that there is this matter, there will be days of weeping ahead.
Xuefeng came to visit him. When it was time for him to depart, the Master saw him off at the gate. Once Xuefeng had entered his sedan chair, the Master said, "This one is carried by four people;
how many carry that one? Xuefeng straightened his body and rose up, saying, "What are you talking about? The Master asked again. Xuefeng said, "Going, going."
He did not. The Master said, "To know is to know; it is precisely this that cannot be grasped.

Two Zen guests from Qiangde were traveling along the road when they saw the Master riding an ox. One guest remarked, "The horns are very distinct, yet how unfortunate that the rider does not recognize them!
The Master spurred the ox and departed. The two Zen guests rested beneath a tree and brewed tea. The Master—

He returned. Xuansha descended from his seat, inquired after him, offered him a place to sit, and served him tea. The Master asked, "Where have you recently come from? The monk replied, "From over there.
The Master said, "What is the matter over there? The monk lifted up his tea bowl. The Master said, "That is still a matter of 'this side.'"
"What is that matter over there? The two men had no reply. The Master said, "Do not say that the rider does not recognize what is good.
Chan Master Yungai Zhiyuan of Tanzhou (Third Case). The Master asked Yunju, "When I am at a loss, what should I do?
Yunju said, "It is simply because your practice has not reached its limit. The Master did not bow and withdrew. Later, he asked Shishuang.
Shuangyun said, "It is not only you, Disciple (Ajari), that I cannot do anything about; even this old monk is helpless. Yun asked, "Master, why are you helpless?
Shuangyun replied, "If I were able to do anything about it, I would have already removed your 'helplessness'. The Master then prostrated himself and requested to enter the room for instruction.
The Master once had a monk ask Shishuang, "When all ten thousand doors are closed, we do not ask about that; but what is it like when all a hundred doors are open?
Shishuang said, "What about the matter within the hall? The monk said, "No one can receive him. Shishuang said, "You have spoken quite well, but you have only spoken eighty percent.
When the Master heard this, he went to pay his respects and requested Shishuang to explain further, but Shishuang would not speak. The Master...
Baoshu Xiang went out from behind the abbot’s quarters and prostrated again without ceasing, saying, "I beg the Master to speak for me;
if you do not speak, I must strike the Master. Xiang replied, "You may do so. The Master prostrated once more, and Xiang said, "No one recognizes him. At these words, the Master attained realization.
Cuiyan said, "The former practice did not reach the goal; the final stage went too far.
Miaoxi said, "A pair of iron hammers without holes; among them, one is the heaviest."
The Way-rectifier (Daozheng) reported this to the Horse King (Aśvapati), requesting that he debate with the Master. The Horse King invited the Master to his presence and related the matter in detail.
After finishing his tea, the Master went before the Great King and borrowed a sword. Grasping the sword, he asked Daozheng: "In your own teaching, it is said:
'Vague and indistinct, yet within it there is something; profound and dark, yet within it there is an essence. What is this thing? What is this essence?"

"What kind of person is this? If he understands the Way, he shall not be executed; if he does not understand the Way, he shall be executed. Daozheng then performed a prostration to express his remorse.
The Master said to the Great King, "Do you still recognize this man? [The King] replied, "I do. The Master asked, "Who is he? [The King] replied, "Daozheng. The Master said, "It is not so.
If his Way were truly correct, he would have been able to respond to Your Majesty. He is merely a solitary soul without a master. Because of this, Dao...
The gate is no longer cluttered with complications.
Regarding Chan Master Fu Xian of Fuzhou (four cases total): Daowu asked, "I have long heard that you, Master, understand Chan; is this true?"
The Master said, "Heaven! Heaven! I stepped forward and covered the Master’s mouth, saying, "Lower your voice, lower your voice.
The Master gave me a slap. I said, "Heaven! Heaven! The Master stepped forward, seized me, and said, "How can you be so impertinent?
I in turn gave the Master a slap. The Master said, "This old monk has committed a transgression. I shook out my sleeves and departed. The Master laughed heartily.
Xiaoyun said, "Had I known it would be thus earlier, I would have regretted not being thus.
When the Master saw a monk approaching, he made a gesture of rising; the monk then departed. The Master called out, "Dharma brother, please stay for a moment to exchange greetings."
The monk turned his body and made a gesture of withdrawing his sitting mat. The Master returned to the abbot’s quarters. The monk said, "Heaven! Heaven!

The Master said, "A dragon's head with a snake's tail. The monk joined his palms, stepped forward, and stood there. The Master said, "A defeated general who flees to his lord does not spare his own life."
A monk asked, "Please speak, Master, regarding that place where neither hook nor awl reaches. The Master remained silent for a long while.
The monk said, "The mechanism of a flashing bolt of lightning—vain indeed is the labor of waiting upon thought. The Master said, "Try and say a phrase that transcends the ordinary.

The monk stepped forward three paces and then withdrew. The Master said, "This is a phrase that transcends the ordinary; but as for the matter at hand right now, what is it? The monk gave a single sweep with his sleeve.
He then went out. The Master said, "He is just a fellow from Tianjin Bridge.
A monk asked, "What is it to be a lion cub? The Master said, "It is well able to roar. The monk clapped his hands and said, "A fine hand! A fine hand!
The Master said, "Under the clear blue sky and bright daylight, you have been bewitched by a ghost. The monk made a gesture as if to overturn the meditation seat, whereupon the Master [struck him].
[The Master] struck him. The monk said, "The donkey’s business has not yet gone, and the horse’s business has already arrived. The Master said, "Truly, you are an adept.
The monk brushed out his sleeves and departed. The Master said, "To take a bowl and fill it with water, intending to compare it to the great ocean."
Chan Master Juhui of Daguang in Tanzhou (three cases). The Master relied upon Shishuang for ten years.

Shishuang asked, "Every year the state grants the degrees to those who pass the examinations; are they still permitted to pay their respects at the palace gate? The Master said, "There is one person."
Fengxue said, "He does not seek advancement. Xuefeng asked, "On what basis do you say this? The Master said, "He does not act for the sake of fame.
Xuefeng asked, "Apart from today, is there another time [when he acts thus]? The Master said, "He would not even say that it is 'today'."
He addressed the assembly, saying: "The teachings of a lifetime are merely for the purpose of setting right the hands and feet of people of this present age.
Even if one were to strip them away until nothing remains, it would only result in a person who has 'settled the matter. This cannot be taken as the business of those beneath the patched robe.
Therefore, throughout forty-nine years, [the Buddha] could not fully clarify it nor point it out. Reaching this point, what should be done? If you continue to prattle on further,"
"I fear it would become a burden. A monk asked, "Is Bodhidharma still the Patriarch? The Master said, "He is not the Patriarch. The monk said, "If he is not the Patriarch, why has he come here?
The Master said, "It is because you do not recognize the Patriarch. The monk asked, "What is it like after one has recognized him? The Master said, "Only then will you know he is not."
This is the Patriarch.
Regarding the Monk Shizhu of Fengxiang Prefecture (one instance): The Master visited Dongshan, who then offered this "hanging word" (chuǐyǔ), saying: "There are four kinds of people.
One person has spoken beyond the Buddhas and patriarchs, yet not a single step can be taken. Another person has walked beyond the Buddhas and patriarchs..."
It cannot be expressed in words. One person can speak it and practice it; another cannot speak it and cannot practice it. Now tell me: which one is that person?
The Master stepped forward from the assembly and said: "One person has spoken beyond the Buddhas and Patriarchs, yet not a single step can be taken."

It is simply that he has no tongue and is not permitted to speak; one person has already transcended Buddhas and Patriarchs, yet cannot utter a single word—it is simply that he has no feet and is not permitted to walk.
One person can both speak and walk; this is precisely the "box and lid" fitting together.
One who cannot speak and cannot walk is like seeking life after having one's vitality severed—this is a stone child bearing a cangue and wearing shackles.
[The Master] said, "Lock. Dongshan asked, "As for you yourself, Reverend, how about that? The Master said, "Pervasive throughout one's own portion;
how could it not be manifest? Dongshan asked, "What about Minggong Xiù on the sea? The Master said, "Two illusory people meet;
they clap their hands and laugh 'he-he'."
Chan Master Wenshu of Tanzhou (Case 1). A monk asked, "Why was it that Sengyou could not capture the true likeness of Master Zhigong?
The Master said, "It is not only Sengyou; even Zhigong himself could not capture his own likeness. The monk asked, "Why could Zhigong not capture his own likeness?
The Master said, "Because colors and paints cannot bring him forth. The monk asked, "Can you, Reverend, capture his likeness? The Master said, "I..."
[The monk] said, "I also cannot capture it. He asked, "Why, Master, can you not capture it? The Master said, "He does not conform to my countenance;
how could I be instructed to capture him?"
The scholar Zhang Gongzhuo (Vol. I) once went to Shishuang to visit the Chan poet Qi Ji, who was wearing a coarse cotton robe.
Shishuang received him with only a brief glance; instead, he engaged in intense conversation with the other three men all day long. Suddenly, Gongzhuo asked:
Among the three men, why did he not recommend one to serve as the elder? Chan-yueh knew that Master Zhi was as light as frost, so he said, "You should visit the Abbot;
he is an incarnate Bodhisattva. Among the five hundred disciples in the hall, two hundred and fifty are superior to me.
Zhi then held him in high esteem and immediately went to the abbot’s quarters to pay his respects. Zhi asked:

The scholar asked, "What is your surname? The Master said, "My surname is Zhang and my name is Zhuo. The scholar said, "Since you have searched for 'cleverness' (qiao) and found it cannot be obtained, from where does 'clumsiness' (zhuo) come?

Upon these words, the scholar had an awakening. He then composed a verse, saying: "Radiant and silent illumination pervades the sands of the Ganges; Ordinary beings and sages, all living creatures, share my home.
When a single thought does not arise, the entire body is revealed; As soon as the six sense-faculties stir, they are obscured by clouds. He then cut off [his ties].

To eliminate afflictions is to increase one's illness; to strive toward True Suchness is likewise a deviation. To accord with worldly conditions without obstruction—nirvana and birth-and-death are but empty flowers.

Chan Master Caoshan Benji of Fuzhou, a successor of Chan Master Dongshan Liangjie of Yunzhou (twenty-three cases in total). He was the son of the Zhang family of Putian, Quanzhou. He went to visit Dongshan.
Shan asked the Master, "What is your name? The Master replied, "Benji (Original Quiescence). Shan said, "Why do you not speak of that which is above?
The Master said, "I do not speak. Shan asked, "Why do you not speak? The Master said, "It is not named 'Original Quiescence. Dongshan held him in high esteem.
The Master took his leave of Dongshan. Dongshan asked, "Where are you going? The Master replied, "I am going to the place of non-alteration.
Dongshan said, "In a place of non-alteration, how can there be going? The Master said, "Going, too, is non-alteration."
Addressing the assembly, he said: "Everywhere, people merely hold up their standards and rules. Why not give them a turning word to make them free from doubt?
Yunmen then asked, "In the place of profound secrecy, why is it that one does not know what exists? The Master said, "Precisely because it is so profoundly secret, one does not know what exists.
Yunmen asked, "How should one approach such a person? The Master said, "Do not go toward the place of profound secrecy."
Dongshan asked, "How is it when one does not approach in a secret place? The Master said, "Only then do you understand approaching.
Dongshan said, "Yes, yes."
Miaoxi said: "Add more turbid oil to a lamp with a damp wick.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "Do not travel the path of the mind; do not don the garment of the original source. Why need one act further like this?
One must strictly avoid the time before birth."
Upon hearing the sound of the bell, the Master said, "Ayaya! Ayaya! A monk asked, "What are you doing, Preceptor?
The Master replied, "It struck my heart."
The Fifth Patriarch Jie said, "The heart of a thief is always apprehensive.
Yunmen asked, "What is the practice of a śramaṇa? The Master replied, "It is those who eat the crops of the monastery's permanent property. Yunmen said:
"If one goes thus, what then? The Master said, "Can you maintain it? Wumen said, "I can maintain it.
The Master said, "How do you maintain it? Wumen said, "Wearing clothes and eating food—what difficulty is there in that?
The Master said, "Why not say, 'Wearing fur and carrying horns'? Wumen then paid his respects.
Jingqing asked, "The principle of pure emptiness is ultimately without form; what is it like at such a time? The Master said, "The principle is indeed thus;
but as for phenomena, how is it? Jingqing said, "It is just like the principle and just like phenomena. The Master said, "You may deceive Cao Shan alone, but what about the eyes of the various sages?
Jingqing said, "If there were no eyes of the various sages, how could they discern that which is not so? The Master said, "Official!"
"No needle can enter it; carriages and horses pass through it in private.
Daowei Zhe said: "Although Caoshan was skilled at cutting, polishing, and refining, what could he do?
Jingqing’s jade was originally without flaw. Do you understand? Without passing through the hands of a master craftsman, it would remain a useless vessel."
The monk Qingrui asked, "I am solitary and poor; I beg the Master for relief. The Master called out, "Acarya Rui! Rui responded, "Yes.
The Master said, "Three cups of wine at the Bai family inn in Qingyuan—having drunk them, he still says he has not even touched his lips."

The Master asked the two senior monks, Qiang and De: "When a Bodhisattva is in meditative concentration and hears that an elephant with a fragrant trunk is crossing a river, from which sutra does this come?
They replied, "The *Nirvāṇa Sūtra*. The Master said, "Did you hear it before entering concentration, or did you hear it after emerging from concentration?

They replied, "It was heard by the Master’s grace. The Master said, "You have spoken quite well, but you have only spoken half of it. They asked, "And what about the Master? The Master said, "At the foot of the rapids."
[The Master] received him.
The Master asked the monk, "Where have you come from? He replied, "I have come from sweeping the floor. The Master said, "Did you sweep before the Buddha or after the Buddha?
He replied, "I swept both before and after at the same time. The Master said, "Give me your kashaya robe."
A monk asked, "I bring this raw jade to the Master; I pray that the Master will carve it. The Master said, "I do not carve it. The monk asked, "Why do you not carve it?
The Master said, "You must know that Cao Shan is a master craftsman."
A monk asked, "The student is sick throughout his entire being; I beg the Master to treat me. The Master said, "I will not treat you. The monk asked, "Why will you not treat me?
The Master said, "It is so that I may teach you that you cannot seek life and find it, nor can you seek death and find it."
A monk asked, "The son returns to his father; why does the father not acknowledge him at all? The Master said, "It is only fitting that it should be so.

The monk asked, "Wherein lies the bond of affection between father and son? The Master said, "Only then is the bond of affection between father and son truly established. The monk asked, "What is this bond of affection between father and son?
The Master said, "Even blades and axes cannot cleave it open."
A monk asked, "What is the most precious thing in the world? The Master said, "A dead cat is the most precious.
The monk asked, "Why is a dead cat so precious? The Master said, "Because no one puts a price on it."
A monk asked, "What is the lion? The Master said, "No beasts can approach it. The monk asked, "What is the cub of the lion?
The Master said, "It can swallow its parents. The monk asked, "Since no beasts can approach it, why is it instead swallowed by its cub?
The Master said, "If it roars, both grandfather and grandmother are utterly exhausted. The monk asked, "As for the grandfather and grandmother, are they truly exhausted?"
[The student] said, "There is none. The Master said, "Exhausted. [The student] asked, "After exhaustion, what then? The Master said, "The whole body returns to the father.
[The student] asked, "Why did you previously say that both father and mother are exhausted? The Master said, "Have you not heard it said: 'A prince can accomplish the affairs of a nation'?
[He added,] "Upon the withered tree, a few more blossoms are scattered."
A monk asked, "The teachings state that 'the great ocean does not harbor a corpse. What is the ocean? The Master said, "It contains all things.
The monk asked, "Why does it not harbor a corpse? The Master said, "That which has ceased its breath does not remain there.
The monk asked, "Since it contains all things, why does that which has ceased its breath not remain there? The Master said, "All things are not its [true] self."
[The monk] Gong said, "One who has cut off the breath possesses this virtue. [Gong] asked, "I do not yet understand whether there is anything further above this or not?

The Master said, "There is. [Gong] asked, "What is the matter above this? The Master said, "To say 'there is' or 'there is not' would suffice; however, what can you do about the Dragon King brandishing his sword?"
A monk asked, "What is the reality underlying illusion? The Master said, "The reality underlying illusion is fundamentally real. The monk asked, "When it is illusory, what is revealed?

The Master said, "Illusion itself is the revelation. The monk asked, "If that is so, then from beginning to end there is nothing apart from illusion. The Master said, "If you seek the characteristics of illusion, they are utterly unobtainable."
A monk asked, "How is it before the sun has risen? The Master said, "Thirty years ago, Caoshan also came this way.
The monk asked, "How is it after the sun has risen? The Master said, "It is still half a month's journey behind Caoshan."
A monk asked, "Who is it that wields the sword within the borders of the kingdom? The Master said, "Caoshan. The monk asked, "Whom do you intend to kill?
The Master said, "I would kill everyone who exists. The monk asked, "What if you suddenly encounter your own parents?
How then? The Master said, "Why choose? The monk asked, "But what about yourself? The Master said, "Who can do anything to me? The monk asked, "Why does the Master not [kill] himself?"
