"No. Yunmen said, "It is not that you are suffering from dumbness. At these words, the monk had an awakening.
After Xuedou finished citing this, he gave a shout and said, "This blind, deaf, and mute fellow! Had it not been for Yunmen..."
"In what year of the donkey’s life will he go? Now, there are some who brandish their mallets and raise their fly-whisks, yet he pays them no mind.
When you tell him to come forward, he does not come; do you understand? When you call out to him, he does not respond.
Can anyone from all quarters deal with him? If Xuedou could not deal with him, what would be the use of this whole crew of donkeys?"
With his staff, he drove them all away at once.
Longmen Yuan’s verse says: "Xuansha’s three types of sick people—reason does not lie in a loud voice.
It drew forth Old Man Xiangyan, who came to hang himself upon a tree."
He addressed the assembly, saying, "I have studied together with the Old Śākyamuni. At that time, a monk came forward and asked, "I wonder, whom did you study under?
The Master said, "Xie Sanlang on the fishing boat."

The Master ascended the hall. Hearing the sound of swallows, he said, "Profoundly expounding the true mark (*dharmatā*), skillfully preaching the essentials of the Dharma. He then descended from his seat.
Shortly thereafter, a monk requested further instruction, saying, "I do not understand, Master. The Master said, "Go away; no one will believe you."
One day the Master said: "I usually say that before the face of a deceased monk is precisely Bodhi before one's eyes;
it is the divine radiance ten thousand miles behind the crown of the head. If you can grasp this, you will be able to transcend the realm of shadows."

A celestial dragon served as the Master’s attendant. Following the Master as they traveled through the mountains, they encountered a tiger. The dragon said, “That in front of us is a tiger. The Master replied, “That is your tiger.
Later that evening, while standing in attendance, the dragon asked, “Today we saw a tiger; I wonder what your Reverence’s intention was regarding this?
The Master said, “In this Sahā world, there are four kinds of heavy obstructions. If a person can penetrate them, I will grant you permission to leave.”
Regarding the "Skandhas and Dhātus," Xuedou said: "If you wish to act as a teacher for gods and humans, right before you is a tiger.
Baoning Yong’s verse says: "A fierce tiger stands alone in the path, its majesty alone; its claws and fangs are truly sharp as swords."
A Chisel. How pitiable are those who do not realize their own loss! To gather up shattered bones is truly lamentable.
The Master asked Jingqing, "I see not a single dharma; this is a great calamity. Tell me, what dharma do you not see?
Jingqing pointed to a pillar and said, "Is it that you do not see this dharma? The Master said, "The clear water of Zhejiang."
"White rice. You may eat it, but you have not even dreamed of the Buddha-dharma.
Xuedou said, "How great was Jingqing! He was thoroughly deceived by Xuansha. Had I been there at the time, I would have simply told him:
'Even receiving the prediction on Vulture Peak does not yet reach this level.'"
Baoning Yong was the successor of Jingqing. He would clap his hands and laugh loudly, "Ha ha!
One day the Master said: "In deep mountains and rocky cliffs, for thousands and tens of thousands of years, in places where no human footprints have reached—does the Buddha-dharma exist there or not?
If you say it exists, what do you call 'Buddha-dharma'? If you say it does not exist, yet the Buddha-dharma is nonetheless present."
[The Master] was everywhere. Changqing Ling arrived, and the Master said, "Set aside your medicinal taboos; how do you speak? Ling said, "Why do you act so foolishly?
The Master said, "At Mount Xuefeng, the elephant picks up food, yet here it is that the sparrow drops its dung."
The Master visited the Hermit of Sandou Hermitage. As soon as they met, the Hermit said, "Do not take offense that I have had many years living in this hermitage and yet possess no meditation mat.
The Master said, "Everyone has one; why do you, Hermit, lack it? The Hermit said, "Sit for a moment and drink some tea.
The Master said, "So, it turns out there is one after all!"
When the Master saw Gushan approaching, he drew a circle and showed it to him. Gushan said, "No one can get out of this.
The Master said, "I knew you would make your livelihood within the wombs of donkeys and horses. Gushan asked, "And what about you, Preceptor?
The Master said, "No one can get out of this. Gushan said, "If you speak thus, Preceptor, then you have indeed attained it."
Jiashan asked, "Why did you not get it? The Master said, "I got it; you did not.
As the Master was conversing with Dizang, it grew late at night. The Master said, "The attendant has bolted the door.
How will you get out? Dizang said, "What do you call a 'door'?"
*Fadeng* (Fa-deng) says differently: "The Preceptor does not wish to retire.
*Xuedou* says differently: "Be careful, and then he departs.

When the Tripiṭaka Master Śrīmitra arrived at the King's court, the Great King invited the Master and requested him to test [the Master]. The Master took a copper fire-tongs and struck an iron [vessel].
The Fire Pit. [A monk] asked, "What sound is that? He replied, "The sound of copper and iron. The Master said, "Great King, do not allow yourself to be deceived by foreigners.
Xuedou offered an alternative reading: "Great King, you should increase your respectful faith. He also offered another reading for the Tripitaka Master: "Do not deceive the outsider."
The people of the country said, "Master Faden has deceived the Great King.
When the Master entered the assembly, Attendant Guang said, "If you, Uncle, can learn Chan, I shall forge an iron boat and go down to sea.
After the Master took up residence there, he sent someone with a letter to ask Guang, "Have you finished forging the iron boat yet?"
Fadeng took his place as the acting abbot and invited the Master to disembark from the boat.
The Master said to Dapuan Xuantong, "You shall remain there; do not deceive the men and women of that household. Xuantong replied:
"I have opened a door for making offerings. How would I dare do such a thing? The Master said, "The matter is difficult.
Daotong said, "I am truly at a loss. The Master asked, "In what way is it difficult? He replied, "Because he is unwilling to take responsibility.
The Master then returned to his quarters.
The Master was conversing with the Governor of Izumi inside the room. A novice monk lifted the curtain intending to enter;
seeing them, he stepped back and went out. The Master said, "That novice deserves thirty blows. The Governor said, "In that case, I am at fault.
The Master said, "The Buddha-dharma is not a matter of this sort."
Inspector Wei remarked, "The monk Cao Shan is truly extraordinary. The Master then asked, "How far is it from Fuzhou to Cao Shan?
Wei pointed to a nearby monk and said, "Have you ever been to Cao Shan, Senior? The monk replied, "I have. Wei asked, "How far is it from Fuzhou to Cao Shan?
The monk replied, "One hundred and twenty li. Wei said, "If that is so, then you, Senior..."
[The monk] had never been to Caoshan. Wei, however, rose and prostrated. The Master said, "The Military Inspector ought to pay homage to this monk.
The monk, in turn, felt deep shame and remorse.
Chengtian Zong said, "This monk is pitiable and tragic; even if Xuansha possessed the Vajra-eye, [he would have been unable to save him]."
[The Master] said, "I have already missed Wei the Military Commissioner.
The Commissioner asked, "The people of Campā speak a language that is somewhat difficult to understand; how much more so the Sanskrit of the Five Indias?
Is there anyone who can distinguish it? The Master picked up his bag and said, "If you recognize this, you will be able to distinguish it."
Xuedou said, "What need was there for Xuansha’s prolixity? He also said, "Just now, what did you say?
While sitting, the Master pointed to a single white spot before him and asked an attendant monk, "Do you see it? The monk replied, "I see it.
The Master asked this three times, and the monk responded three times. The Master said, "You see it, and I see it too. Why do you not understand?"
The Master asked a monk, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From Deshan. The Master said, "What words or phrases were spoken recently?
He replied, "One day, when the assembly had gathered and settled, the Abbot held up his staff, pointed it directly at me, and then went straight back to his quarters and closed the door.
The Master said, "You have already made a mistake in recounting this. The monk asked, "Where was the mistake? The Master said, "Try recounting it again."
The monk raised the point again. The Master said, "I do not contradict the nature of grass.
The monk asked, "I have heard your words that the entire world of the ten directions is a single bright pearl.
Why is it that I, as a student, cannot understand this? The Master said, "The entire world of the ten directions is a single bright pearl; what need is there to understand it?"
Xuedou said, "In other quarters it may be so, but here it is not.
Ciyun Long said, "To speak in such a manner is like chewing food and feeding it to an infant, or giving a staff to one who is already holding hands.
If you still do not understand, you must investigate by turning inward; you must be truly earnest—it cannot be otherwise."
To speak with empty words is merely to live and die in vain.
A monk asked, "What is it that makes it so difficult to see? The Master said, "It is precisely because it is too near."
Fayan said, "There is nothing to be found nearby; it is right here, before you, that you are the Elder.
When the Master arrived at Putian County in Quanzhou, he was welcomed with a hundred kinds of performances.
The following day, he asked Elder Xiaotang, "Where did all that clamor and commotion go yesterday? Xiaotang lifted the corner of his *kāṣāya*. The Master said, "I see."
This was a case of missing the point entirely.
Faldeng remarked separately, "Today is even more laughable.
Jingqing asked, "I am a student newly entering the monastic community; I beg the Master to point out a path for me to enter. The Master said, "Have you heard of Yanguan?"
"Is there the sound of the mountain stream? He replied, "I hear it. The Master said, "Enter from here.
One day, three newly arrived monks came. The Master went out himself and struck the work-call drum three times, then returned to his quarters.
After the newcomers had performed their formal observances, they also struck the work-call drum three times and entered the Sangha hall. Long...
The resident monks informed the Master, saying, "A newcomer has been showing disrespect to the Master. The Master said, "Ring the bell to assemble the assembly for an interrogation.
Once the assembly had gathered, the newcomer did not appear. The Master ordered an attendant to go and summon him.

As soon as he reached the Dharma Hall, the newcomer struck the attendant on the back once and said, "The Master is calling you. When the attendant arrived by the Master's side, the newcomer simply turned and departed.
In the Hall, a long-resident monk asked, "Why did you not examine him? The Master said, "I have already examined you.
Once, the Master accidentally took the wrong medicine, and his entire body became red and festering. A monk asked, "What is the solid Dharma-body?
The Master replied, "Droplets of pus."
A verse by Tianyi Huai says: Every drop dried up, the whole body is festering pus; On the fishing boat, the family style is revealed.
People of this age look only at the fishing line, Failing to see the reeds facing the red smartweed.

The Master [Yunmen] took up the words that Xuefeng had suspended, saying: "Sitting by the edge of a grain basket, a man who starves to death; standing on the brink of a river, a man who dies of thirst. Yunmen said:
"Sitting inside the grain basket, a man who starves to death; submerged head-first in the water, a man who dies of thirst."
Yunmen said, "The whole body is rice; the whole body is water.
Miaoxi, having cited the words of these three masters, let out a shout and said, "Those talkative fellows!
They were truly unable to restrain their impatience. 'The whole body is rice; the whole body is water'—where did they get this kind of news?"
The Essential Records of the Linked Lamp,
Volume Twenty-Three and Volume Twenty-Four,
compiled by the monk Wuming, a successor of the Patriarchs who resided at Chongfu Chan Monastery in Quanzhou.
Seventh generation under Qingyuan;
Dharma heirs of Chan Master Xuefeng Yicun of Fuzhou (total fifty-one):
Chan Master Yunmen Wenyuan of Shaoyou (51), a native of Jiaxing in Suzhou. He first studied under Muzhou.
He clarified the essential points of the enlightened mind. Later, he went to visit Xuefeng. Just as Xuefeng was ascending the hall, the Master stepped forward from the assembly.

Xuefeng stared at him intently and said, "Why have you not removed that three-hundred-jin iron cangue upon your neck? The Master rubbed his eyes with his hand and hurried out. Xuefeng marveled at him;
from then on, he entered the inner quarters of the master's room and attained even greater profundity in the mysterious and abstruse teachings.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "Having no choice in the matter, I speak thus to you all: that there is 'nothing at all' from the very outset is already a form of obscuration.

If you further intend to step forward, seeking understanding by chasing after words and phrases, you will create a thousand differences and ten thousand distinctions, setting up extensive challenges and difficulties.
You will only gain a slippery tongue, moving further and further away from the Way; how can there be any rest?"
At that time, if this matter were merely within the realm of words and phrases, how could the Three Vehicles and the twelve divisions of the teachings not be considered such?

Why, then, would there be a further "separate transmission outside the teachings"? If it were something obtained through scholarly understanding or intellectual acuity, then even the sages of the Ten Stages—who preach the Dharma like clouds and rain—would still be rebuked for their realization of the nature as being "like looking through a gauze screen. For this reason...
Therefore, know that all who possess a mind are as vastly separated from the Way as heaven is from earth.
Nevertheless, for one who has attained it, how could the fire of the Way ever burn their mouth? All day long they speak of matters, yet they never move their lips;
all day long they wear clothes, yet they have never attached so much as a single thread; all day long they eat rice, yet they have never bitten through a single grain. This is still...
This is merely a discourse for the gate and courtyard; one must truly attain such realization before it is possible.

If you present your spiritual mechanism within the phrases of the patch-robed monks' school, your efforts will be in vain. Even if you can take responsibility under a single phrase, you are still but a dozing fellow.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "Students, all gathered together, what are you deliberating upon?
To cite a single phrase and tell you to accept it directly—this is already to have spat in your face.

Even if you were to grasp a single hair-tip and suddenly comprehend the entire world, that would already be to gouge out your own flesh and create a wound. Nevertheless, you must still arrive at the reality."
Only when you have attained this ground can it be so. If you have not yet attained such a state, you must by no means engage in empty verbiage.
Instead, take a step back and seek within the very root of your own feet: what principle is there? There is truly not even a hair’s breadth to provide you with an intellectual understanding.
This great matter of each individual person is entirely manifest before you; do not trouble yourself with even a single hair’s breadth of effort.
As for spiritual power, it is no different from that of the patriarchs and Buddhas.

It is simply because you people have developed so much self-importance that you carry your alms-bags across thousands of villages and ten thousand miles, enduring such hardship. But tell me, what is lacking in you?
For a great man, who does not have their share? If one can directly take responsibility for it, that is already beyond the reach of ordinary convenience; one must not accept it from others.
Deceptive and deceitful, you take matters into your own hands; as soon as you see the Old Monk open his mouth, you ought to take a millstone and shove it right into his mouth.
You are just like flies on excrement, fighting over and sucking at it. Three or five of you gather your heads together to deliberate, piteously pleading with your brothers.
The ancient masters of the past had no choice but to employ skillful means for all of you.
I shall offer you a word or two to open a path for your entry. Once you understand such matters, set them aside and exert your own spirit.
Is this not a matter of mutual affinity? Hurry, hurry! Time does not wait for man;
one cannot guarantee that the next breath will follow the outgoing one. What other use have you for body and mind elsewhere? You must be urgent.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "I observe that among you, even within two or three turns of the teaching, you are still unable to grasp it.
What benefit is there in vainly donning the patched robe? Do you understand? I shall explain it for you so that, in the future, when you travel to various regions and meet elder masters,"
He raises a finger. He holds up a whisk and says, "Is this Chan? Is this the Way? He drags his staff and strikes [the student] on the head, then walks away.
If you do not act in this way, you will all fall into the retinue of the celestial Māras and destroy my school.
If you truly do not understand, then go look within the thicket of entanglements. I have always told you: within the lands of as many atoms as there are, throughout the three periods of time...
The Buddha, the twenty-eight patriarchs of the Western Heaven, and the six patriarchs of the Tang land—all of them preach the Dharma from atop this staff.
Their spiritual powers and transformations resound throughout the ten directions; they act with total freedom as they please. Do you understand?
If you do not, do not merely deceive yourself with empty words. Even so, have you yet seen it with true, authentic clarity? Even if you reach such a state...
"I have not yet dreamed of the monk-sandhis being present. In this village of three households, one does not meet a single person.
Suddenly he picked up his staff, drew a line, and said, "Everyone must go out from here!"
He addressed the assembly, saying: "You all have come here for no reason; what are you looking for? This old monk does nothing but eat and defecate.
What else could he possibly do? You travel to various places to practice Zen and inquire about the Way, so let me ask you this:"
As for those who have attained something by traveling to various quarters—how is it? Try to bring it forth and show me! Can you call out to the old man in your own house?
If you find even a drop of spit from behind this old fellow’s rump and chew it up as your own, you will immediately claim, "I understand Zen, I understand the Way!
Even if you could recite the entire Tripitaka, what would you do with it? As the Ancients said:
Having no other choice, seeing you running about in confusion, I told you that Bodhi and Nirvana are what bury you;
they are the stakes that pin you down. Seeing again that you do not understand, I told you it is neither Bodhi nor Nirvana.
To know such matters as these is already to find no foothold; yet you still seek further commentaries on them—such people as this destroy the Dharma.
"Lineage. From the beginning until now, it has always been like this for you;
where was there ever a 'today'? He addressed the assembly, saying: "What is this matter that has continued from the beginning until now? Now, being constrained by necessity, I shall speak to you all:
throughout the entire earth, what object exists to serve as a condition or an object of opposition for you? If there were even a needle-point..."
"Granted. It creates an obstruction for you. Pick it up and bring it here to me. What do you call 'Buddha'? What do you call 'Patriarch'?
What do you call 'mountains, rivers, and the great earth,' or 'the sun, moon, and stars'? What do you take to be the four elements and the five aggregates?
When I speak thus, people call it the talk of an old woman from a common village. Suddenly, were you to encounter the Original [Nature]..."
"Colorful" traveling monk! Hearing such talk, one might grab him by the feet and drag him down the steps—what crime would there be in that?
Even so, upon what principle do you act this way? Do not merely follow the impulse of your tongue and speak recklessly here;
you must be a true man before you can succeed. Suddenly, if the old fellow traces you back to the very root of your heels, you will have nowhere to go.
"I have broken your legs. Do not say I did not warn you.
He addressed the assembly, saying, "Venerable monks, do not engage in false conceptualization. Heaven is heaven; earth is earth; mountains are mountains; waters are waters;
monastics are monastics; laypeople are laypeople. After a long silence, he said, "Bring me the mountain that serves as my desk! At that time, there was a monk...
A monk asked, "When a student perceives the mountain as a mountain and the water as water, what is that like?

The Master said, "Why pass through here by riding over the Buddha Hall at the three gates? The monk said, "In that case, there is no false conceptualization. The Master said, "Give me back the head of the dialogue!"
He addressed the assembly, saying: "If you do not find it appropriate, then seek at least a point of entry. The myriad Buddhas of the fine dust reside upon your tongues;
the holy teachings of the Tripitaka rest beneath your heels. It would be better to simply remain in a state of non-action.
Is there anyone who can realize this? Come forth and speak before the assembly!"

He addressed the assembly. Holding up his staff, he pointed toward the space before him and said, "The great earth and the heavens, and all the buddhas as numerous as motes of dust—all are here together.
Who can settle the dispute over the superiority or inferiority of the Buddha-dharma? Is there anyone who can offer a rebuke? If no one can rebuke it, wait until this old monk rebukes it for you!
At that time, a monk came forward and said, "We request the Master to rebuke it. The Master said, "This wild fox spirit!"
The Master took up his staff and addressed the assembly, saying: "Ordinary people call it 'existent. Those of the Two Vehicles call it 'non-existent.
Those who have realized awakening call it 'illusory existence. Bodhisattvas see its very substance as emptiness. But for us Zen monks, when we see this staff, we simply call it a staff."
When walking, simply walk; when sitting, simply sit. You must not stir or shift.
The Master picked up his staff and addressed the assembly, saying: "This staff has transformed into a dragon and swallowed up heaven and earth.
From where do the mountains, rivers, and the great earth come?"

The Master had a verse that said: "A phrase that does not reveal its wind-bone, entrusted before a word is even spoken; When you step forward with your mouth chattering, I know you are utterly at a loss.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "The veteran masters of all quarters all say that beyond sound and form there is a matter of a certain kind—such as this sort of talk."
"Talk! Within this three-bay Dharma Hall, you sit alone indulging in deluded thoughts; you have never even dreamed of the fundamental tenets of my Master.
How can you possibly digest the offerings of the faithful? On the thirtieth day of the twelfth month, each of you must settle your accounts.
Then, he leaped up and said: 'All of you, each of you must exert yourselves!'"
The Master gave this instruction: "The lantern is your own self. You hold the alms bowl and eat the rice; yet the rice is not your own self.
At that time, a monk asked, "What is it like when the rice is one's own self? The Master said, "You wild fox spirit!
You fellow from a village of three households! He spoke again: "Come, come. It is not that you say the rice is your own self. [If you] say it is," the Master said, "A donkey!"
Nian dreamed of a man from a village of three households.
Miaoxi said, "Exhausting one's own mind, one laughs until others' mouths are split.
The Master cited Sanping’s verse: "This very seeing and hearing is not seeing and hearing. The Master asked, "What do you call this 'seeing'?"
[The student] said, "I have heard that there is no further sound or form to present to you. The Master said, "What sounds or forms are there at the head?

[The student] said, "If one understands within this, there is nothing at all. The Master said, "What 'thing' could there be? How could essence and function be hindered by being divided or not divided?
[The student] said, "Speech is essence; essence is speech. Then, picking up his staff, the Master said, "The staff is essence; the lantern is function. This is division."
[The Master] did not distinguish [between them]. He did not say, "The wisdom of all wisdoms is pure.
At times the Master would say, "When the Great Function manifests, no rules or regulations are maintained. Once, a monk asked, "What is the Great Function manifesting?
The Master picked up his staff and called out in a loud voice, "Śākyamuni Buddha is coming!"
The Master cited Master Zhì, who said: "As my body is empty, so too are phenomena empty; the thousand species and myriad kinds are all the same.

The Master said: "When you stand, you do not see standing; when you walk, you do not see walking. Since the four elements and five aggregates cannot be apprehended, from where do mountains, rivers, and the great earth come?
When you take up your alms bowl every day to eat your rice, what do you call that rice?"
"Where else could there be even a single grain of rice?
At other times, the Master said: "Do you wish to recognize the Patriarch? Pointing with his staff, he said:
'The Patriarch is leaping and bounding right above your head! Do you wish to recognize the Patriarch’s eyes? They are beneath the soles of your feet. He further said: 'This is the offering.'"
It is like food and drink for ghosts and spirits. Yet, even so, ghosts and spirits never have enough.
Miaoxi said, "Have you not heard it said: 'Retaining delusions to moisten rebirth'? At that moment, a monk standing nearby coughed once.
Miaoxi said, "In my saying this, what fault is there? The monk hesitated, and Miaoxi— [continued].
[The Master] would then strike him. On another occasion, the Master said: "If you say that bodhi and nirvana are [the truth], I will burn *fengxiang* incense to offer to you.

If you say that the Buddhas and patriarchs are [the truth], I will burn *huangshu* incense to offer to you. If you say that talk which transcends the Buddhas and patriarchs is [the truth], I will burn a cake."
I offer incense to you. I take refuge in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṃgha.
[The student] goes down. At times the Master picks up his whisk and says: "If one finds an entrance here, it is truly marvelous!
In the land of Japan, they speak of Chan. Suppose someone from the Thirty-three Heavens were to come out and shout: 'Ho! Ho! Teshari! [He] carries it.
Regarding "confessing one's transgressions":
The Master sometimes said, "Even if one reaches the point where heaven and earth have not the slightest flaw or affliction, this is still a 'turning phrase.
Only when not seeing a single dharma is it half-raised; you must know that there is yet a time for the full raising."
The Master said, "There are three kinds of people: one who attains awakening because of an explanation; one who attains awakening because of being called by name;
and one who, upon hearing a mention, immediately turns back. You tell me, what is the meaning of 'immediately turning back'? Furthermore, he said, 'He too deserves thirty blows of the staff.'"
One day the Master said: "The entire world of the ten directions, the heavens and the earth, all the old monks under heaven—[he drew a line with his staff]—all shattered into a hundred fragments."
Xuedou said, "It is indeed so, yet for now there is still no way out. Now, this staff is in Xuedou’s hand.
He then held it horizontally across his body and said, "East, west, south, north—from where did you get it?"
One day the Master said: "Regarding the Three Vehicles and the twelve divisions of the teachings—the fact that Bodhidharma came from the West cannot be overlooked.
If it were not for this, a single shout would suffice."
One day the Master said: "To awaken to the Way upon hearing sound, and to clarify the mind upon seeing form—what is it to hear sound and awaken to the Way, and see form and clarify the mind?
He then said: "The Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara buys sesame cakes with his money; having let go, he does not pick them up. Thus he spoke.
It turns out they were actually steamed buns.
One day the Master said, "True emptiness does not destroy existence; true emptiness is not different from form. A monk asked, "What is true emptiness?
The Master said, "Do you hear the sound of the bell? The monk replied, "This is the sound of the bell. The Master said, "You will see it in a dream as long as you live on this donkey."
"Ma. At times the Master said: "On level ground there are countless dead men; he who can pass through the thorn-brake is a true adept.
A monk said: "If that is so, then the first seat in the hall has a point of excellence. The Master said: "Soruh soru."

"Ruh. The Master sometimes said: "When light does not penetrate through, there are two kinds of illnesses. First, there is a lack of clarity in all places, as if there were an object directly before one's face.
Second, even when one has penetrated through so that all phenomena are empty, there is still a lingering sense, as if there were some kind of thing remaining."
This light does not penetrate through to liberation. Furthermore, the Dharma-body also has two kinds of illnesses.

First, upon reaching the Dharma-body, one fails to forget the attachment to dharmas, and one's own views still persist; thus one remains seated within the precincts of the Dharma-body. Second, even if one manages to penetrate through to the Dharma-body, [the illness remains].
To let it pass is not permissible; examine it closely. What breath of life is there?
This too is a sickness. Miaoxi said: "Do not take this as a matter of Chan; do not take it as a matter of the Way; do not engage in 'upward' deliberations.
This is the old fellow Yunmen speaking according to reality. When I speak thus, is there anything [to be grasped]?
Measure the extent of your transgressions. If you can examine them and expose them, I will grant that you possess the eye of discerning dharmas;
if you cannot expose them through examination, then for now, go and study within the tangles of Yunmen.
The Master once cited Mazu Daoshi, who said: "All speech and language belong to the school of Deva; take this as the primary principle.
He then remarked, "These are excellent words, yet no one asks about them. At that time, a monk asked, "What is the school of Deva?
The Master replied, "Among the ninety-six types of heterodox schools in India, you are the lowest of them all."
Xuedou said, "The red banner has been snatched away by this monk.
The Master cited Linji’s three phrases and asked the stupa keeper, "As for the Master in the stupa, which of these three phrases did he attain?"
The Master said, "I have no opponent. The host said, "Ask me. The Master then asked. The host said, "If it is not right, then speak. The Master said, "'One' is not established; 'two' is not so.
The host said, "What is it that is 'if it is not right, then speak'? The Master said, "'One' is not established; 'two' is not so."
The Master asked Wo-long, "One who has clarified their own nature—do they still see a self? Long replied, "I do not see a self; only then does one clarify the self.
The Master asked again, "That which is learned upon the long benches—what rank of capacity is that?
Long replied, "The second capacity. The Master said, "What is the first capacity? Long replied, "Tie your straw sandals tight."
Miaoxi said: "Riding the thief’s horse to pursue the thief’s band; borrowing the old woman’s shawl to bow for her New Year’s greeting.
A monk cited the words of Guankui and asked the Master: "The ten directions have no walls, and the four sides have no gates.
Pure and naked, bare and clear—there is nothing to grasp. What do you say? The Master said: "To speak in such a way is easy; it is truly difficult to get out of it."
The monk said, "Does the Senior not approve of him speaking in that way? The Master said, "Was it you who just now raised that point?
The monk said, "It was. The Master said, "When will you ever dream of seeing Guankui? The monk said, "My question remains. The Master said, "I ask you:
where there are no walls on the ten directions and no gates on the four sides—pure, naked, and starkly clear—is there anything [to be grasped]?"
"Tell me, what were Mahābrahmā and Śakra consulting about? [The monk] said, 'It was not about his own affairs.
The Master shouted, 'You fellows who just eat your rice in line!'"
The Master arrived at Tiantong. Tiantong asked, "Have you attained certainty? The Master said, "What does the Abbot say?
Tiantong said, "If you do not understand, you are immediately wrapped up right before your eyes. The Master said, "If you understand, you are immediately wrapped up right before your eyes."
The Master was ascending the hall at鹅湖 (E’u). Someone said, "Do not say that only those who have not yet attained realization are constantly in a state of restless agitation.
Even those who have attained realization and clearly know where they are going are still in a state of restless agitation.
After the Master descended from the hall, he raised this matter and asked the Head Seat, "What was the meaning of the Master’s discourse just now? The Head Seat replied, "Restless agitation."
[The monk] pressed forward toward the ground. The Master said, "The Head Seat has lived here for a long time; his hair is white and his teeth are yellow, yet he speaks such words.
The Head Seat asked, "And what about you, Senior Monk? The Master said, "If you wish to speak, you may; if you see, then you see. If you do not see—"
"Do not speak so confusedly. Zuozhuo said, "As for what the Head of the Hall said—that it is 'floating and hurried'—what does that mean?
The Master said, "A cangue upon the head and shackles upon the feet. Zuozhuo said, "In that case, there is no Buddha-dharma. The Master said:
"This is the realm of the Great Beings, Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra.
Daomeng Zhe said: "In general, when one brushes aside the grass to gaze upon the wind, one must be such a person.
Yunmen may truly be called a thunderbolt from the blue sky, a rolling peal of thunder in a drought; it is enough to make one’s soul tremble with terror. Have you not heard it said: "Startled!"?
The multitude must be heroic men; to overcome the enemy, one must be a lion’s cub.
When the Master was in Zhejiang, while at the assembly of Master Yun, during a tea break, Yun posed a statement for discourse, saying: "Seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing are the Dharma;
yet the Dharma is apart from seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing. What is it? At that time, a monk said: "It is precisely what is seen right now with the eyes."
"Previously, all that is seen, heard, sensed, and known is the Dharma; yet even this Dharma cannot be apprehended. The Master then clapped his hands once.
Daoyun raised his head, and the Master said, "You still lack one move. Daoyun said, "When I reach this point, I do not understand."
The Elder raised the banner from the Bodhisattva’s hand and asked the Master, “What is this? The Master said, “You are an ill-mannered fellow.
The Elder asked, “In what way am I ill-mannered? The Master said, “Even you, a slave to the non-Buddhists, could not have done it.”
The Master asked the Head Seat, "Tell me, are the heavens, the earth, and the great world the same as or different from your own self?
The Seat replied, "They are the same. The Master said, "Are all living beings—moths, silkworms, and ants—the same as or different from your own self?
The Seat replied, "They are the same. The Master said, "Why then do you meet me with weapons?"
The Master traveled as a wandering monk and arrived in Jiangxi. Chancellor Chen Cao invited him for a meal.

Chen asked, "I shall not ask about the scriptures of the Three Vehicles, nor do I need to speak of Confucian texts. What is the matter of traveling on pilgrimage? The Master said, "I have already asked several people.
Chen said, "I am asking you, the Venerable One, right now. The Master said, "Let that wait for a moment. What is the teaching?"
Yanwei Chen said, "The yellow scrolls and red axes. The Master said, "This is merely language and writing. What is the meaning of the teachings?

Chen said, "The mouth wishes to speak, yet words fail; the mind wishes to contemplate, yet thoughts vanish. The Master said, "'The mouth wishes to speak, yet words fail'—this is in response to the existence of speech.
'The mind wishes to contemplate, yet thoughts vanish'—this is in response to the existence of deluded thought. What [is the meaning]?"
Sheng said, "This is the intent of the teaching. Chen had no reply. The Master asked, "I hear you have studied the *Book of Documents* (*Shangshu*) and read the *Lotus Sutra*.

Is this true? Chen replied, "It is true. The Master said, "The sutra states that worldly speech and the means of livelihood for sustaining life are all non-contradictory to the True Mark (*bhūtalakṣaṇa*).
Now tell me, how many people in the Heaven of Neither Thought nor Non-Thought (*naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatana*) have fallen from their station? Chen again had no reply. The Master said, "Even so..."

When writing, do not be careless. As for the ten sutras and five treatises, even if a master-monk were to cast them aside and enter a monastic community for ten or twenty years, he would still be unable to grasp them;
how much less could a Minister of State understand them? Chen Zuoli said, "I am at fault."
The Master asked the steward, "Where have you come from? He replied, "I have come to harvest the thatch. The Master said, "How many patriarchs have you harvested? The steward said, "Three hundred.

The Master said, "Three thousand in the morning and eight hundred in the evening; the handle of the ladle at the eastern house is long, while the handle of the ladle at the western house is short—what about that?
The steward was speechless. The Master then struck him.
The Master asked a monk, "The light of wisdom shines silently and universally throughout the sands of the Ganges; is this not the words of the scholar Zhang Zhuo? The monk replied, "It is.
The Master said, "Your words have already fallen away."
Miaoxi said: "The donkey chooses a damp spot to urinate.
Daguang Guo’s verse says: "Ten-thousand-fathom Dragon Gate, its momentum leaning against the void; letting go of the hand at the precipice to distinguish fish from dragons.
People of this age look only at the fishing line, failing to see the red of the *liǎo* flowers facing the reeds."
The Master asked a monk, "Where are you from? The monk replied, "A man from Silla. The Master said, "What did you bring across the sea?
The monk said, "The grass bandits have been utterly defeated. The Master said, "Why are they in my hands? The monk said, "Exactly so. The Master said, "Feel free to leap about as you please."
Xuedou said: "Old man Yunmen had the head of a dragon but the tail of a snake. Why did he let this fellow go when he was right in his own hands?
It would have been better to strike him with a staff then and there."
The Master asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk replied, "Xichan. The Master said, "What words or phrases did Xichan have?
The monk spread his two hands. The Master gave him a slap. The monk said, "I still have my story. The Master then spread his own two hands. The monk was speechless.
The Master struck him again.
Upon arriving at the storehouse, he saw a monk and asked, "What are you doing? The monk replied, "I am preparing an offering. The Master asked, "Where are you from?
The monk said, "I am from such-and-such a place. The Master called for the head cook and said, "Provide this monk with an offering."

Daguang Zhe said: "Yunmen’s compassion for a single occasion resulted in nothing but trouble. Had he simply turned back then and there, he would have spared future generations from having his words chomped upon by others.
After a long silence, he said: 'If one does not ascend the tower to look out, how can one know the depth of the vast ocean?'"
The Master asked a monk, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From Jiangxi. The Master said, "Do those old fellows in Jiangxi still talk in their sleep?
The monk was speechless. Later, he recounted this to Fayan. Fayan said, "Master Yunmen, great as he was, has been exposed by this monk."
The Master asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk replied, "From Mount Nanyue. The Master said, "I do not engage in idle entanglements with people;
come closer. As the monk approached, the Master said, "Go!"
A monk asked, "What is the matter regarding that which transcends the Dharma-body? The Master said, "To tell you what transcends it is not difficult.
But what is the Dharma-body? The monk said, "I ask the Master to examine this. The Master said, "Setting aside the examination for a moment, what is the Dharma-body?
The monk said, "Just so, just so. The Master said, "This is merely what can be learned on the long benches of the assembly hall."
"Let me ask you this: does the Dharma-body eat rice? The monk had no reply.
Xuedou said, "He was on the verge of completing a mountain nine fathoms high, yet he failed to advance even a single basket of earth. Where does the fault lie?
Master Liangjia said, "Yunmen truly went as far as entering the mud and entering the water."
There was a monk who, having finished his studies of the sutras and śāstras, came to visit the Master. He asked, "Before you reached Yunmen, it was just like the newly risen moon;
yet by the time you arrived there, it had become all crooked and bent. The Master said, "Is that what you say? The monk replied, "Yes.
The Master said, "Very well. Let me ask you: what is the newly risen moon? The monk squinted his eyes and made a gesture of gazing at the moon. The Master said:
"You are like this; later you will lose your eyesight. After ten days had passed, the monk returned. The Master asked, "Have you understood yet?
The monk said, "I have not understood. The Master said, "Ask me. The monk then asked, "What is the newly risen moon?
The Master said, "It is curved and bent. The monk was at a loss. Later, he indeed lost his eyesight.
Langya Huijue said: "Tell me, does the Buddha-dharma have spiritual efficacy? If someone were to ask Langya now, 'What is the newly risen moon?
I would tell them: 'The sound of the wooden board being struck before the sutra hall.'"
Baizhang Yuanwen said, "This monk has lost his eyes. Yunmen added, "He does not even see his nostrils.
Nevertheless, his home is in the western part of the prefecture.

The Master asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "I have come to pay respects at the stupa. The Master said, "You are mocking me. The monk said, "I am truly paying my respects at the stupa."
[The monk] approached. The Master said, "I do not even observe the five precepts.
Fenzhou said, "We have both been left standing there in mutual dullness.
A monk asked, "I do not ask about the Blessed Ones of the ten directions; what is the single path to the gate of nirvana? The Master said:
"I cannot say it. "Master, why can you not say it? The Master said, "If you were to raise the case [of the koan], you could.
Xuedou said, "There are no fish in shallow water; toiling in vain to cast the line."
A monk asked, "At the end of summer and the beginning of autumn, if someone suddenly questions you on the road ahead, how will you respond?
The Master said, "The assembly, step back! The monk said, "I do not understand; where does the fault lie? The Master said, "Bring me back the payment for my ninety days' worth of rice."
Daguang Zhe said: "This monk was too hasty in his journey, which caused Yunmen to demand the price of the meal.
Is there anyone here now who understands Yunmen? After a long silence, he said: 'If you are not one who plays in the tide, do not enter the surging waves.'"
A monk asked, "The Buddha-dharma is like the moon in the water—is this so? The Master said, "In the clear waves there is no path through. The monk asked, "From where did you, Reverend, obtain it?
The Master said, "If you ask again, from where would it come? The monk asked, "What is it like when one goes forth in this very manner?
The Master said, "Layer upon layer, the mountain passes and roads."
A monk asked, "What is the 'Single Tune of Yunmen'? The Master said, "The twenty-fifth day of the twelfth lunar month. The monk asked, "And what about the one who sings it?
The Master said, "Now, proceed slowly."
A monk asked, "What is the Dharma-body? The Master said, "Not included within the six. Xuedou’s verse says:
"One, two, three, four, five, six— The blue-eyed barbarian monk could not count them all.
At Shaolin, he spoke in vain of transmitting to Shen Guang; Then, folding his robes, he spoke of returning to India. India is vast and boundless—what is there?"
While staying at Xun, he came one night to lodge at Rufen Peak.
He asked, "What is the phrase that penetrates the Dharma-body? The Master said, "Hide your body within the Big Dipper.

Baizhang Yuanwen composed a verse on this: "The young masters of the Five Tombs are accustomed to wandering among the flowers; The poor scholar who has not yet passed the examinations has always been so."
Much. Watching others' wealth and status from a cold distance; casually, one cannot even do anything with their head-covering.
A monk asked, "If not a single thought arises, is there still transgression? The Master said, "Mount Sumeru."
Baoning Yong’s verse says: Standing atop a ten-thousand-fathom peak is utterly improper; In the blink of an eye, one falls over the precipice.
He whose entire body is not harmed by so much as a hair— How could Heaven above or the world below dare to bury him?
Question: "What is the Way? The Master said: "A single word that penetrates through. Question: "After it has penetrated through, what then? The Master said: "The same breeze at a thousand miles.
Question: "What is the pure Dharma-body? The Master said: "A flower-and-medicine railing. Question: "If one proceeds in this very manner..."
"What? The Master said, "A golden-haired lion.
Question: "What is the samādhi of every dust-mote? The Master said, "Rice in the bowl; water in the bucket. Question:
"What is it like when a single word exhausts all expression? The Master said, "Torn asunder. Question: "What is the discourse that transcends Buddhas and patriarchs? The Master said: [Silence].
Hu-bing (Wu-bing). He asked: "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said: "Facing south, look at the Big Dipper.
He asked: "What is the Buddha? The Master said: "A dried-up dung pellet. He asked: "When all-encompassing wisdom penetrates without obstruction, what then? The Master said: [Silence].
"Sweeping the floor and splashing water—the young master has arrived.
This refers to Chan Master Hui-ling of Changqing in Fuzhou (the twelfth). He was the son of the Sun family of Yanguan in Hangzhou.

Initially, he went to visit Lingyun and asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? Lingyun replied, "The donkey’s business is not yet finished, and the horse’s business has already arrived. The Master...

He traveled back and forth for twenty years without gaining any realization or movement [toward awakening]. Later, he visited Xuefeng, and one day, as he rolled up the curtain, he suddenly attained great enlightenment.
He spoke a verse, saying: "How very mistaken! How very mistaken! Rolling up the curtain, one sees the whole world.
If someone asks me what school I understand, I raise my whisk and strike them straight across the mouth. Xuefeng said to Xuansha, "This lad..."
“Chéyè,” he said. Shā replied, “Not yet. This is merely a composition of the conscious mind; wait until it has been verified before it will do.
That evening, when the Master went up to inquire after his health, Fēng asked him, “Běi Tóu-tuó refuses to accept you. If you truly possess correct realization, demonstrate it to the assembly.
The Master again composed a verse, saying: “Amidst the myriad phenomena, the body alone is revealed; Only when a person personally consents does it appear.”
Just this intimacy! In the past, you mistakenly sought it along the road; today, when looked upon, it is ice within fire.
Fenggu said to Xuansha, "Even 'it cannot be' is merely the fabrication of the conscious mind."
He addressed the assembly, saying: "I have swept everything clean and put it all away. Now, stepping forward, you ask me to find the self.
I strike you once across the back. When this one blow reaches you, you must feel shame and remorse; when no blow reaches you, where will you go to understand?"
Xuedou said: "I am not like that. Having already swept everything clean and put it away, you must come forward and seek me from me.
I will strike you once with my staff; when that one blow reaches you, you will surely find yourself at a loss."
"A single blow does not reach you; it is delivered to you level with you. Just understand it in this way.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "When you encounter a fellow traveler on the Way, pass each other shoulder-to-shoulder, and the task of a lifetime of study will be complete."
Xuedou said, "It is so, it is so. But if the needle cannot pierce it and the wind cannot enter, what use is there?
To the assembly he said, 'If everyone were like the old man today, what hope would there be?'"
Baofu Zhan said, "If it were all like today, the Old Barbarian would be utterly hopeless.
The Master took up his staff and showed it to the assembly, saying, "If you recognize this, the business of a lifetime of study is finished."
Yunmen said, "Having recognized this, why do you not consent to abide in it?
Lingyan An said, "To abide in such a way is to lose one's descendants; to go forth in such a way is for cold ashes to emit flames.
Even so, it is still not yet completely eradicated. He raised his staff and said, "Recognize!"
Having attained this, he struck the ground once and said: "Striking out the five-colored marrow of the phoenix;
smashing to pieces the bright moon-jewel of the black dragon.
The Master, along with Baofu and Gushan, went mountain-walking. Baofu pointed to the old monastery of Xuefeng and said: "The teachings of the Canon state—"
"At the summit of Mount Sumeru. "Is it not simply this very place? The Master said, "It is indeed so, but it is a pity.
Gushan said, "Had it not been for Master Sun, skulls would have covered the wilds."
Xuedou said, "Today I am wandering the mountains with this fellow; what do we hope to gain?
He further said, 'In hundreds or thousands of years hence, it is not that there will be nothing at all, but rather that it will be scarce.'"
Furthermore, a verse says: On the solitary peak of Wondrous Summit, the grass grows lush; Picking it up with clarity, to whom is it entrusted?
Were it not for Master Sun, who discerned the essential point, How many would know that skulls lie scattered across the wilds?
One day, the Master ascended the hall. Once the assembly had gathered and settled, the Master dragged out a monk and said, "The assembly, prostrate to this monk!
He then added, "Now tell me, what excellence does this monk possess that you must command the assembly to bow to him? The assembly was speechless.
The Raising of Sleeping Dragon. A monk asked Caoshan, "Vimalakīrti remained silent, and Mañjuśrī praised him as excellent.
I wonder, did this accord with Vimalakīrti’s own intent? Caoshan said, "Can you bind empty space? The monk said, "If that is so, then it does not accord with Vimalakīrti’s intent.
Caoshan said, "How could he have consented to it? The monk asked, "Ultimately, where does it lead? Caoshan said, "If..."
"To have a place of refuge is to be the same as those two masters. [Wolong] asked, "What about the Master?

Caoshan said, "Wait until you suffer from the illness of Vimalakīrti, and then you will understand. After Wolong had finished speaking, the Master said, "Although I have not met Caoshan, I dare to act as a host for his discourse.
Wolong was startled and said, "This old monk has recently become quite topsy-turvy; why is that? Caoshan—
"You old fellow! How many people have found rest through Vimalakīrti’s silence? Yet you say he acted as a 'host for a story' for Caoshan!
The Master rebuked him, saying, "This bed-wetting little devil! If you don't understand, then stop. Why do you cause such a muddle?"
A monk asked, "What is it like when the wild goat has not yet hung its horns? The Master said, "A fellow among the grass. The monk asked, "What is it like after it has hung its horns?
The Master said, "He is crying out in confusion. The monk asked, "Ultimately, what is it? The Master said, "Before the donkey's business is finished, the horse's business arrives."
The Master asked a monk, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From Gushan. The Master said, "Gushan has a saying that does not cross the stone gate.
If someone were to ask you, what would you say? He replied, "Last night I stayed at Baoci. The Master said, "I would strike you across the back with my staff right now. What then?
He replied, "If you, Reverend, were to deliver this blow, it would not be in vain for me to receive the offerings of devas and humans. The Master said, "..."
When it came time for him to let the matter pass, a monk asked, "When many hands sift through gold, who is the one that obtains it? The Master said, "The one with skillful means obtains it.
The monk asked, "Does this student obtain it as well? The Master said, "It is still very far off."
Xuedou, acting on behalf of this monk, then gave a shout. He further said: "To those with skillful means, it is given with one hand;
to those without skillful means, it is given with both hands. Does the student receive it or not?"
"O Heavens, O Heavens!
The Lady Consort of the Military Governor of Min, Master Lian, the Lady Cui, has sent an envoy to deliver garments and goods.

She says that Master Lian has instructed me to request a reply from the Great Master. The Master said, 'Convey this message to Master Lian: go and receive the reply. The following day, the Master entered the governor’s residence."
The Master of Discipline said, "Yesterday, I received a reply from the Great Master. The Master said, "Then please show me that reply from yesterday.

The Master of Discipline extended both hands. The Master said, "When the Master of Discipline presents his letter in this manner, does it satisfy the Great Master's intent? The Master said, [silently].
It was still slightly lacking. [The student] asked, "I do not yet understand the meaning of the Great Master’s intent. The Master remained silent for a long time.
The student said, "Inconceivable, Great Master! The Buddha-dharma is profound and far-reaching."
Master Mingzhen of Anguo in Fuzhou (Part Two). The Master asked a monk, "When it is attained within the mind, even *eranda* grass becomes a sandalwood tree;
when one loses the essential meaning, even nectar becomes a garden of thorns. I want a phrase that possesses both the sense of attainment and loss.
The monk held up his fist and said, "It cannot be called a 'fist'. The Master said, "It is precisely because you call it..."
He made a fist.
Xuedou said, "A fellow who binds himself without a rope; he does not even recognize his own fist.
One day, Xuefeng grabbed him by the chest and twisted him, saying, "The entire great earth is this gate of liberation. Take my hand!"
He pulled him along, but the man refused to enter. The Master said, "I cannot blame you for this, Reverend.
Feng said, "Even so, what can be done about all these monks behind us?"
Chan Master Baofu Congzhan of Zhangzhou (12th case). A native of the Chen family of Fuzhou, he addressed the assembly, saying:
"This matter is like the spark struck from flint; it is like a flash of lightning. Whether you grasp it or fail to grasp it, you cannot avoid losing your life. A monk asked:
"I do not know, Master—does one who grasps it still avoid losing their life? The Master said: "Just now..."
"For now, let it be. Can you, Ācārya, still grasp it? The monk said, "If I cannot grasp it, I shall not escape the ridicule and suspicion of the assembly.
The Master said, "An adept! An adept! [The monk] asked, "What kind of mental activity is this? The Master said, "A ladle of excrement splashed across the face."
He did not even know it was foul.
Xuedou said, "Baofu possessed the fangs and claws to capture tigers and rhinoceroses alive;
this monk was no easy opponent to face. Nevertheless, let us for now let Baofu off the hook. But as for Xuedou himself—"

It is best to depart in pure stillness. During the course of daily activities, do not linger upon things; otherwise, it will be easy for this very thing to be exposed.
These words of exhortation are used only when there is no other choice; the ancients called them "the medicine for a dead horse.

If one were a true man of the Way, being addressed in such a manner would be like speaking in one's sleep. Now, as for you all—how is it within your own sphere? As for the twelve divisions of the teachings, have they...?
Can you employ even a single word? Can you employ even a single phrase from the sayings of the venerable elders of all quarters?
If it is the twelve divisions of the teachings, brothers, in which teaching do you reside? If it is the sayings of the venerable elders of all quarters, in which phrase do you reside?
Therefore it is said: the twelve divisions of the teachings cannot be chanted; they cannot be encompassed by either sage or ordinary person.
It has not flowed through past and present; it cannot be encompassed by words and teachings. To speak in such a manner is to have thrust one's head into the gateway of the teachings.
Let me break it apart for you. If there were a man who had not yet fully comprehended this message, and you spoke to him in this way, he would strike you right in the mouth.
Why do you get all worked up and agitated? You should not find it strange that he does so either, brothers.

This requires great discernment; do not fail to distinguish between the auspicious and the inauspicious. If there is anyone capable of such discernment, come forth and demonstrate it before the assembly for all to verify.
It was cold, and they stood for a long time.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "If one were truly quick-witted and sharp, they would simply leave as soon as they encountered [the teaching].
As for those like this, even if they travel thousands of miles away, what remedy is there? Advancing or retreating, they can only offer a 'How so?'—like a drunkard."
"What monk’s scent is there? Since it is thus, how is the matter of the Gate of the School?
All you venerable masters, here one must also be a man of substance before it can be attained; it is not at all easy.
Brothers, Drumshan does not begrudge his verbal karma in speaking to you all: it does not rely on remembering a single word, nor does it employ a single bit of effort, nor does it..."
Use a blink of an eye; do not even use a sigh. Sit firmly, and then hand it over and depart. O venerable masters, tell me: what is being handed over?
Is it the Buddha being handed over, or the Patriarch? Is it Chan being handed over, or the Way? Is it the matter above the Buddha, the phrase after nirvana?
If you hand this phrase over, you will be guilty of a great falsehood; it is called "the mind looking upward never ceasing. To my brothers—
Brother, there is no connection whatsoever. Regarding the portion of all people, how do you succeed to it?
Let us all be invited to examine it: what is it? Is it ordinary or is it sacred? Is it the Master Vairocana? Is it the Lord of the Dharmakāya? In what place does it dwell?
In what year did it exist? As for its squareness or roundness, its width or narrowness, its length or shortness, its greatness or smallness—try to say something about it!
Is there anything as large as a single hair that can cover it? Is there even a hair’s breadth of interval between it?
Where do you copy it from? Where do you write it down? O monks, it is so manifest and so immediate; why not simply [realize it]?

To accept and take up [the teachings] at a lower level, and furthermore to prick one's head into the tracks of others' words—learning within the realm of consciousness—what connection does this have [to the Truth]?
Have you not seen it said: "The intellect is a thief; consciousness is a wave"? To run about and seek in such ways, there will never be a moment of rest.

If you do not possess the eye yourself, but instead rely on others to discern and judge, copying from scrolls and transcribing from notebooks—even if you were to do so a hundred or a thousand times...
Ten thousand phrases from the Dragon Palace and the Ocean Treasury are swallowed up all at once; yet these are entirely the property of others and do not concern one's own affair.
This is also called "relying on knowledge through supernatural powers. It is like a water jellyfish that borrows a shrimp for eyes—it has no share of independence.
It is also like a blind person discerning colors; because they rely on the words of others, they truly cannot discern the true characteristics of color. If this is studying the scriptures...

Regarding the Vinaya and the Śāstras, there have always been those who specialize in them; thus, Mount Gushan has long maintained that "the Sūtras have Sūtra masters, the Vinaya has Vinaya masters, and the Śāstras have Śāstra masters.
They possess their respective cases and titles, their divisions and orders; by day they are studied at bright windows, and by night they are pursued by lamplight."
"The candle has been passed down and maintained by people for a long time. What do you say, Master? Is there anyone who can express this? Come forward and try to speak.
At that time, a monk asked, "What is the manifest principle of the present moment? The Master said, "Say something!
When the monk asked again, the Master shouted and sent him out.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "Venerable elders, whenever one travels on pilgrimage, one must recognize and discern the essential style of our school.
Do not merely seek words and pursue phrases, for there will be no end to it. Master Xuefeng said: 'The Buddhas of the three periods cannot chant it;
the twelve divisions of the teachings cannot contain it. Therefore, Master Gushan said: 'If someone were to come in such a manner, [the teachings] would never have been able to penetrate him.'"
When I spoke of this matter to him in such a way, he took yellow clay and stuffed it into my mouth. Is he not to be blamed?
Fearing that people might recklessly stuff others' mouths, I therefore say: Gushan has a phrase that does not cross the stone gate.
"How do you say it? Here, one must be the right person; do not speak recklessly. At that time, a monk asked, "What is the matter of not crossing over?
The Master picked up his whisk and struck him across the mouth, saying, "Do you understand? The monk said, "I do not understand.
The Master scolded him, saying, "You do not have the mettle for this!"
Addressing the assembly, he said: "I truly do not dare deceive you, my brothers, nor do I dare mislead you. Yet, no one can discern it.
A monk asked, "How should one proclaim the ancestral vehicle of the ultimate lineage? The Master struck him.
The monk bowed and intended to ask again, but the Master said, "Brother, you do not have the mettle for this."
Addressing the assembly, he said: "Under the gate of Gushan, one must not cough. At that time, there was a monk who let out a single cough. The Master said:
"What are you doing? A monk said, "I have a fever. The Master said, "A fever is fine.
He addressed the assembly, saying, "If one discusses this matter, it is like a single-edged sword. At that time, a monk asked, "The Master is a corpse;
the student is a corpse. What is the sword? The Master said, "Drag out this corpse! The monk responded.
"Yes," he replied. He returned his robe and bowl, packed his belongings, and departed immediately. That evening, the Master asked the Head Seat, "Is the monk who engaged in dialogue still here?
The Head Seat said, "He left right then. The Master said, "A good thirty blows for you!"
Yunju Qi said: "Gushan’s staff is both a reward for him and a punishment for him.
Those with eyes, try to deliberate upon this! Xuedou said: "The old masters everywhere all say that Gushan lost one eye;
yet they do not realize that beneath a heavy reward there must be a brave man. Nevertheless, even so, if you—”
If you examine this closely, you cannot avoid burying it all at once.

The Master asked a monk: "To understand directly is already difficult; to follow words only makes it more remote. If we speak of Buddhas and Patriarchs, they are separated by the vast distance of heaven and earth.
How do you understand this? The monk was speechless. Later, the Master raised this case and asked his attendant, "I..."

At the assembly, he requested the attendant to provide a turning word on his behalf. The attendant said, "If the Master speaks in such a manner, it is still as far apart as the ends of heaven and earth.
When the monk reported this to the Master, the Master summoned the attendant and asked, "Did you provide that turning word for the newcomer? Is that so?
When he replied, "Yes," the Master struck him and expelled him from the monastery.

There was a monk who compiled the *Shixue Shilu* (True Record of Xuefeng), which states: "The Master, having ascended the hall, remained silent for a long while and then looked at the assembly, saying, 'What is it?
The monk asked: 'Did Xuefeng have only this one phrase, or was there something else besides? The monk replied:"
"Is there anything else? The Master said, "It is according to the circle. He then went down the mountain.
Because Qunshan had previously ascended Xuefeng with the Master, Qunshan said, "I shall compete with the Master in walking. The Master said, "I have lost."
Chan Master Lingcan of Cuiyan in Mingzhou (three times) addressed the assembly, saying:
"Throughout this summer retreat, I have been talking here and there with you, my brothers; look—do my eyebrows still remain?"
Changqing said, "He was born. Yunmen said, "A barrier. Baofu said, "The heart of a thief is always apprehensive.
Cuoyan Zhi said, "Exerting one's utmost strength for the sake of the assembly; yet disaster arises from within the private door."
A monk asked, "A single grain of elixir can turn iron into gold; a single word of ultimate truth can transform an ordinary person into a sage.

As a student who has come before you, I beg the Master for that one point. The Master said, "I will not point it out. The monk asked, "Why will you not point it out? The Master said, "I fear you would fall back into the categories of ordinary and sage.
The monk said, "I beg the Master for the ultimate truth. The Master called to his attendant, "Bring some tea! and said, "Serve it here."
A monk asked, "When the ancients raised their mallets or held up their fly-whisks, what was their underlying meaning? The Master said, "Heretical teachings are difficult to support.
The monk asked, "Why was it that Zengyou could not paint a true likeness of Zhigong? The Master said, "How would you resolve this?
The monk asked, "In the midst of a perilous and evil path, what serves as the bridge and ferry? The Master said, "Yaoshan’s repeated and earnest instructions."

Chan Master Wolong Daopu of Quanzhou (Part Two). Addressing the assembly, he said: "Do not say that in this empty mountain there is no one to attend to you," and he immediately returned to his quarters.

A monk asked: "For those who have newly set their initial resolve and are beginners entering the monastic community, we pray for the Master’s instruction regarding the gates of expedient means. The Master struck [the meditation seat].
[The Master] struck the lintel of the gate and showed it to him, saying, "Is there anything further above this? The teacher said, "There is.
[The student] asked, "What is the matter above this? The teacher struck the lintel again.
Chan Master Shinaï of Yue Mountain in Yue Province (Part Three). Initially, he visited Xuefeng and gained a preliminary taste of the Way.
Later, at the invitation of the ruler of Min, he attended a vegetarian feast atop Qingfeng Tower. After sitting for a long time, he looked up and suddenly beheld the sunlight;

he attained a sudden, great enlightenment. He composed a verse, saying: "At the Qingfeng Tower, attending the official feast, On this day, the eyes of my entire life are opened wide. Only now do I believe..."
It is an ordinary matter from long ago; it was not brought here from Mount Hushu.
A monk asked, "What is the Buddha-body? The Master said, "Which Buddha-body are you asking about? [The monk] said, "The body of Śākyamuni Buddha."
The Master said: "The tongue covers the three thousand worlds.
When the Master was about to pass into nirvana, he presented this verse: "The visual faculty perishes along with forms; Auditory consciousness dissolves as sounds fade away.
To return to the source there is no other principle: Today is the same as tomorrow."
Chan Master Zhìyuán of Báizhāoshān in Ānzhōu (Part Two). A monk asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?
The Master said, "Suffering. [The monk] asked, "What is the Way? The Master said, "Pervasive."
Xuánzé asked, "What is the student's own self? The Master said, "The child of the fire element comes seeking fire.
Nányuè Jīnlún Kěguān Chánshī (1). The Master went to visit Xuěfēng. Xuěfēng called out to him, "Come closer!"
The Master stepped forward. Xuefeng gave him a kick. The Master immediately attained a profound resonance with it. Later, while presiding over the assembly, he said:
"Ever since that one kick from Xuefeng, until this very day my eyes have remained open; I do not know what kind of realm this is."
Chan Master Ba’en Huaiyue of Zhangzhou (Part II). A monk asked, "How should one conduct oneself throughout the twelve periods of the day?
The Master said, "To move is to die. The monk asked, "What about when one does not move? The Master said, "That is still merely guarding an ancient grave."
A monk asked, "What is the place where a student emerges? The Master said, "What fetters bind you?
The monk said, "How can I avoid failing to emerge? The Master said, "On whom does the fault lie?"
Chan Master Shaohang Longshou of Zhangzhou (Fanyi). While the Master was attending Xuefeng, he saw the wind blowing the leaves of taro plants.
Xuefeng pointed this out to him. The Master said, "I am very afraid. Xuefeng said, "This is a matter within your own house;
what is there to fear? At these words, the Master attained realization.
Chan Master Lingzhao of Longhua in Hangzhou (1): The Master pointed to the crescent moon and asked the senior monk Pu, "Where has that slice gone?
Pu said, "Do not engage in false conceptualization. The Master said, "You have lost a slice.
Pu was speechless.
There was a Confucian scholar from the Southern Monastery in the Capital (Luojing), who had extensively studied the past and present and was known as Zhang Baihui.
One day he went to visit the Master. The Master asked, "Are you not Zhang Baihui? He replied, "I dare not say so. The Master drew a circle in the air with his hand and asked, "Do you understand?
Zhang said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "If you do not understand even one, where [do you understand]?"
Baohui arrived from Taiyuan.
The first was the Venerable Fu (ten in total), originally known as Zuozhu; he resided at Guangxiao Temple in Yangzhou and lectured on the *Nirvāṇa Sūtra*.
There was a practitioner of Chan who was staying at a temple during a snow blockade. [Hui]fu happened to go there to participate in the merit-making ceremony.

When the lecture reached the topic of the three causes of Buddha-nature and the Dharma-body of the three virtues, he spoke extensively on the subtle principles of the Dharma-body. The Chan practitioner could not help but laugh. After the lecture concluded, [Hui]fu invited the Chan practitioner to drink tea.
[The Master] asked: "I, so-and-so, have always been of narrow and inferior intent. Relying on the literal text to explain the meaning, I have just incurred your laughter.

There are points where I have failed; I humbly hope for your instruction. The Chan practitioner said: "I truly laughed because you, Master of Commentaries, do not recognize the Dharmakāya. The Master said: "If this is how you explain it..."
"Where is it not so? [The student] said, "I request the Master to explain it once more. The Master said, "The principle of the Dharma-body is like the vast void:
vertically it exhausts the three periods of time; horizontally it spans the ten directions; it encompasses the eight poles and includes the two meanings.

Responding to conditions and meeting with stimuli, there is nowhere it does not pervade. The Zen practitioner said, "I do not say that what the Master has explained is incorrect; it is simply that..."
[The Master] said, "You have attained the measure and limits of the Dharma-body, yet in truth you do not yet recognize the Dharma-body within.

The Master said, "Since it is so, Zen practitioner, you should explain it for me. [The Master] asked, "Seat-master, do you believe it? The Master said, "How could I dare not believe? [The Master] said, "If it is thus..."

The Abbot suspended his lectures for ten days and sat upright in meditation within his chamber. Gathering his mind and concentrating his thoughts, he cast aside all conditions of both good and evil at once.
Following the instructions exactly, from the first watch of the night until the fifth watch, upon hearing the sound of drums and horns, he suddenly attained realization.
He ran to knock on the door of the Chan master, who asked, "Who is it? The Master replied, "It is I. The Chan master—
The other exclaimed, "Alas! You were taught to uphold the Great Teaching and proclaim it on behalf of the Buddha. Why did you come here last night drunk and lying in the street?
The Master replied, "Dharma-teacher, you have been lecturing on the sutras for some time now, twisting the nostrils of one's biological parents.
From this day forward, I shall never dare to act like this again. The Zen practitioner said, "Go for now; we shall meet tomorrow. The Master then departed.
The lecture ended. He traveled extensively to visit various masters.
When the Master first arrived at Xuefeng, as soon as he stepped onto the Dharma Hall, he looked around at Xuefeng and immediately went down to see the administrative officials.
Xuedou said: "The spiritual teacher of fifteen hundred people was caught in a single glance by Old Fu, who immediately raised high his banner of surrender.
The next day, he went up to the abbot’s quarters and paid his respects, saying, 'Yesterday I offended you, Master. Feng said, 'I knew it.'"
The matter was thus concluded.
Xuedou said, "As expected.
Later, a monk asked Yunmen, "What is the point of offending him? Yunmen immediately struck him.
Xuedou said: "Even if you were to strike a hundred thousand, ten million, or even a billion people, what use would that be?
You must have all the people of the entire world eat the staff before you can truly uphold Xuefeng. But tell me, Senior Monk Fu—what kind of eye does he possess?"
One day, Xuefeng pointed to the sun and showed it to the Master. The Master shook his head and departed. Xuefeng said, "Do you not approve of me, old monk?
The Master replied, "When you, the Abbot, shake your head, I wag my tail. Where is there any lack of approval toward you, the Abbot?"
Fengyun said, "Even when you arrive at another place, you must still conceal it.
Xuefeng asked the Master, "I have heard it said that Linji has three phrases; is this true? The Master replied, "Yes. Fengyun asked, "What is the first phrase?
The Master raised his eyes and looked at him. Fengyun said, "This is the second phrase. What is the third?"
The Master folded his hands and withdrew. Master Fēng held him in high esteem.
National Teacher Yàn asked, "Before your parents were born, where was your nose? The Master said, "You say first, elder brother.
Yàn said, "Now that you are born, where is your nose? The Master did not approve. Yàn then asked, "As for you..."
"How is it? The Master said, "Bring me the fan. Yan handed him the fan; when the Master questioned him again, he remained silent.
Yan then struck the Master once with his fist.

Xuefeng said, “He will return, but he will not return empty-handed. The Master said, “He will bring something back. Xuefeng said, “What will he bring back? "He is a man who has reached the ultimate," the Master said. "If you do not believe me, wait until I go and investigate him myself.

The Master asked, "What if you suddenly encounter an encirclement by the three armies? Yan replied, "He has his own path that reaches through the heavens. The Master said, "In that case..."
"If that were so, you would have left the palace and lost the hall. Yan said, "Where would one not be entitled to be honored?

one should strike him right here; this is where the sage’s arrow breaks. Others say: 'What if one suddenly encounters being surrounded by a threefold army?

"To deceive others is also to deceive oneself. Do you understand? It was like when the Marquis of Xiang seized the Jade of the Linked Cities, yet the Lord of Qin remained at ease and brought about peace.
