A monk came forward, circled the meditation seat once, struck his staff once, and said, "In the place where neither ordinary beings nor sages reach, please speak, Master.
The Master snapped his fingers once. The monk said, "How marvelous! Tongan has startled me into forgetting what came before and losing track of what follows. The Master said, "..."

"Where is the Acharya departing from? The monk replied, "I take my leave. The Master said, "Monks from the Five Lakes, practitioners with a single staff—before you have even reached Tongan, you will surely be struck with doubt. The monk said, "What I see nearby is not as good as what I hear from afar.
The Master said, "Greedy for a single cup of wine, he lost the fish in his entire boat."
The Master asked a monk, "When good and evil are not contemplated, the essence of mind manifests of itself. Did the ancients have a principle regarding this or not?
[The monk] said, "Is this not the profound meaning of the ancients? The Master said, "A foreigner drinking milk, yet returning to blame the skilled physician.
The monk bowed and departed. The Master said, "If you go to other places, do not say that you came to see Tong’an."

The Master asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "Wutai. The Master said, "Have you seen Mañjuśrī? The monk spread out both hands. The Master said, "Spreading out your hands is quite common;
who beholds Mañjuśrī? The monk said, "It is killing me with its urgency! The Master said, "If you do not see the wild geese in the clouds, how can you know the cold of the sandy deserts?
The monk said, "I am coming from afar to the Abbot’s quarters to beg for a word from the Master. The Master said, "Sun Bin."

[The monk] said, "Under your gate, I have merely discussed the divination of tortoise shells; it is said that a name is not bestowed in vain. The Master said, "Go and drink tea. The monk said, "I take my leave, Reverend Sir.
The Master said, "Though you have won one round of glory, you have lopped off a pair of feet."
The Master asked a monk, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From Jiangxi. The Master said, "How is the Dharma-way of Jiangxi compared to this place?
He replied, "Master, it is fortunate that you asked me; had you asked someone else, trouble would have arisen.
The Master said, "I was a bit hasty just now. He replied, "I am no infant; there is no need for these yellow leaves used merely to stop a child's crying. The Master said, "Forgive me."
The turtle was injured by the tortoise; whether it lives or dies depends on me. The monk asked again, "Having long cultivated the profound and subtle, how does one attain thorough understanding?
The Master said, "This old monk is deaf; ask clearly. The monk said, "A swift hawk does not strike at a sparrow by the fence. The Master said, "..."
"Standing before a mirror in the dark, who can distinguish beauty from ugliness? You say, 'How can one thoroughly understand the higher mechanism?
The Master said, 'Why bother? He said, 'Enough, enough. The Master said, 'Only now do you know how to board a boat; yet you already wish to cut through the waters.'"
The Master asked a monk, "Where do you come from? The monk replied, "From Taiyuan. The Master said, "How is the Dharma-way in Taiyuan these days?
The monk said, "I have only seen clouds following the rising sun and water following the ripples; I do not know how the Dharma-way in Taiyuan is.
The Master said, "Are you not from Taiyuan? The monk said, "Suffering! Suffering! The Master said, "You have not beheld the color of the ocean clouds; you have only a faint perception."
The sound of a drought-thunder. It is said that he exchanged gold for brass; hating the real and loving the false. The Master then returned to his quarters.

the sheep are lost because one looks for them on the long road. The monk said, "I have long admired the Master. The Master said, "Carrying the bamboo case [to study]."

The Master said, "How many hues of cloud emerge from the mountain peak? How uniform is the sound of the spring falling before the balustrade? The master said, "I did not ask about that matter."
"What is the Dharma of the One Vehicle? The Master said, "You, Ācārya, are brilliant and wise; this old monk is dull-witted. Try speaking on it before the assembly.

The Master said, "Understand beating the drum. [The monk] asked, "What is the Absolute Truth (*paramārtha-satya*)? The Master said, "Understand beating the drum.
He asked again, "I do not ask about 'this very mind is Buddha' (*cittam eva buddhaḥ*); what is 'neither mind nor Buddha' (*na cittaṃ na buddhaḥ*)? The Master said, "Understand beating the drum.

He asked, "What is the matter that transcends [all things]? The Master said, "Understand beating the drum. He asked, "When the myriad dharmas arise all at once, what then? The Master said, "Understand."
The drum was beaten.

[Regarding] the locus: How does one refine it? The Master said: "Both hands cannot lift it up.

Chan Master Jinfeng Congzhi of Fuzhou, a Dharma heir of Chan Master Caoshan Benji of Fuzhou (sixteen in total), addressed the assembly, saying: "The matter lies in the fitting together of the lid and the box;
the principle corresponds to the meeting point of arrowheads. Is there anyone who can say it? If there is someone who can say it, Jinfeng will divide half his monastery with them."
While he was staying there, a monk came out to pay his respects. The Master said, "It is easy to meet well; it is difficult for one to dwell together with others.

He then descended from his seat and addressed the assembly, saying: "If I were to bring up [this matter], I fear I would incur the criticism of others; yet if I do not bring it up, I fear [the consequences]."
The people were astonished and laughed. During that interval, [the Master] asked, "How was it? At that moment, as soon as a monk stepped out, the Master returned to his quarters.
That evening, a monk requested further instruction, saying, "Master, today when you uttered a phrase and a monk came forward, why did you not answer him?
The Master said, "It is very much like losing one's money and then suffering the penalty."
The Master picked up a pillow and said to the monk, "Everyone calls this a pillow; Jinfeng says it is not. The monk asked, "I wonder, Master, what do you call it?
The Master picked up the pillow again. The monk said, "In that case, I shall follow your lead.
The Master asked, "What do you call it? The monk replied, "A pillow. The Master said, "You have fallen into Jinfeng’s trap."
The Master was standing with a monk in attendance. The Master said, "I have a kōan (a causal occasion) that I shall present to you; you must not misunderstand it at all.
The monk said, "Please, Reverend, present it. The Master held up his whisk. After a long silence, the Master said, "I knew, Dharma brother, that you would misunderstand.
The monk looked here and there. The Master said, "Adding frost upon snow."
A monk came to inquire after him. The Master seized him and said, "I have a kōan; let me present it to you. The monk made a gesture as if listening.
The Master gave him a slap. The monk asked, "Why did you strike me? The Master said, "You simply take this slap;
I want this story to circulate."
Kaishan Xian said: "What a pity! A fine karmic occasion at Jingu Peak has been squandered by this monk.
If one wishes for the teaching to be propagated, this blow must be taken by Jingu himself; only then will it be effective."

While the Master was eating *hūbǐng* (sesame cakes), he picked up a piece, walked once around from the head of the seat (*shàngzuò bǎntóu*), and the assembly, seeing this, each and every one joined their palms in reverence.
The Master said, "Even if you raise your hands with full devotion, you will still only have attained half. That evening—

A monk requested instruction, saying, "Today, when the Master was distributing *hūbǐng* (sesame cakes), you saw the assembly of monks with palms joined and yet said, 'Even if one raises one's hands to the full extent, one still only gets half. We beg the Master to explain this completely.
The Master made a gesture with his hand as if picking up a cake and asked, "Do you understand? The monk replied, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Even Jinfeng could only speak of half."
Seeing a monk approaching, the Master said, "No need for seasonal greetings; bring me the first phrase. The monk said, "The early spring is still cold;
we humbly wish the Master ten thousand blessings in health. The Master said, "There is still this remaining. The monk said, "It cannot be helped that one must be scrutinized by others.
The Master said, "Who? The monk pointed to himself. The Master said, "It is no hindrance to be scrutinized by others."
The Master asked a monk, "Where did you set out from? He replied, "Zhaozhou. The Master said, "Whose Dharma heir was Zhaozhou? He replied, "Nanquan.
The Master said, "When did you ever leave Zhaozhou? He asked, "I do not know; what is your honorable intention, Master? The Master said:
Zhaozhou was indeed the successor of Nanquan. A monk came in the evening to seek instruction, saying, "Today I have received the Master’s compassion, yet I do not yet understand.
I beg the Master for further guidance. The Master said, "If you go to other places, do not say that these are the final words from Jinfeng.
The monk asked, "Why is it so? The Master replied, "I fear it would bring shame upon Zhaozhou."
When the Master saw the monk approaching, he rose from his seat. The monk then departed.
The Master said, "Just now, that monk from yesterday and I were of one and the same understanding. The monk turned his head and asked, "What did that monk from yesterday say?
The Master replied, "He was just like this. The monk said, "I knew Gold Peak had eyes. The Master said, "Setting aside Gold Peak for a moment, where will you eat your meal today?"

[The student] said, "If one speaks of the Way, it is immediately off the mark. The Master said, "In that case, there is no place from which it comes. [The student] said, "That is the 'old woman's heart' (compassionate persistence);
what can it possibly do? The Master said, "Jin-feng asked a monk, 'I have never been weak toward anyone; among them all, you, Reverend, are the one with whom I have nothing to say.'"
[The monk] said, "How could this be considered outside of one's lot? The Master said, "Small kindness obstructs great kindness.
When the Master saw a monk approaching, he held up his whisk and said, "This is a matter for a person of great capacity. Try to deliver a message and let me see it.
[The monk] said, "I do not wish to deceive the Master. The Master said, "Even those who practice filial piety are still rare."
[The monk] said, "Is this not a matter pertaining to the Great Man? The Master said, "I do not wish to deceive you, Venerable.
The monk said, "When it comes to this point, it is not easy to discern clearly. The Master said, "Quite so, quite so. The monk bowed.
The Master asked, "From where did you set out? The monk said, "Right here. The Master said, "Not only have you deceived yourself, but you have also deceived me."
The Master asked a monk, “Do you still know the single phrase of Jingu Peak? The monk replied, “I have known it for a long time. The Master said, “How so?
The monk then gave a shout and said, “Jingu Peak’s single phrase is today smashed to pieces! The Master said, “It seems you have once questioned others;
among them, your style, Reverend, is solitary and steep. The monk said, “One must not require someone else to examine it. The Master said, “Truly.”
Brass does not equal gold in value.

The monk said, "My conduct and movements are clear and distinct. The Master said, "Try presenting them to this old monk and see.

The Master said, "The grass-robbers have been utterly defeated."

After he took up residence, whenever anyone questioned him, he would often say, "Good brother," before answering. Consequently, people of the time called him "Brother Monk."
The Master was serving as the head gardener at Qinglin. Qinglin asked, "What are you doing today? The Master replied, "Planting vegetables.
Qinglin said, "The entire world is the Buddha-body; where do you plant them? The Master said, "As soon as the golden hoe moves the earth, the spiritual sprouts grow everywhere."
Linji went to the garden the following day and summoned Master Yun. The Master responded with an assent. Linji said, "I have planted a tree without a shadow;
I leave it for later generations to behold. The Master said, "If it is a tree without a shadow, how could it ever receive planting? Linji said, "It does not receive planting."
"Did you see its branches and leaves when you returned? The Master said, "I did not see them.

Lin said, "Since you did not see them, how do you know it does not receive planting? The Master said, "Precisely because I did not see them, I say it does not receive planting. Lin said, "So it is, so it is."
He addressed the assembly, saying: "Upon the palace of lapis lazuli, the radiance shines daily without partiality;

amidst the mountains of the seven treasures, the brilliance manifests at every turn with a firm foundation. The mud ox strides forth; the wooden horse neighs. The village elder sings his song; the woodcutter waves his sleeves.
Upon the road of the great sun, there are ancient melodies and profound sounds. Meeting beneath the forest trees, what further matters remain?"
King Ma. Having invited the Master from Qinglin, they passed through Jia Shan. The King came out to welcome him from afar and asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "A fine brother! Your imperial carriage with its six dragons is a marvel of a thousand ages; the ceremonial ranks line the jade steps as you emerge from the golden gate."
A monk asked, “When the moon rises above the clouds, what is it like? The Master said, “Three children embrace a flower drum; good brother, do not come to block my path to the goal.
The monk asked, “What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, “Good brother, the jade seal never leaves the Emperor’s hand;
how could the golden casket be permitted for outsiders to know? The monk asked, “What is...? (The question was left unfinished). The Master said, [as before].
"The style of our Master’s house. The Master said, "Riding a fine steed up a high tower; pointing out the Hu man's path with an iron whip.
[The monk] asked, "Regarding 'not falling into a mechanical trap,' please let the Master speak of it differently. The Master said, "The swift mechanism of the clear moon is beyond compare.
How many people have you questioned on this until now? [The monk] said, "I am asking the Master right now. The Master said, "Good brother! When the clouds part, there is no need for..."
"Conceal the nine-tailed fox; spare the life of your lord and return quickly to the hills.
Master Guangde of Wancu Mountain in Xiangzhou (Case 1). A monk asked: "The entire earth is a single corpse."
"Where will you be buried? The Master said, "Beneath Mount Beimang, among a thousand hills and ten thousand mounds.
Chan Master Huangbo Hui of Yungzhou, a successor of Chan Master Shushan Qiangren of Fuzhou (Case 1).
The Master went to visit Shushan, arriving just as he was sitting in the Dharma Hall. After paying his respects, he entered for an interview.
The Master first looked over the assembly and then posed a question, saying, "When one departs in a single kṣaṇa, how is it?
Shishuang said, "It fills the void; how will you go? The Master said, "It fills the void; it would be better not to go. Shishuang ceased speaking.
The Master went down to the front of the Sangha hall, where the Head Seat addressed him, saying, "Just now I observed how the Senior Monk (Upādhyāya) responded."

"Shang, your words are most extraordinary. The Master said, "This was merely a casual remark; it happened quite by chance. I venture to hope that you will show compassion and instruct this ignorant and deluded one.
The Seat-holder asked, "In the span of a single kṣaṇa, is there still any room for deliberation? At these words, the Master attained realization.
Chan Master Shoucheng Jingguo Huguo of Suizhou (Part Two). Together with Master Yanhua, they were at Baoci Monastery in Hunan.
While Master Ci was ascending the hall, Yanhua came forward and asked, "What is the true nature of *tathatā* (suchness) and Buddha-nature? Master Ci replied, "Who does not have it?
Yanhua did not find this satisfactory and requested further instruction from Master Shoucheng. The Master said, "Just ask. Yanhua repeated his previous question. The Master said:
Huishua attained enlightenment upon hearing these words and said, "Whether you serve as the head seat or as the abbot, I vow to assist you for the rest of my life.
Later, Huishua succeeded his teacher and resided at Huguo Temple.
A monk asked, "Who is it that walks where the Buddhas do not reach? The Master said, "Long-lobed ears and shaggy hair; a donkey’s face and a beast’s snout.
A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "One person transmits the empty; ten thousand people transmit the real.

A monk asked, "When everything is finished and all is settled at once, what then? The Master said, "A fellow standing on the steps. A monk asked, "A crane stands upon a withered pine. The Master said, [as before].
"How is it at that time? The Master said, "The one beneath the ground; what a mess! Question:
"When the Huichang persecution occurred, where did the Dharma-protecting benevolent spirits go? The Master said, "Two outside the main gate;
what a mess! Question: "How is it when a drop of water freezes? The Master said, "After the sun rises; what a mess!"
Chan Master Guiren of Changshui in the Capital (1). A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "Looking up, he alone raised his eyebrows; turning his head, he clapped his own hands. [The monk] asked, "What is the house style of the Master?"
The Master said: "Riding an ox while wearing a straw hat; crossing water while wearing boots and a tunic. He was asked, "What is the livelihood of Lingquan?
The Master said, "Striking the east wall with the west wall."
Chan Master Xing of Mount Dà'ān in Fǔzhōu (in three parts). A monk asked, "A person who has lost their way and is bewildered—please, Master, point directly.
The Master said, "Go forward through the triple gate. The monk asked, "Leaving behind the four propositions and cutting off the hundred negations—please, Master, speak.
The Master said, "Within the treasury of our King, there is no such sword."
A questioner asked, "When there are successive layers of locks and the message cannot pass through, what then? The Master said, "How could you have reached this point?
The questioner asked, "Once you have reached it, what then? The Master said, "What is the situation over there?"
Question: "What is the true within the true? The Master said: "The clay Buddha at the crossroads.

Chan Master Huanzhang of Ruilong Monastery in Hangzhou, successor to Chan Master Benren of Baishui in Gaoyang, Junzhou (Case 1), addressed the assembly, saying: "In years past, this old monk traveled throughout the Jiang..."
Externally, throughout Lingnan, Jing, and Hu, there is no monastery of those with true realization where he did not go to inquire.

This was because he wished to know the ultimate destination for himself and to gather with others today; yet, in all quarters, there were ultimately no divergent teachings, as they all simply instructed people to look within themselves.
Cease this frantic mind; do not seek it elsewhere. Simply follow the direction and let things be as they are, yet there is no "reality" to be so allowed.
Enjoy things as they come with the times, yet there is no "time" that can be employed. Even if one were to show compassion and speak with bitter words, one still cannot call day night.

Even with further skillful means and various methods, one can ultimately never point east and call it west. Should one somehow be able to do so, that would merely be a supernatural feat or a magical trick;

it would have nothing to do with me. If you are of the class who merely parrot words, yet fail to reflect upon yourselves and recognize your error, you are truly attempting to pluck flowers from the sky or grasp the moon in the waves. Will you ever succeed in applying your mind’s power? You should each now [exert yourselves accordingly].
Reflecting upon this, it suddenly dawned on me. Only then did I realize that the old man of Rui Long, having no other choice, had gone to such great lengths in his detours.
Would he have consented?
[He was] the Dharma heir of Chan Master Yuan’an of Luopu in Lizhou.
Chan Master Chuanchu of Qingfeng in Fengxiang Prefecture (Part Two). During a meal, the Master asked Beiyuan, "The former master said, 'Grass picked up at random with the hand.
Elder brother, what do you make of this? Beiyuan picked up a pair of chopsticks.
The Master said, "Even if you act like that, how have you ever dreamed of the former master? Beiyuan said, "Even if you understand it like this, how have you ever dreamed of him?"
The former master, Baishui, asked the Master, "I have heard that Luopu has a path of 'vital energy' (*shengji*). Is this so? The Master said, "It is.
Baishui said, "Setting aside the path of vital energy, bring me a phrase from the path of 'maturity' (*shu'). The Master said, "On the path of vital energy, the dead have none."
Shu said, "On the familiar road, there is no room for a living man. Shui asked, "This is the territory of Luopu; what about your own station, Senior?
The Master said, "Not only Luopu, even Jiashan could not cope with it. Shui asked, "Why could Jiashan not cope with it?
The Master said, "Have you not heard it said: 'The single path of the vital mechanism'?"
Chan Master Wuya Yanbin of Qizhou (Case 1). A monk asked, "Before one has yet taken human form, what was one doing?

The Master said, "A three-legged stone ox gallops upon the waves; a branch of auspicious qi divides before the moon. The monk asked, "When one enters directly on horseback with a single spear, how is it?
The Master said, "Even if you possess heroic faith and understanding enough to grasp the spear, you are still far from it."

The King of Qin [shot] at a hundred paces. [A monk] asked: "Having fought on the battlefields for so long, why was it that he did not achieve fame and merit? The Master said: "The two vultures fell at his hand; Li Guang did not deserve his name. [The monk] asked:

"Who was it that pierced the willow leaf at a hundred paces? The Master said: *Note: This passage is a dialogue from a Chan (Zen) kōan collection. The references to the King of Qin and Li Guang allude to historical anecdotes of archery skill found in the *Records of the Grand Historian* (Shiji). The Master’s responses employ paradoxical language characteristic of Chan pedagogy to point toward the ineffable nature of realization.*
If the General does not mount the Bian Bridge, the golden teeth will labor in vain to pick up the arrowhead.

The Dharma Successor of Chan Master Kewen Panlong of Yuanzhou was Chan Master Shandao of Muping in Yuanzhou (five cases total). He asked Luopo: "What is the state before the single bubble has yet arisen?"

Regarding this previous matter, Baofu said: "When moving the boat, one becomes familiar with the currents; when lifting the oars, one distinguishes the waves. The Master did not approve. He then questioned Panlong, who said:
"When moving the boat, one does not leave the water; when lifting the oars, one immediately loses the source. From this, the Master attained awakening.
Yunfeng Yue said, "If Muping had attained awakening upon hearing Lu Pu’s words, he would still have been slightly better off.
What a pity! He was drowned in the stagnant water of Panlong. Later, when someone asked, 'What is Muping? he replied, 'No need for the axe.
The Master said, 'As expected; he remains right here. All you practitioners of Zen," [he continued].** *(Note: The final sentence is left open as the source text ends abruptly.)*
Generally speaking, when setting out to transcend the mundane, one must distinguish between the heterodox and the orthodox, and discern the genuine from the counterfeit;
only by possessing a trace of the "eye-fiber" can this be achieved. Nevertheless, even so, it is like drawing a bow after the thief has already fled.
A monk asked, "What is the single phrase of Muping? The Master said, "It fills and obstructs empty space.
The monk asked, "What is the meaning of 'it fills and obstructs empty space'? The Master then struck him.
King Li asked, "What is Muping? The Master said, "No need for the axe. The King said, "Why is there no need for the axe?
The Master said, "I told you, it is Muping."
A monk asked, "When a deceased monk passes away, where does he go? The Master said, "The stone ox follows the ancient road;
the bright lamp shines in the daylight.
Whenever a monk came to consult him, the Master first had him carry three loads of mud. He had a verse that went: "Beside the eastern path on the southern mountain..."

The mountain is low; you who have newly arrived, do not refuse the mud on the three eaves. Alas, you have been traveling for many days; though the truth is clear, you do not understand and thus remain lost.
—Dharma Heir of Chan Master Yuelun of Huangshan in Fuzhou.
The Monk Tongquan of Yingzhou (Case 1). Huangshan asked the Master, "When the gates of heaven close, there is no path in the ten directions.
If you can speak, you may wave your hand and depart through the Zhang River. The Master said, "The hibernation chamber has not yet opened;
the dragon lacks its dragon-sentence. Huangshan said, "Is it because you speak thus? The Master said, "If it is so, say directly that it is; if it is not, say directly that it is not."
This is Shan Yun. He shook his hand and departed across the Zhang River.
He was the dharma successor of Chan Master Daoxian of Luoshan in Fuzhou, the eighth generation descendant of Qingyuan.
Chan Master Mingzhao Deqian of Wuzhou (23). After receiving the seal of approval from Luoshan, the Master rose above his contemporaries;
his spiritual acuity was so sharp and swift that no one dared to confront him.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "To meet with equal blades and contend for victory is rarely encountered; those who share the same death and the same life are but one in ten thousand.

Those who seek words and pursue phrases are as numerous as the sands of the Ganges; those who cite the ancients and the present destroy their own ancestral lineage. As for the single path beyond, even 'cracking the shell' and 'pecking the egg' are still at odds.
When Confucian scholars meet, they grasp their whips and turn their heads; what the śramaṇas see is truly a bitter thing indeed. He then cast [the whisk] aside.

Rejecting true gold, you follow the crowd to gather mere earth; report this to all the young children: do not waste yourselves in vain agitation. Even if you could understand his mystery, it would still be no more than adding tiles and rubble;

it is better to cast it aside once and for all, soaring beyond the great void. With this very sharp blade, who dares to approach? Let your arrows come as you will—only then can you be called a man of honor.
If you intend to swallow your voice in silence, a single spade-stroke will suffice to end it.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "The sword is hung high to manifest our school. Within this field for selecting Buddhas, are there any tiger-like or wolf-like Zen practitioners?
Whether entering birth or facing death, let them display their prowess as they will. If you are like one searching the ground for a needle, take care not to present a confused, blind bag;
I shall break your back—do not say I did not warn you."

Addressing the assembly, he said: "Upon the crown of the whirling wheel of the dry blade, the great jewel-light flies; before the edge of the tiger’s eye, the essential point of our school is revealed wide open.
What brilliant falcon is there who does not shrink from life and death? Raise your eyebrows and meet me!
As soon as a monk stepped forward, the Master said: "What a pity!"
He addressed the assembly, saying: "The bright star of midnight appears at midday; yet the foolish man still waits for the cock to crow at dawn. He then descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, he remained silent for a long while and said: "The wind here is somewhat harsh; this is not a place where you all can settle yourselves or establish your lives.
For now, let us go to a warm place to deliberate. He then returned to his quarters. The assembly followed him to the quarters, where they stood waiting.
[The Master] was in meditative concentration. The Teacher said, "As soon as one reaches a warm place, one immediately falls asleep. He took up his staff and drove them all away at once.
The Teacher arrived at Futian, where the assembly invited him to ascend the hall. Just as he took his seat, a monk stepped forward and said, "I, this humble monk, address the Master."

The Master then shouted him out. He then said, "Is there no one of heroic spirit? Let them freely lift and display [the banner]. Whether selecting a Buddha or selecting a Patriarch, now is precisely the time.
Therefore it is said: 'To startle the multitude, one must be a man of heroic spirit; to oppose the victor, one must be a lion’s cub.
If one lacks such an eye for selecting a Buddha, what is the use even after a thousand years?"

One day, the Master went to visit Shengguang. As soon as he stepped across the threshold, Shengguang was just about to lower his foot. The Master said, "Your skillful means are exhausted," and swept out his sleeves, departing.
When the Master arrived at Gushan, he was exhausted from his journey. Upon seeing him, the Mountain Master asked, "This man from Zhejiang—have you not come to Gushan at all?
The Master replied, "Since I entered the mountain ranges, I have suffered from a wind ailment and have been unable to pay my respects to the Great Master.

The Mountain Master walked several paces, then turned back and said to the Master, "Do you still have that wind ailment? The Master slightly extended both legs. The Mountain Master said, "I see now it is just that."
Huìchán said, "Venerable Master, you are fortunately a person of high station; you must not act so precipitately.
Guǐshān said, "If you do not acknowledge Gūshān, wait until you come up here and I will give you thirty blows. Huìchán said, "There are others who shall receive the blows."

Qing, the Eighth Patriarch, took up the story of Yangshan thrusting in his hoe. He asked the Master, "The ancient’s intention—was it in the act of thrusting the hoe, or was it in the gesture of joining the palms?
The Master called out, "Venerable Qing! Qing responded, "Yes. The Master said, "Do you still see Yangshan in a dream? Qing said:
"Do not speak down to the senior monks; simply engage in consultation. The Master said, "If you wish to consult, there is already the Great Teacher of five hundred men at the Head Seat."

While the Master was at Zhaoqing, there was a communal work assignment (pǔqǐng) to carry earth. Zhaoqing took up his staff, sat in the middle of the road, and asked a monk, "Carrying it to the upper cave?
Carrying it to the lower cave? The monk replied, "Carrying it to the upper cave. Zhaoqing struck him with the staff. He then asked another monk, who replied, "Carrying it to the lower cave.
Zhaoqing likewise struck him with the staff. He then turned to ask the Master. The Master set down the earth, joined his palms, and said, "I request the Master [to strike me]."
Jian asked, "Qingxiu has departed.
Miaoxi said, "I would have struck him across the back with a staff; let us see how he would have settled the matter.
While the Master was at Zhaoqing, he pointed to a mural on the wall in the hall and asked a monk, "What deity is this? The monk replied, "A protective benevolent deity."
The Master said, "When the Huichang persecution took place, where did you go? The monk was speechless. The Master then ordered the monk to ask Attendant Yan.
Yan replied, "In what kalpa have you encountered such hardship? The monk reported this to the Master.
The Master said, "Even if Attendant Yan were to have a thousand followers hereafter, what use would that be? The monk requested the Master to provide another answer. The Master—
[The monk] asked, "Where have you been? The Master was at Fayun Monastery;
he was carrying a torch and passing in front of the refectory when he encountered several brothers. One of them said, "This is the fire of the community of monks;
where are you taking it by stealth? The Master turned the torch around and held it up, saying, "In the portion belonging to the Elder [Upādhyāya], there is much."
He had been inside for a short while. The monk said nothing. The Master said, "This lot of fellows will all freeze to death tonight.

While the Master was at Zhiyi’s monastery, he served as the head seat (shouzuo). He usually would not accept purified water. The warden became angry and said, "The Elder does not understand the distinction between the defiled and the pure;
why do you not accept the purified water? The Master leaped down from his bed, picked up the pitcher of purified water, and said, "This..."
"Which one is defiled and which one is pure? The master remained silent. The Teacher smashed the pure vase.
While the Teacher was at the residence of Imperial Tutor Wang, he went to welcome a wooden Buddha. The Tutor asked, "What would you do if you suddenly encountered Danxia?
The Teacher seized it by the head and lifted it up, saying, "I must also entrust it to someone."
Shuangyan was about to hand over his monastery to the Master. He invited the Master to drink tea and said, "I have a question to ask you, Senior.
If you can answer it, I shall hand over the monastery to you. He then cited the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*:
"All Buddhas and the Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi of all Buddhas emerge from this sūtra. He then asked, "Tell me, what is this sūtra?"
The man said, "Master, as for 'speaking' or 'not speaking,' set that aside for a moment. Master, what exactly do you call this sutra?
Yanku was speechless. The Master then cited the sutra, saying: "All worthy sages are distinguished by means of the unconditioned dharma (asaṃskṛta-dharma).
All worthy sages take the unconditioned as the ultimate standard. Based on what, then, could there be distinctions? [Yanku] remained silent. The Master continued: "Only..."
"Regarding 'as differentiation,' this is a word that transcends [convention]; it is not a word that transcends [convention].
If it were to transcend, then all worthies and sages would transcend it. If it does not transcend, what exactly do you call 'differentiation'? Yan remained silent. The Master said:
"Alas! Xuefeng spoke from the very bottom [of his realization].
When you, Master, arrived at the place of Elder Tan, Tan said: 'As for those who study the Way, one must reach the dwelling place of the whole person;
one must also reach the dwelling place of the half-person. You asked about the dwelling place of the whole person, but you did not ask: 'What is the half-person?'"
Wherever he was, Tan remained silent without response. Later, he instead had a junior monk ask the Master, "Do you wish to recognize this half-person?
He is merely a fellow who plays with lumps of mud."
Among the assembly of the Master, there was a monk who had gone to live in a hermitage. After one year, he returned to pay his respects.

The Master said, "An ancient said, 'If you do not see someone for three days, do not look upon them as the person they once were. Then, opening wide his chest, he said, 'Tell me, how many hairs on my chest do you see?
The monk was speechless. The Master asked, 'When did you leave your hermitage? He replied, 'This morning.'"

The Master said, "When you came, to whom did you entrust this broken-legged cauldron? The monk remained speechless. The Master then shouted him out. Later, while visiting Baoning, they met on the road. The Master said, "Brother, you are one of my fellow practitioners. He then pointed at his nose with his hand and said, "This thing is a hindrance; I cannot penetrate it. Could you remove it for a moment? Ning replied, "I can. The Master said, "If you can, then remove it. Ning remained silent. The Master said, "If you cannot, then do not speak. Ning again remained silent. The Master said, "If you cannot even do this much, how will you ever be able to save others? Ning was speechless. The Master struck him once and departed. Later, when Ning was teaching at Changqing, the Master went there to visit him. Ning asked, "What is the meaning of Bodhidharma coming from the West? The Master said, "The Great Way has no gate. Ning said, "I have already understood. The Master said, "Have you understood? Have you understood? Ning remained silent. The Master said, "If you cannot even answer this much, how will you ever be able to save others? Ning was speechless. The Master struck him once and departed. When the Master was about to pass away, he called for Ning. Ning entered the room. The Master said, "I am going now. Ning said, "Where are you going? The Master said, "To the place where there is no place to go. Ning remained silent. The Master said, "If you cannot even say this much, how will you ever be able to save others? Ning was speechless. The Master struck him once and passed away. It is said that when the Master was first at Baoning, he saw Ning’s portrait and remarked, "This man has a bit of spirit. Later, when he encountered him on the road, he said, "This fellow has some power. When Ning later visited him at Changqing, the Master said, "I have been looking for you for a long time. Ning said, "I have been here all along. The Master said, "Where have you been? Ning remained silent. The Master said, "If you cannot even say this much, how will you ever be able to save others? Ning was speechless. The Master struck him once and departed. Thus, the Master’s words were like a thunderbolt, shattering the barriers of the world. Those who hear them should reflect upon them deeply. Do not merely take them as empty talk. If you can understand this, you will see that the ancient masters were not merely playing with words; they were pointing directly to the source of life and death. If you can grasp it here, you will know that the Buddhas and patriarchs have never been anything other than this. If you fail to grasp it here, you will wander in birth and death for aeons. Therefore, I urge you: do not let this opportunity pass. Examine it thoroughly. If you can penetrate it, you will realize that from the very beginning there has been nothing to attain, and from the very beginning there has been nothing to lose. This is what is meant by "the Great Way has no gate. It is not something to be sought through intellectual speculation; it is something to be realized within oneself. If you can awaken to this, you will be free from all obstructions. If you cannot, you will remain stuck in the delusions of the mundane world. Therefore, I urge you to investigate this matter with all your heart. Do not let it be lost in vain. This is the true teaching of the Buddhas and patriarchs. May you all realize it. Do not doubt it. Cao Tang Qing said: "Mingzhao only recognized the traveler from Guazhou; he did not recognize Guotai.

While the Master was lying ill, National Teacher Taishen came to visit him. As soon as he entered the abbot’s quarters, the Master said, “A-ye-ye!
A-ye-ye! Uncle Taishen, save this old monk! Taishen replied, “What is there for the Master to save?
The Master raised his head, took a look, and said, “Ei! Those eyes are dark and piercing; they remain exactly as they were before, Uncle Taishen.”
The Master sat down, then turned his body to face the wall, and they did not see one another again.
When the Master’s illness had healed, he went to visit Guo Tai. Guo Tai led his assembly to the gate to receive him. The Master pointed to two *vajra* statues and said, "These two fellows—"
"What are you doing here? [The Master] assumed the *vajra* posture. The Master said, "The Yellow-Faced Old Man in the hall is laughing at you.
A monk asked, "What is it like before the lion has emerged from its den? The Master said, "A swift hawk cannot catch up. [The monk] said, "Once it has emerged from the den..."
"What then? The Master said, "Ten thousand miles of swirling confusion. "How is it when one wishes to emerge but has not yet emerged?
The Master said, "Perilous. "How is it when proceeding onward? The Master said, "Exiled."
Chan Master Weikang of Qingping in Jizhou (1) addressed the assembly, saying: "Without moving one's spirit or expression, there is already the sense of winning or losing.

[The Master] went out. A monk asked, "What is the first phrase? The Master said, "If you want your head, cut it off right now.
Chan Master Yizhao of Jinzhu in Wuzhou (the second of two cases). When a newly arrived monk came, the Master lifted the curtain with his hand and made a gesture as if removing his hat.

The Master addressed the assembly with this verse: "The tiger’s head with its horns—hard for anyone to handle; The spark of flint and the flash of lightning must be spread thickly.
Even for a heroic man, it would be difficult to offer a response; How could one who is bewildered understand the shifting interplay?"

The Monk of Kuangshan in Jizhou (Case 1) addressed the assembly, saying: "The road to Kuangshan, the road to Kuangshan! Its cliffs and precipices are so steep and perilous that people find it difficult to tread upon them.
If a traveler hesitates for even a moment, they are separated by a thousand mountains. One clear phrase transcends both Buddhas and patriarchs."
Master Xichuan Hui (Case 3): Luoshan asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "I have traveled far from Xichuan and have recently departed from Kaiyuan.
He then stepped forward and asked, "As for the matter at hand right now, what is it? Luoshan made a gesture of dismissal and said, "Sit down and drink some tea."
The Master hesitated. Shanshan said, "The autumn air is somewhat warm; go out.
The Master descended from the Dharma Hall and sighed to himself, saying, "Under Mount Emei, I picked up a single arrow of thistle and mugwort, intending to settle the chaos of the world.
Today, having arrived at Old Teacher Chen’s camp in the Fujian region, my bow is broken and my arrows are spent. Alas! Alas!"
The next day, Luoshan ascended the seat. The Master stepped forward and asked, "The doors and windows are wide open; who is standing in the courtyard? Luoshan gave a shout. The Master was speechless.
Luoshan said, "Your feathers are not yet complete; the tips of your wings are not yet whole. Go for now."
The Master went to visit Shenguang. As Shenguang was seated, the Master went directly up to his side, stood with palms joined, and remained there.
Shenguang asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "I am still waiting for your answer," and then he descended.
Shenguang took up his staff and whisk, went down to the front of the Sangha hall, and upon seeing the Master, raised the whisk and asked him, "What do you call this? The Master said:
Daring to die while still breathing, Guang then lowered his head and returned to the abbot’s quarters.
Chan Master Huiji of Huanglong in Yuezhou was a successor of Chan Master Yan of Xuanchuan in Huai Prefecture (total of two). He was the son of the Zhang family of Qinghe. A monk asked: "What is..."
"The King’s Sword. The Master said, "It does not harm the myriad species. [The student] asked, "What of the one who wears it? The Master said, "Blood splatters against the Brahma Heaven.
[The student] said, "Truly excellent that it does not harm the myriad species! The Master then struck him.
A monk asked, "A hair swallows the vast ocean; a mustard seed contains Mount Sumeru. These are not the fundamental matter of a student. What, then, is the student’s fundamental matter?
The Master said, "The sealed casket is opened in the marketplace. The monk asked, "What is one who is in great doubt?
The Master said, "The bow falls from the cup within the plate set before him. The monk asked, "What is one who is without doubt? The Master said—
[The Master] said: "While seated again, the bow fell from the tray onto the cup. He asked, "What is it like when the wind is calm and the waves are still?
The Master replied, "A five-liang weight hanging from the top of a hundred-foot pole."

"Mind-only. What do you say to this, my son? The Master pointed to the leaning board and said, "What does the Master call this?

Dizang had no reply. Xuansha asked the Master (Dizang), and the Master said, "This fellow, having been struck by a staff, does not know where it came from."

The Master was performing the memorial service for Xuansha and invited Baoen to offer the *yaoshi* (medicinal food). When Baoen saw that there was no portrait of the deceased at the altar, he asked, "Is there a true likeness here?
The Master gestured with his hand and said, "Look! Baoen said, "So, there is truly no likeness. The Master replied, "It is very much as if we do not know each other."
The Master, along with Changqing and Baofu, entered the prefectural seat and saw a screen depicting peonies. Baofu said, "What a beautiful peony flower!
Changqing said, "Do not let your eyes deceive you. The Master said, "What a pity for such a fine flower."
Xuánjué said: "Regarding the words of the three venerable elders, are there any distinctions between the intimate and the distant?

A monk came from Baofu; the Master asked him, "How do they instruct their disciples there? The monk said, "One day the Abbot addressed the assembly, saying:
'Block up your eyes so that you cannot see; block up your ears so that you cannot hear.'"
"I have sat down and suppressed your faculty of thought, teaching you that it cannot be used for discrimination. The Master said, "I ask you this:
I have not blocked your eyes; what do you see? I have not blocked your ears; what do you hear? I have not sat upon your faculty of thought."
"How do you distinguish them? The monk had an awakening upon these words.

The Master asked a monk, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From Qinzhou. The Master said, "What have you brought with you?

The Master asked a monk from Zhaoqing, "While you were at Zhaoqing, was there anything unusual that you heard? Try to recount it.

The Master said, "Your words have fallen into error."
The Master asked a monk, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From Baoen. The Master said, "Why do you not remain there?

It is finished. If you enter through the gate of Mañjuśrī, all grasses, trees, tiles, and pebbles shall assist you in triggering your awakening.

Chan Master Shuilong of Quanzhou (Case 1) held up his staff and said to the assembly, "In thirty years of dwelling in the mountains, I have gained its strength.
A monk asked, "What kind of strength did the Master gain? The Master said, "Crossing mountains and crossing ridges, eastward..."
He leaned on his staff and returned directly to the abbot’s quarters.
Master Yung-feng K’uang-shu of T’ien-t’ai addressed the assembly, saying: “It is simply that sentient beings do not realize it in their daily activities.
For example, consider the trichiliocosm with its suns, moons, stars, rivers, mountains, seas, and marshes—all of them...”
Sentient beings enter from one pore into another pore; yet the pores do not become smaller, nor do the worlds become larger.
The beings therein neither perceive nor know this. To make this easy to understand: even the daily activities of the Venerable Elder are likewise unknown to him.
A monk asked, "The monk carries the image by day; the image carries the monk by night. I do not understand the meaning of this.
The Master said, "Acarya, did you not just come from the tea hall?"
The Venerable Master Jing of Tiantai Guoqing (Part Two). When the Master went to visit Xuansha, he encountered the Master ascending the hall and saying:
"All of you, if you can for the duration of your lives act as if you had lost your parents, I guarantee that you will attain thorough penetration. The Master then asked:
"As it is said in the scriptures, one must not use a mind of known knowledge to fathom the unsurpassed wisdom and vision of the Tathāgata. Furthermore..."

"How is it? Sha said, "You say you have thoroughly investigated to the very bottom. Can the mind of knowing still be measured by calculation? At these words, the Master gained faith and entered [the Way].
A question was asked: "Whenever I sit in meditation, my thoughts fly about in confusion. I do not yet understand the method for subduing them;

I pray that you will grant me your instruction. The Master said: "If, while sitting at ease, your thoughts fly about in confusion, take that very mind which is flying about and investigate the place from which it flies.
When you investigate and find no such place, then where can the wandering thought exist? Turn back and investigate the investigating mind itself."
Where does the mind that can investigate abide? The wisdom that can illuminate is fundamentally empty. The objects upon which it relies are likewise quiescent.
That which is quiescent yet not-quiescent is because there is no person capable of quiescing. That which illuminates yet does not-illuminate is because there is no object to be illuminated.

When both object and wisdom are quiescent, the mind and its deliberations are at ease. It does not seek out branches externally, nor does it dwell in meditative concentration internally. These two paths—
Both are extinguished; the single nature is serene. This is the essential path for returning to the source.

"City Tail. "The butcher, the executioner, the meat-carver. "The cauldron-and-broth place of hell. "To grasp it through conceptualization. If you understand it in this way, you may serve as a teacher or a craftsman for gods and humans;
yet, compared to the gate of the patch-robed monks, there is a vast difference between heaven and earth. Furthermore, there is another kind of person.
Simply remain on your long bed and act as a true person. You ask, "Between these two types of people, which one has the superior quality?
There is no need for concern; take care.

The Master said, "What a fine, unburdened Chan guest! The monk said, "That is already quite a burden. The Master said, "You spent last summer here, did you not? The monk said, "I did not.

The Parting Words at Liangshan Guan state: "One must also sweep them away.

Chan Master Shikuan of Zhimen in Suizhou (Five Cases). When the Master returned from traveling the mountains, the Head Seat went out to the pine gate to receive him.
The Head Seat said, "Traveling through the mountain crags was no easy matter. The Master picked up his staff and said, "I relied entirely on the power of this.
The Head Seat snatched the staff away and threw it to one side. The Master threw himself down. The assembly stepped forward to help him up. The Master picked [up the staff].
With his staff, he drove them all away at once. Then, looking back, he said to the Head Seat, "I told you that this very power is what one must fully attain.
Huanglong Nan remarked, "Although Mingjiao knows how to fall and how to rise, he did not realize that his cleverness resulted in clumsiness."
The Master visited Baimiao. Baimiao said, "I have a verse on the wooden fish. The Master said, "Please recite it for me.

Baimiao said, "We humbly observe that this piece of rotten wood makes no distinction between Buddhas and sentient beings; yet, if struck with a staff, it cuts off the paths of both the holy and the ordinary.
The Master asked, "Does this verse have a point of attainment, or does it lack one? Baimiao said, "It lacks a point of attainment. The Master [laughed].

The Master said, "The Buddha and sentient beings are not distinct. Huh? His attendants hurriedly tried to rescue him, saying, "There is a distinction. The Master said, "It must be such that the paths of the sage and the ordinary person are utterly severed.
Huh? At that moment, the entire assembly at Baidiyo turned pale with alarm.
Wuzu Keizan came to attend upon the Master. The Master asked, "I do not ask about the various doctrines and teachings;
bring me a phrase that does not involve mud or water. Keizan said, "The talk has fallen. The Master said, "A fellow who drags through the mud and carries water.
Keizan said, "Fortunately, the Master is a great man. The Master said, "You bald-headed fellow! Go to the hall!"
One day the Master raised his whisk and said, "This of mine is for those of middling and inferior capacity.
A monk asked, "What if a person of superior capacity were to arrive? The Master replied, "Beat the drum for the three armies."
A monk asked, "At the beginning of the new year, is there still Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "No. The monk said, "Every day is a good day;
every year is a good year. Why then is there none? The Master said, "When Mr. Zhang drinks wine, Mr. Li gets drunk."
[The master] said, "To be so old and decrepit, yet to have a dragon's head and a snake's tail! The Master said, "Mingjiao has lost ground today.
Chan Master Shouchu of Dongshan in Xiangzhou (the ninth): He visited Yunmen. Yunmen asked, "Where have you recently come from?"
The Master said, "Chadu. Mumon asked, "Where did you spend the summer retreat? The Master said, "Baoci in Hunan. Mumon asked, "When did you leave there?
The Master said, "On the twenty-fifth of the eighth month. Mumon said, "I grant you three blows of the staff.
The next day, the Master went up to pay his respects and said, "Yesterday I received the Master’s three blows of the staff; I do not know what my fault was."
[The Master asked: "Where? The Gatekeeper said, "You rice-bag! In Jiangxi and Hunan, people are already discussing it like this.
At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment and said, "In the future, at some other time, I shall pitch a hermitage in a place where there is no human habitation.
I will not store a single grain of rice nor plant a single stalk of hemp. I will receive those coming and going from the ten directions and give them all [what they need], and then I shall depart."
Drive out the nail. Pull out the wedge. Strip off the greasy cap. Cast off the stinking robe of the hawk.
Let him be free and unencumbered, becoming a true monk—would that not be a joy? Yunmen said: "Your body is no larger than a coconut, yet you can open such a wide mouth!"
Xuedou said: "Yunmen’s bearing was like that of a king; yet when pressed, he would melt away like ice and crumble like tiles.
Had he enforced his command at that time, his descendants would not have been cut off. Baizhang Wendeng said: "Great Yunmen!
At the single question from Dongshan, he was reduced to breaking into a sweat on his forehead and having glue stick in his mouth."

He reveals it to sentient beings: on the northern slope of Mount Chu, by the southern bank of the Han River, he beats the Dharma drum to assemble the disciples of Chan, raises the ancestral wind to clarify the Patriarchs' intent.
If you say it is raising an eyebrow or blinking an eye, pointing a finger or holding up a whisk, or even clearing one's throat and coughing—this is merely a cloth for wiping bowls in the kitchen.
What are you talking about? Do you understand? This is just a patch-robed monk’s worn-out straw sandals; this blind fellow!
This lacquer bucket is a ghost playing with its own spirit. Whether it is "all like this" or "not all like this," it is merely a toilet stick from the latrine.
To use such things to uphold the matters of the ancestral lineage is entirely the work of demons and heretics; it is a slander against the Mahāyāna.
To exterminate the Hu race would be worlds apart from you. But tell me: upon what principle do these patch-robed monks rely?
Come forth and speak before the assembly! Each must lend a hand to this broken-legged cauldron, for it is precious that the lineage of the school remain unbroken.
This also demonstrates that there are people within the monastic community. Is there anyone? If not, Dongshan will not spare his eyebrows and shall unravel this tangle for you.

The matter of this tangle is right before your eyes: the myriad phenomena, the heavens and earth, the hundreds of thousands of Buddhas, the sun, moon, and stars, the hells and the three evil realms—all these are encountered daily through every thought and movement of the mind; they are all [the Buddha-nature].

"Virtue lies within oneself. Why not seek it here? If you can suddenly perceive it with distinct clarity, your journey will not have been in vain, and you will naturally attain a field of peace and ease.
Dongshan’s words here are merely like trying to cure a dead horse with medicine.
As for a monk with clear eyes, he would simply take his straw sandals and shove them into [the teacher’s] mouth—would such a person still be considered at fault?
What seems strange is not actually strange. Tell me: on what basis do you catch it? Search beneath your own heels;
if there is even the slightest discrepancy, I shall break your waist. Do not be careless!

He addressed the assembly, saying: "The enlightened faculty is obscured by itself; when thoughts cease, one is lost at the source. The myriad dharmas are but dust; whether speaking or remaining silent, they are difficult to manifest.
This is not a dharma within the realm of emotion—do not give rise to various kinds of mental states. Apart from these words and phrases, there is another way to deliberate.
But tell me, setting these aside, how do you deliberate? Is there anyone here who truly understands? Clearly and directly, I shall analyze and break it down for you. Clearly and directly...
It is displayed; it is proclaimed with clarity; it is chanted with clarity. There is no further concealment or covering; it is purely the dry, bare teaching of Chan.

Why is this? Because wisdom has both the deviant and the correct.

Chan Master Daizun of Nantai in Tanzhou (the second of two entries) addressed the assembly, saying: "Regarding the ancestral vehicle from above, how should it be handled?"
This is the essential framework for arising. How can one engage in discourse? Can the two characters "Buddha-Dharma" suffice?

Although this is so, the subtle does not admit a breeze, yet the great thoroughfare allows for carriages and horses. If one speaks but a single word from the perspective of principle and realization, it shakes heaven and earth;
mountains, rivers, and the great earth become tranquil, and the seas and rivers are clear. The Dharma-preaching of all Buddhas of the three periods of time is manifest before us. If...
It is clearly so. Before the Hall of the Ancient Buddha, we shall ascend together to the other shore.
A monk asked, "What was it like before Niutou saw the Fourth Patriarch? The Master said, "He put on his clothes and ate his meals. The monk asked, "What was it like after he saw him?
The Master said, "The alms bowl was hung upon the wall."
Nanyue Poyuan addressed Chan Master Qiyou (in two parts). While ascending the hall, upon hearing the sound of the wooden board, he said: "How excellent! Three strikes of the board;
all you masters of the Way come to inquire. Since you already well know the proper timing, I shall not speak further."
A monk asked, "In the Western Heavens, they use a wax figure as a test; what do you use as a test here in this land?
The Master said, "A Korean person’s straw sandals. Xinzhou Ehu Yunzhen Chan Master (Case 1): A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "The teacher."
"No. [The monk] asked, "What is the house style of鹅湖 (Ehu)? The Master said, "The guest is the host's teacher.

Chan Master Tianwang Hui of Luzhou (Part Two). A monk asked, "What is the Great Canon of the Teachings?

The subsequent text is extensive; we shall leave it for another day. As for the fence of the eastern house and the wall of the western house—within one's own domain, what should be done?
The monk had no reply, so the Master struck him.
A monk asked, "How is it that [the Dharma] descends from heaven? The Master said, "The wind and rain follow their proper seasons.

The two senior monks, Shenming and Shangzuo (two individuals), heard that when a monk asked Fayan, "What is form? Fayan held up his whisk;
sometimes he said, "Cockscomb flower," and sometimes he said, "An undershirt against the skin. These two masters traveled a great distance specifically to visit him.
He then asked, "I have heard that the Master has three kinds of speech; is this true? Fayen said, "Yes.
Shen said, "A hawk flies over Silla," and immediately returned to the assembly. At that time, Li Houzhu was present among the disciples and did not agree with this.
He said to Fayen, "Tomorrow, I shall prepare a tea ceremony for Your Reverence and invite these two men to engage in further dialogue. The next day, after the tea ceremony was concluded—

"Today I have received an imperial decree to engage in formal dialogue. Does the Master grant permission? Yan said, "Permission granted. Shen said, "A hawk flies over Silla.
He took the ceremonial silk and departed immediately; the assembly dispersed all at once. At that time, Faden was serving as the *vina* (chant master).
He struck the bell to assemble the monks before the Sangha Hall to interrogate the two masters. Once the assembly had gathered, Faden asked, "I have heard that the two Senior Masters have long..."
At Yunmen, there was a most extraordinary circumstance. Let me cite one or two cases for you to deliberate upon. Desheng said, "An ancient said:
'A white egret descends to the field—a thousand dots of snow; a yellow oriole perches on a tree—a single branch of blossoms. Venerable Director, how would you deliberate upon this?
As Deng hesitated, Desheng struck him with his sitting mat and immediately returned to the assembly.
The two elders arrived at the Huai River and saw a man pulling in a net. A fish had escaped through the mesh.
Xuedou said, "Brother Ming, how brilliant! He is just like a true monk. Ming said, "Even so, it would have been better if he had not run right into the net in the first place.
Xuedou said, "Brother Ming, you lack awakening. It was not until midnight that Ming finally realized this.
Chan Master Gu of Jianfu in Ruzhou (Part Three). The Master’s reputation had reached Yunmen for over a hundred years.
Upon reading his records, he gained insight into his own realization and thus became his successor. He addressed the assembly, saying: "The Buddhas of the three periods cannot look up to him;
the ancestral masters of the world have no choice but to remain tongue-tied. Those who know this should skillfully maintain it themselves; those who do not yet know it must not cease their efforts."
"What is there to wait for?
He addressed the assembly, saying, "The sword has gone far away; you are merely marking the boat. Then he descended from his seat.
Addressing the assembly again, he raised the case of Master Heng of Baizhang: "Sometimes when he ascended the hall and the assembly had just gathered, he would simply say, 'Go drink tea.'"
Sometimes, as soon as the assembly has gathered, he would say, "Take care" (*zhēnzhòng*). Sometimes, as soon as the assembly has gathered, he would say, "Rest," and immediately descend from his seat.
He frequently used these three occasions as teaching opportunities. Later, he composed a verse on these three turns of circumstance, which says:
"Bai Zhang has three secrets: 'Drink tea,' 'Take care,' and 'Rest. If you can directly accept them, I dare say you have not yet."
Chè: "O Great Assembly! As for Master Héng composing this verse—tell me, what was his realization?
Do you know where he gained or lost? According to him, during his three previous formal sermons, he was like a fine man;

yet later, by composing this verse, it was as if he had carved two lines of characters upon his face. If one were a person of penetrating understanding, they would know immediately upon its being raised."
For beginners who have first set out in their studies, it is difficult to discern the truth. I, this old monk, shall provide you with a commentary from the very beginning.

Baizhang had three secrets; the thief’s own body has already been revealed. “Drink tea; take care; rest. The stolen goods are brought forth; one must directly and immediately accept them. I dare say that you have not yet reached the bottom.
This is much like holding stolen goods while presiding over a legal case. Nevertheless, O worthy ones, if you possess the power of discernment...
Only then can one verify it with one's own eyes. If the false and the true have not yet been distinguished, one may be said to possess a "blunt" Buddha-nature;
one must further consult the wise and virtuous. Otherwise, it is a pity to live and die in vain.

Chan Master Dao Kuang of Zhaoqing, a native of Chaozhou and a successor of Chan Master Hui Leng of Changqing in Fuzhou (fourth in the lineage). He addressed the assembly, saying: "To realize it before the sound is to辜负 (betray) one’s lifelong efforts;
to seize the opportunity after the phrase is to deviate from the essence of the Way. Tell me, how has it been from the beginning?"
Sheng addressed the assembly, saying, "Today at Zhaqing, I shall speak it all at once for you all. Do you know where it lands?
A monk stepped forward and said, "If the entire assembly were to disperse at once, would that accord with your intention, Master? The Master said, "A fine three..."
The staff was raised ten times. The monks prostrated. The Master said, "Though there is the intent of the blind turtle, there is as yet no journey of the bright moon.
At that time, a monk asked, "What is the journey of the bright moon? The Master said, "This is the intent of the blind turtle.
[The monk] asked, "What is the practice of a śramaṇa? The Master said, "Neither practicing nor not practicing. [The monk] asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?"
The Master said, "A mosquito on an iron ox.
When the Master was at Changqing, he served as the head of the kitchen (tǒngtóu) and frequently conversed with the assembly of monks. One day, Changqing entered the quarters and saw him.
He then asked, "You have been chattering all day long; what are you doing? The Master said, "If one does not work for a day, one does not eat for a day.
Qing said, "In that case, you are sharpening your bow and honing your arrows. The Master said, "I am waiting specifically for Weichi to arrive."
Qingyun asked, "What was it like when Weichi arrived? The Master said, "He was made to have his sinews and bones spread across the ground, and his eyes bulging out.
Qingyun then went out.
A monk asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "Seven topsy-turvy, eight upside-down.
The monk asked, "What is the house style of Zhaoqing? The Master said, "Pure poverty brings constant joy; turbid wealth brings much sorrow."
Chan Master Baoci Guangyun of Fuzhou (three cases). The King of Min asked, "How far apart are Baoji and Shenquan?
The Master said, "If one speaks of distance, it is better not to go there oneself. The Master then asked, "Your Majesty must respond to a thousand differences every day."
"What kind of mind is this? The King asked. "Where did you get this mind? the Master replied. "How could there be such a thing as no-mind? the Master said.
"What about that matter over there? the King asked. "Please ask about that over there," the Master said. "The Great Master may deceive others, but not me," the King said. The Master then withdrew.

He addressed the assembly, saying: "The medicine for curing illness does not require a donkey to carry it. As for now, it would be well for each of you to return to your own hall. The Master asked a monk, "Where have you come from?
The monk replied, "From Sleeping Dragon. The Master said, "How long have you been there? The monk replied, "I have spent the winter and passed through the summer there.
The Master said, "The Dragon Gate has no guests who stay overnight. Why have you remained there for so long? The monk replied, "The Lion’s Den."
There was no other beast within it. The Master said, "Try to let out a lion's roar and see. [The monk] said, "If I were to let out a lion's roar, the Master would immediately be gone.
The Master said, "Out of consideration for you being newly arrived, I grant you thirty blows of the staff."
Xuedou said: "How extraordinary, O virtuous Chan practitioners! If one proceeds with straightforwardness, then neither side is harmed;
yet if one enforces the command, then both parties are in peril. Can you still discern this?"
Chan Master Baoen Baozi of Wuzhou (Part II). A monk asked, "When waves surge and cauldrons boil, arising must be entirely true.
I wonder, what was the meaning of the ancients? The Master rebuked him. The monk said, "If that is so, then even in moments of haste [the truth remains].
The Master said, "Your words have fallen. He added, "My words have also fallen; how will you handle this? The monk had no reply.

The Master ordered an attendant to take water from the West Bridge and pour it into the lotus basin on the East side. When the attendant had finished pouring, the Master asked, "Where did you pour it?

Chan Master Mingyuan of Jue-ling Peak in Xiangzhou (three cases). Changqing asked the Master, "What is your name? The Master said, "Mingyuan.

Mingyuan. At this, the Master explained the essential meaning.

the monk attained realization.

Chan Master Xiantian Shoubian of Fuzhou (Case 1). A monk asked, "Is the person who is always present throughout the twelve periods of the day able to receive the offerings of devas and humans? The Master said, "He cannot. The monk asked, "Why can he not?

In this case, the people here will laugh at you as something strange. If no one can respond to this, the people here will laugh at you as something strange.

[The following is from] *Dàchuán Wánggōng Yánbīn* (Volume 3). Because he entered the Buddha hall, he pointed to the alms bowl and asked the hall attendant, "What kind of bowl is this?

While the King was conversing with Changqing, Changqing cited the following: "When Xuefeng saw a monk approaching, he held up his whisk, and the monk immediately departed.

When the Duke arrived at Zhaoqing, while they were boiling tea, the Senior Monk Lang and Mingzhao were holding the tea kettle. Suddenly, the kettle overturned.

The Duke said, "Since you are the Spirit Who Supports the Stove, why did you overturn the tea kettle? Lang replied, "After serving the official for a thousand days, one may fail in a single morning."
The Master shook his sleeves and departed. Zhao said, "Upādhyāya Lang, having finished eating the meal at Zhaoqing, you have gone out beyond the river to gather firewood.

"Grand Councilor Wang was much like Sima Qian seizing the jade; his hair bristled with rage. Mingzhao also could not restrain his impatience.
A favorable opportunity is difficult to encounter. If Daowei had been Master Lang at that time, upon being questioned, he would have simply let out a great "ha ha" laugh.
Why? Because if you do not seize it when you see it, it will be difficult to forget for a thousand years.
Chan Master Shengxiong of Zhaoqing in Quanzhou, Dharma heir of Chan Master Congzhan of Baofu in Zhangzhou (Case 1). Together with Baofu, they entered the Buddha hall.

Huanglong then asked, "I have long heard of Huanglong; having arrived, I see only a striped red snake.

The Master asked, "If you suddenly encounter a garuḍa coming, what then? Long said, "My life and nature would be difficult to preserve. The Master said, "In that case, you have been swallowed by it.

Chan Master Jianzhou Baiyun Zizuo (three instances). Once, while Drum Mountain was ascending the hall, he called to the assembly.

Chan Master Zixing of Longce in Hangzhou, Dharma heir of Chan Master Lingcan of Cuiyan in Mingzhou (Part Two). A monk asked: "Within the state of the correct position, is there still the attainment of Buddhahood?"
The Master said, "Who is a sentient being? [The monk] said, "If that is so, then one becomes a Buddha. The Master said, "Return to my true position.
[The monk] asked, "What is the true position? The Master said, "You are a sentient being."
A monk asked, "What is the priceless treasure? The Master said, "Bian He vainly cradles the jade. The monk asked, "If he were suddenly to meet the King of Chu, would he still present it?
The Master said, "Only after having his feet cut off did he realize it was not [the true treasure]."
Chan Master Baofu Qinghuo of Zangzhou, Dharma Heir of Chan Master Wolong Daopu of Quanzhou (Part II). He was a native of Yongtai, Fuzhou. Wolong questioned the Master:
"Master Ho, which venerable elder did you visit? The Master replied, "I visited Dazhang and attained a point of entry into faith.
Long then ascended the seat. When the assembly had gathered, Long called out, "Master Ho, come forward and burn incense; explain your realization before the assembly."
"I, the old monk, shall bear witness for you. The Master came forward, burned incense, and said, "The incense has already been burned; whether Wuzhuo awakens or not, Longshen deeply approves of him.
A monk asked, "What is it like when a poor household suffers a robbery? The Master said, "They cannot be stripped completely bare. The monk asked, "Why is that?"

[The student] said, "I cannot exhaustively reach the bottom. The Master said, "The thief is a member of the family. [The student] asked, "Since he is a member of the family, why does he instead become a family thief?
The Master said, "Since there is no one inside to respond, there is nothing outside that can act. [The student] asked, "If he is suddenly caught and defeated, where does the credit go?
The Master said, "No reward has ever been heard of. [The student] said, "In that case, it is labor without merit."

The Master said, "The merit is indeed not absent, yet once it is accomplished, one does not dwell within it. [The student] asked, "Why does one not dwell within it? The Master said, "Have you not seen it said:
'Peace itself was brought about by the generals, yet we do not permit the generals to witness that peace'?"
Miaoxi said: "The shuttle comes and the thread goes; they merely toy with the spirit.
Chan Master Lingchong of Fenghua in Yangzhou, a successor of Chan Master Huaiyue of Yunju in Hongzhou (Case 1). A monk asked: "What is the single game of chess against a rival state?"
The Master said, "Bring it down. [The monk] asked, "What is it like when one blow breaks through empty space? The Master said, "Bring me a piece of it.
Chan Master Zhiyuan of Baimiao in Anzhou was a successor of [Master Xuefeng].
Chan Master Dazhong Zhihong of Langzhou (Case 1). A monk asked, “What is the Buddha? The Master said, “It is you.

Chan Master Xing’ai of Baima in Xiangzhou (Case 1). A monk asked, "What is the pure Dharma-body?
