Master Puchan Xinghua of Jinzhou (Part Two). A monk asked, "It fills the dragon palaces and overflows the ocean treasuries; I do not ask about the true exposition.
What is this matter of the separate transmission outside the teachings? The Master said, "In the eyes, in the ears, in the nose."
The Master said, "Do not say that this is it. The monk asked, "What is it? The monk then shouted; the Master then struck him.
The Master asked another monk, "Where have you recently come from? He replied, "From the military camp. The Master asked, "Did you encounter any bandits?
He replied, "I captured some today. The Master said, "I grant you thirty blows."
Chan Master Tong’an Zhi of Hongzhou, Dharma successor of Chan Master Tong’an Pi of Hongzhou (Case 1). A monk asked: “When not a single device reaches it, how can one proclaim it?
The Master said: “Not encountered anywhere; not lost within the profound. The monk asked: “If every word and phrase falls into the present age, how does the student [proceed]?”

[The student] said, "Please, Master, point directly. The Master said, "It does not appear before the eyes; one is not deluded after the phrase. [The student] asked, "How is it regarding the matter above?
The Master said, "It is utterly unchanging; if you aim at it, you have already missed the mark."
Chan Master Chizhou Ba’en Qichong (1), Dharma Heir of Chan Master Mingzhao Deqian of Wuzhou, Ninth Generation under Qingyuan.
Addressing the assembly, he said: "Among those who stand before the blade’s edge, is there anyone truly outstanding?"
"A hawk, a falcon—let one out and see! At that time, a monk stepped forward. The Master said, "Bring forth your full brilliance.
As the monk hesitated, the Master said, "Where have you gone? He asked, "What is it like when the lion has not yet emerged from its den? The Master said:

[The student said: "Its sharp edge is difficult to strike against. [He asked: "After it has emerged from the cave, what then? The Master said: "There is no way to hide the body. [He asked: "When it wishes to emerge but has not yet emerged, what then?
The Master said: "Life is like a dangling thread. [He asked: "As for the matter of going forward, what then? The Master said: "Press!"
Master Zao-shu (also known as Huanglong Huiji), a successor of Chan Master Huanglong Huiji of Ezhou.
(Four cases total. Once, while a monk was paying his respects, the Master asked him, "Who have you seen that you do not even offer a greeting?"
A monk said, "I saw the Master but did not inquire after his well-being; my ritual was incomplete. The Master replied, "In fact, you have failed me, old monk.
The monk reported this to the Head Seat (Śrāmaṇera). The Head Seat said, "Lately, our Abbot has been truly thorough in dealing with people.

When the Master heard this, he struck the Head Seat seven blows. The Head Seat said, "I spoke thus because there was no fault in me; why do you strike me so recklessly? The Master said, "Eat [your punishment]."
"How much salt and vinegar have I used up? he said, and struck him seven more blows. A monk took his leave;
the Master asked, "When you arrive at various places, if someone asks you about the Dharma-way of this old monk, how will you answer them?
The monk replied, "I will wait until they ask, and then I will speak. The Master said, "Where is there a Buddha who has no mouth? The monk replied, "It is just this."
[The monk] replied, "It is also difficult. The Master held up his whisk and said, "Do you see it? The monk said, "Where is there a Buddha with eyes that do not see?
The Master said, "Even this is difficult. The monk circumambulated the meditation seat once and departed. The Master said, "You are well able to respond. The monk then shouted.
The Master said, "I do not recognize you, old man. [The monk] said, "What is the use of recognizing? The Master struck the meditation seat.
[The Master] descended from his seat three times.
He asked a monk, "Where have you set out from? The monk replied, "From Min Province. The Master said, "How sharp! The monk said, "I thank the Master for your instruction.
The Master said, "How pitiful! The monk bowed. The Master said, "When I speak in this manner, where does it fall? The monk had no reply.
The Master said, "He has no wound himself; do not injure him.
The Master asked a monk, "Before you arrived here, where did you establish yourself and sustain your life? The monk joined his palms and stepped forward;
the Master also stepped forward, and they stood side by side. The monk said, "Before I reached this place, the Master and..."
"Who stands alongside you? The Master pointed behind him and said, "Is it not he? The monk remained silent.
The Master said, "Not only do you deceive yourself, but you also deceive this old monk. The monk prostrated himself. The Master said, "That is precisely deceiving yourself."
The Monk of Black Water at Jiazhou (Case 1) asked Huanglong, "What is it like when snow covers the reeds?
Huanglong said, "Fierce! The Master said, "Not fierce. Huanglong said again, "Fierce! The Master said again, "Not fierce.
Huanglong then struck him, and the Master attained realization thereupon.
Chan Master Fayan Wenyi of Qingliang in Jinling, successor to Chan Master Luohan Guichen of Zhangzhou (thirteen in total). He was the son of the Ru family of Yuhang. He studied under Changqing.
He did not achieve great renown. Later, together with Jing and Faxin—three men in total—they intended to cross the mountain pass.

While passing through Dizang, they were detained by snow and rested for a short while. This Dizang was Chan Master Chen. Chen asked, "Where are you going on this journey? The Master replied, "I am going to travel as a wandering monk."
Baoshan Cheng said, "What is the matter of traveling on pilgrimage? The Master (Nanyue Huairang) said, "I do not know. Baoshan said, "Not knowing is most intimate.
Later, while discussing the *Zhaolun* with three others, they reached the passage: "Heaven and earth share the same root as I.
Baoshan asked, "Are the mountains, rivers, and the great earth the same as your own self, or are they different? The Master said, "The same. Baoshan held up two fingers and stared at him intently.

[The Master] said, "Two. He then rose and departed. Question: "There is not even a hair’s breadth of separation. Why then is it not seen when one looks? The Master said, "A master at play with shadows. Question:

A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "One person transmits what is false; ten thousand people transmit what is real."
Chan Master Huai-zhi of Guangjiao in Qizhou (Part II). Addressing the assembly, he said: "When the command is raised and the guiding principle is upheld, the hordes of demons vanish from sight.
When the ancestral seal is fully wielded, the ten directions are cut off in one stroke. At such a time as this, even if the Old Barbarian were to appear, he would have to beg for his life.
Among you, if there be any true masters, I hope you will exercise your discerning insight."
A monk asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "How long has it been since you began to take notes?
The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "The words are still ringing in my ears."
Chan Master Yong of Longmen in Shu Prefecture (three fascicles) addressed the assembly, saying: "The verbal explanations of the Buddhas have 'stopping the crying' as their purpose.
The Mind-Seal of the Patriarchs is beyond discussion. As for the path that leads upward, who would dare set foot upon it? If you can realize it directly..."
This was already not to the point.
A monk asked, "The patriarchs have transmitted it from one to another; I wonder what it is they transmit? The Master said, "Deshan’s staff. The monk said, [further questioning].
"If that is so, then you, Master, have attained the subtle essence. The Master then struck him.
A monk asked, "What is the path to Longmen? The Master said, "Perilous. The monk asked, "Why is it so? The Master said, "One returns having merely dented one's forehead."

Chan Master Tianmu Qiman of Tangzhou (Case 1) addressed the assembly, saying: "Kāśyapa personally transmitted the Tathāgata’s secret seal, yet the coming of Bodhidharma from the West was mostly empty and little substantial.
If one were to discuss this matter, for the time being we might identify a servant as the master;
to speak of Buddhas and Patriarchs is like carving flesh to create a sore. To directly clarify this alone is not yet the livelihood of a patch-robed monk. How is it?"
"This is the livelihood of a patch-robed monk; why do you not come forth to testify before the assembly? At that time, a monk came forward and prostrated.

The Master said, "If you were a true *siddha*, you would not even wait for me to raise my eyebrows. The monk responded with an assent. The Master said, "On the Diamond Path, they go two by two and three by three."
Chan Master Jian Fuzhitong of Ezhou (total of two entries) addressed the assembly, saying:

"Even if one were to attain a decisive and clear realization under a single phrase, that would already be failing to grasp the opportunity; one has already been stained by it. How should a patch-robed monk act?
[He] then descended from his seat."
A monk asked, "What is the phrase that penetrates the Dharma-body? The Master said, "A parrot yearns for Western Qin.

Chan Master Muzhou of Qianming in Yuezhou, a successor of Chan Master Shouchu of Dongshan in Xiangzhou (two cases total), asked Dongshan, "When the mind's activity has ceased and all rewards have been set aside, what is it like?"

Shan said, "Playing puppet shows at the bottom of the water. The Master asked, "Who is it that watches and enjoys this? Shan said, "Those who have ceased their mental activity and stopped their appreciation.
The Master said, "If that is so, then those who know the sound do not harmonize with one another. Shan asked, "As for the matter of knowing the sound, how would you describe it?"
The Master said, "The great month has thirty days. Xuefeng said, "That is not it; speak further.
The Master said, "I deserve to receive a severe blow from the Master's hand. Xuefeng desisted.
A monk asked, "Regarding the prediction at Vulture Peak in the past, who does he succeed this morning? The Master said, "Mount Chu rises steeply;
the Han River flows eastward. The monk said, "If that is so, then he succeeds Dongshan. The Master said, "Hearing things incorrectly, you call a bell a water jar."
Chan Master Guangji Tong of Dengzhou (Case 1). A monk asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?

The Master said, "A jet-black Kunlun man leading a white elephant. The monk said, "Master, do not deceive those who have come after you. The Master said, "A good heart does not receive a good reward."
Chan Master Kai Fu De Xian of Jingnan Prefecture (1) addressed the assembly, saying:

"To know without using thought, and to understand without using deliberation—when both knowledge and understanding have vanished, what matter is there to discuss? After a long silence, he said: "When one leaf falls, autumn comes to the world."
A monk asked, "What is the livelihood of a patch-robed monk? The Master said, "Plowing fields in one's ears.
Chan Master Nantai Qin of Nanyue, a successor of Chan Master Deshan Mi of Langzhou (two cases total), addressed the assembly, saying: "It is cold inside Mount Nanyue; it is not like elsewhere."
It is in the midst of cold. When it is cold, the trees form silver branches and the grasses spread out shards of jade. Rivers and streams freeze solid; the four seas become ice.
Space becomes congealed and the path of birds is blocked. Clouds blanket the long plains, and dragons and fish lock their doors. At such a time as this—
Life is like a thread suspended from above. How do you speak of this? If you can speak it, then the red sun reaches to the heavens; if you cannot speak it, there is only the dark, eternal night.
A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "An inch of tortoise hair weighs seven catties.
Chan Master Wenshu Yingzhen of Dingzhou (the second of two entries) addressed the assembly, saying: "A straight hook catches the black dragon;
a curved hook catches frogs and earthworms. Is there any dragon here? After a long silence, he said, "Labor expended without merit."
A monk asked, "How is it when the precious sword has not yet emerged from its scabbard? The Master said, "Where is it? The monk asked, "How is it after it has emerged from the scabbard?
The Master said, "The arms are long, but the sleeves of the robe are short."
Chan Master Shaoyan of Dingshou (Part II) addressed the assembly, saying: "When a single speck of dust arises, the entire earth is fully contained within it.
Upon a single hair-tip, the lion’s whole body is present. When a single speck of dust arises, the entire earth is fully contained within it—how many pounds and ounces does Mount Sumeru weigh?
Upon a single hair-tip, the lion’s whole body is present—how many drops are there in the waters of the great ocean?"
"Listen! If someone can speak [the truth], I will give you this staff to walk freely throughout the world.
If you cannot speak it, Mount Sumeru shall cover your head, and the great ocean shall drown your body."
A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master said, "The waters of Taoyuan wind around the White Cloud Pavilion.
Chan Master Wenshu Kuan of Dingzhou (three instances) addressed the assembly, saying: "I would have you hear a single phrase and resolve everything at once;
even that would not be sufficient, for you would still be stained by it. How should one act?"
A monk asked, "What is the single phrase by which Mañjuśrī acts for others? The Master said, "One who roughly recognizes good from evil.
The monk asked, "Regarding the ancients rolling up their mats—what was their intent? The Master said, "It is because you yourself do not know the time."
A monk asked, "What is the Yunmen phrase that penetrates the Dharma-body? The Master said, "Be careful of your eyebrows.
The monk asked, "Why is it so? The Master said, "It is not within your realm."

Chan Master Deshan Huiyuan of Dingzhou, Dharma successor of Chan Master Yuru of Shuangquan in Suizhou (Part II). Opening the Hall, he addressed the assembly, saying: "The immeasurable Dharma gates are all fully complete.
Nevertheless, even so, you must first attain thorough understanding before you can proceed. As for other expedient means, they were [taught by] the sages of old..."
When people transmit [the Dharma] to one another, it is called "transmitting the lamp. Thereafter, worthy ones appeared shoulder to shoulder; thus, it is said they "succeeded the patriarchs.
Therefore, mind transmits to mind, and dharma seals dharma. But how is it transmitted? How is it sealed? Raising up his whisk, he said:
"This is what is realized by humans and devas alike. If it is thus, they also provide mutual proof. Yet, for those who have not yet understood—"

[The Master] said, "I shall grant you an audience; please put forward your question. A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master replied, "The path through the iron gate is perilous.
Addressing the assembly, he said, "For those who have left the household life, the matter of birth and death is of great importance. You must directly investigate the dharma of arising and ceasing."
Since, at every single moment, it is like the flash of lightning; and as for the nature of lightning, it has no place of abiding.
When all phenomena arise and cease, and having ceased, do you understand? If you understand, then you understand; if you do not understand, this is the very root of birth and death.

Master Xiang of Lotus Peak Hermitage on Mount Tiantai, Dharma Heir of Chan Master Shen of Fengxian in Jiangling Prefecture (total of two entries). The Master held up his staff and addressed the assembly, saying:
"When the ancients reached this point, why did they refuse to stay? No one in the assembly replied. The Master spoke for them himself: "Because their path was not yet finished."
He attained realization. He asked again, "Ultimately, how is it? Then he said of himself: "Carrying my staff slung across my shoulder, I heed no one;
I go straight toward a thousand peaks and ten thousand peaks."
He addressed the assembly, saying: "If one discusses this matter, it is most urgent and critical; you must clearly grasp it before you can succeed.

If you can grasp it clearly, you will avoid being bound by circumstances during your daily life, and you will be able to remain at ease wherever you are. Furthermore, there is no need to suppress the mind with effort."

One must naturally follow in the ancient tracks of others. If you study by merely dividing things into categories and portions, you will have to spread out a system of logic and treat that as the Buddha-dharma;
when will you ever find rest? Elder, I ask you instead to understand this well.

Chan Master Zhiguang of Fenghuang Mountain in Xijianzhou, Dharma Heir of Chan Master Jingtuo of Linxi in Yingzhou (Part II). Addressing the assembly, he said: "Day after day it is the same; morning after morning it is just as it was.
Even if there were something new or extraordinary, it could not be brought forth. This is true even when the various sages appear—they dare not [do otherwise]."
"You have deceived the Elder. Why is this so? It is because the Elder is a wandering monk.

Now that you and the Elder have gathered here for but a short while, you have already brought shame upon all people. If we were to linger further, disputes would arise like the tips of spears; it would be better to simply stop."
A monk asked, "What is the Buddha-dharma here in your monastery, Master? The Master said, "Striking the west wall with the east wall.
Chan Master Cheng of Daopei in Tanzhou, a successor of Chan Master Zhen of Miaosheng in Lu Prefecture (one case): A monk asked, "Why did Emperor Wu of Liang fail to recognize Bodhidharma?"
The Master said, "Both are men of stature. [The monk] asked, "What was the intent behind facing the wall for nine years? The Master said, "One person transmits a rumor;
ten thousand people transmit reality."
Chan Master Zhimen Guangzuo of Suizhou, Dharma Heir of Chan Master Xinglin Chengyuan of Yizhou (Twelfth Case). Addressing the assembly, he said:
"All of you, carrying your staffs across your shoulders, leave one grove and enter another. I ask you: how many kinds of groves are there? There may be sandalwood [groves]..."
There are groves of sandalwood surrounded by thorns; there are groves of thorns surrounded by sandalwood;
there are groves of thorns surrounded by sandalwood; and there are groves of sandalwood surrounded by thorns.
As for these four kinds of groves, in which one of them do you all dwell to establish yourselves and sustain your lives? If you have no place to rest...
Standing in the body and dwelling in life, you have vainly worn out your straw sandals. There will come a day when King Yama demands the money for those sandals from you.
Addressing the assembly, he said: "For these past two or three days there has been fine rain; it may truly be called a downpour.
To ordinary people, water is water; to devas, water is lapis lazuli; to dragons and fish, water is their home; to hungry ghosts, water is fire. You..."
For those of us in the lineage of patch-robed monks, what would you call it? If you call it water, that is the same as the view of an ordinary person.
If you call it lapis lazuli, that is the same as the view of the devas. If you call it a dwelling place, that is the same as the view of dragons and fish.
If you call it fire, that is the same as the view of hungry ghosts. As for your usual practice, how do you proceed? Therefore it is said: "If one attains..."
This person says: "The fire of the Way does not burn the mouth; the water of the Way does not drown the body. When you eat your daily meals, have you ever lacked even a single grain? An ancient said:
'All day long we wear clothes and eat food, yet we have never bitten into a single grain of rice, nor have we ever hung upon a single thread of silk.
Although this is so, one must still truly arrive at this point before it is attained. If you have not yet...
Having reached this stage, do not merely engage in empty talk.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "Xuefeng rolling the ball; Luohan writing characters; Guian slaying the snake; Daisui burning the slash-and-burn fields.
Tell me, what matter does this clarify? Is there anyone who can clarify it? Try to say something. If you cannot clarify it..."
To "cut the snake" one must be the one who cuts the snake; to "burn the slash-cleared field" one must be the one who burns the slash-cleared field.
When the dust of emotion stirs and deluded views arise, if there is no sinew in one's eyes, one will be poor for a lifetime.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "It has been raining well for several days. Now tell me, from where does it come?
If you say it descends from heaven, then which one is heaven? If you say it emerges from the earth, then what do you call 'earth'? If you still do not understand..."

Therefore it is said: "The direct path before heaven and earth—people of this age must not attempt to alter it. To give rise to conceptual understanding within this is like placing an awl upon the eye.

He addressed the assembly, saying: "In the scorching sun, there is the 'self' and 'other. In the clouds and mist, there is compassion. In the frost and snow, there is the patched robe. In the hailstones..."
"Conceal your body within. "Can you still conceal your body? "If you cannot conceal it, you will have your skull shattered by a hailstone.

He addressed the assembly, saying: "Nanquan said: 'Since my youth, I have raised a water buffalo. If I intend to let it loose to the east of the stream, it cannot avoid eating the king's water and grass;
if I intend to let it loose to the west of the stream, it cannot avoid eating the king's water and grass.'"
"One cannot help but offer a bit according to one's capacity," yet he does not see it at all. Therefore, Master Yunmen said:
"There are countless dead people on level ground; those who can pass through the thorny forest are true adepts.

Even if you were to sever the distinction between the mundane and the sacred, and exhaust all existence and non-existence, it would still be nothing more than a rat entering a rice jar—yet you would still not know that which lies beyond.
The "opening" exists. At that time, a monk asked, "What is the opening that points upward?
The Master struck him and said, "I have already taken a piece of excrement and smeared it across your mouth; why do you come here again to make me work my hands for you?"
A monk asked, "What is it like when the lotus flower has not yet emerged from the water? The Master said, "The lotus flower. The monk asked, "What is it like after it has emerged?
The Master said, "The lotus leaf."
Xuedou’s verse says: "The lotus and its leaves tell you to know: How can it be when emerged compared to when it has not yet emerged?
Ask the old man Wang north of the river and south of the river: One doubt resolved, another doubt ends."
Question: What is the essence of prajñā? The Master said: "An oyster containing the bright moon. Question: What is the function of prajñā?
The Master said: "A rabbit conceiving a fetus."
Xuedou said: "Not only does he hold fast to the world, but he also brings peace and stability to the state.
If you are well able to investigate and examine this, then please walk alone upon the crimson heavens."
Another verse says: A single expanse of void stillness, cut off from all conceptualization— From this, humans and devas see emptiness arise.
The oyster holds the dark hare; how deep is its meaning! It has once waged war against the monastic groves.
A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Treading through grass shoes, walking barefoot. The monk asked, "What is the matter beyond the Buddha?
The Master said, "Carrying the sun and moon upon the tip of my staff."
Xuedou said: "A thousand soldiers are easy to find; a single general is hard to seek.
A monk asked, "What can be placed within the adamantine eye? The Master said, "A handful of sand. The monk asked, "Why is it so?
The Master said, "It is not your realm."
A monk asked, "What was the meaning of the National Teacher’s three calls to his attendant? The Master said, "Out of love for one's child, one does not notice their ugliness.
The monk asked, "What was the meaning of the National Teacher’s 'I have let my attendant down'? The Master said, "Delicious food is not for the hungry man to eat.
The monk asked, "What was the meaning of the attendant’s 'I have let the National Teacher down'? The Master said, "Even grinding one's bones to powder would not suffice as retribution."
A monk asked, "What is the phrase that penetrates the Dharma-body? The Master said, "A monkey tied to a dew-pillar.
He asked, "On the road to Caoxi, is there still any worldly talk? The Master said, "The Sixth Patriarch was Layman Lu.
He asked, "In the purity of the wisdom of all-knowledge, is there still hell? The Master said, "King Yama is made by ghosts."
Chan Master Yuan Guan of Liangshan in Dingzhou, Dharma Heir of Chan Master Zhi of Tong’an in Hongzhou (Sixth Case). Addressing the assembly, he said: "The line hangs down a thousand feet;
the intent lies in the deep pool. A single phrase spans the void; the white clouds are naturally distinct. A solitary boat rows alone, not disturbing the clear waves. Across the sea..."
He traveled. Not encountering a clear mirror [to reflect his truth], he addressed the assembly, saying:
"Cease the activity of the mind and desist from seeking rewards; hide your traces and remain in obscurity. In a bamboo door and thatched hall, sleep amidst the clouds and lie beneath the moon;

by the green pines and blue streams, rest upon the rocks and rinse your mouth with flowing water. The Way does not belong to cultivation; it is realized spontaneously through a mindless state. To discuss the profound and sing of the Way—do not..."

This is not the path of lofty recluses who wander like clouds and water; it is the trackless way of the birds, the very footsteps of the Way-farer. To speak of the profound mystery, it does not touch the lips;

to tread upon it, even ghosts and spirits find it difficult to seek. To awaken to it is to attain Buddhahood in a single instant; to be deluded by it is to remain in birth and death for eternal kalpas.

If you have doubts, resolve them at once; do not sit by a stump waiting for a rabbit. Do not harbor such "simplicity" or cling to such "foolishness," for such a state is merely a state of ruinous decay.
It was accomplished. Time passed in vain.

As the Master sat with Elder Duan, during the course of their conversation, a monk asked, "Since two Honored Ones do not appear together in the world, for what reason do you two both occupy the abbot’s quarters? The Master said, "Even one is not."
A monk asked, "When it is difficult to guard against a thief in one's own house, what then? The Master said, "Once you recognize him, he will no longer be an enemy.

The monk asked, "What is it like after you have recognized him? The Master said, "Exile him to the Land of Non-arising. The monk asked, "Is this not the place where he establishes his body and sustains his life?
The Master said, "A dead pool does not harbor dragons. The monk asked, "What is a dragon in living water? The Master said, "To arise."
"Clouds do not emit mist. [The student asked: "What about when clouds suddenly encounter the occasion for gathering and sending down rain?
The Master descended from his rope-seat, seized him, and said, "Do not let it soak the corner of this old monk’s kashaya."
A monk asked, "What is the matter transmitted from of old? The Master said, "The barbarian monk crossing the water has no knee-pants;
his back carries Buddhist scriptures, yet he does not recite the sutras. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Westerner's coming?
The Master said, "At the Pamir Pass, no news of the Tang lands was passed; the barbarian man vainly sings songs of peace."
The Master addressed the assembly with this verse: "The brilliant sun still lacks half its light; The crow has not yet reached fullness.
If you can understand the meaning herein, A cow’s head will be placed upon its tail."

Chan Master Xilan of Taoyuan in Cizhou, successor to Chan Master Shaosheng of Shaozhou, (Case 1), addressed the assembly, saying: "If one were to sing the praises of the school’s style, it would merely be a provisional designation.
But if one discusses the fundamental principles of our ancestors, it is difficult even to open one's mouth. Therefore, the former sage said: 'Above this...'"
"The single path has not been transmitted by the thousand sages. Students weary their bodies like monkeys grasping at reflections.
All you venerable Chan practitioners, how will you deliberate so as to become equal to the ancient sages? Is there anyone among you who is a true master?
If so, please cast aside your former errors and enter directly with a single blade. At that time, a monk came forward and paid his respects. The Master said, "A true lion cub! [The monk] asked:
"How is this assembly on Vulture Peak any different from today? The Master said, "The deluded thoughts of that time still persist today.
[He was] a successor of Chan Master Fayan of Qingliang in Jinling, the tenth generation under Qingyuan.
National Teacher Deshao of Tiantai (9 total): The Master was the son of the Chen family in Longquan County, Chuzhou.
He asked Longya, "The heavens cannot cover it; the earth cannot support it. What is this state? Longya said, "A practitioner ought to be thus. The Master asked this seventeen times in all.
Longya said, "If I were to explain it for you, you would later curse me away. Later, the Master resided at [Tiantai].
At Tongxuan Peak on Mount Tiantai, while bathing, he suddenly recalled his previous conversation. He then assumed a formal posture, burned incense, and prostrated from afar toward Longya, saying:
"If you had explained it to me at that time, I would certainly have scolded you today."
Miaoxi said, "Right now, it is not lacking.
The Master asked Shushan, "The hundredfold encirclements and thousandfold layers—whose realm is this? Shushan said, "Twisting straw ropes on the left to bind the children of ghosts.
The Master said, "It does not fall within the past or present; please explain it for me. Shushan said, "I will not speak. The Master said, "Why not?"
He did not speak. Shanshan said, "Within this, there is no distinction between existence and non-existence. The Master said, "Master, you have spoken well. Shanshan was startled by this.
The Master had studied under fifty-three spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*) before visiting Fayan. He merely followed the assembly.
One day, a monk asked Fayan, "What is a single drop of water from the Cao River source? Fayan said, "It is a single drop of water from the Cao River source."

[The Master] said, "Water. The monks were at a loss for words. The Master was by the side of his seat; he suddenly attained enlightenment, and his lingering obstructions were dissolved like ice melting away.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "True emptiness is non-dual, and the myriad virtues are beyond speech. At this very moment of clarity, it is like a king’s precious sword.
Therefore, the Tathāgata attains equal and right enlightenment in all places—even upon mountains of knives and trees of swords, he attains equal and right enlightenment."
Awakening occurs within the cauldrons and amidst the furnace coals; awakening to Equal and Perfect Enlightenment occurs beneath the staff.

Thus, in every movement and stillness, every departure and arrival, every birth and extinction, there has never been the slightest mark of difference, nor the slightest mark of distinction—not even so much as a hair’s breadth or a single thread.
There is nothing whatsoever to be grasped by the mind-consciousness through seeing or hearing.
Why is this? O benevolent one, it is truly because the path of right and wrong is severed; it is the wondrous nature and celestial mechanism.
Thus it is said: "When you are born, I am also born; when you kill, I also kill. This wheel-turning sovereign of birth and killing races back and forth like a flash of lightning.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "The skillful means of the ancient sages are as numerous as the sands of the Ganges. The Patriarch said, 'It is not the wind or the banner that moves;
it is the mind of the wise man that moves. This is the Dharma-gate of the Unsurpassed Mind-Seal. We are disciples under the Patriarch’s gate—how should we act?
Is it that the wind and banner do not move while your own mind moves delusively? Or is it that you do not strike at the wind and banner, but rather [turn back to]..."
Regarding the Way of the Wind and the Banner, what is it that you take as the point? Is it the place where they move? Some say, "The object reveals the mind. Others say, "Form is emptiness.
Still others say, "It is neither the wind nor the banner that moves; one must realize this through wondrous understanding.
If you interpret it in such ways, what connection does this have with the Patriarch? Since such interpretations are not permitted, you venerable seniors should know this for yourselves. This—
Once you have realized this within yourself, what dharma would not be clear? You will simultaneously and thoroughly comprehend the skillful means of the hundreds of thousands of Buddhas.
If it were not thus, even if one spent aeons as numerous as dust motes, one would merely exhaust one's own spirit; there is no other way.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "The Buddha-dharma is already perfected; all things are fully complete. It is as vast as the great void—neither lacking nor superfluous.
If one can realize it thus, then who is deficient and who is redundant? Who is right and who is wrong? Who understands and who does not? Therefore it is said:"
Going east, it is the Venerable One; going west, it is the Venerable One; going south, it is the Venerable One;
going north, it is the Venerable One. Why is it that the Venerable One is able to go east, west, south, and north?
If you can understand this, the paths of seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing will naturally be cut off, and all dharmas will manifest before you. Why is this so? It is because of the Dharmakāya.
It is formless; yet whatever it touches takes on form. Prajñā is without knowing, yet it illuminates in response to conditions. It is well to understand this thoroughly and all at once.
While the Master resided atop Tongxuan Peak, he spoke a verse: "At the summit of Tongxuan Peak, it is not of the human world. Outside the mind, there is no dharma."
Fayan Wende, seeing the green mountains filling his view, said: "This single verse alone can revive my school.
Miaoxi said: "It was precisely because of this one verse that Fayan’s entire school was extinguished."

A monk asked, "Regarding the provisional nature of names and the provisional nature of phenomena, and the emptiness of persons and the emptiness of phenomena—having set aside all such conditions, I ask the Master to point directly.
The Master said, "Thank you for this question. The monk said, "If one has not seen the majesty of the royal palace, how can one know the dignity of the Son of Heaven?
The Master said, "In greedily gazing at the moon in the sky, you have lost the oar in your hand."
A monk asked, "Striking the void, the *gu-gu* sounds; the stone man and the wooden man respond in unison.
Snow falls thickly in the sixth month—this is the Tathāgata’s Great Perfect Enlightenment. What is it that strikes the void? The Master said:
The Kunlun boy wears iron trousers; he takes one step for every blow he receives.
A monk said, "In that case, even the stone man and the wooden man would respond in unison. The Master said, "Do you hear them?"

A monk asked, "The mark of the cessation of all dharmas cannot be proclaimed in words. How do you, O Master, act for the sake of others? The Master said, "If you go to other places, raise this up once more.

The monk said, "In that case, it would be beyond words and phrases. The Master said: *Note: The text provided ends abruptly with the Master's response. A full dialogue would typically conclude with the monk’s subsequent action or realization.*
Vividly awake even within a dream.
[A monk] asked, "What is the mind of the ancient Buddhas? The Master said, "This question is no weakling. [The monk] asked, "What is the phrase that is free from leakage?
The Master said, "The mouth is like the nostrils."
Question: "Why do the Buddhas of the three periods of time not know that [it] exists? The Master said, "In fact, it is you who know that it exists. Question:
"Why then do the 'tawny cat' and the 'white ox' know that it exists? The Master said, "Where have you seen the Buddhas of the three periods of time?"
A questioner asked, "The Jewel Seal of Pure Wisdom was personally transmitted by the Master; I wonder whom you entrust with it this day at this assembly?
The Master said, "Dong-dong! The drum is struck at one end, yet it resounds at both ends."
Chan Master Taiqin of Qingliang in Jinling (Four Parts). On the day of opening the hall, he addressed the assembly, saying:

"I originally intended to dwell in the mountains to hide my ineptitude and spend my time tending to my illness. However, because my late master has a case that remains unresolved, I have come forth to settle it for him.
At that time, a monk stepped forward and asked: "What is this unresolved case of the late master? The Master—
He struck him and said, "The patriarchs failed to resolve it; the calamity now reaches their descendants. The monk asked, "Where does the fault lie?
The Master said, "The fault lies with me; the calamity reaches you."
Cuiyan Zhi said, "Exerting one's utmost effort for the sake of the assembly, yet the disaster arises from within one's own gate.
Yunfeng Yue said, "This old fellow, in this single instance of giving and taking away, seems to have outshone his predecessors;

Chan Master Dongshan Xiaocong of Junzhou, Dharma Heir of Chan Master Wenshu Yingzhen of Dingzhou (Sixth in the lineage). A native of the Lin family of Qujiang, Shaoyou Prefecture. He addressed the assembly, saying:
"When we meet, no brow is raised; you go east, and I go west. Red clouds pierce the azure void; the white sun circles Mount Sumeru."
He addressed the assembly, saying: "Red dust arises from the bottom of the well; white waves surge from the high peak.

Taking the entire earth and making it into a single sesame cake, all people under heaven may eat of it; there is only the deep-sand demon who cannot."
The deity could not eat it. In a fit of rage, he took up a thorn-studded mallet and struck once; [the deity] was like a crumbling wall or melting ice. A monk asked:
