Chan Master Xuedou Chongxian of Xuedou, Mingzhou, Dharma heir of Chan Master Zhimen Guangzuo of Suizhou (twenty-fourth in the lineage). He was the son of the Li family in Suzhou. He asked Zhimen, "If one does not give rise to a single thought, how can there be transgression?
Zhimen called to the Master to come forward. As soon as the Master approached, Zhimen suddenly struck him with his whisk.
[The Master] struck him with his staff. As the Master was about to open his mouth, the Gatekeeper struck him again. The Master attained sudden enlightenment.
On the day the Master opened the hall for teaching, he surveyed the great assembly and said: "Heavenly beings and humans are gathered here; what matter should we together clarify?"
How could one possibly divide this into guest and host, or engage in a mere display of question and answer? This is the very essence of the *zongcheng* (the vehicle of the lineage);

it is a vast and magnificent tradition, its majestic power sovereign and its brilliance transcending past and present. It firmly grasps heaven and earth; the thousand sages have said only that it must be known by oneself, for even the five vehicles cannot establish it.
Thus, though one may awaken to the meaning before a sound is uttered, one still remains confused regarding the point of the turning mirror; though one may know the source beneath a word...

Beyond the realm of dull consciousness and emotional sentiment, you people must know that the true mark is this: simply by having nothing above to grasp at or look up to, and nothing below to cling to as one's own self, the natural, eternal light manifests before you.
Each and every one stands like a cliff rising ten thousand fathoms—can you discern this clearly or not? If you have not yet discerned it, discern it;
if you have not yet made it clear, make it clear. Once you have discerned it clearly, you will be able to cut off the stream of birth and death and dwell together [in liberation].

The station of the Buddhas and Patriarchs—this wondrous, perfect, and transcendent awakening occurs precisely at this moment. It is here that one may repay the unrequitable debt of gratitude and assist in the transformation of non-action.

Addressing the assembly, he said: "Before form arose, there was no substance; before names emerged, there was no naming. Once form and name had manifested, the wandering vapors disturbed the clarity. [He] picked up [the whisk].
Raising his staff, he said: "O Great Assembly! This staff—this simultaneous raising of both form and name—does it have any fault?

If there is, it is like the moon reflected in water; if there is not, it is the very sign of form and name. If you can investigate this thoroughly, it is truly what is called a great kindness difficult to repay."
He addressed the assembly, saying: "A single question and a single answer—neither has yet reached the reality of things.

Even if the heavens, the earth, the grasses, the trees, and the forests were all transformed into monks, each with a different mouth but a single voice, posing hundreds of thousands of difficult questions, they would not require the Elder to snap his fingers even once.
All would be universally answered, high and low, without the slightest discrepancy, manifesting the wondrous and numinous spirit of the Buddhas and Patriarchs."

It clarifies the profound traces of humans and devas. Thus, why should one rely on the eastern outskirts of the City of Enlightenment? Let the five assemblies all dwell before the temple of the Ancient Buddha;
at this time, the retreat is concluded.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "One whose field of practice is stable and secure—neither Buddhas nor Patriarchs dare approach him. Why is it that he cannot lift his foot?
One who sports with supernatural powers—neither ghosts nor spirits can fathom him. Why is it that he cannot set his foot down?
Even if one were to move freely in all directions, striking three thousand blows in the morning and eight hundred blows in the evening."

He addressed the assembly, saying: "The spring mountains layer upon layer in wild green; the spring waters ripple in empty azure. Vast and silent between heaven and earth, standing alone, what can one gaze upon to the limit?
He then descended from his seat and looked back at his attendant, asking, "Was there anyone just now looking at the abbot’s quarters? The attendant replied, "There was.
The Master said, "The heart of a thief is always fearful."
He addressed the assembly, saying: "The land has no sword for suppressing disorder; the four seas are tranquil and clear. This is not an extraordinary feat.
Are there any yet who have climbed the mountain passes to present tribute?"
He addressed the assembly, saying: "In the ten directions there is no azure sky; on all four sides there is likewise no gate. Where did the ancients see their guests?
If you can produce a phrase that takes up the hand [of the teaching], I grant you dominion over the heavens above and the earth below."
He addressed the assembly, saying: "When those of superior capacity meet, a single word or half-phrase is like a spark struck from flint; it passes in a mere flash.
It must not be that one takes the words as the fixed meaning, for to linger in phrases is to lose the source. Regarding the ancestral vehicle of the Buddhas, how could one possibly discuss it?
It is such that the Buddhas of the three periods cannot proclaim it themselves, and the six generations of patriarchs cannot fully raise it up. Even the entire Great Canon..."

The teachings and commentaries cannot reach it. Therefore, one must realize it at the tip of the staff and take responsibility under the shout. When meanings and phrases race against one another, it is still the same as drifting in the current.
Only those who are masters who penetrate all quarters can together provide mutual verification.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "To establish guest and host is to carve flesh and create sores; to cite the ancients and the present is to scatter sand and spread earth.
To be directly without affairs is precisely an unperforated iron hammer. To have any other mechanism is to deserve entry into the Avīci Hell.
Enlightened monks must examine this for yourselves."
The Master asked Dàlóng, "Neither speech nor silence is it; that which is neither speech nor silence is even more so. All together, all is not—it must be cast aside.
When the Great Function manifests, people know it exists. As for Dàlóng, what do you say? Dàlóng said, "Do you have such a view and understanding?
The Master said, "Old man, today your fortress crumbles like ice melting away. That evening, Dàlóng questioned him further.
The Master said, "Where is that place where this old monk has crumbled like ice and vanished? The student said, "Seeing it again makes it even more unbearable. He shook his sleeves and left.
Longshu said, "How vexing! How vexing! The Master paid him no heed. Later, he brought up this incident to Fuyan Ya, who said, "Why did you not give him the fodder appropriate to his own station?
The Master said, "Only then would the Master need to buy straw sandals and travel on foot."
One day, five newly arrived monks came for an audience. The Master said, "At the summit of Mount Dongting, there is no path; without relying on ladders or boats, try to tell me how you would proceed.
They replied, "We have come specifically to pay our respects to the Master. The Master said, "To moor a boat in still waters is merely to labor in vain.
The monks were speechless. The Master said, "Come over here. The monks all stepped over together. The Master said, "If one does not take the lead with vigor, one will fail."
"Bringing misfortune upon the three armies. Go to the hall.
The Master asked a monk, "What is your name? The monk replied, "Zongya. The Master said, "I do not ask about 'Ya' (elegant); what is the 'Zong' (essence)? The monk had no reply.
The Master said, "Set aside three days for consideration. The monk came frequently to offer his interpretations, but the Master did not approve. The monk said, "Master..."
"Furthermore, how is it? The Master said, "Why do you not ask? As the monk was about to speak, the Master struck him several times with his staff.
One day, six newly arrived monks came for an audience. The Master asked the head monk, "One who acts as a supreme general must have seven things at his side.
When two blades clash, what then? The monk replied, "I have long heard of the Master having this particular stroke. The Master said:
"One slip and you are let go; now bring me back the price for my straw sandals! The monk then shouted. The Master struck him. The monk caught hold of the staff and gave the Master a slap.
The Master said, "Before you reached Cui-feng, I already gave you thirty blows of the staff. The monk was speechless.
The Master said, "Stand aside for a moment," and then asked the second monk, "What about you, Lieutenant? The monk was at a loss.
The Master said, "I accept this one statement. After they had finished drinking tea, the Master seized the head monk and said, "Regarding that case just now, it was handled like this here;
how would you present it in the hall? As the monk hesitated, the Master struck him with his sitting mat and pushed him out.
One day, six newly arrived monks came for an audience. The Master asked, "Is there any master-level Chan practitioner here?
The head monk replied, "What does the Master say? The Master said, "The point is reached, but it is not yet realized. As the monk hesitated, the Master gave a shout. The monk was left speechless.
The Master said, "A fellow with a dragon's head and a snake's tail. He then questioned the second monk. The monk pointed to the head monk and said, "The Master is questioning you;
why do you not answer? The Master gave him a slap, and the monk was speechless. He then pointed to the third monk, who stood there bewildered.
The Master said, "One tally is accepted for all."
The Master asked a monk, "Where are you from? The monk held up his sitting mat. The Master said, "A shrimp cannot leap out of its basket. The monk said, "It leaps! The Master struck him.
The monk said, "It leaps even further! The Master struck him again. The monk then ran off. The Master called him back.
The monk prostrated and said, "I have offended you, Reverend. The Master said, "I wanted this story to circulate; why did you run away? The monk...
The Master said, "It has already gone throughout the world. He then struck him five blows. The monk said, "There are still other quarters [of the Dharma].
The Master said, "You just keep taking these blows. The Master then called the second person forward. As the monk approached, the Master asked, "Where are you from?
He replied, "Dingzhou. The Master said, "Defeated! The monk said, "Blue sky and bright day. The Master said, "A double offense."
The Master said, "Exactly so. He pointed with his staff and said, "You were about to leap up, weren't you? As the monk hesitated, the Master struck him five blows.
The head monk remarked, "This monk’s receiving the blows is not the same as mine. The Master said, "All of you come forward at once! The monk said, "Take care," and ran off.
The Master followed after him and gave him another blow with the staff.
The Master asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk said, "What are you saying, Preceptor? The Master said, "I am asking you: where have you recently come from?
The monk stepped back and stood there. The Master said, "Truly intolerable! You do not say where you have come from. He called for his staff.
The monk said, "I have recently come from Fengchuan. The Master said, "You wild scavenger! Why did you not speak like this sooner?"
The Master asked the second man, "Did you also come from that same place? He replied, "I recently left Damei.
The Master said, "Two different accounts—well-deserved thirty blows! For now, I let you go."
The Master asked the practitioner Congdao, "How is it with your long-standing practice? Cong replied, "Blue sky and bright day.
The Master said, "Why are you wandering about in confusion? Cong then gave a shout. The Master said, "You deserve a beating.
As Cong was about to raise his hand, the Master struck him with his sitting cloth and said, "Look! This blind fellow is acting recklessly!"
The Master asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk replied, "From Tiantai. The Master said, "Did you see Zhiwei? The monk replied, "I saw him.
The Master said, "Why was he under my feet? The monk was speechless. The Master said, "You liar who speaks empty falsehoods!"
The Master asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk replied, "Wenzhou. The Master said, "Do you know the Great Master Yongjia? The monk said, "He was a fellow countryman of mine.
The Master said, "He is separated from you by the sea. The monk said, "That is certainly so. The Master said, "A flushed face is not as good as straightforward speech.
The monk was speechless. The Master let out a single sigh.
While the Master was at Daowei, the Court Official Li came as the guest prefect (zhike). He asked, "Is the guest prefect a fellow villager of the Elder? The Master replied, "I dare not say so.
Li said, "Stay here for now; you must not wander about recklessly. The Master said, "I am originally here for the purpose of traveling on pilgrimage.
Li asked, "For what purpose does one travel on pilgrimage? The Master said, "To observe those who wander recklessly. Li laughed heartily.
A monk asked, "It is right before one's eyes; why is it that one does not see it again and again? The Master said, "Cut off your ears and lie in the street.

The monk asked, "What is it like when the black bean has not yet sprouted? The Master said, "To feed the donkeys and feed the horses. The monk asked, "What is it like after the sprout has grown? The Master said, "To feed the donkeys and feed the horses."
The Master said, "It penetrates through water and through sand.
A monk asked, "What was it like before Niu-tou had seen the Fourth Patriarch? The Master said, "Precisely so. The monk asked, "What was it like after he saw him?
The Master said, "Sixty kalpas in three lifetimes."
A monk asked, "What is the realm of Xuedou? The Master said, "The sky has no four walls. The monk asked, "Who is the person within the realm?
The Master said, "The moon is at the central peak."
Chan Master Sisi of Dingzhou, who illuminated the Dharma-lamp (1). A monk asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?
The Master said, "How many people fail to grasp it by groping for it? The monk asked, "What happens when one suddenly grasps it? The Master said, "What could it possibly be used for?"
Chan Master Jipeng of Yungai in Tanzhou (Part Three). Initially, he visited Chan Master Shuangquan Ya, who appointed him as his attendant.
Ya presented him with the koan of the *bājiāo* staff, yet for a long time he failed to achieve any realization. One day, while Ya was warming himself by the fire, [Jipeng asked]:
The Master stood in attendance. Ya suddenly asked, "Regarding the story of the staff, try bringing it up so that I may deliberate with you.
As the Master was about to speak, Ya picked up his fire tongs and struck him with them; the Master attained sudden and great enlightenment.
Baizhang Yuan’s verse says: Bestowing and taking away proceed together to test the right and the wrong; As soon as one contends over the staff, the family is lost.
Suddenly an iron mace arrives like the wind; One loses the flowers before one's eyes that were there all along.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "Exaltedness does not reside at the summit; wealth does not reside at Fuyan; joy does not reside in the celestial palaces;
suffering does not reside in the hells. After a long silence, he said: "Familiar faces fill the world, but how many can truly know one's heart?"
A monk asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "The tongue has no bone.
Chan Master Jingyan of Taiyang in Yingzhou, successor to Chan Master Yuanquan of Liangshan in Dingzhou (11th in the lineage). The Master asked Liangshan, "What is the Unborn?"
Xiang was at the Dharma Hall. Liang pointed to an image of Avalokiteśvara and said, "This was painted by the Refined Scholar Wu.
As the Master was about to offer a word in response, Liang hurriedly asked, "Which of these two has form, and which is formless? At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment.
He prostrated and stood with palms joined. Liang said, "Why do you not utter a single phrase? The Master said, "I would not decline to speak, but I fear it would take up ink and paper.
Liangshan laughed heartily and said, "After these words, they shall be inscribed upon a monument."

He addressed the assembly, saying: "All you practitioners of Chan, you must clearly understand the phrase of ordinary non-arising, the phrase of wondrous mystery and lack of partiality, and the phrase of essential clarity and inexhaustibility.
The first phrase opens a single path; the second phrase is without guest or host; the third phrase carries both together.
To speak the first phrase is for the lion to stretch; to speak the second phrase is for the lion to leap back; to speak the third phrase—"
He attained it. Like a lion crouching on the ground: to let go is to pervade the ten directions; to seize is to sit and cut off everything at once.
At such a time, how can one communicate this message? Let the assembly bear witness. If you cannot communicate it, tomorrow we shall present it to the King of Chu.
At that moment, a monk came forward and asked, "What is the phrase of ordinary non-arising? The Master said, "White."

Clouds cover the green mountains; the peaks of the green mountains are not revealed. [The student] asked: "What is the wondrous, profound, and impartial phrase? The Master said: "In the jeweled palace, there is no one who does not stand in attendance;
by not planting the *wutong* tree, one avoids the arrival of the phoenix. [The student] asked: "What is the phrase of the inexhaustible clarity of essence?
The Master said: "When the finger points to space, heaven and earth revolve; turning back on the path, the stone horse emerges from the gauze cage. [The student] asked.
"What is the lion’s yawn? The Master said, "Ultimately there is no intention to look back; how could he deign to fall into the ordinary? "What is the lion’s backward leap?
The Master said, "Circling and returning, everything is fully returned to the Father; though manifold activities and great functions arise, their essence remains undiminished.
"What is the lion’s crouching on the ground? The Master said, "Utterly transcending the mechanism of coming and going, throughout past and present."
There is no change. He said to the assembly: "Do not travel the path of the mind; do not sit upon the effort of non-existence.

Depart from both existence and non-existence, and the heavens and earth will be vast emptiness. Therefore, Nanquan said: "Everyone is here eating stalks of vegetables. If you seek anything more than this—"
Leafy vegetables. To enter hell is like being struck by an arrow. Now tell me, what kind of talk is this? He addressed the assembly, saying:
"Mañjuśrī appears and disappears among humanity; Samantabhadra emerges and withdraws within the multitude.

If you can achieve clear penetration in a single thought-moment, you will trigger the mechanism within the gate of Mañjuśrī. If you can harmonize the past with the future, you will transcend all quarters without weakness."
Having emerged from within the gate of Samantabhadra, you now move up and down; what is this upon your head and beneath your feet?
If you come up, I shall discern you; if you go down, you shall discern me. It is easy to clarify the essence within the phrase, but difficult to discern the essence within the essence itself.
Clarifying the essence within the phrase is because you have come in such a manner; discerning the essence within the essence is for you all—
"Let someone try to pass along a message; let everyone provide witness. Is there anyone who can? He then said: "Today this old monk has had a bout of drunkenness.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "A single phrase: when picked up, light fills the eyes; when set down, cold clouds gather in the valley."

Now tell me: when neither grasping nor releasing, what is it called? The vast waves roll on, white billows flood the heavens; the bright sun hangs in the sky, and all things manifest in their full majesty.
If you seek the standard within words or clarify the pivot within phrases, it is like losing one's head and recognizing only its reflection.
If the teaching of the School is proclaimed, the stone man claps his hands. Now tell me: what does the stone man understand?
The Master then said: "A candela pillar conceiving a fetus is still not permissible; yet the place where the iron ox gives birth is not difficult to pass through.

He addressed the assembly, saying: "If you allow a single thread of the Way, there is freedom to go forward or back, to affirm or deny. If you do not allow a single thread of the Way, it is a great difficulty, a great difficulty."
Therefore, Master Muzhou said: "To let out a single thread of the Way is also due to Muzhou; not to let out a single thread of the Way is also due to Muzhou.
A monk asked, "What is letting out a single thread of the Way? Muzhou said, "Appointing to office according to one's talent.
"What is not letting out a single thread of the Way? Muzhou said, "Ten thousand miles to Yazu. Although it is thus, each remains within the gate.
He establishes the foundational teachings and institutes the vehicle of the school, opening wide the path and the ordinary way of the great sun.
Clenching his fist and extending his hand, he seeks out those who understand; when extended, it arises right where it is; when clenched, it is extinguished wherever it goes. Thus he proclaims.

If one has not yet attained realization even here, how much less can one navigate within words or conceal the blade within phrases? To meet face-to-face without artifice, it is a waste to merely proffer one's intentions.
A single phrase facing the hall; joining palms at the triple gate; walking the path through the two corridors;
performing a dance in the central courtyard; shaking the head beneath the rear gate. Furthermore, there is the lion upon the needle-point—how will you speak of this? If you understand...
Clear them all away. Leave open a single path. If one were to raise the essential teaching (zongcheng), this old monk’s mouth is too narrow.
He addresses the assembly, saying: Depart with vast openness; depart with resolute acceptance; depart with a mind that seeks nothing; depart with a mind of equanimity;
depart free from the notions of "self" and "other. Only then can you sit securely. Thus, an ancient worthy said: "Lead the ox toward the water and go east."
One cannot avoid the corvée taxes of the government. Leading the ox toward the water to the west, one still cannot avoid the corvée taxes of the government.
It is better to pay a little according to one's means, so as to avoid being troubled by them. What is the principle of paying a little according to one's means? Simply cut off both extremes;
when the sentiments of sagehood and ordinariness are exhausted, the true permanence is revealed. This is the principle of phenomena and reality.

Non-duality is precisely the Buddha of Suchness (*tathatā*). If one can be thus, then every phenomenon is without dependence; it is the Great Path of equality where the myriad existents are unattached.
Amidst the bustling affairs of every place, what further matter could there be?
The Master asked Senior Monk Cong (who was later known as Cizhao of Shimen): "Where have you recently come from? Cong replied, "Xiangzhou.
The Master said, "What is the phrase that is not separated [from here]? Cong said, "It is no easy matter for the Abbot to preside over this monastery. The Master said, "Sit and drink some tea."
Congbian went to the hall for the formal visit. The attendant then asked him, "When you arrive briefly, you must respond to the abbot;
this is no easy matter. The Master said, "I offered him a Korean aconite, and he repaid me with shipboard fennel.
Go ask him yourself; he has something to say. The attendant then questioned Congbian: "Just now, when you responded to the Abbot..."
"The position of abbot is not easy to maintain. [The Master asked: "What is your intention? Cong replied, "True brass does not equal gold.
The Master asked a monk, "Where have you come from? He said, "From Hongshan. The Master said, "Is the former master still there? He said, "He is.
The Master said, "His being there is not in doubt, but please have him come out; I wish to meet him. The monk said, "Huh? The Master said, "This one is still..."
The attendant remained silent. The Master said, "Go drink tea.
The Master then asked the attendant, "Suppose there is a person whose entire body is red and raw, standing in a thicket of thorns, surrounded on all sides by fire."
"How can one draw near to him and save this person? The man said, "His six sense organs are incomplete and his seven consciousnesses are not whole.
The Master said, "Tell him to come out; I wish to meet him face to face. The man said, "At this very moment, there is no other [self] besides this to respond."
The Master said, "The official does not permit even a needle.
A monk asked, "What is the meaning of Yunmen’s 'phrase that penetrates the Dharma-body'? The Master said, "How long has it been since you began memorizing [these things]?"
Yun said, "I have deeply received the Master’s instruction.
The Master said, "There is no need for further guidance.
*Liandeng Huiyao*, Scroll 27 and Scroll 28.
Compiled by the monk Wuming, a successor to the Patriarchs residing at Chongfu Chan Monastery in Quanzhou,
a dharma heir of Zen Master Deshao of Tiantai, the eleventh generation descendant of Qingyuan.
Chan Master Yongming Yanshou Zhijue of Hangzhou (Four Parts). Initially residing at Xuedou, he addressed the assembly, saying:
"At this place, Xuedou, a torrential waterfall plunges a thousand fathoms without pausing for even a grain of dust; wondrous cliffs rise ten thousand cubits with no place to set foot.
Where, then, do you all take your next step?"
The Master asked a monk, "Have you ever been here before? The monk replied, "I have. He then asked another monk, and that monk said, "I have not.
The Master said, "One has gained; one has lost. After a short while, an attendant asked, "I wonder which one gained and which one lost?
The Master said, "Did you know these monks? The attendant replied, "I did not know them. The Master said, "In the same pit, there is no difference in the soil."
A monk asked, "Having been at Yongming for so long, why do you not understand the house style of Yongming? The Master said, "Understand it where there is no understanding.
The monk asked, "How can one understand where there is no understanding? The Master said, "An elephant's cub is born from within an ox's womb;
red dust rises from the azure sea. The monk asked, "What is the Great Perfect Mirror? The Master said, "A sand bowl."
A monk asked, "What is the essential meaning of Yongming? The Master said, "Add more incense. The monk said, "Thank you for your instruction.
The Master said, "Be glad that there is no connection at all. The monk bowed; the Master said, "Listen to this verse:
'If you wish to know the essential meaning of Yongming, look at the pool of water before the gate. When the sun shines, radiance arises; when the wind comes, waves stir.'"
Chan Master An of Xianyan in Wenzhou (Part II). Because the Master read the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* with broken phrasing, he said:
"When knowledge and vision establish knowledge, that is the root of ignorance; when knowledge and vision are without seeing, this is nirvāṇa.

Through this, he attained awakening and received the seal of mind from National Teacher Shao. Thereafter, he read it in this manner for the rest of his life. Someone once told him, "Master, you are reading with broken phrasing."
"I have understood," he said. The Master remarked, "This is my place of awakening.
The Vice Prefect Yao Kui asked: "Jingqing once questioned Xuansha, saying: 'A student has newly entered the monastic community;
I beg the Master to point out a path of entry. Xuansha replied: 'Do you hear the sound of the Yan River water? Jingqing said: 'I hear it. Xuansha said: 'Enter from here.'"
"If you had suddenly said 'I have not heard' at that time, what then? The Master called out, "Scholar! Yao responded, "Yes.
The Master said, "Enter from here. Yao also attained realization.
Chan Master Zhifeng of Wuyun in Hangzhou (Part II) addressed the assembly, saying:
"To abandon one teacher and go to study under another teacher is entirely the pattern followed by those who travel south. Now I ask you, venerable ones:
when Sudhana paid homage to Mañjuśrī and intended to ascend Mount Miaofeng to pay homage to the Bhikṣu Meghashiri, once he had arrived at that place, how did Meghashiri [respond]?"
Meeting on a separate peak: the meaning of the Teachings and the meaning of the Patriarchs are one and the same expedient; ultimately, there is no other principle.
If that person understands clearly, this too will be illuminated. All you venerable elders gathered here before me now—this is meeting, or is it not meeting?
"This place is a separate peak; it is not a separate peak. Should you happen to depart from here, you may be said not to have disgraced this old monk.
You will also see that De-yun has never, for even a single moment, been separated from him. Do you still believe this?"
He addressed the assembly, saying: "The ancients traveled for the sake of the Dharma, undaunted by toil and hardship. Take Xuefeng Wushan as an example;
he went to Touzi three times and ascended Dongshan nine times, lingering and returning repeatedly, yet still failed to find a point of entry. Look at you all:
as soon as you step through the gate, you immediately demand that this old monk provide guidance and instruction, speaking of Chan or speaking of the Way. Now—"
"You wish to cultivate the Way of the Ultimate Mystery; how could this be a trivial matter? Furthermore, this matter has its own proper timing.
How can it be attained through restless seeking? Do you wish to know when the time of awakening is? Each of you go down and sit quietly within the hall.
Wait until Mount Jia nods its head, and I, the old monk, shall explain it for you. At that time, a monk stepped forward and said, "Mount Jia..."
Feng nodded his head. "Please, Preceptor, speak. The Master called to the assembly, saying, "Tell me, does this monk understand or not?
The monk prostrated. The Master said, "Today, by chance, my mirror has failed me."
Chan Master Huguang Shihuh of Guangzhou (Case 1). A monk asked, "The student has come to enter the monastic community; I beg the Master for instruction.
The Master said, "Before you had even entered the assembly, I had already instructed you. The monk asked, "How am I to understand this?
The Master said, "There is no need to understand."
Chan Master Huiju of Longhua in Hangzhou (Fanyi) addressed the assembly, saying: "Regarding the ancestral vehicle of the Buddhas and patriarchs, how can it be proclaimed upon reaching this point?
Take, for instance, Śākyamuni Buddha’s preaching of the Dharma throughout his entire lifetime—like pouring water from one vessel into another.
Even the ancient worthies have said that it is like the affairs of a dream or the prattle of a sleeper. But tell me, according to what principle did those ancient worthies speak?"

He spoke thus. Do you understand? The Great Gate of Generosity is open; when has it ever been obstructed? Producing ordinary beings and nurturing sages, there is not a hair’s breadth of separation between them.
To speak of the ordinary, they are entirely ordinary; to cite the sage, they are entirely sage. Ordinary and sage do not wait for one another;
each and every one is uniquely honored. Therefore it is said: "The mountains, rivers, and the great earth preach the Dharma at all times and radiate light at all times. Earth and water...
"Fire and wind—each is like this. At that time, a monk came forward to pay his respects. The Master said, "What an excellent question! Ask it according to the Dharma.
Just as the monk was about to step forward, the Master said, "And again, you have missed the point."
Chan Master Benxian of Ruizhu in Wenzhou (the fifth in the series) addressed the assembly, saying: "When I first met [Master] Tiantai, I attained realization upon his words.
Yet for a thousand days thereafter, throughout the four modes of deportment, it was as if something were obstructing my chest; it was like being in the company of an enemy.
One day, I suddenly had a profound awakening, as if while washing my face, I finally touched my own nose."

He addressed the assembly, saying: "In general, when studying the Way, it is not necessarily the case that studying 'questions' constitutes studying the Way; it is not necessarily the case that studying 'selections of words' constitutes studying the Way;
it is not necessarily the case that studying 'substitutes' constitutes studying the Way; it is not necessarily the case that studying 'alternative responses' constitutes studying the Way;

it is not necessarily the case that studying the 'extraordinary phrases' within the sutras and treatises and breaking them apart constitutes studying the Way; it is not necessarily the case that studying the breaking apart of various..."

The words of the Patriarchs are for the purpose of study. If you study in this manner, even if you become proficient in all seven ways and reach mastery in all eight directions, if you lack a truly authentic place of realization within the Buddha-dharma, you are called a follower of dry wisdom (*śuṣka-prajñā*). Have you not heard the ancient masters say:
"Cleverness cannot withstand birth and death; dry wisdom does not escape the wheel of suffering"? You people, if you are to study, you should...
One must engage in authentic study and practice to attain it. As for authentic study and practice: when walking, walk while practicing;
when standing, stand while practicing; when sitting, sit while practicing; when sleeping, sleep while practicing; when speaking, speak while practicing;
when silent, remain silent while practicing; and during all tasks, perform them while practicing. Having thus turned toward...
At times such as these, one engages in inquiry. But tell me: what person do you inquire of? What teaching do you inquire about?
Only when you reach a point of clarity here can you truly succeed. If there is no such clarity, it is called hasty study; in that case, there will be no ultimate realization.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "In the teachings of Tiantai, it is said that there are three gates: the gate of Mañjuśrī, the gate of Avalokiteśvara, and the gate of Samantabhadra.
The gate of Mañjuśrī refers to all forms; the gate of Avalokiteśvara refers to all sounds; and the gate of Samantabhadra refers to arriving without moving a step.
My teaching, however, is this: the gate of Mañjuśrī is not all forms; the gate of Avalokiteśvara is not all sounds; and the gate of Samantabhadra..."
"What is this 'Gate of the Sages'? Do not say that it is merely speaking according to the teachings of Tiantai; there is nothing to it—withdraw for now.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "The birds call in the deep forest; the fish leap in the emerald stream. The clouds unfurl, and the sound of the waterfall is plaintive.
Do you recognize all these phenomena as the point of entry shown to you? If you can recognize them, you may proceed with your study."
Excellent.
The Master has a verse that says: "Throughout vast kalpas, it has always been thus; thus it is the same as heaven and the same as earth.
What form can there be in being the same as earth and the same as heaven? In what form is there anything that is not so?"
Chan Master Yuanqi of Yandang, Wenzhou (Case 1). A monk asked, "When the night moon spreads its light, why is there no reflection in the azure pool?
The Master said, "A master at play with his own shadow. The monk walked from west to east and stood there. The Master said, "Not only do you play with shadows;
you are truly terrified of your own head."
Chan Master Hongshou of Xingjiao Monastery in Hangzhou (Case 1) addressed the assembly, saying: "What falls is not another thing; what spreads out is not dust.
Mountains, rivers, and the great earth—all fully manifest the King’s body."
Chan Master Qiji of Yunju in Hongzhou, Dharma Heir of Chan Master Taiqin of Qingliang in Jinling (Four Cases). While the Master was under the seat of Chan Master Fadeng, he served as the Librarian.
One day, Fadeng said to the Master: "Today, a monk asked me, 'What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? To which I replied:"
He said, "Neither east nor west. The Abbot asked, "What about it? The Master replied, "Neither east nor west. Yunmen said, "Even so, how can you attain it? The Master was at a loss.
That evening, he went to the abbot’s quarters to seek further instruction. Yunmen said, "His descendants are already there of their own accord.
At these words, the Master suddenly realized the essential meaning. He composed a verse which says: "To receive beings and benefit living things—how exquisite!"
"Those born outside the family will ultimately be unworthy; the lineage belongs to those within the house, who will find perfect utility in the future.
The Master asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From the hall. The Master said, "How can you speak such falsehoods?"
Cishou said, "This monk is a minor liar; Yunju is a major liar.
A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Who are you?"
When the Master was about to pass away, he addressed the assembly, saying: "Today this old monk, pressed by the winds and fires [of death], has come specifically to meet you all.
But where do we meet? Do you see me in the four elements and five aggregates? Or do you see me in the six sense bases and twelve sense fields?
Since I cannot be seen in any of these various places, then who is it that asks these questions right now?"
Who? If anyone can see this, it may be said that future students will have something to rely upon.

Chan Master Chengti of Xiqian on Mount Lu, a successor of Chan Master Heng of Baizhang in Hongzhou (total of two entries), addressed the assembly, saying: "The Buddha-dharma is a matter of no concern; everyone together..."
Practice! Dwell together with the great assembly. Let the eyes be filled with forms and the ears with sounds. The wondrous meaning of all Buddhas is clearly realized right here;
it extends for thousands and tens of thousands of miles.
A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Zhang San and Li Si.
Tiantai Shan Chongjin Chan Master (1), successor to Chan Master Yunju Qingxi of Hongzhou.
A monk asked, "How is it when there is a cold spring in an ancient ravine? The Master said:
"Be careful not to drink it. A monk asked, "What of one who drinks? The Master said, "You will lose your very life.
Chan Master Mingzhou Tiantong Xin, Dharma heir of Chan Master Lushan Guizong Yirou (Case 1). A monk asked, "What is the secret application? The Master said, "When has it ever been..."
He attained the secret [teaching]. He asked, "When the path of the mind has not yet been traversed, how is it? The Master said, "What thing obstructs you?
He asked, "When one seeks it but cannot find it, how is it? The Master said, "Why seek it? He asked, "How is it then? The Master said, "When did you ever lose it?"
Chan Master Yongqing of Yungai in Tanzhou, Dharma Heir of Chan Master Chang'an Yan Gui of Mount Lu (Case 1). A monk asked: "Suppose there is a person in a ten-thousand-foot well."
"How can you get out? The Master said, "I am glad to meet you. The monk said, "In that case, I shall pass through the clouds and pierce the sun.
The Master said, "What about the affairs of the Thirty-three Heavens? The monk had no reply. The Master said, "You are a fellow who speaks empty lies and deceives others."
Chan Master Da Jue Huailian of Ayuwang Temple in Mingzhou, a dharma successor of Chan Master Letan Cheng of Hongzhou (Part II), addressed the assembly, saying:

"If one discusses the two characters 'Buddha-dharma,' they are merely superfluous words and trivial explanations. If you all can take responsibility for this right here, you will exhaust [all such attachments]."
These two heads and three faces are like gold dust: though precious, it cannot remain in the eye.

If one is a monk of genuine caliber, upon merely hearing this raised, they will shake it off and cut it through, not tolerating even a speck of dust; thus they are uniquely liberated and autonomous, most intimately attuned to reality.
Only then can they be as heaven when among heaven, as humans when among humans, as monks when among monks, and as laypeople when among laypeople.
He conforms to the mundane. Among the ordinary, he is the same as the ordinary; among the sages, he is the same as the sages. He appears and disappears with sovereign freedom in all places;
no one can restrain him, nor can anyone surpass him. Why is this? It is because he is able to establish all phenomena, yet he himself is not those phenomena.
Since he has neither front nor back, one must by all means refrain from making arbitrary arrangements. One need only know the twelve periods of the day.
In the midst of daily eating and drinking, there is joy and no sorrow; let us simply expect this much of one another, with nothing else. Thus the ancients said:
"Leisurely and expansive, forever like a simpleton; his own household naturally has those who love him."
The Master raised his fist and said to the assembly: "When the fist is clenched, the Five Peaks stand upside down; when the hand is opened, the five fingers are distinct.
Sometimes he locks the barrier of the Buddhas and Patriarchs; sometimes he pushes open the dwelling of the thousand sages. Today, I present this here."
Tell me, how is it to be used? [The Master] strikes the meditation seat and says: "The subsequent text is long; it is entrusted for another day.
Chan Master Weilan of Chengtian Temple in Wuzhou (Case 1) addressed the assembly, saying: "To cut in one stroke and create two parts is to bury the ancestral wind.
For a lion to turn its body is to drag through mud and water. Even if you were to sit and cut off the ten directions, allowing passage neither to the mundane nor the sacred, with your feet..."
[The lineage] continues with thirty more [generations].

Next is Chan Master Chenghao of Yuyuan in Jingmen Commandery, a dharma heir of Chan Master Tansheng of Beita in Fuzhou (fourth in this section). Addressing the assembly, he said: "When I was at Guyin, for ten..."
For years, I have never drunk a single drop of water from Guyin, nor have I ever chewed a single grain of rice from Guyin.
If you do not understand this, Dayang will explain it to you. (He raised his staff and descended from the seat.)

He addressed the assembly, saying: "When the congee is thin, sit later; when the bed is narrow, lie down first. If you have deaf ears, prefer a loud voice; if your eyesight is dim, large characters are suitable. Take care.
Once, as a monk was entering the room, there was a dog inside. The Master gave a shout, and the dog immediately went out. The Master said: "..."
The dog, however, knows; you, however, do not know.
A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Cut off his heels. [The monk] asked, "What is the Dharma?
The Master said, "Lift off the skull."
Chan Master Fachang Yiyu of Hongzhou, successor to Chan Master Zhixian of Beichen in Tanzhou (fifteen cases total). Beichen asked the Master, "Where have you recently departed from? The Master said:
Fuyan said, "Xian, how long is Dashi’s nostril? The Master replied, "It is just as it was when you, Reverend, first saw it.
Xian said, "Tell me, when I saw it, how long was it? The Master replied, "Reverend, it seems you have never been to Fuyan.
Xian said, "You are merely one who parrots the words of others. He then asked, "When you came, was Mazu Daoshi well? The Master...
Xuanzang said, "Peace and happiness. Xian said, "What were you just saying to me? The Master said, "I was telling the Abbot not to be so reckless.
Xian said, "Out of consideration for you being newly arrived, I cannot bring myself to beat you. The Master said, "I, too, shall let the Abbot off. After the tea was finished.
Xian asked, "Where is your native place? The Master said, "Zhangzhou. Xian asked, "What is Sanping doing there? The Master said, "He speaks of Chan and speaks of the Way.
Xian asked, "How old are you? The Master said, "I am the same age as the pillar. Xian said, "As for having a pillar, that is one thing;
but when there is no pillar, how old are you? The Master said, "Even without a pillar, I am not even one year old."
[The Master] said, "Not many. Xian said, "At midnight, he released the black chicken.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "Vimalakīrti’s silence was a mere imitation of the lineage of the patriarchs; Śākyamuni’s picking up of the flower on Vulture Peak turned into a poisonous drug.
Sitting in face-to-face meditation for nine years was to stifle the former patriarchs; transmitting the robe at midnight was to deceive later students. Mazu’s 'This very mind is...'"
The Buddha was much like one who waits by a stump for a rabbit. Panshan’s “neither mind nor Buddha” may be called muddling through with mud and water.
Such views as these all serve to ruin the ancestral style and extinguish the lineage of the Hu; they merely catch echoes in the void, deceiving the sages and insulting the worthy.
Later students are innocent victims, falling under their pointed annotations. If we discuss this matter, the Buddhas have never appeared in the world, nor...
Not a single dharma was given to anyone; Bodhidharma did not come from the West, and the Second Patriarch did not receive the marrow.
Truly, the imperial wind sweeps vast and wide, and the village elders sing in joy. With no reliance in mind and no dependence in action, hearing of "Chan" or "the Way" is like encountering an enemy;
speaking of "form" or "mind" is like meeting a fierce tiger. After Fachang, I shall pick wild vegetables and pound millet for you.
Eat rice and prepare *vyañjana* (mixed) meals; cook vegetable soups. When hungry, eat; when weary, sleep.
Do not seek self-exaltation through various ranks, nor emulate the three vehicles by performing ritual recitations.

He addressed the assembly, saying: "To awaken to the Way by hearing sounds is no different from climbing a tree to seek fish; to clarify the mind by seeing forms is much like losing one's head and recognizing only its reflection.
O worthy ones, there is no need to shorten the crane or lengthen the duck, nor to move mountains to fill a valley. The Southern Dipper and the Northern Dipper [are as they are]."

The celestial mansions and degrees are clearly defined; the sun fades while the moon shines bright, their rising and setting naturally distinct. I simply request that you cease military expeditions and put an end to war, remaining upright and non-active (*wuwei*).
Thus, the state will naturally be at peace, and you shall stand shoulder-to-shoulder with the Buddhas and Patriarchs.

Furthermore, if one seeks to discern the mark within words and clarify the pivot within phrases, one is like a man waiting by a tree stump under the moonlit breeze—the cool rabbit grows ever more distant as the spring grass turns green.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "The Patriarch came from the West specifically to sing of this matter, desiring only that people of the time would know it exists.
It is like the poor man’s jewel on his robe; it was not obtained from another. All Buddhas of the thousand ages are merely those who play with the jewel. As for Bodhisattvas of the Ten Stages..."
You are merely people seeking pearls; you are truly but wretched beggars, clutching jewels while lost in a foreign land.
A man of keen intelligence, upon hearing a single mention of this, will immediately frown his brows and know its true place.
If you continue to step forward, it would be better to take up your staff and return to the mountains, letting out a long啸 (shout) as the mist deepens.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "If you withdraw a thousand feet, I shall sprout right where you stand.
If you present yourself face-to-face, I shall hide my body while revealing my shadow. If you pick up pebbles from a spring pond, I shall scatter bright pearls.
Thus it reaches a state where water cannot wet it and wind cannot enter, like a solid iron hammer without a hole. Now tell me, what is this Dharma?"
"Does Chang still have a way of dealing with people? After a long silence, he said: "A sharp blade may cut the flesh, yet the wound eventually heals;
but words that wound others leave a resentment that does not fade.
The Master then uttered these words: "I want someone who does not understand Chan to be National Teacher."
Miaoxi said, "Tell me, is this a sentence of *amṛta* (clarified butter), or is it a sentence of poison?
The Master and Chan Master Nan discussed the story of Provincial Governor Cheng looking at his place of birth.
The Master said, "Why not cut him off completely right here and now? Nan said, "I have even painted legs on a snake for him; it is simply that he himself has not yet awakened. The Master [laughed].
[Zhaozhou] asked, "How do you act for them, Master? Nanquan said, "I chew all the ginger and drink all the vinegar.
Zhaozhou said, "That is just the way of a common, worldly master. Nanquan said, "What about you, Master? Zhaozhou picked up his whisk and struck him.
Nanquan said, "This old fellow is truly heartless."
The Master and Nan Chan-shi cited an old story about once having asked Xinghua:
"Where does a person who 'knows' go? Xinghua said, "Sudhana’s staff. I said, "I am not asking about Sudhana’s staff;
where does the person who 'knows' go? Xinghua said, "Sometimes he climbs mountains; sometimes he crosses rivers. I said, "Master..."
"You only know how to climb higher step by step; you do not know how to let go from the void.
Huayan said, "Although this old monk is advanced in years, I shall certainly not fail the intent of your coming. Nanquan asked, "How about you, Master?
The Master said, "At that time, I wrongly blamed Xinghua. Nanquan said, "I understand now. But tell me, where did he go? The Master said, "Ask him yourself."
"Who? Nan said. "What is the point of feigning deafness and pretending to be mute? The Master said, "Even so, I have not failed to respond to the occasion of your coming.
While the Master was receiving an invitation at Shuangling, he took his leave of the two head seats, Ying and Sheng, saying, "We have been together for three years. There was no further word.
"I do not understand this matter. Examining it closely, there is no lack of leakage. With his staff, he drew a line and said, "Let us set this aside for now.
As for the matter of the Zen school, what is it? Ying said, "Mount Sumeru has its nostrils placed upon it.

The Master said, "In that case, looking down from a cliff at the water's edge, one suddenly finds oneself in a state of deep sorrow. Ying said, "Deep-Sand (the Dragon King) sticks out his eyes. The Master said, [He drew another line with his staff.]
"How can it be that the paths of the sage and the commoner are not different, yet there are so many gates of expedient means? Yingshan said, "A coin-snake cannot penetrate.
The Master said, "What common ground is there for conversation with a fellow like you? Yingshan said, "It is simply because my own faculties are shallow; do not resent the great springtime.
He then drew a line and said, "Let us set aside the matters of the Zen school for a moment—what about this matter? The Master then gave him a slap.
Ying said, "This man from Zhangzhou has no sense of propriety. The Master said, "If I do not strike you for such a view, when shall I ever do so?
He struck him again. Ying said, "It was also I who invited this from the old monk."
Yingsheng, one of the two head seats, came to the mountain to visit him. Yingsheng said, "The Master usually likes to scrutinize those from all quarters;
why is it that today you have instead come to make a living inside an ancient temple? The Master said, "I only strike the grass so as to startle the snake.
Yingsheng said, "Do not try to deceive people! The Master said, "And what are you doing thrusting your head into the glue pot?"
Ying said, "An ancient said, 'I saw two earthen oxen fighting their way into the sea; that is why I dwell on this mountain.
I do not know, Master, what you have seen. The Master said, "In the future, when you have a thatch roof over your head and someone asks you, 'How would you respond?
Ying said, "The summit of the mountain is not as good as its base. The Master said, "For now..."
Daowu asked, "In the future, will you be able to remain in the mountain retreat? Ying said, "I am not fit to wield a mattock; I am better suited to drag a plow.
The Master said, "Have you ever seen the ancients in a dream? Ying said, "How about you, Master? The Master spread his two hands wide. Ying said, "A shrimp cannot leap out of its measure.
The Master said, "Do not take a three-inch candle and attempt to compare it to the brilliance of the great sun. Ying said, "But what can be done?"
The public case is present. The Master said, "Disciples of Chan are as numerous as hemp and millet.
As the Master was about to enter the Dharma Hall, he asked the two head seat monks, Ying and Sheng, "I wish to come here and raise the Dharma Hall."
"Tell me, what have you accomplished here? Yingshuo said, "The thief is the petty man. The Master said, "Zi of Shaowu moves and immediately emits the stench of excrement.
Yingshuo said, "Having endured the bitterness of frost and snow. The Master said, "A bright pearl has a price of its own worth a thousand pieces of gold;
who would be willing to beat a sparrow in the woods? Yingshuo said, "It is very much like being unable to hold the alms bowl, yet falsely claiming—"
[The Master] did not eat. The Master, however, pointed at Sheng and said, "Tell me, what have you done to respond to this?
Sheng said, "Originally there is no rank or position; there is no need for forced arrangement. The Master said, "You donkey! Where will you put yourself?"
Sheng said, "I leave it entirely to you to bore through the tortoise shell or strike the roof tiles. The Master said, "It is still merely a fabricated magistrate.

Ying said, "If it were a treasure worth a thousand pieces of gold, why would one need to strike at a sparrow? The Master said, "When a member of the eastern family dies, the members of the western family offer their condolences.
Ying said, "Seeing injustice on the road, one cannot remain indifferent."
Winter night. While eating fruit with the Head Seat Gan, the Master picked up a tangerine and said, "How does this flavor compare to that of Huanglong?
Gan replied, "One must wait until it has been tasted before one can know. The Master said, "In the definitive point of testing a person, one knows them the moment they open their mouth.
It is said that in the Dharma-ending age, Zen masters are mostly empty and rarely substantial. The Master then picked up a bag and said, "This..."
[The Master] asked again, "How about this? Yunju said, "It must be the Master [Heshang] himself who can do it. The Master said, "A single sack is already beyond my power.
Yunju said, "To yield to others is not the mark of a weak man."

The Head Seat Zhe arrived. The Master asked, "The mountain is deep and the path remote; why trouble yourself to visit? Zhe replied, "Within the Way of benevolence and righteousness, this is not considered an extra burden.
The Master said, "What have you brought with you? Zhe stepped forward with his hands clasped. The Master said, "Is it only this, or is there something else?
Zhe opened both hands. The Master said, "In the beginning, you were nearly there; in the end, you will not get a beating."
Zhe bowed. Zhaozhou said, “Let me attend to my own business first. Once the business was concluded, the Master asked again, “Where have you recently departed from?
Zhe replied, “Yunju. The Master said, “What is the matter with the peak? Zhe said, “How many people are perplexed by it?
The Master struck his staff on the ground and said, “As for Hongjue’s nostrils, how do they compare to this? Zhe said, “The grass-thief has been utterly defeated. The Master said, “This...”
The monk said, "I do not even recognize the *huatou*. Zhe asked, "What did the Master ask? The teacher said, "I asked you about Hongjue’s nostrils.
Zhe said, "And yet you say you do not recognize the *huatou*. The teacher said, "It is no mistake for you to be a disciple of Cuiyan."
The Master asked a monk, "All sounds are the voice of the Buddha; is this so? The monk replied, "Yes. The Master said, "Why then does the crow caw like a crow and the magpie chirp like a magpie?
The monk said, "It is you, Preceptor, who gives rise to discrimination. The Master then struck him.
He asked another monk, "Is it true that all sounds are the voice of the Buddha? The monk replied, "No. The Master asked, "Why is it not so?
The monk said, "The crow caws as a crow; the magpie chirps as a magpie. The Master struck him as well.
Later, a monk asked, "The first monk was right; let us set him aside for now. But why did you strike the second monk, who was wrong?
The Master struck him and said, "Listen, and let those with clear eyes pass judgment."

Chan Master Yunju Xiaoshun of Nankang Commandery, Dharma heir of Chan Master Dongshan Xiaocong of Junzhou (the tenth): Having gone from Mount Dong to Wuchang to beg for alms, he first visited the home of Layman Liu Gong.
The Layman was a man of noble conduct, revered by his contemporaries; whether in matters of bestowing or withholding, there was nothing he would not do according to his own intent.
He followed him. At that time, the Master was young and, unaware of the Layman’s extensive training, treated him with some degree of contempt.
The Layman said, "I, an old man, have a question. If your words accord with mine, you shall open my robe; if they do not, I ask that you return it to me.
He then asked, "How is it when an ancient mirror has not yet been polished? The Master said, "Black as lacquer. The Layman said, "And after it has been polished? The Master said, "It reflects."
He illuminated heaven and earth. The layman gave a long bow and said, "If that is so, Master, please return to Dongshan for now.

With a sweep of his sleeve, he entered his residence. The Master stroked his chin and immediately returned to Dongshan. When Dongshan asked him the reason, the Master recounted the incident in full. Dongshan said:
"You have asked; I shall answer you. The Master repeated his previous question. Baoshan said, "It is not far from here to Hanyang. The Master then offered the latter part of the verse.
Baoshan said, "Before the Yellow Crane Tower lies Parrot Isle. At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment; his spiritual acuity was such that it could not be provoked.

On the day the Master opened the hall, he addressed the assembly, saying: "The ultimate truth of the Tathāgata is truly difficult to expose. The mind-seal and its profound mechanism—how can they be grasped through intellectual understanding?
Since beginningless time, sentient beings have turned their backs on the mind to grasp at dharmas, clinging to phenomena and wandering in delusion.

Consequently, the Buddhas appeared in the world, establishing teachings according to the capacities of beings; these are called the 'gateways of expedient means. But as for the school of the patch-robed monks..."
[The Master] descended. "A single word in mutual accord—ten thousand miles away. Is there no one among this assembly who can engage in a thorough discussion?
Come forward and reveal the news before the multitude. A monk asked, "I have heard the Master say: 'Do not speak of the mysterious, do not speak of the wondrous.
Having departed from these two paths, how do you provide instruction? The Master said, "A toad chasing a hawk. The monk said, "It is entirely because of this."
[The student] asked. The Master said, "A mouse playing with a monkey. The Master then said, "Let this questioning cease.
An ancient said, 'Much speaking and much talking have from of old only led to mutual error. Today, I have needlessly created a scene of defeat before you all.
If a person of clear eyes were to see this, they would laugh until their mouths split. Why? Because 'if one has no wound oneself, do not... [The text ends here].
This is to express regret for them. Nevertheless, even so, one must truly reach this state before it can be attained.

He addressed the assembly, saying: "Deshan said, 'I will strip you of your head-stall and unload you from your pack-saddle, teaching you to become a true person—one whom the three realms do not contain and the six paths do not encompass. Is that which you have learned from various quarters not exactly this?"
"Carrying a load on one's head and horns. "Deishan’s staff. "Linji’s shout. Are these not carrying a load on one's head and horns?
You people have been ruined by the old bones of all quarters; you have learned a heap of antiquities and stored them within your chests.
He then said, "I understand Zen. Is there still blood beneath your skin? Thus he was deceived by him.
Daoyu speaking thus today is also merely increasing ignorance for the sake of idle matters.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "The ancients said, 'Not seeing a single dharma is the Tathāgata;
only then can one be named Avalokiteśvara. Now I ask you all: how do you explain the principle of not seeing a single dharma?
Is it that originally there is not a single dharma? Is it that originally there is purity? If you understand it in such a way, you have not even dreamed of it."
"Even the wife in Sanjia Village does not hold such a view. Is there anyone under Dayu who can explain the principle?
Come forward and speak before the assembly; Dayu will testify for you. Is there anyone?
Once a word has been spoken, even four horses cannot overtake it."
He addressed the assembly, saying: "To hear the two words 'Buddha-dharma' is already enough to make my ears and eyes sweat.

Before you have even stepped through the gate of Dayu, I would give thirty blows to the soles of your feet. Nevertheless, today as well, I am exerting myself to the utmost for the sake of the assembly."
He addressed the assembly, saying: "The flying snow-blade slashes horizontally; not a blade of grass remains. The great earth is shrouded in gloom; heaven and earth lose their luster.
At this very moment, even if a Buddha or a Patriarch were to appear, they would have to sink three feet into the ground.
Nevertheless, today at Dayu, I shall suffer a total defeat before you all. Tell me, where exactly is the defeat? Is there anyone who can see it?"
Can you examine this thoroughly? If you can examine it thoroughly, your journey as a wandering monk is complete.
If you cannot examine it thoroughly, you shall remain for now a mere rice-eating monk.
He addressed the assembly, saying: "To bring forth the essential subtlety, the incense pillar frowns; for discourse that transcends the ordinary, the tortoise turns toward the fire.
To speak of plain reality and the absence of affairs is like feeding a child with already-chewed rice; to praise or disparage the ancients and the present cannot save oneself.
O Zen practitioners, apart from these, how do you deliberate? Is it not the case that one encounters an intercalary month every three years, and the ninth month is the Double Ninth Festival?"

Prostrations! Where it penetrates your nose, the world of Fragrant Accumulation perfumes the heavens and scorches the earth. Where it penetrates your tongue, the supreme flavor of clarified butter turns into poison.

The Heart of Reflection. If one can act in this manner, only then will one understand how to walk among those of different species.

The Venerable Prajñātāra was asked by King Hīnayāna of India, "What is the Buddha? The Master replied, "To see one's own nature is to be the Buddha.
The King asked, "Does the Master see his own nature? The Master replied, "I see the Buddha-nature. The King asked, "Where does this nature reside?
The Master replied, "It resides in its functioning. The King asked, "What is this functioning? I do not see it now. The Master replied, "It is functioning right now."
[The Master] said, "It is used. But Your Majesty does not see it yourself. The King asked, "Does it exist within me? The Master said, "If Your Majesty employs it, there is nothing that is not it.
If Your Majesty does not employ it, its substance is difficult to perceive. The King asked, "When it is being employed, in how many places does it manifest?
The Master said, "When it manifests, it has eight locations. The King said, "Please explain to me these eight manifestations. The Master—

A verse says: In the womb it is called the body; In the world it is called a person. In the eye it is called seeing; In the ear it is called hearing. In the nose it smells fragrances; In the tongue it engages in discourse.
In the hands it grasps and seizes; In the feet it moves and runs. Manifesting everywhere, it encompasses all lands as numerous as grains of sand;
Yet when withdrawn, it is contained within a single minute atom. Those who recognize it know it to be Buddha-nature; Those who do not recognize it call it the vital spirit.
When the King heard this, his mind was awakened; he prostrated and offered his thanks.

“Empty. The Master asked, “Before the various subtle elements have yet gathered, what would you call it? Sheng was at a loss for an answer. The Master asked again, “Which sutras or treatises do you study?

“Nirvāṇa. “Which of these is the Nirvāṇa of the Dharma Master? What is the meaning of Nirvāṇa? Could there be two? “I am just like this,” [the monk] said.
“I do not yet know how the Zen Master explains Nirvāṇa. The Master picked up his *ruyi* (ceremonial fly-whisk) and asked, “Do you see it?
“I see it,” [the monk] replied. “What do you see? the Master asked. “I see the *ruyi* in the Zen Master’s hand,” [the monk] replied. The Master then took the *ruyi*...

He threw it to the ground and asked, "Do you see it? The monk replied, "I see it. The Master asked, "What do you see? The monk said, "I see the *ruyi* (ceremonial fly-whisk) in the Zen Master’s hand falling to the ground.
The Master rebuked him, saying, "Judging by your understanding, you have not yet emerged from the ranks of the common crowd.

How can you claim that your fame shall resound through the universe? He then brushed off his robes and departed. His disciples were left with lingering doubts and pursued the Master to question him further, saying, "Our teacher said..."
"Form is emptiness, emptiness is nirvana"—this does not accord [with my teaching]. I do not yet understand how you, Master Chan, explain the meaning of the emptiness of form.

The Master said: "I do not say that your teacher’s explanation is incorrect; however, your teacher only explains the emptiness of form in the state of fruition (*phala*), but does not understand how to explain the emptiness of form within the causal state (*hetu*.
His disciple asked: "What is the emptiness of form within the causal state? The Master said: "Because a single atom (*paramāṇu*) is empty, the many..."

The aggregate of atoms is empty because the aggregate of atoms is empty. A single atom is empty; within a single atom there is no aggregate of atoms, and within the aggregate of atoms there is no single atom.
Fenyang replied on his behalf, "Stop this entanglement.
When Master Nanyue Huixiang was told by Master Zhigong to send a message, saying, "Why do you not go down the mountain to teach and transform sentient beings?
Why do you gaze at the clouds and sky? the Master replied, "The Buddhas of the three periods of time have been swallowed by me in a single gulp."
[If] all [beings] are exhausted, where else could there be sentient beings to be transformed?
Wuzu Ke said: "Let us further discuss the principle.
When the Chan Master Zhiyi of Tiantai was at Mount Nanyue, he was reciting the Lotus Sūtra; upon reaching the "Chapter on the Bodhisattva Medicine King," it says: "This is truly..."

Through such diligence, this is called the true Dharma-offering to the Tathāgata. Thereupon, he realized the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-samādhi* and attained the *Pratyāhāra-dhāraṇī*, seeing that the single assembly on Vulture Peak remained solemnly as if it had never dispersed.
Miaoxi said: "If those who have not yet attained the *svādhisthāna-dhāraṇī* (the dhāraṇī of revolving) still see the single assembly on Vulture Peak today, by what do they take it as proof?
If they do not see it, that is true diligence; that is called the true Dharma-offering to the Tathāgata.
To merely recite [the name] in this manner, however, results in a superfluous dharma."
When Master Fenggan of Tiantai was asked by Hanshan, "How does the ancient mirror illuminate when it has not yet been polished?
the Master replied, "The ice-clear pitcher has no reflection; the monkey reaches for the moon in the water. Hanshan said, "This is not illumination. Please speak further.
The Master replied, "Since you do not bring forth the myriad virtues, what am I to say? Both Hanshan and Shide were thus [enlightened].
Having performed his duties, he withdrew.
The Master intended to travel to Mount Wutai and asked Hanshan and Shide, "Will you go with me to travel to Mount Wutai?
If you go with me to travel to Mount Wutai, you shall be of my same lineage; if you do not go with me to travel to Mount Wutai, you are not of my same lineage. Hanshan said, "You go."
"Going to Mount Wutai—what for? The Master said, "To pay homage to Mañjuśrī. The Mountain said, "You are not of my kind.
When Chan Master Daoyou of Daomei was a śrāmaṇera, he went to Guoqing Temple to receive the precepts. Hanshan, having foreknowledge of this, went with Shide to the entrance of Songmen to meet him.
As soon as Daoyou arrived, the two men leaped out from the side of the road and let out three roars like tigers.
Shengyu remained silent. Hanshan said, "Since our parting at Vulture Peak until this very day, do you still remember?
Shengyu again had no reply. Shide took up his staff and said, "What would you call this?
Shengyu again had no reply. Hanshan said, "Enough, enough! There is no need to ask him; since we parted, he has already been born as a king for three lifetimes."
I have completely forgotten it.
Formerly, Zen Master Jingzhao asked National Teacher Lengyan: "The sutra says, 'If one can turn things over, one is identical to the Tathāgata;
if one is turned by things, one is called an ordinary person. Now, regarding Shengyuan Pavilion—how does one turn it?"
Fenyang replied on his behalf, "We are both old men.
Zhigong of Jinling asked a foreign monk, "I have heard that you, Venerable One, called me a butcher.
Have you ever seen me kill? The monk said, "Yes, I have seen it. The Master said, "There is the seeing of seeing; there is the non-seeing of seeing; there is neither being nor non-being of seeing."
"If there is the view of having a view, that is the view of an ordinary person (*pṛthagjana*). The view of not having a view, that is the view of a *śrāvaka*.
The view of neither being nor non-being, that is the view of a non-Buddhist (*tīrthika*). I do not yet know, Venerable Sir, how you see. The Indian monk said: "Do you have such views as these?"
Fenyang said, "His coming from the West was not in vain.
The Master [Yunmen] gave this instruction: "All day long he picks up incense and chooses firewood, yet he does not know that his own body is the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa).
Xuansha said, "All day long he picks up incense and chooses firewood, yet he does not know what the true site of enlightenment is."
Xuedou said: "A pair of unperforated iron hammers. Zhaojue Qin said:
"All day long one picks up incense and chooses firewood, yet one does not know how to pick up incense or choose firewood."
The Monk布袋 (Fotu) of Mingzhou once stood on a busy thoroughfare. A monk asked him, "What are you doing here? The Master said, "I am waiting for someone.
Or he would say, "He is coming! He is coming! Then, reaching into his robe, he took out a tangerine and offered it to the monk.
As the monk reached out to receive it, the Master withdrew his hand and said, "You are not that person."
A monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master dropped his cloth bag, stood with his hands folded, and remained there.
The monk said, "Is it only this? Is there anything more? The Master picked up the cloth bag, placed it on his shoulder, and walked away.
One day, as the Master saw a monk walking ahead of him, he suddenly patted the monk on the back. The monk turned his head, and the Master said, "Hand me over a coin.
At other times, the Master would carry a cloth bag and a tattered mat while traveling along the main thoroughfares; the cloth bag contained his alms bowl.
Wooden clogs, fish, meat, vegetables, rice, tiles, stones, wood, earth—there were all manner of things.
Sometimes, amidst a dense crowd, he would open his cloth bag, scatter the objects down, and say, "Look! Look! Then, picking each one up one by one, he would ask the people, "What is this called?"
The Great Being Shanhui of Wuzhou was invited by Emperor Wu of the Liang dynasty to lecture on the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*.

As soon as the Master ascended the seat, he struck the lectern once with a ruler and immediately descended. The Emperor was astonished. Master Zhi said, "Your Majesty, do you understand? The Emperor replied, "I do not understand.
Master Zhi said, "The Great Being has finished his lecture on the sutra."
Baizhang Yuan said: "The Great Being and Master Zhi were both led away by the Emperor of Liang in a single indictment.
Xuedou’s verse says: "He did not lodge this body in the Twin Trees, yet he brought up dust and grime in the land of Liang."
Had we not encountered Master Zhizong at that time, we too would have been a weary traveler departing for another land.

One day, the Great Being (Bodhisattva) donned his patched robe, placed a crown upon his head, and slipped on sandals to have an audience with the Emperor. The Emperor asked, "Is this a monk? The Master pointed to his crown.
The Emperor said, "Is this the Way (Dao)? The Master pointed to his sandals. The Emperor said, "Is this a layperson? The Master pointed to—
Regarding "Fingers in the patched robe," Fenyang provided the following substitute response: "The Great Being is versatile.

The Great Being has a verse that says: "Night after night, one embraces the Buddha in sleep; morning after morning, one rises together with him. Whether rising or sitting, he is always in attendance."
Speech and silence dwell together; not even a hair’s breadth separates them. Like a shadow following a form, if you wish to know where the Buddha goes—(Xuedou says:
"Sixty kalpas in three lifetimes")—it is simply this very sound of speech.
Xuansha said, "Master Fu Dashi, great as he was, recognized only that which is bright and alert.
Xuedou said, "Not a single monk in the world can leap out of this; even those whose mouths hang on the wall have another aperture—examine them thoroughly and then strike!
He further said, "Xuansha was striking the grass to startle the snake."

As for the Great Sage of Sizhou, someone asked him, "What is your surname? The Master said, "My surname is He. The person asked, "What country are you from? The Master said, "I am from the country of He."
When Master Wuzhuo went to Mount Tai, Mañjuśrī came forth to meet him and asked, "Virtuous One, from where have you come?
The Master replied, "From the South. [Mañjuśrī] asked, "How is the Dharma maintained in the South? The Master said, "In this age of the final dharma, the bhikṣus rarely uphold the precepts and rules.
[Mañjuśrī] asked, "How many followers do they have? The Master said, "Sometimes three hundred, sometimes five hundred. The Master then asked in turn, "As for this Master, how..."
[The Master] asked, "How do you maintain the Buddha-dharma? Shu replied, "Ordinary people and sages dwell together; dragons and snakes are intermingled.
The Master asked, "How many followers do you have? Shu replied, "Three times three before, and three times three after."
Fenyang spoke in his place, saying: "I recognize you.
Xuedou’s verse says: "A thousand peaks winding and curling, their color like indigo; who would say that Mañjuśrī is here in conversation?"
How laughable that so many in the Qingliang assembly recite, "Three by three in front, and three by three behind.
When Mañjuśrī and his teacher were drinking tea, [Mañjuśrī] picked up a crystal cup and asked, "Is there such a thing as this in the South?"
The Master said, "None. Xuanzhui asked, "What do you usually use to drink tea? The Master had no reply.
Changqing Ling said, "If it is so, it is like a foolish guest advising his host."
As the sun was already low, the Master observed this and asked Mañjuśrī, "I wish to stay here for one night; would that be possible?
Mañjuśrī replied, "You still possess a mind of attachment; you may not stay. The Master said, "I have no mind of attachment. Mañjuśrī asked, "Have you ever received the precepts?"
The Master said, "I have received the precepts for a long time. Shu said, "If you had no mind of attachment, what need would there be to receive the precepts?
The Master took his leave, and the boy Junti escorted him to the gate. The Master asked the boy, "When the Master just now said 'three before, three after,' how many were there?
The boy called out, "Virtuous One! The Master turned his head; the boy said, "How many?"
Dongshan said: "If you wish to observe the person before you, first observe what they employ.
When the Master saw that the temple had no name plaque, he asked a youth, "What is the name of this temple?
The youth pointed behind the Vajra deity and said, "Look! As the Master turned his head, the manifested temple vanished.
The Master traveled to Mount Wutai and encountered an old man. The Master asked, "Are you not Mañjuśrī? The man replied, "How could there be two Mañjuśrīs?
As soon as the Master prostrated himself, the old man suddenly vanished.
Zhaozhou spoke on his behalf, saying: "Mañjuśrī, Mañjuśrī! Tianyi Huai said: "Wuzhuo has only the vanguard;
he lacks the rearguard. Had the old man not vanished, what face would he have had to see Wuzhuo?"
Master Gōngqī was on his way to Luóhàn when he encountered a young gentleman riding an ox along the road.
The Master asked, "Which way does the road to Luóhàn go? The gentleman patted the ox and said, "Speak! Speak! The Master shouted, "This beast!
The gentleman replied, "Which way does the road to Luóhàn go? The Master then patted the ox and said, "Speak! Speak! The gentleman said, "Even if it were as you say..."
There were still some hooves and horns remaining. The Master struck him. The young master patted the ox and fled.
Regarding the Paper-Clothed Wayfarer (Zhīyī Dàozhě), Cáo Shān asked the Master, "Are you not the Paper-Clothed Wayfarer? The Master replied, "I dare not say so.
